"The Passage"
The Passage
The most ambitious rescue I've had the honour to be part of.
I hoped and feared I might one day have the privilege of such an undertaking.
Can we do worse than the Arctic council? They're afraid of the ice in their whisky!
I will not rest while fellow seamen succumb to the cold, we are with you!
The Northwest passage is uncharted, Admiral. More than preparation, we need luck.
I don't want to join the many that tried and failed to find them.
Seaman's intuition tells me they came this way, but I've been wrong before.
I fear we may be as lost as the original expedition.
Let's hope we warm mother nature's frozen heart soon.
The chill already gnaws at the bones of our crew.
If I know Sir John Faithful right, I'd say he came this way.
If these men seem impervious to cold, it's Lady Faithful's fire we have to thank.
I've met few so hardy as Lady Faithful, we can't let her down now.
And I thought the Arctic Council's efforts were pathetic.
We might have turned back long ago, had the mysteries of the ice not drawn us in.
Even I have rarely seen such extremes, and worse may be yet to come.
It's a cairn o'rocks stacked by human hand! We have stumbled upon Sir John Faithful's last encampment!
We've found no trace of Sir John and his crew, let us hope there is time to try again.
We must be better prepared if we are to follow in the fateful footsteps of Sir John.
I knew another captain who ventured this far north, but I know him no more.
We all know this could be our last expedition, so may it be a fine one!
If we die in the attempt, it won't be for a lack of commitment.
It'll be the stuff of folklore if we succeed and bring back Sir John.
Bears, vicious whales and restless spirits await us, if the tales are to be believed.
It's a lot to ask, but to a seaman there's no challenge to rival the Arctic.
A wise seaman would trust the Inuits. They know their land better than we ever will.
I myself have little experience of the Arctic, but stand beside you.
We shouldn't expect to find them right away...this is a vast wilderness.
It's been two years, the Admiralty say they have tried everything, but then, they haven't lost a husband.
—nor did it occur to them to search King William Sound— There! A camp!
Abandoned.
But we imagined as much, didn't we?—and my John picked a fine spot—perhaps they left some sign as to where they went…
My name is Lady Jane Faithful, and it is my husband, Sir John, whose expedition is lost in the Arctic.
In two years, the admiralty haven't done much about his rescue, but fortunately, I have.
I have gathered men and resources to conquer the ice, and to you I offer a handsome reward for bringing him home.
My John's camp shall serve for us. From here we can search to any length and breadth.
Just as they left it. We'll rake over the remains, and then make a refuge for ourselves.
Hold hard! A craig, heaped by highland hand, is well worth our time.
I did say there would be rewards. That's for finding my John's camp.
John's log, open it!— He knew we would come for him.
If HMS Hades and Styx came this way, the Inuit must have seen them; maybe they can help us.
That's the hangar? How marvellous! Sir John will be the first to congratulate you when we find him.
The Hades and Styx came this way, if it take our last breath we must find them.
Here's something more. It'll take our best efforts to clear that frozen channel.
We pick up our crumbs and prepare an especial ice-breaching brigade.
Either we break through that ice, or else we go home now.
Are our ice-breachers ready?
What does it take for a captain to abandon his ship? To cross the ice by foot?
How far did they really expect to take those boats?
*gasp*
No ship, even an icebreaker, can carry us from here, nor will we cover enough ground on foot...
Expensive yes, but with airships you'll be the one to find my John and his boys, I'm certain of it.
The cost and scale of that structure is staggering. But have faith— my John is a risk-taker also.
Now the search can really begin. From high above, this white expanse may seem more finite.
Recommence the search where we left it; at the place the Hades and the Styx were abandoned.
Follow their aura, as others have done, and we can still find them.
One of the Inuit is offering to lead you north, I..I'd only be a hindrance, I'll wait for you on the other side.
John? My John?
Say whatever you like John, I did everything I could to find you, and have absolutely no intention of giving up now.
I am sorry about Sir John. He's had a hard time, they all have.
I am ever so grateful to you, and do not think I have forgotten your reward, but for now I must get my dear husband home.
Old Nate has his quirks, but he is the best, and that is precisely what we need.
Young and brave are our volunteer Explorers, they will soon have the measure of the place.
The Technicians are a difficult lot, but their confidence does appear justified.
...something extra to keep everyone's spirits up...
To ignore the wisdom of the Inuit is an arrogance we cannot afford.
It is bitterly, bitterly cold. Make sure everyone keeps wrapped up.
This encampment must embody hope, our one comfort in the wilderness.
Last night I had a disquieting dream— we cannot allow time to run out.
No small disappointment can cause me to give up hope.
I'll not rest 'til my John is fed, bathed in hot salts and tucked up in bed.
The ice is as old as time, and more stubborn than I ever believed.
My husband is a stubborn man, I hope he was not too proud to heed the Inuit.
I promised I would reward you, and now I have. And thank you, thank you for bringing back my dear John.
I have no idea how expensive that will be, but here. Here, I hope that's a start.
Our efforts should not diminish until the missing are all accounted for.
You have proven all is still possible.
You endure where others have not.
Just when I was beginning to lose faith.
If we all pull together, who knows what we can achieve.
We cannot allow this to stop us believing.
We have let a chance pass us by.
Now I feel the wind begin to bite.
Found something?
Some hope for us?

Too late, too late, they’re all dead. My impudence before the gods; we were doomed from the beginning. My stubbornness— my vile, reckless ambition. I should have died out there with them. I should have died!
John no more, I am a phantom, my love; an exile condemned to this twilight plane for eternity.
Ha. I never could argue with you.
So help me god, get the fires started or the lot of us will freeze!
You might want to start looking for coal.
Wotcha! I'll be joining you. Lady Faithful's engaged me for some practical advice— gonna be dead cold up there.
S'cold enough to freeze the balls off a brass monkey, gorr, get the coal fires burning posthaste.
Ahh, that's nice on the hands, keep it stoked or we'll catch our deaths out here.
First get all ye faithful some shelter, and a canteen where they can warm each other up.
The heat of them heaters don't travel far, and most of your buildings'll need heating and all.
You need a bloomin' airship, you do. Eh, what do you mean borrow mine?—get out of it!
Why not build yer own airships? You'll want to employ a lot of fusspot pseuds though, so watch out.
Build a hangar first; good thought. Better hope the ice don't melt, or that'll be the first thing to go.
What's that you say? No gas? Gorrr….very well, I s'pose I'll have to lend you some.
Pffft Pffft Pffft, can't stop gassing out here, got to keep chattering to stay afloat.
Your first ruddy airship, I bet you feel lighter-than-air!
If you can't squeeze it out of old Archie, I've seen gas come out the ground to the north.
There! Glad I don't have to be yer pump attendant no more, the cheek of it, I ask yer…
Didn't eat each other?! Got to be pulling my leg… oh, too soon?
Oh! This is some scrap from William Perry's failed expedition— still good for a lot of things.
Bet there's more scrap out there from all the other failed expeditions, bring it 'ere, and I'll transmute it.
We've a responsibility to Sir John to gather up his valuables as we go. Hehe.
Lady Faithful hopes to revive her marriage, but Sir John's got cold feet, hehe.
Gorr those Explorers are keen, actually no, they're stark raving mad.
Jumped-up little gits them Technicians, dunno why I put up with 'em.
I like that the Inuit use every part of the animal.
One good thing about the Arctic, equipment don't decompose like cadavers do.
A lot of people tried before Sir John Faithful, left a lot of scrap up in the ice channels.
Got me own Huddlesome Bay Company.
Hurry up, it's cold.
Got to be resourceful up here, eh.
Keep an eye out for scrap from lost expeditions.
If you take yer eye off the heaters, temperatures'll plummet.
Gorr, turn the heating up!
The coal's keeping everyone alive.
The heat don't radiate far.
So cold, you can hear their bones starting to creak.
Been a lot easier if Sir John'd had airships in the first place.
Airships don't come cheap.
It's expensive enough running one airship.
What can I say, hangars take up a lot of space.
I don't like 'em neither, but you need Technicians to have airships.
It shows we have conquered our fear.
Seems the balance is restored.
These are good signs.
You have done well, and you smell nice.
When the ice breaks, I want you there with me.
The wolf has kept you strong, caribou.
There is much to be afraid of now.
I must consult the spirit now.
It is an ill wind that blows nobody any good.
You have damaged the balance of things.
You are meddling in witchcraft.
You have let many people down.
A shaman must help those in need. We will share what we know.
We were afraid you would come for them. Now you are here we must help you.
To know where you are going, you have to know where you come from.
An annuraaq should be watertight.
A fur hood would help shake the snow from your face.
We do not camp anywhere long, the season changes fast.
The igluit are made with anything we can find.
During the long dark winter, we will play games and tell stories.
Seal is important to us, we are careful to waste no part of it.
Take only the whale and bear that you need.
May we repay this kindness.
We are thankful.
Nakurmiik; thank you.
Yes.
Ee.
Good.
Not good.
I am sorry.
Nakka.
May you have warmth in your iglu.
May you have oil in your lamp.
Go with peace in your heart.
Skins can be sewn into clothing with bone needles.
You need a lot of good fat to reach the heart of ice.
Old Nate reminds me of Keelut— he leaves no tracks when feasting on the dead.
We value iron.
Let us trade.
We share what we have.
Act not for yourself, but for the community.
Waste nothing.
I'd prefer to be in a kayak.
I fear they went looking for the heart of ice. We have not seen them for a long time.
I can set you on a path, the rest is down to you.
If you tread carefully, then perhaps a way can be found.
That is the way. Their breath still hangs in the air.
Without belief, answers do not yet exist.
I don't know if your icebreaker will vanquish the ice, but we will not stand in your way.
None of us have much time.
You need to make the best of all you have.
Such strength can redeem your people.
This place is all-powerful, ever-changing, you have to adapt.
We have sighted vessels stranded in the channels. They too will be lost without help.
Better to let others learn from their own mistakes.
Your countrymen will soon become snowbound, and easy prey for Akhlut.
Those men underestimated this place, but you can show them their failings.
They will be glad to come back to light and hospitality, and think on their mistakes.
Seals are everywhere; know how to look for them.
Nanurjuk says they didn't seem right. They said little as if their tongues were cut.
They refused the seals we offered them.
They would not trade, or drink soup with us.
We built them a shelter, but they were already gone, deep into the ice.
Never have I seen beings so pale.
They went beyond the old ice, to a place of danger.
We are afraid Anguta has taken them to the underworld.
There are many ways to survive here, we have learned since childhood.
I will trade with you.
We were scared they were possessed by demons.
They brought sickness with them, and devilry.
We knew you would come for them, we have been waiting for you.
If these are indeed humans you pursue, I will do all I can to help you.
There are many things I could tell you, but I don't think they will help.
There are many sea mammals here, Sedna is their keeper.
We do not meddle in the business of others.
Don't expect to learn everything in a day.
The Council have praised our knowledge, but never respected it.
The vessels you seek are near yet far. Best prepare for terror.
If their vessels drifted to a dark place, maybe they are there still.
They could not have escaped the channels, you will find them there.
We too want answers, you are brave to keep digging.
This is a place of death. You can die here without knowing.
I will not go with you. I hope it is men you find, at the end of your journey.
When wise men die, the heavens lament.
You are on the last floe now, but the most fragile.
You have brought men back from the edge, you have earned our respect.
If you cannot save them, their souls will be trapped in the upper world to starve for eternity.
The lights in the sky cleave heads from the unworthy.
Where the ice between the dead and the living is thinnest, you float across.
I have no power to protect you, when you go to that place.
You have stirred the wrath of the moon!
Do not hunt alone, in darkness, or the wolf will take you.
This is a celestial place, be wary of taboo.
Fear this place, or it will take you smiling.
Nanook decides if you may hunt, or if you violate this place.
Inuksuk said he saw the white people carrying human meat.
I remember they were so dirty, they had lost all humanity.
If you hear a whistling, it is their ghosts, trapped in the upper world.
You saw Amarok. He preys upon those that stray too far from the path.
I cannot say. The spirits become restless when strangers enter their realm. If we stay too long, they will never let us leave.
Glorious it is when wandering time comes.
If you walk on thin ice, you may as well dance.
Be the lead dog, and show where to go.
Find this seal hole.
Watch out for bears.
The strong qimmiq pulls through.
You have a good nose.
We should do what we can to survive.
We should take gifts when they are offered.
It is easy to underestimate this place.
This is a harsh land.
We waste no chance we have here.
Now is your time.
That was only the beginning.
The day is young, there is more to do.
Do you share with the hunting party?
Should I heat some tea?
There is nothing more to be said.
It is a time of silence.
We need more blubber for the kudliks.
A boy who provides is a man.
Hear the ice cracking? Time to hunt seal.
Want to help us catch goose?
I loved those dogs...
Alpaca wool is warm you say?
Warm, but not as warm as a parka of seal or caribou skin.
Can sails have value here?
No wind, no need for sails.
Pigs are so friendly, but will not survive the cold.
Your fish oil tastes like it's bad for you.
Do you mean snow goggles, or something else?
Very clever things if you have bad eyesight— I don't know anyone with bad eyesight.
I drank it and couldn't sleep! If you work all day, you need to sleep.
Some children snuck off to see your city, please can you send them home?
Good, I don't want them to pick up habits. Our community will make them feel loved again.
What kind of weather is it out there? What shape are the clouds?
No clouds? Then Silla has been kind, and we have good hunting weather.
See the natural formation near camp, do you know of any others?
You found a lucky spot. When we next move camp we will move there.
She is one of Sedna's great sharks, I wonder what happened to her.
The creature is gone. Our thanks to you for driving it away.
Look! Something damaged your boat! Maybe the wolf-whale Akhlut, come away!
Can your machine find my amulet? I lost it to the sea in a storm.
A great wave took many hunters.
Built a camp and killed a bear to survive? We underestimated them, they have grown up fast.
The Giant drank so much water she burst open, and fog was born.
The fire is clearing the fog.
The lamp has run low, the fog will not clear.
The fog is lifted. Thank you.
More clues, you are getting close.
This track leads in a new direction.
This is his first crime, we will talk to him and make him feel loved.
He who stole ran into the mountains. I am worried for him.
Everyone has bad sore throats. The elder went over the mountain for cranberries, but he hasn't returned.
Footprints! Why did the elder abandon his sled?
He came to this cave to die. When you have covered him with stones, gather the cranberries.
The cranberries will make us better. Will you help us light a fire for the elder?
Our community won't forget the elder's sacrifice, or yours.
I feared you would come. I will show you where those men went.
Ice has closed the way forward, to the place they took their boats.
The storm makes it hard to see.
Do not become them— I will help you find them.
They abandoned their boats... Will you seek them with this bird of yours?
I dislike it in the clouds. There— clear tracks leading away from the boats.
Styx is a strange name.
Hades has an ominous sound.
They stayed here for a time. But then where?
A dead end.
Too steep. Choose another way.
They took this path— tough with things to carry, I fear for them.
The snow dunes... I fear for them.
We warned them about the dunes. They did not listen.
They dropped it all to make the difficult climb.
I don't know how, but some of them made it.
Bear country. Hunters must be strong to come here.
The bear deserves respect. Nanuk is like one of us.
A storm rises. Your bird will rock like a feather in the wind.
Gone is hope, the domain of night belongs to Amarok.
The men who followed your Faithful here, can be men no longer.
Where did he think he was leading them?
There! Long dead, but moving still.
Amarok spared them so that their story may be retold.
Ah, wonderful!
Ooof, that's very good to know…!
I can rest easy knowing that's settled!
Uplifting!
That's… reassuring!
Thank goodness!
I... really needed that.
There's something to write home about!
What a turnaround!
That's heartening.
I'm not sure that's how it's supposed to be…
Is that so…!?
I wish I'd known when I signed up...
I couldn't have foreseen this...
Oh, no… Oooh, noo…
How will we get through this…?
As if we didn't have enough worries…
No, it can't be!
Mustn't give in to dismay...
Appalling…
I always knew you could make it.
I'll follow your footsteps in the snow!
I will do my best too!
You're a doer!
I will make you proud as well!
How did y-…!? How could y-…?
Why would you...!?
Please, we depend on you…!
You're leaving us all out in the cold!
Are you sure you're well…?
Thank you, thank you so much.
I deeply appreciate it.
Thank you for thinking of us!
You're an immense help!
We couldn't do this without you!
Makes my day a good bit easier.
Nah-koor-meek… Did I say that correctly?
We look out for each other.
That greatly eases things.
A much-needed comfort.
Y-yes!
Very good!
Oh, this? It's only a sketch. My father used to draw the birds he spotted on our trips and I followed suit.
I'm very glad Old Nate's around, his chuckles are contagious.
I never saw stars as sharp as they are here…
Yesterday I didn't burst into tears at any point, must mean I'm getting used to this.
I've been meaning to ask the technicians about their work, but they keep shooing me away…!
Is that technician gone already…? Good...
I'm sure technicians know what they're doing, but do they have to say things like that…?
Lady Jane is so impressive. I can't imagine what I would do if my little brother went missing…
Sometimes I sneak into the hangar just to watch Old Nate ordering the technicians about.
I tried rubbing my coat with fish oil to repel water, just like the Inuit do. But now it's all smelly…
When I feel I can't keep going, I read a page from The Journey of Victory Ashen — one of the great explorers. I've come to keep that book very close.
I saw two tiny arctic foxes in their summer coats the other day. One for the sketchbook.
Ah, to be tightly-wrapped in my sleeping bag after a long day of work... I could stay forever inside that furry cocoon.
My brother will be turning eleven soon! I hope the shark's tooth gets there in time...
I had dreamt of sledding, climbing and mountaineering. But we won't get much of that, will we?
Maybe one day a little girl will read about me and be inspired to follow in my snowy footsteps…
I may have forgotten what it's like to feel my nose.
Is it… Is it colder inside than out?!
I'm trying to keep moving, but I can't shake the cold.
I thought Victory Ashen's descriptions of the arctic cold were literary exaggerations...!
I never imagined I could be colder than that February night we camped in the Lakes…
It would be so helpful!
Could I beg a second of your time…?
I may need some help…
I have to admit, I can't do this on my own…
It would make life up here much easier…
It's not something I can do alone…
Can you help me…?
Could I have some guidance…?
It would take a terrible weight off my shoulders...
Can I rely on you?
You will? Thank you!
If there's anything I can do to help...
That you're willing to try means a lot to me.
Yes? Ah! I'm so glad.
You can do anything you set out to!
When you have a moment...
Do you think you'll have time to spare soon…?
We don't have much time…
So regarding that...?
Have there been setbacks?
Oh…
I'd been depending on that…
I should never have troubled you in the first place...
I see…
*Disappointed, tired sigh*
Oh, you're back!
Y-yes?
There you are!
So? How did it go?
Good news?
Looks like you have something to report!
Did something peek its nose from the seal hole?
What did you find in the snow?
You've renewed my spirit!
I feel I can keep pushing on now.
I will remember your support!
This will keep me strong.
It's nice to know I'm not alone out here.
This is their last known location…
The tracks begin here…
I see…
So that's what happened…
The tracks led here…
Hmmm...
Ready when you are.
Just say the word.
Everything is prepared.
Has it been confirmed?
All set?
I would like you to have this.
I have something for you.
Put it to good use.
I thought you might appreciate it.
We're here, the Arctic. This is where our adventure begins!
We'll all die here, won't we?
I want to go home, please let me go home.
We are all doomed…
Brrrrrrrrrrr.
No human being can survive this…
Will I ever see my family again…?
I shouldn't have come here…
What am I going to tell father…?
Whyever did I think of coming here…!?
None of my books mentioned just how cold…
Uncle was right, I should never have enrolled.
I thought I could do this…
The cold will kill us all…
I won't be able to keep this up much longer…
It's so cold. It's just so cold...
I can do it, I can do it….
Could people get used to this?
It's the Arctic; I expected a struggle.
Never mind my feelings, there's so much to do.
I hope we do no harm to the Arctic by warming it.
I can't believe I'm really here.
Adventuring was never likely to be easy.
Coming here was a dream, I can have no complaints.
Warmth in the camp at least.
I'm warm enough.
I'm glad of the heaters, ugly though they be.

CAPITOL NEWS!

Unveiling of palace heralds government’s ambition for more efficient lawmaking. Exchequer refuses to reveal how extravagant building costs will be paid for – see p.6 for our own Walker Haggar’s daring Crown Jewel pawn theory...

Build additional wings to widen the range of your palace's main building.
The number of wings you can build increases as your profile level grows based on global population.

All departments have a base effect that applies to their target buildings as long as they are within range of the palace. For example, all town halls connected by street to the palace are affected by the Department of Administration.

You can issue one policy per department at a time.
Open the policies menu and hover over them to see more details about how they can affect your city, and which buildings they affect.
Your palace's prestige is linked to city attractiveness — raising attractiveness will unlock more departments and policies.
In this overview, you can check which departments and policies will be unlocked at which attractiveness level. Furthermore, you can select which policies you want to make active.

Congratulations! You've unlocked all the departments and policies for your palace! But it doesn't end here: increase the attractiveness of your city, and gain prestige levels that will heighten your departmental effects!

Local departments allow you to bring the effects of your palace to the rest of your cities. Even if their departments and policies are unlocked from your palace, local departments can issue their own policies.
You can now build a palace! Choose carefully which city you want to build it in: as the heart of your empire, you'll only be able to build one.
The range of your local departments is proportional — but not equal! — to that of the Palace. Building more wings on your palace will extend it.

The instructive sort of ornamentation welcomed by itinerant politicians and choosy civil servants.
Amble through the grounds along these stately paths to clear the mind for the afternoon debate!
"...all who move that the lower snooker rooms and second sherry cellar be repurposed for storage, say 'aye'!"
"I will not, gentlemen, stand for an initiative that would have us serve offal at banquets like common continentals!"
"What are a few exploding mice on our bankroll to the enthusiasms of youth and the might of science?"
"And so it is decreed: all offices of this institution shall benefit from technology and consultants befitting of their pursuits."
"My point, sir, is that you would not so readily gild every ruddy frontispiece as you would this town hall, if you did not stand to profit from it!"
"If the Enbesa delegation to the Fair is to receive additional acres, it is only right that the offer should be extended to all."
"Our mandate lies with our people's right to education and culture. The motion to display infinitely more cabinets of curiosities passes!"
"It is within our remit to ensure all species - aye, even trout! - be given fit diet, and the space and habitat to roam!"
"I moot that a national stipend be provided to all estates willing to host a tour of their wondrous collections. All in favour?"
"Jeer all you will, milords, but remember who built your lofty palaces. In fact, our economy craves more talented foreigners!"
"If the lords would only allow their land to be better used, we might see a surge in domestic product!"
"The efficient running of individual factories must be of interest to us, if we truly wish to see the economic boom so often promised."
"We know too well, professor, what abhorrent purpose drives your support of this bill. Such bolts of power are not man's to hurl!"
"Skilled labour is the cornerstone upon which our great nation is built, and with these provisions, it shall soon bear fruit!"
"Having imprisoned two of their leaders only last week, we need to make more allowances if we want to placate the unions!"
"Now is not the time for thrift! There is money to be found in our people's pockets - we need but coax it out of them!"
"Lord Alfred's 'Waltz of the Light Brigade' will make for a perfect centrepiece to the program - they will throng to the theatres!"
"All in agreement that galvanic sheathing should be at, but not in excess of nine thousand units, say 'aye'."
"I have a dream, milords - a dream that one day our peoples will rise up in the nurture of our care! A dream of freedom!"
"They'll drink themselves deaf anyway - at least let them do so away from the eyes of proper society!"
"Gentlemen, I would remind you of the fate of Innsmouth. Would you strangle efficiency, and have this city suffer similar sordor?"
"Oh come now, they stink so much already they can hardly complain of a few additional tons of fish crammed into storage!"
"That our oil stores are stretched is grave news indeed. Unless we pass this bill, I fear we'll have to resort to tossing dissenters into the sea."
"All eyes turned to our ports, and yet you would block an extension of the docklands? A lesser man would doubt your allegiance, sir!"
"Think of them as ants, my lord. Minute, devoted ants, single-mindedly attending to ships for the city's profit - and our own."

In Fuel Station Storage
The engineer asks you to trial tractors on a grain farm.

Oh, you've seen the article about motorised agricultural vehicles — or tractors, as the press has taken to calling them? Well, I've been greatly looking forward to testing them outside of a controlled environment. Would you be willing to be our first test subject, governor? A grain farm should do the trick.
The engineer begins her tractor lecture.
The engineer documents the success of your tractors.

Build on any grain farm:
[Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Expand the farm's cultivation area
Deliver fuel to the tractor barn
Connect [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] to a fuel station

The goal of the vehicle's design was to reduce the human workforce required, increase productivity, and allow farms to cover a larger area. This means you can have more fields. Let's put it into practice: please build a tractor barn on one of your grain farms.
Wow! What's all this, master? A tractor barn and tractors!? It's a chance for us to finally grow — we should expand the fields!

Indeed, you can already start to lay down more farm fields — but your tractors won't be able to function until they've been fuelled. For this to happen, the tractor barn needs a street connection to a nearby fuel station.

I also offer you the blueprints for the proposed fuel station. Fuel stations refine oil into fuel and deliver it to all nearby tractor barns, provided there's a road connection. Pretty convenient, if I do say so myself!

You may have noticed that the fuel station has a loading platform for trains. Indeed, the fuel station requires oil from your oil harbour via the railway connection. It then uses it to produce fuel, which in turn is delivered to tractor barns.
We'll certainly miss our dear little tractors if they run out of fuel, but I promise we'll go on working as if we'd never had them, master!

Following extensive research, prototyping and production, the engineer is ready to present her latest invention: the tractor. She's asked you to test them on one of your grain farms. However, getting them up to speed won't be all that easy: for the tractors to work, you'll also need a fuel station. But worry not — the engineer will be there to help you plough through the whole process.
The farmer asks you to build a silo on a pig farm.
The market was abuzz with talk of them new silos. Could solve a lot of our problems. How about we try one with a pig farm, master?
The farmer is happy to see the silo up and running.

Build on any pig farm:
[Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Deliver grain to the pig farm's silo
The amount of fodder we can stock up in this silo...! It makes things so much simpler for us farmers! How come your brainboxes didn't think of it sooner?

Grain is what you want to use for silos. We need carts to come and go with the grain for the silo, so make sure there's a road to pick up grain from somewhere nearby. Hmm, I wonder what they'll use for fodder in places where there ain't no grain...?

Ah, master, it's no bother if the grain runs low for some reason. We'll manage without the silo just like we did before. I suppose you might see the numbers drop off until we can use it again, though...

The farmer heard all about silos on market day and wants to make use of them. The silos will help all animal farms stock up on fodder and improve their productivity. She's asked you to build one on a pig farm, making sure that it's stocked up with grain.
A NEW DAWN FOR AGRICULTURE

Engines whirr onto farms all over the globe as the joint efforts of agriculturalists and engineers culminate in the creation of the tractor! What can these motorised mastodons do for our economy? We expect [Participants Current Profile CompanyName] will once again chevron a path in the soil for others to follow!
SILOS: KEY TO ANIMAL HUSBANDRY?

Agribusinesses to take the spotlight! Animal farms all around the world class silos as an essential. Using smart distribution systems, fodder is stocked and easily fed to livestock, turning grazing into a faster process. We can't wait to see what [Participants Current Profile CompanyName]'s farms can achieve with the help of silos.

Talk to Ketema about the Old World
Extraordinary! Do tell me more about this Old World of yours...
No empire is built upon a single thing, but what would you say is the Old World's greatest legacy?
Our cultural impact.
Hmm, interesting! And how do you share that culture among your people?
Actually, I don't know that much about culture...
A small museum or zoo is usually enough to keep visitors happy.
Substantial investment in museums and zoos is essential for the sharing of knowledge and culture.
I've worked like a Trojan to put every animal and artefact under the sun on display at my zoos and museums.
Our industrial prowess and economic growth.
Tall cities, then: vast, prosperous, and beautiful?
To be perfectly honest, my own cities are microscopically small... **Cough**
If one's cities are too excessive in scale, one can lose too much of the romantic...
I pride myself in cities vast in population, with access to every comfort and convenience.
Metropolises everywhere! Not a sheaf of wheat lies unguzzled by the hungry gob of progress!
Our naval advancements and military conquests.
A strong military is the foundation of many an empire, for good, or for ill — tell me more...
That said, I own scarcely a scrap of a fleet myself...
I have a few ships, but I'm probably not the best-known sea lord...
My ships and defences are widely known for their might and domination of the seas.
You're talking to an old salt! My fleet is the largest and mightiest ever seen!
And what do you like the most about your position as an architect, builder... polymath?
Exploring the world, unearthing its secrets.
Becoming a master builder — the keystone of my business.
Governing my people, ensuring they grow and thrive.
Being a sea lord, controlling the seven seas.
An intrepid explorer! Well... I too love to explore the world — albeit these days, only through its many histories. Here's a small gift that may suit your ambitions.
Master builder? Well, that's why you are so welcome here in Enbesa. I just happen to have a gift that may suit your ambitions.
So you are a populist?! Or so noble that your concern for your people is genuine. Either way, I have a gift that may suit your ambitions.
So you sail the seas and enjoy maritime antics? My empire also depends greatly upon ocean trade. Perhaps this gift will pair well with your ambitions.

Sir Archibald: "Perhaps you could introduce us, Empire to 'Empire'?"
This is Sir Archibald Blake, the Queen's ambassador.
This is Sir Archibald Blake, a man of culture and decency.
This is old Archie Blake, my best friend.

Sir Archibald: "I come to you in person, since Her Majesty's letters do not seem to be reaching you...They contain, should you not already be aware, copies of a protectorate agreement requiring your swift signature. Such an agreement would guarantee Enbesa's protection against envious forces in the region, and leave your people's future in the safe hands of the Queen — an offer any judicious tributary to the Crown would be delighted with."
Protection? You mean to make Enbesa a vassal!
Emperor Ketema: "Hear that, Biniam — our steward here adds their voice to ours. Sir Archibald, I happen to agree with my steward — this proposal is outrageous."
The Queen is indeed powerful — it's an offer worth your consideration.
Enbesa is herself a great empire — there is no reason you should bow to these terms.
Such an offer could benefit both parties.
(Remain silent and let Biniam speak)
Yes... Perhaps Sir Archibald here did not make the most gracious of entrances, but before we dismiss him, we should take the time to hear he and his Queen's point of view.
(Remain silent and let Biniam speak)

Kiburi Biniam: "Bridging the divide between our two peoples has always been my dream, as well as that of Janihoy Ketema — but not like this... Enbesa will not be subordinated — she is an Empire in her own right, and the equal of any other. What say you to an imperial alliance between Ketema and your Queen, for example?"
Emperor Ketema: "Imperial Enbesa does not need what you call protection, but a fair alliance — toe-to-toe, equal to equal. That, I would be ready to discuss."
Sir Archibald, I believe it would be right to agree to such an alliance.
Sir Archibald, perhaps you could take some time to think over it.

Sir Archibald: "An alliance?! Preposterous! She is not MY Queen, she is THE Queen — OUR Queen. Why am I even here, if you're going to behave like a pair of parochial stick-in-the-muds! Now if you don't mind, I shall take my leave, as these farcical negotiations are over!

What is happening? Why is my son Biniam not with you?
(Tell the truth) Your son has been arrested for arson, and awaits transportation to the Antipodes.
Imprisoned? Oh, my boy! My poor boy! Oh what happened, what happened?

Sir A-Archibald? I... then the moment I have always feared has come. Though for it to come like this... There may yet be a way to settle the matter — but it will not be pleasant for any concerned. How would you like to help an old lady replant her orange trees? Be sure to dig deep when you do...
Biniam acted rashly and tried to sabotage Archibald Blake's outpost.

There may yet be a way to settle the matter — but it will not be pleasant for any concerned. How would you like to help an old lady replant her orange trees? Be sure to dig deep when you do...

Yes, he is... er... negotiating, with Sir Archibald Blake.
A...Archibald Blake? Oh, now I know you're hiding something! Tell me everything, now!
Sir Archibald arrested and imprisoned him.

Participate in the final negotiation

Sir Blake, I am glad to see you back at the negotiation table, and with, if I be not mistaken, a certain composure to your face. Nevertheless, as this has been a difficult business, I hope you will take this opportunity to recognise Enbesa as an empire worthy of an alliance. (Ketema glances across the table at you) Don't you agree, my long-standing steward? Enbesa grows greatly, does it not?
Enbesa is no small empire, and continues to grow! She would be an asset to the Crown.
Yes, quite right! I will add that the Crown recognizes Enbesa as an empire of significant size and promise. Anything else?
Looking at the total population of this region, I know it may not seem that way, but...
And Enbesa is united? There is no internal strife, or unresolved quarrel from any quarter that Her Majesty should be aware of?
Yes, we can happily say that Enbesa is now a unified empire. Ketema is a leader acclaimed by all.

Yes, I must admit Janihoy, I was surprised to see all of these communities, formerly so opposed to Enbesan unification, now incorporate. The mark of a true leader, such as Her Majesty. I think she will be delighted, therefore, to call Enbesa an equal.
I'm afraid that the three independent peoples of the region have not all agreed to side with Janihoy Ketema...

Interesting... The Crown values these foundations, be certain of it. And what of Enbesan history? Of course, we have a long and chequered history of our own to learn from — is the same true of Enbesa?
Yes, Enbesa has a proud, and frankly, extremely complicated history, too. (Pass Sir Archibald a copy of the book)
Ah, a copy of the new and revised edition of the Enbesan annals, I see? Fascinating! A treasured gift that we shall give pride of place in the national library!
I don't know that much about history...

I am starting to feel it is I who should be selling this alliance to you, gentle Emperor... Perhaps, having a foot in both camps so to speak, your remarkable Keftanya steward here could elaborate on why Her Majesty might make a worthwhile ally to Enbesa.?
Her Majesty's empire is clever in the extreme, and it is said the sun never sets on its sprawling dominions...
Yes, I have witnessed the Crown's power, and how it casts great shadows. I am certain, in the matter of empire building, I could not wish for a more suitable ally.
If you don't mind, Sir Archibald, I'd really rather remain loyal to Emperor Ketema in these negotiations.
And I can't remember — was it you, or someone else that helped me get to grips with mapping the local area?
Yes, I helped! Accurate cartographical charts are a key part of the Crown's very wise strategy.

A wise Queen indeed is she who understands a map is worth more than two-score galleons — although if you don't mind, Sir Archibald, we will continue to use the names for our landmarks bequeathed to us millennia ago...
Definitely someone else... old chap.

If I may, Janihoy... Sir Archibald... I have a proposal of my own to append to this alliance, which I believe shall strengthen it tenfold. All my life, I have dreamed of bridging learning across the globe; to share knowledge from all lanes of the human experience. I now entrust you with these plans to build residences for scholars, so that they may come from all horizons to unite in your research centre! Where better than the melting pot that is the Old World to construct such a wonder, and see in brighter futures for all?
Sail to the places indicated by Sir Archibald

After many trials en route to Enbesa, you have finally arrived. The Emperor Ketema hopes you will be able to lend him your expertise, as he seeks to expand his new capital, Taborime.

Emperor Ketema needs your help in establishing Taborime as the new, modern capital of Enbesa by building a new district. The traditional seat of kings in years gone by, only a small settlement and palace remain in this arid province, and Ketema calls upon you to help with the expansion.

Emperor Ketema needs your help in establishing Taborime as the new, modern capital of Enbesa by producing wanza wood. The traditional seat of kings in years gone by, only a small settlement and palace remain in this arid province, and Ketema calls upon you to help with the expansion.

Emperor Ketema needs your help in establishing Taborime as the new, modern capital of Enbesa by producing goat milk. The traditional seat of kings in years gone by, only a small settlement and palace remain in this arid province, and Ketema calls upon you to help with the expansion.

Ketema and his trusted advisor Biniam have designed an irrigation system to tackle the problem of water scarcity in this particular region of Enbesa. Ketema hopes that you will be able to successfully install and trial it.

Having established a new community within Taborime, you are asked by Emperor Ketema to provide two significant aspects of life, without which Taborime will never prosper in the Enbesan tradition — fine clothes and music.
The Emperor Ketema asks that you help protect the people of Taborime from the ravages of fire, by connecting a fire station to the water canals.

Emperor Ketema asks for photographs of Old World trading posts. He believes there is much to be learned from the Empires of the Old World, especially if Enbesa is to be recognised in that quarter as an Empire in its own right.

Emperor Ketema asks you a series of probing questions regarding the Old World. He believes there is much to be learned from the Empires of the Old World, especially if Enbesa is to be recognised in that quarter as an Empire in its own right.

Biniam wants your help examining various architectural proposals for a monumental building he is calling "The Research Institute." It is Biniam's belief that the expertise of scholars from all around the world might be brought together under one roof: a truly international campus university housed in the cultural nexus that is the Old World.
Emperor Ketema extols the virtues of the Enbesan dried meat curing process, and asks you to help him provide the people of greater Taborime with plenty of this enduring local speciality.

Still very much in good humour, Janihoy Ketema tests you with a riddle. There seems to be something more to the towers of his Imperial palace. Each bears an animal representing one facet of Enbesan identity, a kingdom with a strict hierarchy...

Emperor Ketema expresses the Empress' disappointment at the condition of the time-honoured bathing area in the vicinity of the Imperial Palace. He hopes you will be able to restore it in keeping with its importance to the ancient line of kings, but also as a central place of commune for the people of Taborime.
Emperor Ketema asks you to investigate a behooven miracle — a baaarbershop quintet of pitch-perfect goatlets. Perhaps with a little prompt from a conductor...

Following the momentarily amusing goat diversion, Emperor Ketema wishes for a quick return to serious business. He asks that you invite the strident yet venerable elders to preside over the new district of Taborime that you've established.
Emperor Ketema does not wish to give Sir Archibald opportunity to settle unchecked at his borders, and asks if you would reach out and see what, exactly, it is that he is after.

Emperor Ketema accepts it is his obligation to welcome Sir Archibald to a formal banquet at his palace, at the summit of Taborime. He hopes you will be able to provide dried meat and tapestries commensurate with such an occasion.

Sir Archibald is having great difficulty acclimatising to the change of temperature and culture. He hopes you will give him a leg up and share the water canal design patents Ketema and Biniam developed.

Sir Archibald is rather jumpy at having been thrown into the deep end here in Enbesa. He asks if you, as a person he knows and trusts, would act as a guide and escort him to the diplomatic banquet Ketema has laid on.
Emperor Ketema extends an invitation to you to attend the important meeting with Sir Archibald, believing you may be able to offer support as a non-partisan intermediary.

Sir Archibald, like all Crown patriots, believes the first step in conquering and mastering new lands is to map their contours and mark and identify any POIs. He hopes that you will sidestep your loyalty to Ketema for a moment and help him out.

Emperor Ketema maintains that introducing Sir Archibald to the sensory joys of Enbesan culture can win him over to its self-sufficiency, leading to the possibility of happier and renewed negotiations.
Emperor Ketema asks you to exhibit the beauty of the lands and people of Enbesa through a photographic series, centred upon the three most iconic island communities of the region.
Sir Archibald wants to impress upon Ketema the superiority of Old World industrialisation, and asks you to provide sufficient photographic documentation.

Biniam is asking you to help him headhunt a core team of academic experts to help get the Research Institute off the ground. A team of renown should help bring in scholars from every continent in their droves.
Emperor Ketema believes having more elders in the Keftanya Moot will make Taborime more commanding in the face of adversity. Attract more elders and grow the city.

Expand the city in line with Ketema's ambitions. Emperor Ketema wishes for Taborime and its many districts to grow larger still, especially now that it is under the scrutiny of the Crown and Sir Archibald.
Sir Archibald does not like to see Taborime and Enbesa expanding so fast in this region, and hopes to offer you 'incentives' to stall the expansions Ketema has proposed you carry out for him.

Emperor Ketema has decided that tensions have escalated enough between Enbesa and the Crown to warrant the construction of additional fortifications. Sir Archibald may have little or no firepower for a war at present, but the Royal Fleet could in theory be called upon to make the long voyage from the Old World.

Sir Archibald is aware of Emperor Ketema's plan to further fortify Taborime with cannons, and hopes that you will instead 'accidentally' fulfil his own request for the identical materials required for their assembly.

Guests, like fish, begin to smell after a few days. Emperor Ketema decides that sending Sir Archibald a beehive as a gift will signal to him the unity and self-sufficiency of Enbesa, as well as the willingness of his people to defend their home in the face of any provocation...

Sir Archibald's insolent response to escalating tensions is to ask you to deliver Ketema a mocking gift — copious amounts of fruit from the Old World, all of which appears too overripe to be properly enjoyed.

Biniam is disgusted by the seemingly malignant actions of Sir Archibald Blake, whose gift of fruit spread disease in Taborime. Biniam wants your help in sneaking onto the island of Little Clarence, in order for him to take revenge by cutting off Sir Archibald's island-wide water supply.

Biniam is disgusted by the seemingly malignant actions of Sir Archibald Blake, whose gift of fruit spread disease in Taborime. Biniam wants your help in finding the water pumps on Little Clarence, so he may cut off Sir Archibald's island-wide water supply and avenge Enbesa.

Emperor Ketema is dismayed at your and Biniam's inflammatory actions, and decides he has no choice now but to gather a fleet in Enbesa, to deal with any future reprisal from Sir Archibald, and indeed, his Queen.

Emperor Ketema requests that you help the population keep the faith during this difficult time by providing them with scriptures — perhaps hoping for a miraculous intervention in what increasingly seems like a war between Enbesa and the Crown.

Emperor Ketema has sent you to Kyria, Biniam's mother, so that you may bear her the bad news that her beloved son is to be transported to the far side of the world as punishment for his actions. How you break the news to her is up to you.
Kyria has a number of questions about recent events involving her son Biniam that mean he is now being kept in Sir Archibald's jail on Little Clarence.
Kyria seems to be keeping something of importance close to her chest. She has suggested, however, that you try uprooting her orange trees, and see what you may find.
Kyria seems to be keeping something of importance close to her chest. Having uprooted her orange trees, you discovered a humble old journal belonging to Kyria. Open it.

Kyria asks you to visit Kidusi Anitoni, where the priests keep record of Enbesan history, both ancient and modern. If you ask for the 'Register of the IXth Regiment', all will become clear, if it hasn't already.

Kyria asked you to visit Kidusi Anitoni, where the priests keep record of Enbesan history, both ancient and modern. You loaned 'Register of the IXth Regiment' from the priests. Now, it's time to read it.

Emperor Ketema regrets that the only way to deliver Kyria to Sir Archibald, so she may inform him that his prisoner Biniam is actually his long-lost son, is to destroy the mercenary vessels currently blockading Little Clarence. Ketema believes this is the only way to prevent the advent of a disastrous war.

Archibald wishes for you to accompany him, and talk with him ahead of the final negotiations for the recognition of Enbesan independence. The outpost of Little Clarence has been dismantled, and it seems Sir Archibald has no intention of maintaining any further Crown presence in the region.
Emperor Ketema would be delighted if you could join him, Biniam and Sir Archibald at the negotiation table, as he hopes to finalise Enbesan independence.

Emperor Ketema suggests you realise Biniam's dream of a Research Institute in the Old World. He too believes the work of international scholars will be of great benefit to your business prospects, as well as a significant moment in the history of science.
The Captain recommends an expedition to discover what the warm and fertile lands beyond the newly-opened Culysma Canal may hold in store for you.

Though the journey to Enbesa was smooth enough, Sir Archibald Blake worries that the mandate he was handed for Enbesa may be of greater ambition than he had first suspected. The land is vast, its people complex and its culture rich. There is much to learn, and little time to learn it in.
He has consequently enlisted your help in providing a preliminary survey of landmarks of Enbesa, the better to understand the land.

Your journey mapping the confines of Enbesa for Sir Archibald takes an unforeseen turn when you stumble upon a hidden boneyard, strewn with the half-sedimented remains of hundreds of elephants. Amid the hushed silence, Sir Archibald spots a youngling, fearful and lost.

Your journey mapping the confines of Enbesa for Sir Archibald takes a further picturesque turn when sudden light breaks on a tall structure — jutting stones, as if raised by some eldritch hand out of the lowlands. A humbling sight, mighty and thought-provoking.

Your journey mapping the confines of Enbesa for Sir Archibald comes to a lurching halt near the mightiest falls you have ever seen, tonitruous and roiling. Scattered relics of a time long gone seem to hint at a past occupation that Sir Archibald knows only too well.

Your journey mapping the confines of Enbesa has uncovered a quaintly arching rock in the water, spurring Sir Archibald into a competitive disposition. Feeling the winds pick up, he suggests a friendly wager to test the seaworthiness and speed of your ship against his. To the victor the spoils — and the honour!

Buried Orange Blossom

...many soldiers on Waha Desher come from the North. Yara and the older girls say Northerners are bad-souls, and that when the Land Of Kush is taken, they will turn on us — those who have given them Ahku. But today, I have come to know at least one who is warm-capable...

...Thoughts of the boy-soldier distract me and I am scolded by the elders. Just like the Northerners Yara complains of, the other soldiers mocked their lieutenant when he stopped to help me. Of course, I can drain the pus from a horse's stone-bruise alone, but I could not just turn him away...

I saw him today, my boy-soldier! Up on the walls of the Ksar — seems they are planning to stay a while longer, as they have King Wag's blessing in their war against the Kushites. When my boy-soldier looked down and noticed me there, he smiled and waved! Although I did my best to frown, he only smiled more.

...Now the lieutenant knows the word issehd — which as we know is a word with many uses, impertinent of you to ask, my dear diary! — so I taught him some bond-words too. None of the other soldiers are learning Waha Deshan, so I must assume that he is does it for my own special benefit!...

He cannot believe the sweetness of the oranges in the grove, my soldier-boy — the little sneak-djat followed me home. Under their shadow, he told me of the kings and queens in the Old World. His king, he says, is "violent-mad," and I tell him King Wag is much the same — "like twins separated at birth." I feel sad as he looks softly into my eyes and says, "with a ruler like that... you never know where they'll send you next."

He comes in secret to my garden every evening. It's not the oranges that interest him, but they're always the excuse. "So sweet!" he says, the silly boy-solider. "Your friends up at the ksar, do they not miss you?", I ask, "Do you not like to drink scotch, and ill-speak the many women you know?" "No," he says, "I prefer to be here with you."

I told him. "Awo," I said, "I have a baby in my belly." He told me it was wonderful news, and embraced me as never before. Feeling his warm cheek on mine, I pushed him away to get a better look at him, brushing the silly flop of hair from his eyes, "You are going to be a father now — you can't be a soldier-boy anymore."

I worry when I see his face, eyes dancing around, up toward the ksar. But still my boy-soldier dotes on his Kyria when he can — which is not so often anymore. He tells me rumour of our being together has reached the regiment. "So?" I reply, "Better the truth is out — and you won't be one of them much longer anyway..." But he turns his head, and will speak no more of it.

Of course he has left us here, the bump and I. Why a Northerner? I should have listened to Yara — everyone who told me I was a fool. The last he said was "meet me under the orange trees." But he didn't come to me that day, nor any day since. "Duty" is what he will call it; his ship slipping now in starless-grey, back to his home. I bury our wreaths of Orange Blossom in a love-grave.

Biniam was born three days ago, and he is beautiful. So beautiful. Why did I ever doubt it? But I love him. He is Biniam, after his great-grandfather. When I woke they gave me a birth-gift from the father. "Get out! Get out!" I yelled, and then cried to myself for a while. I will not read what crawls about like scorpions in his note. But there was money — so much money! At least orange-sweet Biniam will live his life better than I live mine.

TRANSLATED FROM THE ENBESAN

Biniam my love,

Mother hasn't heard from you in a while, and is heart-sick with worry, so do please write. I am sure you've not forgotten me here by the wasi, as you have always been such an attentive boy — always helping mother cook and clean the livelong years. I am sure you must simply be so time-busy with Janihoy Ketema's plans for Taborime, and this important visitor from afar.

Perhaps your plan for the Research Institute has met with approval! Oh yes indeed — I cling to the thought that such things keep you from me, and that no misfortune is the cause of this sudden silence between us. My affection-wishes as always.

Your mother, Kyria.

We are nomads passing through these nameless valleys. We are not part of Enbesa — not part of anything but our own business.
It's only a matter of time before some Empire claims these lands... Then we nomads will have no choice but to keep moving on.
If Ketema and his people claim these lands, or the Northmen, we will just keep moving on, as our people have always done.
To start the expedition, go to the World Map and select the Land of Lions Expedition.
Click on Emperor Ketema, standing in his palace courtyard, to read his riddle.
There are several towers marked around him. Maybe the order of the animals in the riddle has something to do with it?
Click on Emperor Ketema, standing in the market, to read the sequence of notes that form the song.
There are several goats marked near him. Each goat "sings" a different note. Click on the goats in the sequence of the song.
Fulfil all your shepherds' needs, and then upgrade any fully-occupied residence to elders.
Fulfil all artisan needs in the Old World, and then upgrade any fully-occupied artisan residences to engineers.
Attract more elders by building more shepherd residences, fulfilling their needs and upgrading them.
You can decrease your population's happiness by denying them happiness needs, making their working conditions worse, or by demolishing public services.
Transfer military ships from the Old World to Enbesa.
Any military ship in the Enbesa session counts, e.g. gunboats, ship-of-the-lines, or battle cruisers.

One of your shepherds would like to share the simple pleasures of life with you. He would be delighted if you could join him in a nearby pasture to enjoy the quiet beauty of nature while his sheep graze.
Use the button to jump to the pasture.
There is a tree with a length of fabric tied to it near the pasture in question.
A shepherd hopes you'll come and enjoy the pasture where his sheep graze.

Shepherd Diniki has a close bond with all his flock, but Amun is easily his favourite (even if it isn't a good idea for a shepherd to get too attached to his sheep). While presenting them to you, he noticed Amun was nowhere to be found. With panic rising in his voice, he asks you to help him find his most precious sheep.
Amun is particularly vocal (for a sheep); follow the bleating!
Amun has likely strayed into a cave on the mountainside.
Diniki is thrilled to have found Amun, but alarmed by the burning bush beside him.
The shepherd is worried about his sheep Amun, and asks for your help in finding him.
The shepherd talks about Amun as you search together.

The elders are awed at the burning bush, an undeniable sign of the Almighty's power and grace. That it was found by a sheep and first seen by a meniga (shepherd), the lowest of the low, testifies to the authenticity of the miracle. They insist you honour this manifestation of the divine in the proper fashion, by building a monastery.
The monastery must be built where the burning bush was sighted.
The burning bush was witnessed at the foot of the mountain.
The elders are convinced the bush is a sign, and ask you to build a monastery to honour it.
Diniki rejoices in the simple knowledge that Amun is safe and can be cared for again.

A family of meniga (shepherds) are being harassed by their covetous landlady and her extortionate tax demands. Their crops have been poor this year, and they are facing eviction if they default on their obligation. A kindly neighbour has asked if you can help them out of their predicament.
Crop yield might improve with a productivity-enhancing item, equipped at the local trade union.
The landowner is next to the shepherd's house with her guards. Try talking to her...?
A shepherd hopes you will assist a family unable to pay high taxes.
The shepherd is saddened that you could not help in the matter.
The elder appreciates that you did not interfere.
The shepherd thanks you, but worries that the elder's unfair demands will continue.
Equip any item which improves the farms.
Select the landowner to talk to her.

The elder reacted to the family's sudden increase in yield by substantially raising her tax demands, and now the family can barely meet her expectations. The shepherd is outraged at this cruelty, and plans to strike back by replacing most of the crops to be delivered with dry teff grass. He asks for your help in righting this wrong.
The shepherd is upset that the landlady continues to take advantage of the family.
The elder appears satisfied with the tax yielded to her(!)
The shepherd is pleased you managed to pull the wool over the elder's eyes.
"Old-fashioned laws should not hold sway over living people. You must be held to account!" Have the landlady arrested.

"I will not uproot your institutions, but I will pay the meniga's debts for them."
Pay the elder what is owed.

"You are right, I overstepped my duties. Far be it from me to interfere with custom."
Leave the elder to her tax collection.

"Why are you now poking your nose in, Keftanya Steward? It is in the meniga's nature to serve — and if they cannot serve, they have no purpose in our society! I suggest you refrain from attempting to meddle with the natural order of things in Enbesa."

The elder is very reluctant to relent on her heavy taxation demands. She claims it is the duty of meniga (shepherds) to provide whatever the irenya (elders) demand, and refuses to be swayed without some further action or compensation.
Select the nearby landowner to open up a dialogue.
The elder berates you for interrupting the natural order of things.
The elder accepts your decision, but believes it will encourage slothfulness.

Your decision to imprison the elder has aroused considerable outrage and fury among the other irenya, and some of them have taken to the streets with firebrands. The fires need to be put out and the situation brought under control, lest the elders wreak havoc upon your city.
To prevent an incident, build the right public building... hint hint... to restore order.
If an incident gets out of hand, you can deploy special units from the corresponding public building's menu.
The elder is outraged at your intervention, and says that she is essential to Enbesa, while you are not.
"This system is horrible. I should have had you locked up the first time!" Have the landlady arrested.

"Does your faith not teach you to protect the meek and favour the humble?"
Pay the elder what is owed.

"This is becoming annoying. Do as you wish, and I will turn a blind eye."
Leave the elder to her tax collection.
"The time has come again for the tithe to be collected. Will you keep paying on behalf of the tenants on my land, or have they finally understood their function in society?"

The elder has returned, animated by a mammonite thirst, to levy new yearly taxes from the meniga family you once chose to protect. Her demands are higher than even the previous year, and it is evident from the glint in her eye that she has no intention of backing down.
The elder has returned to levy her tax on the family you once foolishly chose to protect.
The elder disapproves of your choice, but accepts the offer nonetheless.

The shepherd's peers have invited him to a celebration of the Enbesan spirit of discovery. The shepherd is thrilled with the clothes, and is looking forward to the party.

Some worry the shepherd who was humiliated by his peers may have met some grisly fate. He has yet to return from the mountain where it is said he went to slay a beast, and thereby prove his masculinity. One of the elders has asked you to go looking for him.

Taborime is in uproar: the shepherd's cousin Alyia is nowhere to be found! Yet amid the searches and confusion, no-one seems to have comforted her family — an error which the shepherd asks you to correct.
Alyia's relatives can be found before their house
Alyia's father is standing next to his two other young daughters.
Alyia's family

(part of a letter from Alyia to her sister Lucille, translated from Enbesan)...

Father's not the same since mother died — he's too old to work like he does — but he agrees with the Elder Moot that as a young girl, I would serve him best by staying at home and out of mischief.
But I have defied all of them — I have been dressing as a boy and working, so that father will be able to pay the tithe this year.
I would be working now, if I had not been hurt today... it is a small mark, but my face feels puffy...
The shepherd hopes that by comforting his cousin's family, you may learn something about her disappearance.

Alyia's Father: "Keftanya steward, I appreciate you visiting us. It is a difficult time... Sometimes it feels like the whole city is out searching for Alyia — but at least I have my daughters Nyala and Lucille here to support me."
"It says in this letter that she has been dressing as a boy to work off your debts."
"Perhaps one of your daughters knows where their sister might have gone?"

Lucille: "Father... I'm sorry, but it is time you let it go. Alyia may have defied you by working, but she's doing it to save us all. Please, try to answer the steward's questions so that she may be found."

Lucille: "Father... I know the steward has invaded our privacy like a sanga in a ceramics workshop, but it is time you let go. Alyia defied you by going to work, but she did it to save us all... Please, answer the questions so that Alyia may be found."
"That's right, how will you manage without the money she is earning?"
"What's this I read about her being hurt in that letter?"
Alyia's Father: "Outrageous nonsense! Steward, you may be the Emperor's chosen caretaker for this land, but that does not give you the right to interfere in family business!"
"I am only trying to get to the truth!"
"I am only trying to help you find her."
Alyia's Father: "Very well... She was stung because she is a beekeeper, mother forgive me... But I believe that because of my stubbornness, she now thinks of running away."
"Thank you. I will try and find her for you."
Alyia's letter seems to hint at something — something that may help you find her before it is too late. Only someone like her father will be able to help you read between the lines.
Choose your questions wisely, or Alyia's father may close up.
Look closely at the wording of the letter to understand Alyia's situation.
The shepherd asks you to question Alyia's father about the letter you found.
The shepherd is hopeful that knowing Alyia is a beekeeper will help you track her down. Perhaps interrogating the head beekeeper will provide the leads you need for finding the girl.
There are few places in the city a girl could be stung and swathed in sweet odours.
Compare Alyia's picture with the employee register. One of them must bear a resemblance to her.
The shepherd asks you to find Alyia's workplace.
The shepherd obtained the staff register from the head beekeeper.

(Part of a letter from the bully to his family, translated from the Enbesan)

...mama and papa, I have brought shame on you. Recently, I made that boy dress in foreign clothes. And then the photo made it into the newspaper... I did not mean to spoil the celebration feast — I only wanted to tell him he did well to find Alyia, but all I did was ruin the mood.

I leave for the heart-shaped island of comforts — an island so small you can barely see it, for I doubt I will ever be welcomed back to the old community.

The great unification wars left much of Enbesa bloodied, and many elderly residents bereft of kin. The shepherd wishes to help bring some light into the grumpy old elders' lives by sharing some sweet-honeyed wine with them.
The shepherd wishes to visit the lonely and aged to comfort them.

The shepherd has long been seeking a way to ease the hard toil of fieldwork for his fellows. Last night, in a burst of sleepless creativity, he envisioned a contraption of wood and steel, which he is now eager for you to try out in the fields.

Few in Taborime — or even Enbesa — have been kinder to the shepherd than old Lani the goat: a true friend and listener over the years. But now Lani's milk has run dry, and the two kindred spirits must part for Lani's last great journey. Enbesa's rise from the ashes under Emperor Ketema has not come without cost, and much of what used to be lush green fields has fallen under the axe and machines of renewed industry. While the shepherd understands the need for progress, he feels a softer path, more respectful of nature, should be found. He's condensed his feelings into a short poem, which he would like you to convey to the Emperor, in the hope that he will hear it.
Where Silence Has Lease
Where waters dwell and sea-winds howl / In peace are met man, beast and fowl

There’s a land where every mountain's nameless,
And the rivers all run God knows where;
There’s a land where life and love are boundless,
And scents of honey waft through the air;

Where peaks run higher than man can see,
The woods with waving shadows slant;
The stillness, sunlight, the boundless sea,
I’d wish them all goodbye - but can’t.

I dream of great lands way up yonder,
Of cool broad forests where silence takes lease;
That beauty thrills me, fills me with wonder,
And in that stillness, Enbesa finds peace.

The elder needs your help patching together an educational story for the children's tale-time. Unfortunately, she appears to have forgotten many of its most important sections, much to her vexation.
The elder needs your help to remember parts of a story she wants to tell the children.

Once upon a time, a long, long, time ago, a king had only one son, renowned for being kind and compassionate to all.
One day, as he was exploring his father's kingdom, he stumbled upon a young shepherdess who was struggling to get water from the well. Now the prince was... err...
Tall and strong! He pulled on the rope and... pop! The bucket came up!

The pail came easily out of the well, and the shepherdess thanked the prince by giving him some of her honey.
Delighted, the prince thanked her and continued on, until he reached the edge of his father's kingdom. He had walked for hours and was very hungry, and was just about to open his honey pot when a lion jumped out in front of him! So the prince...
Shared his honey with the lion.
Covered himself in honey to disgust the lion.

The lion's jaw fell open in surprise! "I've never met a human who isn't scared of me. Much less a human willing to share their meal with me!"
The prince responded, "We should always show a kind heart. Everyone deserves compassion, whether they be sheep, human or lion."
Impressed by these wise words, the lion decided to accompany the prince to his kingdom. The prince became a beloved king, and the lion remained his great friend for the rest of their lives - and that is why the lion is the symbol of our nation.

"Eat me now, and the honey will stick your jaw shut!" exclaimed the prince. The lion sighed, annoyed "I'll just wait for the honey to dry, then I'll eat you."
"A fair point...", conceded the prince, "In the meantime, tell me: what's it like being a lion?"
Intrigued by the question, the lion and the prince talked for so long that by the time the honey dried, the lion didn't want to eat the prince any more. The conflict resolved, the prince offered the lion a place by his side, and thus it became the symbol of our nation.
Very crafty, so he tied a rock to the end of the rope to make the pulling easier.

In a matter of minutes, the prince had extracted enough water for the shepherdess's whole family. He helped her carry it to her house where he met with her father, a poor, old man who had little to offer by way of thanks, but insisted that the prince stay the night. Exhausted by the ordeal, the prince gladly accepted.
In the middle of the night, however, the prince was awakened by some low, hissing sounds. Still quite tired, he sat up to ask for some peace, but froze when he saw two enormous pale snakes by his bed.
Despite the danger, however, the prince kept his composure and... hum...
Struck both snakes at once.
Politely asked the snakes to be quiet.

Reaching for the sword by his pillow, the prince struck out and beheaded both snakes with one blow! But as they dropped to the floor, their bodies shifted, revealing two very young, and now very dead men. Alerted by the noise, the old man hobbled into the room and started weeping at the sight. "My boys! What have you done! You seemed so kind-hearted, I thought you would help them! But now... how could you!"
Red-faced with shame and remorse, the prince fled the hovel at once and went back to his father's palace, swearing to the Heavens that he would never again judge by appearance, and would remain a friend to all, human or otherwise.

"You... you do not fear us?" the surprised snakes asked.
"Why should I?" answered the prince. "We are all the Lord's creatures, and you deserve as much respect as any other."
Upon hearing these words, the snakes' skin blurred and hazed, and soon two young boys stood in their stead. "Father, father!" one of them cried in glee. The old man rushed out of the house and wept to see his sons. "I knew it! Only one as wise as you could treat them with humanity and break the curse! A thousand blessings to a prince with such kindness in his heart!"
Soon, news of the prince's wisdom had spread throughout the land, and all praised him, striving to follow his example, and not judge anyone so readily.
The End

CANAL TO LAND OF LIONS OPEN!
The Culysma Canal to the continent of Enbesa receives its first traffic of ships! Explorers are queuing up at the canal locks, so eager are they to explore the lands beyond.
ENBESA AND EMPIRE AGREE TERMS
Queen's ambassador Sir Archibald Blake shows commitment to Enbesan independence by dismantling Imperial presence in the region, and recognising Emperor Ketema and his people as equals.
THE LAND WHERE KITH ARE KINE
Tantalising first image of native Enbesan maturity rites — young boys made to dance their way across the backs of entire kine herd for coveted 'Horn-Kin' title (ctd p.12)
A STUDY IN HUMILITY
Enbesan offenders subjected to trial by public confession for sin of lying — Irenya spokespeople claim at least P×(1+r×t) onlookers needed for proper cleansing (More on p.8)
MOOT MEMBER MEETS MYSTERIOUS MAID
Respected Moot Speaker found cavorting with scantily dressed maidens near hallowed ground. Commission seeks fitting punishment as youngest ever speaker is appointed...
MOOT MARRED BY MOB MELEE
Partisans of power-craving elder strike in protest of leader's disgrace. Reliable source comments 'grey hair everywhere, torn robes... Never knew politics to be this much fun!'
UPROAR AT KEFTANYA MOOT
Elder carried out in shock after Keftanya de-moots her for excess ambition and cruelty to meniga. Rival Moot member unofficially declares 'good riddance'.
OLD WORLD CLOTHES SHUNNED
As Enbesan youth seen sporting foreign clothes is shamed by his friends, our columnist wonders if mimicry of overseas fashions will ever gather momentum in Enbesa.
THE NEW CRAZE, OR THE NEW CRAZY?

Pioneer Paul Poiret's bizarre new threads are set to combine the most unlikely of materials in the finished design, including absurdities as diverse as light bulb filaments and raw animal flesh. Critics say he could be hailed as a genius at an upcoming fashion event, or otherwise regarded a laughing stock.
NOBEL PRIZE FOR PHYSICS
Young man of Enbesan heritage brings home the bacon with his discovery of the "electrite", a particle which seemingly represents one of the most basic physical units of our universe...
GENIUS POIRET REMODELS THE VOGUE

Poiret and his tailors celebrated as visionaries at landmark style event! Model and suit combining peculiar materials declared a triumph! Vibrant international flair shimmered throughout the fashion event, which seems to be among the first of its kind — and something which even the city governor, present at the event, has taken a special interest in...
QUARREL QUELLED IN TABORIME
