Seek the spear's location. I'll need time to prepare and reconnoitre the grounds if the heist is to succeed.
We know where the spear is. Now to find a way to access it.
There are two routes: through the tunnels, or across the mountain. Choose one, and bring me a picture so I can finish my preparations.
Halt! What are you doing here?
Stop! What are you carrying?
A very old tunnel. Who knows what dangers hide in the darkness.
A seemingly steep path from beach to temple.
Teka the Blind seems to be in the process of writing a book about the many animals of Enbesa, with naively drawn sketches of the animals themselves.

Medical Treatise


... curing seizures. Ensure the fruit is cut at the light of dawn. Before mixing the potion, make sure the water is infused with the Deathless Grace flower, for its healing properties. Drink with...

(...)

...so is the art of the healer commensurate with the art of growing the sacred Deathless Graces; the holy duty passed down from the very age of Sile'Amidos. So can we tell the truly holy, by the Gift of the Goddess that grows all...'

Governors of Kidusi


As the Seven rose, a prince was assigned to govern Kidusi Anitoni and to report matters to the Court of Taborime every year in times of prosperity. However, the priests refused to recognise the prince. Priestess Abeba the Flower relayed the reasons why to the princes in Taborime as follows:

'After the terrible attacks by the Kashta on the granary and the definitive loss of the Deathless Graces, the mighty plants imported from Sile'Amidos, we lost our purpose, our pride, and our function. But Ezana the Pacifist, King of Enbesa, refused to defend Kidusi Anitoni, nor to send any punitive expedition to the land of the thieves.

When Sûrya the Sun-King rose, and desperately looked for the Deathless Graces in Kidusi Anitoni, killing our priests and burning our library, the other islands did not intervene, and our library was destroyed.

We have no trust left in kings or princes. Kidusi Anitoni humbly requests that we be free to govern according to our own tenets and beliefs. We will continue trading for what is needed so that we may uphold our sacred scriptorial mission, and that all may know forever of Sûrya's treachery, and of the glory of the Seven.'

The princes agreed to those terms — and to ensure no tyrant ever returned to Enbesa, they decided to fund a new library on Kidusi Anitoni, to ensure the lessons of the past were never forgotten.

On the Old World


Travellers from the Old World often seek out our holy mountains, believing that they've found the mythical Land of God, Sile'Amidos. We see no reason to contradict them, as there is great power in these dreams and tales. Who will dare assault our land when powerful knights from distant lands come with vast retinues to honour our altars?

Though there is no such bounty of flowers and trees here as is described in the scripture, our knowledge of the ancient script was enough to maintain the illusion. We showed them ancient sacred texts, and bestowed upon them garbled translations to take home as divine commandments.

The holy scriptures we shared were pale copies of the content of the Ark. Written in Sile'Amidos by King Davan, who was said to have received them from the Lord himself, the Tablets of Law were purportedly hidden within the Ark, and brought through cataclysm to Enbesa by Queen Shaba. The Ark was lost in the Fall of the Seven, and many nations now claim to hold the original, without proof. But the Old World knows that the truth resides in Kidusi, as it always has since the Time of the Blessed Land.

And so, as long as the secret of the ancient script lies with Kidusi, the truth will be ours to shape. Let history judge us if it must, or let the truth be forgotten when the last of our order perish.

Symbols of Enbesa


Sile'Amidos, the heart of the world, was a land blessed by God, and a land of plenty: frankincense, myrrh, ebony, hibiscus and even the dragon tree. When it sank, the world of old was lost. History became legend, and all forgot that it is in Enbesa that the remainder of the blood of Sile'Amidos dwells. But to those who know where to look, the symbols of Sile'Amidos still pervade the land and its foundations.

The Phoenix
The dragon tree was known to shed red blood when exposed to great heat. This blood has been known since ancient times to have mystical healing properties, and legend came to claim that these qualities were endowed by the hidden roosting phoenix that nestled within its branches, the blood of which seeped into the tree with every regeneration. To this day, the people of Waha Desher still worship the Djat, one of many incarnations of the phoenix.

The Hibiscus
Long known as Deathless Grace, the hibiscus has always been associated with fertility and birth due to its red flowers, and how it blooms when it gets enough water. As such, it features in most myths as a giver of immortality. Some, including the Sun-King Sûrya, were convinced of the truth of these legends and sought the secret of the hibiscus for many years — a fruitless endeavour, and one which consumed their entire life.

The Lion
The Lion, symbol of King Selamawi of Sile'Amidos, was chosen by Queen Shaba as the protector of her new realm when the lost island sank beneath the waves. The scripture quotes her saying: 'The King is dead, but his cubs will roar his legacy over all of this Land of Lions.'
Possibly the only house to survive the unification wars of Kings Wag and Ketema, it stands sturdy, protecting its ancient family.

An ancient stone from Waha Desher, estimated to have been built around the Golden Age, carefully pieced back together, with two different scripts: one of them you can understand, but the other...The first tells of the Kashtans, primary owners of Waha Desher, lending the oasis to Enbesa.
The house of Kyria. This is where Biniam grew up, surrounded with trees and the Great Issehd.
The shadow and fresh air provided by the orange trees are quite pleasant.
Kyria seems to be growing teff grass here, a small but meaningful contribution to easing the ksar's travails.
A thick crust of salt has enshrined the skiff's remains into eternity.
The ship of Mekdem's guard, who spent the rest of his life in Waha Desher.
I am of the blood of the Seven! Get out of my home immediately!
Don't mind our greatmother — she has lived too long with the shadows of the past to be able to tell what is from what was.
This could be the ship that left Kidusi Anitoni some 91 years ago. The ship's style certainly seems to coincide with the dates.
He arrived on a fishing boat, a few years before I was born. He never could say from where.
He was kind to me. He made me bows and arrows to play at hunting. But I never knew his voice, as he had cut out his own tongue. I didn't dare to ask why.
I was often at his house. I remember it well, though it is now well overgrown.
If you could clear the overgrowth, I would relish seeing it once more.
Armour of the Elamais Guard? So he served that legendary dynasty?
His old desk! He was always writing here. See, there are some letters left...
Leave me, will you? I wish to pray for his soul to find a final resting place. You can see from his eyes that his errantry was unwanted. Let it be my last gift to him.
A stranger on a boat, a century ago? Only our greatmother would know of something that old.
Have you seen greatmother? I can't find her...
The house of the man who escaped Angereb, on the evening of the murder of the last of the Elamais.
A rusty old breastplate, bearing the crest of the Elamais.
An old man's desk, strewn with old ink and rotten paper.
Thank you for bringing me home, Shema. Healing begins with the soul.
The Oracle! People call it Per-Iteru here. There are inscriptions within, look!
The Oracle! People call it Per-Iteru here, the place of future-looking.
The side of Waha Desher's Oracle, where you found a chamber covered with what seem to be Ancient Enbesan inscriptions, and engravings of priests tilling steep fields.
The side of Waha Desher's Oracle, dotted with numerous doorways that are sadly too unstable to allow further access inside.
My wahiyit said she was fishing salahmandirs in the iteru to make them jump from the kebeh. If there is a kebeh, it must be below those wasi given all the issehds around.
So my wahiyit wasn't raving, there was indeed a kebeh and an iteru... Oh Lord, to have had this miracle hidden here all those years...
My wahiyit used to say the most beautiful thing she ever saw was water springing from the kebeh, so now I want to see it myself.
A childlike smile of wonder shines on Yara's face, her eyes lost in the memories of times long gone.

I prefer the calm of the cliff. But from here, the waha looks more beautiful than I ever could have imagined, even from the stories of my wahiyit. I hope I'll meet her again in the afterlife, so I can tell her all about this miracle.
I'd prefer to die with the waha than to leave it. Go now, shema, and never return.
The wasi... What would our wahiyit say...
The ksar of Waha Desher has changed greatly: full houses, children playing in the sand, craftsmen hard at work...
The silence is soul-crushing. Sand sweeps through windows no-one bothered to close. A tragedy told through empty walls.
Gone is the ksar of old. Among the ruins, the laughter of children has been replaced by the din of industry and toil.
The old ruins of Waha Desher's main temple, also known as the Oracle. The waters around it lend it some semblance of its old majesty.
A nexus of life once more, clear of rubble, the Oracle of Waha Desher nurtures the oasis, as it was always meant to.
A nexus of life once more, clear of rubble, the Oracle of Waha Desher nurtures the oasis, as it was always meant to.
Once, the Oracle watched over the waha and its people. But the people are now gone, and whatever power inhabited the Oracle has long since left for greener pastures.
Though its waters flow anew, it is clear from the markings on the Oracle that the level used to be far higher long ago, when Waha Desher was prosperous.
Water flows, bountiful, all through Waha Desher! At the heart of the oasis, a natural fountain is slowly forming.
An antique well, hidden under rubble — the source of the iteru, the dried-up river that once nourished the oasis, if Yara is to be believed.
A time-worn well, once hidden below the rubble. Water now flows out of the artesian well, replenishing river and oasis alike.
A rejuvenated well - but for what? There are none left to care for it, and in time sands will claim it once more, forever.
Workers from Taborime, busy clearing rubble from the well.
Workers from Taborime, idly awaiting orders.
Surprised by the pleasant, slow life of Waha Desher, some of Ketema's workers have decided to tarry here for the time being.
Workers labouring hard to complete thankless tasks.
The people will gladly help, if you but ask. Come find me if their idioms seem impenetrable.

Hmm, what did Yara say?... Wahiyit are our elderly parents, and salahmandir are little water-dwelling lizards. I think the people in Taborime say 'river' for iteru. An issehd is a tree — Kyria has some by her house. But wasi? That sounds old, very old.
You have done what all thought impossible, shema.
Our current focus should be ahku. Without it, we will starve before the crops grow.
Seherut — the floating wood houses for transporting ahku. Please, Shema, then we can focus on growing the waha.
One, two, three... Twenty tons! Cries with relief.
Thirty-two, thirty-three, thirty-... Oh, I forgot to count that crate! Let's start over...
You tried, shema. Let that at least be some comfort to you, in your failure of our people.
Would we have fared better had we not followed you? I wonder.
A new warehouse, to slowly fill with piles of oasis-salt.
Not long ago, there was nothing but salt in the new warehouse, but now supplies and even trees are stockpiled next to bales of white gold.
Scents of spices and luxurious food waft from the warehouse, bringing back memories of the great granary Waha Desher used to be.
Empty rows, deserted stocks. All that remains is a fine trail of thick-grained salt, the last before Waha Desher's fate is sealed.
Wind creaks through doors left ajar. Dust swirls, and the scent of consummate despair gathers.
Life survives near my house in a way it does nowhere else on the island. I know not why, but perhaps Yara will have an idea.
A beautiful gift, you've given to this island. I only hope that I will not be the last to till this good land.
Have you met my son? Biniam? You must see more of him than I do.
See the beauty you have returned to our island? You should stay here and work the land with us. You have a farmer's blessed hands.
I wish Biniam was here for this special day. But his work at the court must take precedence, of course.
I preferred staying with Yara. I'd take her what crops I had, and we'd share them for dinner. But she no longer speaks.
Could you please find a way to quieten that dreadful pump, before it ruins the haven I've painstakingly built here?
Waha Desher is a haven of peace, a place of quiet! No industry should mar the bated stillness of a garden!
I was told you were different to your people. Clearly I was misled. A pity.
Bright colours, warming the waha. Testament that there is beauty here still, and might yet be again.
Already the hibiscus fades, light suddenly burning rather than loving amid the desolation.
A wondrously poetic sight; a flowing weave of nature and farmland, and none can tell where the one begins and the other ends.
Already the sheen of sheaves dims. Colours pale, and soon all will be lost to the waters.
The chirping of thousands of crickets weaves an intricate, if ear-shattering, melody.
Wilted stalks, left bare of grain. Silence more resounding than ten thousand crickets.
Fierce, resilient beasts: it is said an oryx can survive a week without drinking. A perfect animal for the heat of Waha Desher, and delicious when properly prepared.
The enclosure is deserted, the animals roaming wild. Perhaps it is for the best.
Yara knows the most about olden times, but her speech can be... impenetrable.
We must prepare for the return of the waters. The land must be held together - issehds will do the trick.
A desehert no longer! Water flows, life-birthing and tempest-quiet - a true miracle! A Mesyt must be held, in due course!
Abel will help you plan the salt-trade. Thank you, shema, for being an ever-believer.
Speak to Kyria and Eyasu. They will show you how to regrow the waha.
It takes a wise person to restore the waha while respecting our culture. You are one such person. With your help, Waha Desher and the empire will grow great again.
I may be young, but I never thought I would see my people truly happy within my lifetime. I was so wrong!
I think I would have preferred to die young than to witness the departure of our people. I will go to Taborime, with the others, but my heart dies today on these shores.
I... beg of you, shema. These are not ruins, they are our heart! Our history! There must be some other way!
Anything to pay for our survival, I believe... We should have protected Waha Desher. Now we pay dearly for our failure.
Waha Desher survived, shema, but at what cost? I fear our people are changed, and not for the better.
No goat to eat... No djat to hunt... Maybe I should go to Taborime, like the others.
I'm too young to know anything about the waters. But I know how to hunt! Or I used to...
Water! Soon I'll be able to hunt djat again!
I was so looking forward to hunting djat, but now that I see them... Such beauty deserves to live.
The battered remains of the eastern shrine were long ago converted into a ceramics oven. Now the sound of industrious work has replaced the quiet veneration of old.
Though undeniably useful, the pump's location is a daily desecration to the devout folk of the waha.
The Shrine of Western Prayer has been utterly dismantled, its pale bricks used to raise new industrial buildings all across the island, and so does its history fade.
Groups of irenya crowd in to honour the Oracle according to the ways of old. Soul-bound to the waha, their chant weaves hymns of lament and praise alike. Something is here, something holy, somehow.

Is it celebration, or religious ecstasy? It's impossible to say, but a pure, unbridled energy emanates from the villagers' dancing. In a corner, you see Abel and Eysau dancing with a stranger — a young shepherd of unearthly beauty.

If the inscriptions are true, this must be the tomb of the legendary Queen Shaba, hidden from the world for millennia in the cliffs of Waha Desher. Inside the sarcophagus, under her skeleton's silent vigil, lies the mythical Ark of the Covenant, hidden there long ago by a fleeing Almaïr after the Fall of the Seven!

You lean inside the Oracle and examine your surroundings by the dim light of a match.
Ancient engravings, still colourful despite the dampness, depict a sheer island with priests cultivating its rocky hills.
Atop the painting are symbols — writings — probably detailing the location described.
Have you met my son? Biniam? Ah, you probably see more of him than I, his old mother.
This garden is the last of Waha Desher's fertile havens, and second only to my son in my heart.
All strangers are welcome here, shema.
Our humble village has little to offer save for a loving, welcoming heart.
Our youth have been leaving the island. I was elected chieftain because I was one of the few who refused to leave.
The Southern Shrine of the Oracle. It seems to be where the elders used to perform rituals to the southern cross.
The Eastern Shrine of the Oracle. It seems to be where the elders used to perform rituals to the rising sun.

The tomb of Esato, the great general who refused King Sûrya's orders to burn down the Oracle while the local population were imprisoned inside it. Quartered and burnt in retribution, he was gratefully interred in secret here by the people of Waha Desher.
The Western Shrine of the Oracle. Allegedly where the elders used to honour the setting sun.
What remains of the ritual path to the wharf.
Rubble and wreckage from Waha Desher's history, long since past recognition.
This ancient wharf seems to have been used for religious processions. Most probably Kashtan traditions.
The village of Waha Desher, no longer thriving. The locals call it the "ksar".
The withered ruins of Waha Desher's main temple, also known as the Oracle. A dismal sight in the face of its former splendour.
Waha Desher's most ancient tree, now centuries old, revered by locals for its venerable age.
A grim vision of the ravages of a salted, burnt land.
The remains of an old military camp, tents painted with Old World regalia resting among the debris. One of King George's many battles after Trelawney, perhaps?
What little remains of the oasis: a salt-smothered tarn and swarms of angry mosquitoes.
One, two, three... Three left. How many days can we last with three tons of meat...
So you're to be our steward, if the Emperor ordains? We will be watching closely.
The previous capital was... shiver. Let us thank the Lord that we moved here, where the water flows free.
The weather is certainly milder, but did the harbour have to be so far away?
These houses are but the beginning. Soon there will be enough to tell Anita to come over and move in!
A foreigner, on our farm! Wonderful!
Do you think one day food will just... produce itself? Wouldn't that be amazing?
(whistling) Je n’ai besoin de personne en Massey Fergusson
New world, new people to meet, new machines to use!
Leave my land before you spoil the crops stranger!
Change? Pah! Tradition has always done right by us, why should it not continue?
Is that what you want, a world of unified flavours and appearances, churned by machinery? That's why we fight to keep traditions alive!
Hard work makes for a healthy soul.
It starts with just one — then the foreigners bring in their mother, their sister, their third cousin once removed...
Another foreigner? There's enough bother around without this Archibald.
I hear your friend Archibald can procure bombins? If you could put in a kind word for me...
Why people would cross the sea is beyond me. Let each stay home, and their goat pens will be safely guarded!
A kin of yours? Would they like to see my tractor?
That farm over there? Conservative idiots!
I can't help but pity my neighbour when I see him determinedly tilling the land by hand...
I dream of self-milking cows, self-cutting wheat, vegetables so large that you can...
Another foreigner? You people breed like rabbits!
I hold no grudge against foreigners, but even goats have to be separated lest they wreak havoc!
Winds of change, they say. Well there's carrion on that wind, to be sure.
Don’t you have anything better to do than watching me work?
Outrageous! Turning his back on the Emperor himself!
I heard our lord was livid. Can you imagine, such an offense after having been so welcoming?
I saw Biniam leaving the palace in a hurry. He seemed quite distressed if you ask me.
Were you there when they met? Passing on the plates they threw at each other, perhaps?
Sir Archibald has already gone? But he'd only just arrived!
The roar of the engine, leather under your rear, thundering towards the horizon... Tractors are freedom, my friend!
I bought my tractor from the harbour merchant for half price. Bargain!
If your friend Archibald comes back, can you ask him if he has some spare pieces for my tractor?
Good riddance! We've no need of him!
He is not welcome here! I hope he remembers it!
There's plenty of work I can give you if you're bored, child!
Typical brainless youngsters; they want food on their plate, but not to work to grow it!
Ugh, I can't even get out of bed. I knew those fruits were no good.
I should be feeling better by now... This can’t just be simple indigestion!
My friend Anita is sick too, but she didn’t eat anything! Did I contaminate her?
The whole city's contracted the disease! We must be cursed!
Biniam! No, not the boy! You must do something!
Biniam has a temper, sure, but I can’t believe he'd do such a reckless thing!
Has anyone told his mother? She must be worried sick!
The shame his poor mother must feel! A son in prison — what does that say about her parenting?
Biniam, in prison! No no no! He always said that once he'd opened his Research Institute, I'd get state-of-the-art machines for my farm!
Did Biniam leave any of the machines he worked on behind? No? A blueprint? A sketch? Anything really!
My neighbour's been arguing that Biniam’s capture proves we shouldn’t be striving for modernity — nor should we trust foreigners! You'd better prove him wrong!
Poor Kyria, losing a son like that. It must be devastating.
Turns out Biniam, mister “I don’t want to work in the field” was dirty after all. Ha!
Biniam had it coming. No-one truly devout would work on such devilish science.
If Biniam had focused on honest fieldwork instead of reading books, he wouldn’t be where he is now!
I don’t like Biniam, but... It is sad to think of one our own in prison.
How convenient for Archibald to change his mind now that we are of the same blood. Hmph.
I remember little Biniam asking every man in town if he was his dad. Haha... ha.
Sir Archibald must have been a fine piece of work 25 years ago — I can see what Kyria saw in him, hehehe.
May this family gathering ease the tensions for good!
Biniam is free! Proof we can collaborate for a brighter future.
You simply must help Biniam see his research centre through — and send me any prototypes!
Imagine, engineering a chaser bin to add it to my tractor! Or a tiller? Or a...
Peace is restored! I can’t wait to see what the future brings!
Biniam is free, what a blessed day! I am sure this episode has cured him from the frivolities of youth.
You know, the future can be scary sometimes, especially when you know so little of it.
We can be proud of our emperor for his handling of the situation. And you, of course.
It pains me to say it, but... you feel truly Enbesan.
Welcome, foreigner, welcome! May our trade be fruitful!
Come see, all-Enbesan products only! Honey, ceramics, scarves, and more!
Not many clients yet, but I know you will help with that!
People complain, but it's easier for them to walk down to the harbour than for me to drag all my goods uphill!
Ah, new clients! Keep them coming, the city must grow!
Shepherds, I swear. 'Your prices are too high!' they say. Of course they are! I only sell the best!
Could you appeal to the Emperor on my behalf? His taxes on tea are killing me!
(whispering) Yes sir, great wine, smuggled from... (normal) Ah, governor! Can I interest you in anything?
The rush of irenya to Taborime is sure to be good for business!
Elders are easily manipulated. They'll even buy things they don't need if the rebate is attractive enough.
This? No, it looks like scripture — a perfect replica — but the contents... Fifty shades of indigo I call it, but it'll have you beet red.
"I beg of you, no more haggling or I might as well tell my daughter her father is ruined! Her poor dreams..." What do you think? Efficient, no?
Ah, my favourite governor! A prosperous city for you, a prosperous business for me!
Here's a little trade secret: lanterns are profitable because you have to change candles regularly! Obsolescence, I call it.
Oh, don't mind the price. It's not about the money. Hah! Of course it is!
Don’t you think my merchandise would sell better in the Old World?
So many new customers! I'm going to have to expand my store!
Ours is a healthy, profitable and much appreciated relationship.
I should open a subsidiary near the church. After two hours of mass, I’m sure the irenya must crave some more earthy pleasures.
Do you know Madame Kahina? Well, you're talking to the Exotic Emporium's latest associate!
There's plenty of space in this market, but not enough goods to fill it up, apparently.
A visitor! Come in, come in! We value quality over quantity here!
Come back soon, the city is sure to grow faster than you can say 'tabot'!
Those shepherds are working hard, but I'd like to see more of them grace my stands with their money!
Or maybe they just don't see the true value of my goods.
While looking at the elder's stand, you realise that visitors seem much more intrigued by the stalls nearby. Food seems to be the highest priority in Taborime.
An attractive - if pungent - whirl of colours and life sweeps through the markets.
Ceramics! Fresh Stew! Everything to make your house the most comfortable home in all of Taborime!
An empty stand near a sign that reads "Lamps, Opening Soon" is attracting much muttered curiosity.
So many languages! Enbesan dialects, of course, but also Old World tongues and even the queer tang of Waha Desher's idioms.
Exotic goods never before seen garnish the stands of Far Eastern merchants. Taborime thrives with life.
I told Anita to come over. She always wanted to open a hat shop, but I always said she'd never make a living from such a specific set of merchandise! In Taborime, everything is possible nowadays.

The last standing testimony to La Corona's presence in Enbesa, a century ago. It is said that Lebne, the Last Elamais, kicked the Old World empire out of Enbesa for trying to colonise the country from the ruins of Taborime.
Built on the ruins of one the most ancient buildings in Enbesa, the original palace of kings, Emperor Ketema's palace is testament to a land tempered over millennia.
Laid out according to ancient custom, ritually sowed and patiently worked by hand only, as tradition recommends.
Back-breaking labour, of course, but the love we put into our work shines through in our goods in a way that no machine can rival.
See those machines on that farm? They're highly praised for reducing the weariness of work. But what is the value of labour if one does not put one's all into it?
Ketema would have us abandon our roots, destroy them even! What sort of emperor is that?
After a day at the farm, I feel relieved. Exhaustion feels good, and I feel connected to our homeland more than ever.
A unique sight in Enbesa, this farm operates tractors, providing a welcome respite for its farmhands.
A visitor from the Old World? Do you perhaps have any other machinery to show us?...
See that farm, not two hundred yards off? Its people are idiots, and conservative to boot.
The Emperor is a visionary — the first of a long line of kings and queens to see what technology could bring to this country!
Our farm alone can support half of Taborime, yet still has room to grow and expand!

A troubled time in Enbesa's history, when seven princes ruled as one, is commemorated here. Flowers are still left at its foot by the distant descendants of those whose families fell in the destruction of the Seven's rule.
An inscription to Yetbarok adorns every side of this massive wall. Built by the first of the Elamais, those walls were supposed to protect the palace from the risk of invasion from the Sand Kingdoms.

An imposing archway leading to the palace, built to honour the Sun-King Sûrya. All mention of his name has been erased, but his sun is still etched all over it. The sheer magnitude of the monument betrays the megalomania of the last, and cruel, king of the Golden Age of Enbesa.

Known to be the very first building in Enbesa, built on the foundation of Taborime by Queen Shaba for her lost husband Elam, King of Sile'Amidos, this temple was restored under the rule of the Seven. Priests from Kidusi Anitoni claim it once held the Ark of Covenant, a long, long time ago.
An antique wall, marking the limits of Taborime under the Seven. Such a vast city must have seen quite the age of prosperity and growth in the distant Silver Age.
The outmost limits of Taborime under the rule of the Seven. The wealth produced under the Seven in the Silver Age seems to have been limitless.
The house of Emperor Ketema's chief diplomat, Biniam. A promising young man indeed, to obtain such a charge and such a home at his young age.
The Crown has set up a consulate in Enbesa, to ensure the diplomatic relationship between the two empires flourishes in future.

With Kidusi Anitoni joining Ketema's empire, the Emperor has decided to enforce his religion in Taborime. A brand new monastery has replaced La Corona's church, forever suppressing the last remnants of colonisation in Enbesa.

A majestic temple erected by Ketema to honour the rebirth of ancient Enbesan religious traditions on Kidusian soil. Priests regularly perform fertility rituals with the hibiscus here when not actively working the fields.

With Angereb's renewed loyalty, the Emperor has put together a program to train young Enbesans in discipline and alertness, ensuring the protection of all of Enbesa. Special attention has been given to fire hazards and their prevention.

The Emperor has built a vast library to encourage the newly united priests of Kidusi to pursue their research. Their constant collection of scrolls, tomes, and the most secret and extensive lore has led to an increased yield of research points in Enbesa.

The restoration of Waha Desher led Ketema to experiment on his canals, and ultimately to build these wondrous gardens. Meanwhile, the innovation has spread through Enbesa to enhance its existing capacities.
With Waha Desher providing all the ceramics and tapestries Taborime will ever need, additional fields have been sown to supply the artisans of Waha Desher with the food they require.
The renewed waters of Waha Desher inspired the Emperor to build these new gardens in Taborime — a testament to the ever-increasing prosperity and flourishing of Enbesa's land-tilling.
With the bastion of Angereb as a loyal ally and strong guardian of Enbesan waters, trade routes to the country have been protected, and the harbour of Taborime has grown to international proportions.
The Princes of Angereb place great value on the military might of their overlord, so Ketema has had no choice other than to develop strong military defences on Taborime's shores.

The legendary Spear of the Elamais is not just a relic of Enbesa's long lost founding dynasty — it is a symbol, one that could be used by Angereb to rise up behind a new ruler, claiming the legitimacy granted by the spear. But beware — whoever you choose to give it to, their opponents may never forgive you for the deceit.

Merchant: "The Emperor wishes me to deal with you, Keftanya steward? Very well then. I hear you are interested in acquiring land in the valley beyond Mount Riza? Well, I can tell you it is a rich and bounteous land, and I am not willing to part with it easily..."
"100,000 coins. Final offer."
"25,000 seems about fair."
"Maybe it's better if you don't part with it then..."

Merchant: "Oh... I didn't expect that! No, it has to be sold, and I really would be glad to come to a deal and sell it today — I can't afford to wait on that money any longer... Besides, did Emperor Ketema not say he wants it?" (the merchant glances at Ketema briefly in the hope he will say something, but Ketema looks expectantly towards you.)
Merchant: "Impossible! Some even say there's gold floating in the rivers of the Mount Riza valley — it's worth at least 75,000."
Merchant: "Ok then — 50,000, but if you won't take it, I have other people that are interested..."
"75,000 it is, agreed."
"Come on, how about 50,000?"
"Hmm. Perhaps you have more interested buyers elsewhere?"
"I'd hoped we could do 25,000. Ah well, perhaps leave it to your other bidders..."
Merchant: "No, the price is 75,000. Clearly you can't want Mount Riza that much if you aren't willing to pay the going rate..."
"Fine! If it has to be 75,000, it's a deal."
"I don't think many people would be interested at 75,000..."
"Oh fine then, deal!" the merchant exclaims, shaking your hand while shaking his head in frustration. You sense you couldn't possibly have got it for any less than you offered...
"That's a fair deal!" the merchant nods, shaking your hand vigorously. He is smiling slightly more than you like. You sense you could have got it for a little bit less...
"Deal!" the merchant exclaims, shaking your hand vigorously, a broad grin streaking across his face. You sense you could have got it for far less if you hadn't gone rushing in with that offer...

"Yes indeed I will!" says the merchant angrily, "and I'm pretty sure they'll be far more reasonable negotiators than you!" The merchant storms out of the palace. You sense you might have made a bit of a boo-boo."

Emperor Ketema has long had a profound curiosity for the inner workings of all things geared and cogged - machinery, clockwork and, of course, the human mind. He has recently taken a great interest in news of pocket watches spreading across the Old World, and hopes that you might bring a number of them to his palace, so that he may take them apart and study them in his spare time.
Ketema is fascinated by the latest models of pocket watches.

It is rare for Enbesans to resort to modes of transportation of a mechanical nature — much less one of such dandified and exuberant proportions as the latest craze to hit the Old World streets: penny farthing bicycles! Never one to pass up an opportunity for learning, the Emperor tasks you with delivering several of these strange machines to Taborime.
Ketema asks that you deliver him a shipment of those strange penny farthing bicycles.

An immortal, everlasting - well, almost - source of light? Now this is a wonder that could bring much illumination to hearts and minds in Enbesa! The Emperor insists that you deliver several of these strange candles to Enbesa.

Ketema recalls fondly how a young, vagrant inventor had once told him through a mane of matted hair of the promises of steam, and how any inventor capable of harnessing its terrible power might usher in a new age for the world. Well, it seems that young man - Nate, Neet, was it? - was visionary in his own right! At last, the Age of Steam has come, and Ketema is adamant that Enbesa must understand this machinery down to its smallest rods and cogs, if the nation is to become one of the powers.
Intrigued and fascinated by the latest advances in steam motorisation, Ketema asks that you deliver several steam motors to his empire.

With Enbesa being a nation steeped in musical lore and heritage, it is unsurprising that the gramophone should have been immediately adopted by its people. A greater surprise, however, is the way in which it has triggered the Emperor's inventive and tinkering fervour. He insists that the unsightly wrench on the music-making marvels should be replaced, to its advantage, by a more slender and precise crank. To put his theory to the test, he has asked you to deliver a number of gramophones to Enbesa.
The Emperor requests you deliver some gramophones to his city, so that he may take them apart and rebuild them.

Achatina fulica. Tempting to keep as an exotic pet, but this invasive species needs a lot of looking after.
Atelerix albiventris. Rolls into a tiny spiky ball to protect its vulnerable parts.
Phoenicopterus roseus. The pinkish tone to their feathers comes from eating lots of carotene-rich shrimp.
Struthio camelus. Their feathers have become prized among the elite... and their spring-cleaning servants.
Brachypelma albopilosum. A big ol' hairy spider.
Camelus dromedarius. The only mount that can withstand epic journeys through the desert.
Canis simensis. An early account of this canid, endemic to Enbesa, states that they "leap so high, it's like they have wings".
Trioceros balebicornutus. Found, with a lot of luck, deep in the Harenna forest, in Enbesa's Misty Mountains.
Equus grevyi. The largest wild horse, and also very much the stripiest.
Lycaon pictus. Not as prominent in the folklore of Enbesa, but better respected in local hunter-gatherer societies.
Otocyon megalotis. They use their large ears and tail to make points of argument.
Pandinus imperator. Imperious indeed — with a tail so fat it delivers more stab than sting.
Naja ashei. Only try to handle if you have spit-proof spectacles close by!
Balearica regulorum. Once existed in the Old World too, but Earth cooled, and only those in warmer regions survived.
Tragelaphus buxtoni. Lofty and noble, white marks and chevrons contrast against their brown fur.
Oryx beisa. Known to prong the odd lion with those dagger-like antennae.
Crocuta crocuta. A real laugh to hang out with.
Connochaetes taurinus. Let them stampede into your life, or leave them to the lions — your choice.
Aepyceros melampus. Stott and pronk themselves into the air something chronic.
Caracal caracal. Tamed for hunting by Queen Nafir when she ruled the upper crocodile delta.
Vulpes zerda. Finicky eater — only skippy jerboas will do.
Gypaetus barbatus. Often seen suckling bone marrow, turning its beak up at meat.
Hippopotamus amphibius. See that mouthspan? The fat, splintered yellow teeth? Yeah, don't even think about it.
Theropithecus gelada. All the little scandals being nattered around their society will make your heart bleed.
Acinonyx jubatus. It is said Selamawi tamed one and adorned it with a bejewelled collar, but it ran away.
Giraffa camelopardalis. Gets a decent view of the savannah from up there, and all the juiciest leaves.
Panthera Leo. There is a majesty and gentleness in those eyes, from which all may take courage.
Loxodonta africana. Her intelligence cannot be understated, nor the joy she expresses unfurling her trunk.
Diceros bicornis. At least keeping one of these beauties in a zoo will save one of their species from the poachers.
Cattle have even worn such jewellery themselves, such is the reverence held for their kind.
A deathly painted visage reminds the living how fortunate they are still to be.
Strands of raffia still cling to the crevices of this wooden animal used in dances.
An ancient book retelling the story of Queen Shaba's pilgrimage to Enbesa, in which she bore the magnificent Ark.

A fortress home to Enbesan emperors in times gone by, most notably in its later years Surya, the mad sun-king.
One of the most important Deltan deities, the falcon god of the sky, from whom all great leaders were born.
Carved from the living rock of Kidusi Anitoni, when the priests embraced hibiscus back in the 4th century.
Brought to Enbesa by Queen Shaba, proof that the lineage of Enbesan emperors can be traced back to King Selamawi.
A temple dedicated to the peerless Deltan queen Nafir, decorated with colossi and Deltan art.
A map of an island covered in odd flora that some thought had never existed — but with this you know otherwise!
The egg of a bird beyond the realms of probability. Perhaps if nestled among flames, it will hatch.
The many and overflowing treasures of a realm none believed to exist. Clearly they were not hardy enough adventurers!
The holiest book on the shelves of the houses of the holy in the Holy City. Safe to say, it's divine.
Astral crescents studded with smoky quartz, and chrysoprastic swirls.

The legendary spear of Enbesa's Elamais lineage. Its neck, carved with etchings, is said to be an authentic part of the Ark of the Covenant, forged by Almaïr. It reads: 'Verse 1. And upon prayers borne from the Westmost Shrine shall a new shadow form, of a place where Those Above and Those Below are joined, and the Word of God shall hold the First of the Elamais in everlasting sleep there.'

An inner light shines quietly from the sheltered cusp, a sparkle of the splendour of the Gardens of Sile'Amidos. Fine etchings cover the lid: 'Verse 3. Fear not the mountain, but come to it with love. For in that barrow do the Elder Days still reside, in the splendour of their Great Majesty. For those who begin in the cool of the humble shadow, light will show the way.'

The songs of those who held this tabot long ago still echo through the fragile wood. Fine etchings line the contours: 'Verse 2. For what is the beauty of day without the coming of the night? To those who pray in the comfort of day, the Lord brings solace, but to those who pray in the fading of dusk will enlightenment be provisioned!'
A kit of book-binding tools, to achieve the traditional Enbesan book-binding look by hand.
Keeps big stacks of paper in alignment as they are sewn together.
An automated system of needles and levers — simply feed in pages, and watch as it does the rest.

Beekeepers speak honeyed words over the Queenby's patented air-seal that ensures their epidermal safety.
A medium-sized guillotine that makes meat slicing a lot faster.
Vastly speeds up the drying process.

Even a sharp pair of claws seldom makes its way out.

For ceremonial use in the Enbesan Highlands. Made from a hollowed out tree trunk.

Always finds the best spots for her animals to graze peacefully.

It is actually possible to make pulpwood from wanza, although to the expert eye it may appear a little stiff.
Outspoken, charitable and too-often right, he is an easy target for his colleagues in the Keftanya Moot.
The manipulation of punchy, many-coloured powders is an art hidden from view under bright canopies.
Aesop was born in Enbesa before time began. Ever since, he's told stories to any child who might see the morals in them.
His liturgical music has wide popularity among elders, who exert extra effort to hit all the high notes.
The krar and washint obey every gentle press of his fingers, as the rhythm and melody haul all present to their feet.
A provider of saline solutions, this fellow always washes up with a glass of water to hand.
A hero among fishermen — and apparently he doesn't even need to wear the costume!
Really does spend a very long time taking measurements, but all your uppity friends say it's worth it.

The ultimate arbiter of men's fashion, and a complete and utter bore about it, for every would-be-dandy craves his advice.
His mum asks that he call her every day.

Tough on his students, but in the end, they leave the course better equipped than anybody else.

In her grotto of delights, one can find all manner of Enbesan produce. She even delivers direct to your door!
His mind shall never be full, so eager is he to travel the world, meet new people and absorb new languages.
A true designer's work doesn't just cover the body: it makes a statement.
Forged in the fires of years of flame-fighting in Enbesa. An expert in all things fire-related.

A collection of artefacts and ruins closely tied to the roots of Enbesa, rife with lions, and the smouldering seal of the past.

Proof that life will prevail— however harsh the climate— in the nooks and crevices of the scorching Enbesan sands.

You can place livestock in the dry savannah too, but the animals will be healthier if they graze on grassland.
Crops, unlike animals, will not grow unless the soil is properly irrigated.
It's ok for the farm itself to not be placed on irrigated soil, as long as the fields are.
A blue circle around the modules button indicates how many fields are placed on irrigated soil. If the circle is incomplete, something is off somewhere!
Canals need a source of water! Make sure they're connected to a water pump, which can be built on certain river bends. Once water runs into the canals, they will irrigate the land around them!

A water pump is little use on its own: you need to construct canals to carry the water. Did you notice that you can connect canals on both sides of the river? Once water runs into the canals, they will irrigate the land around them!

One water pump can only distribute water up to a certain point; after that, your canals will run dry! If you want to continue irrigating the land, you'll have to connect your canals to another water pump.
This is true of all buildings that need to be placed beside the river: they can be accessed from either shore. If you need a street connection, for example, either side will do.

Venture to the Land of Lions, a roaring southern continent whose people use irrigation to help supply a whole new set of needs! Meet a local Emperor who has faith his empire can be a match for any other.

Venture to the Land of Lions and use canals to help supply a whole new set of needs! Meet a local Emperor and fend off his enemies. Construct a monumental research centre, research and acquire items, and with the new scholar residents, unleash game-changing discoveries!
A Budding Empire

Help Emperor Ketema bring stability to Enbesa from its new capital Taborime. Fend off threats from within and without to bring peace and prosperity to the region. Discover Enbesa's rich history, and benefit from this knowledge with new bonuses.
Harness The Power Of Water
Construct a brand new canal system to irrigate the fields! Fulfil the needs of the shepherds and elders of Enbesa, achieve new economic heights, and watch the desert bloom!
Construct A Monument To Knowledge

Build the new Research Institute in the Old World, and discover new technologies indistinguishable from magic. Turn soil fertile, produce goods from alternative resources, and find the exact specialist or machines you need!
A New Class Of Thinkers
Bring scholars to the Old World from all around the world! Fulfil their cosmopolitan needs so that, alongside your engineers, they may fuel scientific progress!

Emperor Sahle Ketema is the supreme ruler of the mighty nation of Enbesa. He is a proud, ambitious monarch who will levy all resources — even foreign talent — to ensure the Land of Lions is restored to its rightful place among the powers.

A young man of considerable learning, Biniam is Emperor Ketema's chief diplomat. Driven by deep loyalty to his nation, and stalwart pride in his heritage, Biniam will see Enbesa take its rightful place as the beacon of knowledge and innovation across the world.

Even-tempered and caring, Kyria has weathered many a storm and come out undimmed and loyal. There are few on Waha Desher with greater wisdom than she, and even Ambassador Biniam knows to defer to her in herb-lore and memory.

The Princes of Angereb once ruled vast swathes of land and decided the fates of Enbesa. The rule of Emperor Ketema — an outsider to some — has left many of them reticent and belligerent, much to the Emperor's concern.

Time has not been kind to the people of Waha Desher. Much of the once mighty land now lies in a pall of dust and sand, and the cost of supporting its people weighs heavily on Emperor Ketema's young nation. The quaint speech of Waha Desher can still be heard on the island — for now.

Kidusi Anitoni has long been a haven in a war-torn land — a sanctuary devoted to the preservation of a fragile history. Aloof and entrenched in waning privileges, the priests on Kidusi are a monument of Enbesan culture, which Emperor Ketema must, sooner or later, address in his quest for unity.

Onward to Enbesa!

Rations help keep your crew's morale in check. Your crew's morale will be much weaker if they're starving. You can also choose to hand out extra rations to soften the blow of a regrettable outcome on their morale. Try providing them with a variety of food and drink to increase this effect.

You should expect to come across a variety of obstacles on different expeditions. Luckily, you can check what type of threats you're most likely to encounter in advance, and prepare your expedition to face them should the situation arise. To be prepared for the obstacles that await, you can load your ship with goods, items or specialists that have attributes that can help you in those situations. For example, if you expect to deal with diseases, you might want to hire a doctor to come on board. Preparing your expedition accordingly will also increase the crew's initial morale!

You should expect to come across a variety of obstacles on different expeditions. Luckily, you can check what type of threats you're most likely to encounter in advance, and prepare your expedition to face them should the situation arise. To be prepared for the obstacles that await, you can load your ship with goods, items or specialists that have attributes that can help you in those situations. For example, if you expect to deal with diseases, you might want to hire a doctor to come on board. Preparing your expedition accordingly will also increase the crew's initial morale!

Some goods have expedition attributes too. These points are accumulated for every 50t of the goods you have on board. If you bring more or less than 50t, a proportional number of these attribute points will be added.

Sometimes, your expedition will come across an obstacle or opportunity. When this happens, you will be asked to make a decision. Most choices are linked to a certain attribute; the higher your score on that attribute, the higher the chance that this course of action will succeed.

You will immediately learn the outcome of your decisions. Whether it turned out good or bad for your crew will depend on how well prepared they were for that course of action, but luck also plays a key part. Think carefully about your crew's attributes, and try not to make any rash decisions!

The number of skulls next to an expedition indicates its difficulty level. Easy expeditions may not pose many threats, but legendary rewards await those who dare venture into the most dangerous places. Still, it's best not to go taking any chances! Setting out on a hard expedition will require more — and better — equipment to take on the challenges that await.

Select which ship you want to send on this expedition. A higher morale value is of course preferable, but beware: this ship will not return for some time. You will be able to increase the base morale by equipping this ship with goods and items. You can also change the chosen ship here later on.
