The Rise of Emperor Ketema
Pinnable Goods
"Land of Lions"
Land of Lions
The emperor may have granted you stewardship, but it will take more than a piece of paper to prove you care for Enbesa.
Quite right. What use are gifts that cannot be shared, save for ostentatious displays of wealth?
How very like a foreigner to bring a gift that loudly proclaims their means.
Say you were invited to my home... What would you bring to honour the invitation?
It has come time for the bull-leaping ceremony of Ukuli Bula! Rarely have we had so many applicants— I doubt there are enough steers for every boy.
Broad backs, long horns... Yes, these will do nicely.
Scandalous! The cowardly boys took fright at the bulls and fled rather than face the trial like men!
My thanks. I will see to it that they are given the friskiest bulls!
At last, the Ukuli Bula may start! We Irenya recognize your efforts in ensuring it went ahead, and invite you to capture a memory of it.
Let all who succeeded be known from now on as men in their full right! As for the others, they will get another chance next year.
Could you bring Aida to me? It is high time she were wed, and I have the perfect match— a young man from a decent, pious family.
Hm. All tousled and anxious— this will not do. Come, girl, let us get you dressed and prepared to meet your intended!
I thank you for your help — such a match will prove of great interest to Aida and her family.
Aida refuses to honour the arrangement, drivelling instead about a Meniga she claims to love! Convince her of the folly in her position!
A decision worthy of a true Enbesan! The laws of our forebears are who we are; their traditions run in our very blood.
How dare you call yourself a regent when you scorn our very laws! This betrayal will not go unpunished!
Why teach virtue and humility to children if their parents then spoil them with lavish presents like oranges?
It is for the greater good. They will thank us for it one day, be sure of it.
Idleness breeds contempt and unruliness in children. They must be kept busy, and taught the value of labour and an orderly life.
Excellent! This will teach them to contribute to society, and return some quiet to the streets.
The boy was caught lying, and must be cleansed of the evil within him — only a public confession will ensure he is purified of the stain!
A fitting ceremony. Let all who were here stand witness to the mercy of the Lord. In the name of all Irenya, I give you thanks.
Is this your idea of justice? All you have taught them is that they need but complain to see their labour lessened.
The council have finally welcomed me among the elders of the Keftanya Moot! Help me prepare my acceptance speech!
Thank you... for helping me understand what I needed to do in my speech.
How very inappropriate! Now, be serious! This is important.
I'm not saying that, you wicked bushpig!
What is the point of letting me join the Moot if no-one will listen to my ideas? Don't you have any influence?
Success! The proposal was approved by the majority! I think they suspect something though — we'll have to be more creative.
Elder Selassy'e opposes my every proposal! He must certainly have some nefarious plan— I ask you to follow him!
Nothing?... strange. There is more to this, I am sure of it!
There he is! Follow him — it shouldn't be hard to catch him red-handed!
Keep your eyes peeled for any secret signals he might be giving with his hands.
Keep watching his hands— perhaps he will pocket something!
With those girls I sent beside him, the "truth" of his low morals will be out — all you need do is take the picture.
He fell for our trap! Now all will know him for the sinner he is, and my reforms will finally get the audience they deserve!
Idleness and sin everywhere! It is high time I — I mean, the Moot — reminded everyone of the value of work, piety and abstinence!
How dare they! Can't they see how much better the city is now? Ingrates! Well, I shall soon return and see the Lord's will done!
I... I don't understand. I only wanted to make our city better. Can't they see that? The shame... did I really go too far?
How does one extol the glory of the Lord in such miserly temples? The gates of the Holy Realm are gold and basalt, not raw wood and lead!
As is given on this earth, so will be apportioned tenfold in Heaven!
How can the pious pray and worship with the bleating of those wretched beggars before the gates?
Yes, hear how the hymns resonate in the quiet chapel walls? Blessed peace at last!
Pater Dekama distributes food to the poor souls outside the monastery— but he must have officials to make it a formal thing.
Everyone was most impressed with our work - why, the archimandrite himself, in his sermon, praised it as an example of rare virtue!
Must I do everything? The festival but weeks away and there is so much still to arrange— the materials to fashion a proper tabot, for instance!
A pin here, a fold there... perfect! As long as the tabot is complete, the festival may proceed.
How are we to count on you if you squander valuable time and resources on menial matters?
It may seem unfair, but the concerns of the few pale to those of the many.
How typical of the Meniga— wasting good dye for a moment of fun when it could have been used to the glory of all!
It seems my intentions have been misunderstood, and some are unhappy with how the festival was handled.
I trust the message will now be clear! It would be an insult if I had had to suffer such indignity needlessly.
If I must belittle myself to preserve order, then so I will. And you had better help— hand these fruit baskets out to Meniga households.
Only ten stations left...
Take up this cross, Kurati...
And so He was interred by lesser men...
The stain of my unkindness and disregard for the Meniga weighs heavily upon my soul, and I would do penance by fasting.
To think a Meniga could show mercy on she that hurt his fellows... Blessed are they of simple dispositions.
It is storytelling time for the younger ones, to teach them virtue and piety, but I... seem to have forgotten some parts of the tale.
The Moot has noticed very few people read anymore. How can one know who they are if they do not know where they come from?
Refuse everywhere, and none of the youth even consider cleaning up! Do something about it!
How do you expect us to face our children with the city in such a state?
People are upset because they work so hard they don't see their families. If you could only ease things a little...
Young people are forgetting our glorious heritage! A memorial will remind them of our glorious history!
No-one told you it was your duty to provide tea for the weekly Keftanya Moot?
I was planning on visiting Fasika in our hometown, but my nephews are too busy with work to escort me…
Come, come, let us be quick about it!
Rest, again!? I used to walk further than this on daily errands!
The lurching... (heaving) Tell it to stop!
These were once barely paths, let alone roads.
Fasika! It's funny, I almost didn't recognize you because you have so many new wrinkles.
Yes, the way you've decorated is very... interesting.
And he's a farmhand, you say? Well, what a catch!
Returning already? What about the visit to cousin Haji, and aunt Tabi and...and...
People fall ill while you fritter on your foreign trinkets! Perhaps, for once, you could build something for us?
The Irenya trust you more when you take care of such things rather than waste time on the Meniga.
The Moot worry the Scholars have forgotten who they are and what they owe to their homeland— I can give them a good talking-to.
Momentously important work', tch, If the Lord wanted slugs to be important, he'd have made us slugs!
How could he forget everything we taught him so easily! By the end he was squirming with shame!
Of all the arrogant, thankless young grasshoppers... Using someone else's hard work to settle his own petty argument.
A ship, you say, bearing a visitor? It was long ago, but I think I remember. Follow me.
One would not have guessed - he was so frail. His guard days were long ago, and he was afraid. He rests in peace now.
Take his diary, and may it keep his memory alive a moment.
A foolish gesture! Why work, when you have a benevolent overlord to support you? But very well, it is all the same to me.
Do not meddle with traditions you do not understand! It is the Meniga's very purpose to serve, to provide for Enbesa at large…
Tradition is our identity, the foundation of Enbesa! You have no right to refuse the rightful order, steward.
So we come to it again—it is time for the tithe to be paid. Still willing to let these wretches leech off your benevolence?
Very well. It is all the same to me. Until next year, then.
A miracle, a gift from the Almighty! Through the Lamb Amun has He spoken to the lowliest of the low! Raise a temple around this hallowed ground!
Law and tradition exist for a reason. It is good that you understand this.
...And that's the last jar. You see? Efforts yield results, not complaints.
Some Meniga boys came to tell me one of their number went to slay a beast in the mountains and hasn't come back. Shouldn't you be investigating?
We wish to thank our young hero for delivering Alyia back to her family — as much food and drink as you deem you can provide!
Bullies who show up to shame a hero deserve nothing but to be cast into exile, as is tradition.
It's him! It's the king! Here to spy and eavesdrop, so he can point the finger of blame!
We Seifu promise never to forgive the Abate, and neither do we go about breaking promises!
We are losing what we have always been for the modern, and he is too lenient! We should be sticking these foreign powers through as King Wag would have done!
Hmm, I see…
Well, my word!
Oh, happy days!
Thanks to you I can take on a new apprentice to lessen the load!
Slowly, you understand us.
It is good to see the wars of our fathers bred such stock!
Your stewardship is praised by South and North!
Almighty guide you.
Cousin Fasika will be quite jealous. (satisfied little sound)
The council must hear of this!
Perhaps a short respite then.
Certainly.
Very well.
Sigh... Teaching manners to a donkey would offer more reward!
First forgeries, lies, and goat-riding in our city, and now this!
Worse than when Tariku dropped my hymnals in curdled milk!
Don't put honey in my milk and call it tej!
I see why the empress counsels the emperor against you.
Is this how you treat your wards?
The emperor will hear of this!
When I first moved here, Fasika insisted I bring a batch of eggs from our hen Azo, fearing the mountain air would make local hens barren.
The Lord made each for their alotted part - would that all understood this.
I like to think the Lord hears my love when I sing. La la la la…
I saw the empress wearing a dark blue habesha yesterday - she disapproves of the Emperor's decision to let a foreigner teach at the palace.
One is not born an Irenya, it is an honour bestowed.
Fasika almost wedded a Meniga girl once. Fortunately I managed to step in - his heart is in the right place, but his head…
Many feared the Emperor would take after King Wag, his father, but his rule has proven more blessed than any before him - if perhaps too progressive.
Spending so much time alone with animals, in the wild - no wonder the Meniga are such corybantic creatures.
What do goat-herds know of the importance of tradition and order?
Why send Scholar Mihurani to foreign lands if a mother can no longer recognise her son when he returns?
Long ago, our land was ruled by many feuding princes. My husband died in their wars. Fortunately, Emperor Ketema put an end to that age of strife.
Who will teach the Meniga the value of hard work and piety if not us?
Hear the voice of the Irenya.
The emperor said we should call upon you for this.
A lesson to be learned here.
He judges us by our deeds, not our intent.
Truly?
Let us get to it then.
The matter is in your hands now.
Diligence in duty is perhaps a novel notion?
What is one voice to the choir of the faithful?
Surely you would not renege on your word?
Of course. You must have other duties to attend to.
Is this what the emperor wanted?
The Lord works in mysterious ways…
I look away for one minute…!
Fear not my judgement, but that of the Lord.
(disapproving huff)
So?
Shall we?
Now for the final note.
Back already?
Tsigiju?
Ah, excellent!
So His will is done.
Sweet is the mead of success.
Yemesgneka!
A small contribution to the Lord's plans.
The Book teaches us to share our blessings.
A token of appreciation from the Irenya.
It is well-deserved.
A fitting place to spread the word of the Lord.
What manner of city is this?
No more!
Do our laws stand for nothing?
How am I to pay for my son's expenses?
This is not what my father died for!
Hardly the Eden that was promised.
It is hard not to regret the days of the divided realms.
(disgusted sound) What monster drinks unspiced tea?
Can't they take their chatter elsewhere?
Blunt, again! Who keeps using my tools?
If this is to be our alotted part, so be it.
What we lack, the Lord provides for.
Hardly the Garden, but well…
An Irenya does not complain of hardship.
How can the Scholar Mihurani not appreciate this life?
A letter from my son already? It's not been two weeks!
It is such a privilege to pass on one's wisdom!
...My son sent me a bird from overseas. I named it Amanuel, for protection.
Dear Fasika, you should have seen the Lent celebrations here!
It is good to know peace at last.
The sweet scent of injera baked on scalding stone…
Under the Lord, we are but one family.
The subscription for the new monastery was successful!
Every day the city blooms sweeter.
There were so many people, the crowd was spilling out of the church door!
As the Lord provisioned, so the land of His people is built.
They asked me to be the Mother for the spring mass!
Have you heard? The new bishop is from the Kidusi Anitoni monastery!
Not a day where I don't give thanks to our emperor!
Blessed is the land where sheep and lions run free in brotherhood!
Fasika! We didn't expect… are all those… are you moving in?
You there! Take this bucket and help!
Bernahu! (struggling) My brother is in there!
My mother wove that dress!
What are you doing? Water on my scripture! Heathens!
All the memories… Gone.
Lord grant me strength.
Don't come any closer!
Please… I need to write to my son.
No, no doctor! Call for a priest!
You there! Why aren't you wearing your mask?!
Return our fathers' land to us!
We will not wait until the last tree has fallen!
We are Enbesa - time they remembered it!
Rise, sisters! Rise, brothers!
Now for wrath, now for ruin, now for - Enbesa!
Many have tested our strength before. We still stand.
They haven't reached the southlands, have they? I should warn Fasika.
I've stored some food in a vug down the hill, just in case.
They will hear the lion roar!
Besemayi yemitinori…
How shall I get to mass without a road?
Barely a path, let alone a road.
I do not have the time to trace a path myself!
Just give me a minute to put my tools in order.
Tariku! Show them around, will you?
No idling around, you'll need to get your hands dirty.
That? My niece asked me to repair it, but…(sigh)
I said no animals in the workshop!
There's some stew for you if you want it, Tariku.
Hmph. I learnt this as a child. Look here…
I will be back after church - there should be a few more hours of daytime to work.
Someone do something!
The wretched boy forgot to douse the fire again!
Not water, fool, throw dirt!
Just brew me some hot tea with pepper, will you?
Lord, I am not ready to join you yet!
(coughing) Tariku? Is that you? Come into the (cough) light.
By the grace of the Lord, we will not be cowed!
Friends, Enbesans, countrymen!
Let us see how they fare without our know-how!
Cousin Fasika is in town - it will not do to have him see me so idle!
No - see the folded crest? That's a hoopoe.
Where is the boy? Lazy Northerner…
But… what shall we do?
I would rather not abandon this halfway, but…
Time for tea, then.
Stoke the fire, boy!
Ah, at last!
Hmm? Oh, very well.
I cannot be expected to do this alone!
This is not a one-woman task.
Some things only several Irenya can do.
No, I can't simply 'make do with what I have'!
If only Tariku hadn't misplaced my last batch!
Only the Lord can create from nothing.
We are running out of space here.
These goods need proper storage, not an open courtyard!
I'd rather take these home than see the rain spoil them.
All things have a heart apportioned by the Lord, even ore. The true smith knows how to sit and listen for that heart.
It's a subtle craft, wax-etching — not the kind you can do standing up and waving about.
The trick is to smoke the horn with khat before adding the clay bowl. Burns any remaining offal.
Cooking - proper cooking - is a sit-down sort of business. (tutting) Only fools cook standing.
Tef is a holy plant - brought to Enbesa by Queen Shaba herself! Not all are worthy to thresh it.
Whenever someone uses these to pray, a piece of my soul is carried upward with them.
(humming) A song from my youth tells of a traveller from the Land of Crows, who taught our ancestors to build mills such as this...
The Book says the Path Upward is built of such bricks, red and strong. Far too important to let Meniga make them.
When mother was a child, we weaved coloured strands of teff into the fabric — for a different texture, you see...
The Spear is here? My predecessors made no mention of this great secret. Apt precautions, seeing your shameless attempt to break in.
We found a man in the mountains— wounded, who sent us to you for aid. Perhaps you would care to explain?
I will let you have the Spear, for Angereb is its shrine of old, but I will not have Kidusi lose such a treasure rewardlessly.
Our harbour records? Yes, of course, but...
The registry cannot leave the island, but we had a copy prepared for you.
Ah, I suppose Lord Biniam forgot something and sent you back for it? Well, the registers for the campaign are still on display...
The library is restricted to servants of the Lord. The texts here are holy scripture, guarded from unsanctioned influence.
But as you are working on the chronicles, you may enter if you answer this riddle: On quiet meres I lay, never sinking. Yet dipped in water, I am fit for drinking.
The hibiscus flower is the image of what we seek, here in Kidusi Anitoni: knowledge nourishes us, that we may bloom in the eyes of the Lord.
The library? No, no, no! The riddle was but a stepping-stone! Until you understand the meaning of learning, you shan't be let in.
The outer world speaks before it listens. But here the waters of wisdom are drawn from the wellspring of silence.
One must learn to see with the inner eye — the eye of the soul. Tell me, which of the buildings on our island is largest?
Our temple is but a frail offspring of the mighty halls of the Elamais. Tall walls and ornate ceilings, but shallow roots.
He that ordered this tomb built dreamt of glory everlasting. Yet the tomb lies empty, and his name, forgotten.
Yes, our library is vast, but is only the cloud-swathed summit. Look to roots hidden beneath.
Long ago, our library was a beacon of learnedness in a world of darkness. But the treacherous kings of Kashta burnt it all.
Now it is interred deep below our island, but to those who know, the high walls and pale altars live on all around us.
Your understanding is starting to blossom — the time for admittance is at hand.
Loyalty to Lord Ketema does you credit, but we will not join him. He is too narrow in his faith, and I will not see Kidusi's legacy forgotten.
You show yourself to be worthy of trust. Lift now the veil, and enter our famed library.
There are volumes here on every aspect of theology, history, science or poetics. If you read, please turn the pages by their corners.
A fellow scholar of the Golden Age? There is much we could discuss!
History becomes legend, legend myth, and even myth is half-forgotten. But why not dig up the old library— there must be traces to be found.
You are accustomed to such undertakings. Gather a crew and supplies, and we will support you.
Unsurprising. The people of Taborime are wayward, having forgotten the ways of old.
The excavators appear ill-fed, but will have to do for the task at hand.
We cannot accommodate so many. We shall need temporary quarters for these workers.
At last, the excavation can commence. Lord look favourably upon us!
The workers' tools are old and break easily. Could you talk to them? They are adamant this is perfectly normal.
Interesting idea. If Lord Ketema wishes to show friendship, then he will agree to provide tools to his architect.
I feared Ketema would send his horrid steel beasts. But wisdom seems to have prevailed.
The excavation will resume presently— and soon the first unveiling.
Such methods in this holy place shows the extent of your respect. Very well, if you must, but do not disrupt our services!
The labourers strike a hard surface! Fragments of lost history, at last!
Quite a store of history hidden here, more than anticipated! It shall remain exposed while the search continues.
Our predecessors in the Golden Age saw that Kidusi Anitoni's purpose was not to produce goods, but wisdom.
So will Kidusi shine again! We halt the excavation to celebrate this glorious monument's return!
This statue will stand at our gates, to remind visitors that our faith stands the test of time.
We must comply for now. Yet know that not all things will bow to your will, and that there are higher orders than ours.
The excavation can resume, but do inspect the statue — it may inspire you to write your Chronicles.
The good of those entrusted to us often requires compromises.
I expected nothing more from one of Ketema's hounds. This affair is no longer yours to command.
An Imperial Decree? I had expected the Emperor would wish to hear no more of us…
I... Kidusi cannot survive without trade, it would be a death sentence. We have no choice: we must bow to the Emperor in submission.
A boulder fell upon a man's leg at the site! We have treated it, but he is asking specifically for you.
He needs some rest, of course, but if he were to leave, it would mean an additional delay.
A decoction of hibiscus spirit could dull the pain, but we will need more leaves to brew it.
You are kind. Take him home, and we shall proceed with the excavation as best we can.
We have unearthed a strange monolith, with odd inscriptions on the bas-reliefs. A language, we believe.
It appears to be the Ancient Script of Enbesa. A pity it was lost in Sûrya's great cleansing of the clergy — the secrets we might have learned!
Some scholars specialise in deciphering ancient languages — they might be able to help!
Good timing! We come upon the lowest room of the library; covered with verse in the Ancient Script!
See the prostrates down there?— Waha Desher folk bringing tribute to Kidusi: a testament to our proud heritage!
I expect your translation eagerly. Surely with this evidence, Lord Ketema can no longer deny the legitimacy of our claims!
Heresy! We welcome and support you, only for you to repay us with fiendish lies?
The foundations of our faith are built on these very walls. Once it was a place of pilgrimage, and when Ketema recognises our claims, will be again.
I knew a foreigner could never translate such a document. Go to Ketema and tell him Kidusi Anitoni has proof of its ancestry, and will not yield.
Curse the day we ever trusted you! By your fault are we doomed to fade, by your will are these halls destroyed!
I had hoped...Ketema's support at least ensures the library will remain, and time is on our side, as it ever has been on Kidusi.
Kidusi has long been a place of prayer and writing, and will remain so. No Emperor can countermand this.
The stubborn old goat! Well, we shan't be cowed— Kidusi stands for truth, whatever trials this unfair ban bring.
Our stone! What have you done? Heathens! This is how our trust is repayed? If only you had never come here!
So you have found it. Perhaps it is best; secrets weigh heavy, and I weary of deceit.
I suppose you deserve the truth. Come, and listen.
Legend became history, fabrication truth, and the High Priestesses guarded the secret for centuries. Now the veil parts, and I confess there is some comfort to it.
It is time we embraced our duty to the people of Enbesa rather than our pride. We shall join the Emperor and serve the tenets of a renewed faith, for the good of all.
This letter will lay everything out for the Emperor to see. May wisdom guide him.
Much lies ahead of us, but all things I can look to proudly, without shame or deceit. I thank you for this; come find me in Kidusi when you have a moment.
This vase honours the memory of the greatest of our queens, millenia ago. Upon it are the most ancient writings, which I had translated for you, by way of thanks.
Too long have our books remained unread and dustladen. I have had them removed to the harbour, so that all may consult them and grow in wisdom.
The Priests of Kidusi acknowledge you.
It is all a great mystery.
Issehds, you say? What a strange dialect. Trees, I believe — the sort found by the shore, behind the library. Take as many as you wish.
You want the ghastly fiends? Well, Teka has finished studying them for his zoological study of Enbesa, so please, take the brutes!
I dare not leave home while pestilence roams the streets unchecked!
You have brought much change to our land, but not all of it is evil. Under your rule, the Emperor's dream of unity does not seem so hopeless.
Care to help me take the sheep out to pasture? A wonderful place, not far — tall grass, shade, a beautiful waterfall…
It's like family, caring for the sheep, seeing them grow. Amun is my favourite— he was cast aside by his mother, so I raised him myself.
There he is, Amun! Wait, is that bush on fire? Is it... whispering?
Wait, where is Amun? He's... He's not here! Please, please help me find him— there are many dangers around here!
I'm just glad Amun was unhurt... We have the Lord to look out for us, but who does a lost sheep have but its shepherd?
Our neighbours' landlady demands more and more tithe, but they can't keep up, what with the harvest. They're good people, you know ?
It hurts me to see my neighbour suffer like this.
Enough for them to survive this year, but... What the Irenya expect just seems... unfair.
We must do something! The tithe is collected in large jars. What if we only put good stuff on top and stuff the rest with dry teff?
She hasn't noticed! Good. I just hope she won't retaliate against my friends when she realizes...
I have these... friends, I suppose. They like to talk and play qarsa, but forget to tell me where.
Fine new friends! We played and talked and they asked me to help with a celebration— everyone must dress foreign!
These should do nicely! We are all going to look so funny!
They want you to take a picture of us! Even though it seems I'm the only one who dressed up...
It was a rotten prank! How could they, telling me to 'man up'. They want a man? I'll show them a man!
I couldn't kill it. The beast...the lion had a wounded paw— I could only think to help it. That may make me less of a man, but I don't care.
Alyia, my third cousin— she's disappeared! Everyone's out looking for her, but I am just as worried for her family...
Uncle is wary of the Irenya, but ask him about the letter and where Alyia went, and he might open up to you.
Uncle gave us a clue about where she worked, maybe we should go there?
The overseer doesn't recall anyone by the name of Alyia, but he's going to let us look through his staff register.
The worker that could be our Alyia, was stung badly by the bees, the overseer says— went to the hawkers at the harbour for a soothing cream.
Um...I told the Elders she was found praying at a mountain monastery. They were so impressed with her piety, they didn't ask why she was dressed as a boy!
Oh, and instead of paying for that cream for her bee-stings, I suggested beeswax! If she wanted, she could return to work at the beehives...
Alya! There you are. Come home, I promise I'll tell no-one you dressed as a boy. You only wanted to provide for your family.
Why are the Irenya so strict!? I know what it is like to be cast out, and the sting of people's words— we should show him mercy.
The outcast bully must be feeling quite miserable— he will be glad to see a friendly face, I think!
I don't think he expected us to look for him. The light in his eyes when he took my hand... people can change if you show a little understanding.
Have you seen my baby brothers? The little sandmice keep running away!
Hard to imagine what it must be like without kin— weak, alone, the bad moods... We should care for those elders who have no one else.
Long night but I finally have it! All it took was some wanza and a bit of metal, but we could do great things with it in the fields…
See! Sometimes it's good to try new things.
A cousin of mine has brought seeds from the distant countryside. Could you sow them, and bring some life back to Taborime?
There is no better way to feel close to the land than to plant a seed and watch it grow, against all odds.
I'll miss old Lani when she leaves the flock, but she doesn't milk any more…
Just like me they like to go gallivanting off. Could you help me find the goats before they eat Taborime dry?
I know you've brought us much, and people are thriving, but... Sometimes I don't recognise it anymore. Green has become grey, I miss the wind in the trees...
Is it true that in your land there are places where animals of all reaches of creation live together in harmony?
In cages? They're not so free then... (sigh) Well, maybe it will at least help people better understand them...
I... wrote a poem because I worry for nature in Enbesa with all this building. I wish the Emperor could hear it, but I doubt it will ever reach him…
There’s a land where the mountains are nameless, and the rivers all run God knows where…
There’s a land where life and love is boundless, And soft scented honey wafts through the air.
Please, it is enough. I wish such pain on no-one, not even you Elder.
You claim to speak for all in Enbesa, so I come to you: Elder Asikinyi must be made to repent the suffering she has brought upon us Meniga.
Now I wish I had never asked you to punish her. It was selfish of me, and no good comes of hurting another person.
Please, it is enough. I wish such pain on no-one, not even you, Elder.
This festival is a time of joy, of family, of gift-giving... But what about those who have no families?
So long since I last saw such smiles.. So little effort can make such a change for those with nothing...
I know you have an entire city to administrate, but... it would have taken so little effort, and meant so much to them...
How are we to survive if not here? Irenya pass us by in the streets without looking at us...
But King Wag's was a time of violence. I do not wish to live in such a world, only that Ketema would care more for the ordinary people.
Bluebird and goldbrush!
I'll be off to the woods then!
A story in the making!
A bask in the sun for us then, old girl!
Like warm tej in the cool shade!
People smile more when you are kind to them!
It's rare to see that kind of heart.
It takes the right kind of painter to see the colours in a people.
You've shown us that one can rule and be kind.
I knew you were a good person at heart.
It'll make for a nice story!
Thank you!
Well of course!
I'd be happy to!
There are many different perspectives.
Oh, that's not good.
We could do things differently if we tried…
I don't think we'll be laughing over stories tonight.
I feel a little bit overwhelmed.
I'd hoped you'd see things from our side.
If we can't turn to you, who else is there?
I'm no storyteller, so I paint faces and masks on what I can find to show them to my sister!
A campfire is a bit like... the low rumbling of an elephant. Vast and filled with memories and laughter.
What's not to love about bread, you can use it to pick up food and share it around?
I'd love to learn storytelling from one of the great masters, like Maesha…
Even if I could I wouldn't give up this life. All I need is here, on this patch of wind-grown land.
I was taught how to fight when I was younger — had to, 'Pa said. But that's not me.
I wonder, would my father be proud of who I am? And the life we live now…
I don't resent the Irenya. But sometimes I think they forget we are all sheep to the same Shepherd.
I am a Meniga, yes, but I like to think the one above cares about what we do, not where we come from.
The Emperor cares for us, after his own way, and that's enough for me.
Sometimes I wonder what being born a Mihurani — the Scholars — would've been like. But I'm happy just being myself.
Some mornings there's a hush on the city, as though all of Enbesa were slowly waking— it's beautiful.
Can I trouble you for a moment?
You said we could come to you, right?
Everyone is going to be so relieved!
We're in your debt.
I appreciate it — really!
Oh, wonderful!
We're counting on you!
Hard to keep track with such beauty all around, isn't it?
No pressure at all, but… we could use the help.
Well, we'll find a way, I'm sure.
Next time, perhaps.
Oh. O-of course you'd have important things to do!
It's all right — what matters is that you tried!
It's not time lost if you learned something.
I'll manage, don't worry about me!
So what shall it be?
If you could…?
Wonderful!
Well met!
Let's see it then.
I didn't expect you back so soon!
Already?
I never doubted you would.
Thank you kindly.
That… That'll help immensely!
I'm glad we can trust you to look out for us.
It's more than I ever thought we could hope.
I put something aside for you.
It's not much, but I'd like you to have it.
Don't mention it.
It's the little things that matter.
I'll unpack later, there's a garden to explore!
Time and time again, we have to back down…
The dreams won't stop…
Why go home if all we have to come to is… this?
Why — why do we stand for all this?
I made a mask, but its face scares me...
I've been troubled with… strange dreams of late.
Not now, Izara. Big brother's tired…
Maybe we deserve these hardships…
It's hard to be kind when the world is unfair…
A troubled wind blows…
The masinqo is a bit out of tune, but it's a start.
Yes, I think I will invite them to the dance!
Silver linings… Why not honeyed linings?
The city's starting to look…ah...urban.
The story is about a city, like this one, where all was well until…
Sun, rain, wind - these are the true riches!
People keep bringing me eggs, it's wonderful!
Ever noticed how the water shimmers after the rain?
Today's sea-blue on green hills, isn't it?
Lovebird's crest is red, weather'll be fine!
See how the sun shimmers in the morning dew!
A new dawn, a new day, a new life!
Dancing is like… breathing. It's the linen of life.
The great Maesha could write something wondrous of this place.
The sky is open, blue and wide!
This place is a garden!
So wonderful, having this every day!
So many wonders in the world…
So many beautiful languages and colourful garments!
Like sun on a young stream!
I'm living like an Irenya with none of the responsibility!
I can't find Wishaisha!
We can rebuild… can't we?
Please, that cape was my grandfather's!
Just a light burn, there are others worse off!
Don't let it spread to other homes!
Don't come near, you might catch it!
I don't want to be trapped in a box!
I can't go to work - I'll infect everyone!
Just leave my body by the mountainside.
Is (coughs) is everyone else okay?
Occupy their homes, their land!
No more silence! No more pain!
Where is the better future we were promised?
The shepherds stand together on this!
No shepherd sends their lambs to the slaughter!
What are we even fighting for?
If we could just talk to our enemies, I'm sure…
No parent should have to bury their child.
There, there… It's going to be all right.
Can there be any victory when people lie dead?
A road would keep us safer from snakes.
Don't like deathstalker scorpions? You might want a road.
There is tea by the door if you want it.
How may I help?
Oh, I didn't expect you there?
I can teach you how to do this if you wish!
Come on Dagè, you old thing, time to get moving!
Hold a wax-stick to a flame and it'll melt just enough so you can shape it into whatever you want - a bee, for instance!
No time for poetry while I'm here…
I try not to spend too long indoors.
I look forward to home, and the softness of sleep.
Take my cloak, it'll smother the flames!
Call the firemen, I'll fetch water!
I'm sorry, I tried to…
I'll call the doctor — just hold on to Wishaisha for now!
If I can just find some smoked tef leaf…
Well, the ankole were looking sickly yesterday, so maybe…
Better stay with my ox than bear this!
Why work for so little!?
Don't tell us our labour won't be missed!
Who's a good girl, Dagè? You are, you are!
When I'm not busy, there's this huge waterfall, and silverfish…
There's value to work, but so is there to rest!
Let me pick up my walking stick and you can close the door!
Ever wonder what it would be like to close up and just… never come back?
Naptime by the water it is, then!
I knew we'd get back to it eventually.
It is good to feel useful!
I'll be right there - just one verse left to finish!
We may need to draw more water.
There not much water nearby — not even a stream.
It's dry and dusty here.
If the rains weren't so fickle…
We'll need a canal to do that.
Not really suitable for keeping animals.
I don't think the beasts will be happy here.
Good for neither cattle nor goats.
I'm not sure the land is right for that.
That won’t grow well here - it's the local insects, you see.
Isn't that crop too foreign to grow here?
A bit snug for the animals here, don't you think?
Hear that low grunting? It means they need more space.
These colourful fields could be even bigger.
It wouldn't take much to prepare more land.
It's a bit sad, working alone.
It's just not the same if there's no-one to sing with.
I wouldn't mind an extra pair of hands.
We're missing materials.
Wait, where's the… it was just here!
There's only so much I can do with what I have.
There's no storehouse.
Why doesn't anyone come to pick up our goods?
Is our work no longer needed?
See how the branches round and wind like a crown? That's why it's called wanza.
Mind the old goat - it has a mean streak.
The Sanga's horns? No, no — they're for scratching trees.
We used to pay for things with salt, you know? Long ago now…
I used to pack some dried meat as a child, before we'd head up into the mountains and stay for days at a time.
Well the oil is useful, obviously, and the fibers. Now the petals, that's where…
It's tougher - see? I once got my clothes snagged in brambles and it barely even tore.
My mother taught me. She even made some of the tapestries in the Emperor's palace!
My sister used to call the flowers God's Lips — she said the Lord kissed the earth and they blossomed.
Well a tiny bit of milk in the tea can't hurt, can it?
There was just enough clay left to make a doll for my sister.
Well you dip the cloth in a large vat of the dye— the trick is to make sure the cloth doesn't sink, but floats on the surface.
I suppose I could make use of the gloves around the furnace, but…. Why?
I just like the feel of grains of teff rippling through my fingers, I think.
Don't tell, I dipped my finger in the honey and had a taste.
My brother's sense of smell disappeared entirely. Couldn't even taste spices. His cooking was terrible after that.
First you lead the little lobster into the chamber, and then into the parlour. After he has breakfasted with you, there is no way he is leaving.
So, Ketema sends a lackey? Prudent, and expected. Very well then — welcome to Angereb, stranger.
You would have our trust? Earn it then. Show us you are capable of understanding our land and people.
Ours may be a small nation, but there is beauty and glory aplenty here!
You have seen the promises - the beauty of our land. Let us hear now what your master would say to us.
You are a guest on our land. If we are to trust you, you must first prove your goodwill.
At last, the palace stands again! It is only fitting that you, who made miracles possible, celebrate the inauguration!
We doubted you, but you helped us nonetheless. For this, you may now learn more of our secrets.
We have need to deliver hand-carved ceramics to Waha Desher but none of our ships are available...
There it is! Please hurry, or they will be too dry for the monks to carve the inlays!
The priests were expecting their garb earlier, but it'll do.
One of our ships is taking in water every which way - the carpenter needs his tools but they've been mislaid!
Yes, that's it— take it to ship's carpenter swiftly, before it sinks!
Tools? Well unless they're a diving bell it's a bit too late, I fear, unless you can help?
The palace was not just a residence: it was a shrine. With the bones of Yetbarok from the necropolis in Kidusi, it would finally be complete...
This man will know how to arrange for proper transportation of Yetbarok's remains. Take him to Kidusi Anitoni.
To finally set eyes on Yetbarok's tomb... Shall we then?
We are a people of honour above all. It guides heart and spirit through the darkness of these troubled times, it is our foundation.
A century ago, the line of the Elamais died with Lebne, last of the great kings...
His heir, Mekdem the Young, was due to succeed him, but his younger brother Tomasi had other ambitions.
Tomasi desired the throne, so he sent shade-men to slay Mekdem and his kin. But things turned foul as Tomasi tried to flee.
Soon, the last of the Elamais lay dead. But one of Tomasi's retinue escaped, carrying with him the heirloom of Selamawi: the Spear of Darashi.
He came to us for shelter, and we hid him from his enemies. But the Spear disappeared, and only Caleb knows what became of it.
You may recall you helped a man in Kidusi Anitoni. He was on the Spear's trail, and we believe he may be close to finding it.
Selamawi's spear was a gift from the Almighty, to unite all heavens to his command. It belongs in Angereb, where Selamawi ruled of old.
Find the spear, and we will listen to Ketema's proposal. But be discreet — the Spear is a secret to most.
Take your time, look around. I doubt we'll find it immediately, but any clue might lead us, in the end to the Spear.
With those clues, we should be able to determine where the Spear was hidden.
I have scouted the place and I believe I have a plan. Meet me when you are ready.
They will doubtless question us if we are caught. Better learn their lore and rituals and have answers.
Confound those priests and their inquisitiveness!
That could've gone better... Muster your wits— the High Priestess is shrewd old woman.
Silver-tongued, you are. Impressive. Now keep watch here.
At last! Meet me at the harbour — best I go in alone.
Hard going, but at last we have it! The Spear returns to its rightful place!
Treacherous paths, loose rocks. I will need some sort of map to progress.
Into the mountains then. Wait til you hear from me.
Please don't tell the Princes, but I had to use the Spear as a walking staff for that last part. Now, to Angereb!
At last, the Spear returns to Angereb! Let us be on our way then.
I shall have to stay, to clear our trail and tie up loose ends. Sail safe, my friend.
The Spear... You found it? You have it?
To think such a day would come! You have worked wonders; come, tell us all about it!
Look to the registries and harbour manifests. A lone ship with a fleeing mariner should have been recorded somewhere.
Have you found some trace of your quarry?
The time is come for a new king, a new age! Let his rule be a time of glory for Angereb and generosity for its friends!
All hail King Caleb of Angereb, he who will free us of the usurper Ketema! And hail our friend, who brought this joyous day upon us!
Ketema is not our king, but neither would we have war with him. If you will support our independence, he will have no choice but to comply.
We are grateful for your help, but the time has come to choose a side. You stand with us... or against us.
A visitor? Uncommon indeed— the place lost its favour when King Wag passed, and who would for a forsaken advisor like me?
This inscription— 'to Haile, who feared the dark, and Wag, who turned and faced it.' Could this mean King Wag was...
King Wag's office holds the information. I have a key, but I doubt I should be welcome in the castle. You, on the other hand...
The Emperor should know of this. Bring him King Wag's notes, and tell no-one else.
The dog reveals its true colours. You would deny us kingship? Then it is war you will have, relentless and to the end!
You may break our walls, but our hearts and our faith in the line of Selamawi — his true line — will never yield.
You have convinced us of Lord Ketema's virtue. We shall yield to him our fealty, upon the Spear of Selamawi, and be united.
By this Spear and the blood of those who ruled by it will our oath stand. Bring it to our Emperor.
There is wisdom in you, friend. Go, tell your master that Angereb will no longer bow to his whims, but be free!
You were long in returning. I hope it is for good reason, and that you found the Spear.
Pestilent curr! How very like Ketema to ally with bloodthirsty beasts!
You are not the first to hound our walls. If you do it again, we will be ready to strike you down!
So this is the person Ketema sent? And he thinks they will be worthy of the great Yetbarok's palace?
His apartments overlooked the palace ruins, as I recall. Look to the upper floors.
This excavation is none of our business. Dig away if you wish, but we need our workers elsewhere.
So, you return to Angereb.
Be strong.
This is Waha Desher? This... wasteland? Very well. Let's get on with it.
Ah, yes, we were expecting these. The notes says to ask you to take these crates to Kidusi - if you would?
Ketema's forces burnt the harbour when they invaded. All the registries went up in flames.
We will help, but need compensation for the lands left barren while our men are gone!
Resources are thin; any help you could send would be appreciated.
Is that all? It is enough, but...
This would certainly help us survive, if you could allow it.
This would ensure our stores are full, and our future secure!
An oath given is an oath due. Our workers have boarded your ship; may your search prove fruitful!
It is lonely work, excavation, and I miss my home, but a picture of the Ksar of Waha Desher would help greatly.
Perhaps better I do not think too much of home. I do not wish to be reprimanded for slothful work here.

When we returned, it was buried in earth again. They told us it had always been that way and the heat had made us delirious.
I wasn't there when they pulled it out, I was staring longingly at the picture you gave me.
I wanted a look, but they told me a priestess was examining it. When I returned from my break the stone was back in the earth.
My family must worry. Could I be taken home to Waha Desher? I'm no use here anymore anyway.
I knew it! Must have thought poor Waha Desher folk would not notice, but we are wise in the old lore! You have to confront them!
I fear the trail ends here. Perhaps if we'd investigated earlier? Ah well, surely nothing nefarious.
It seems an eternity since last I saw these shores. How the wind sings... may we disembark?
A familiar place and friendly faces; there is no better medicine. Thank you!
How nice of you to visit! There is something I wish to show you— no, not my leg, it is healing just fine.
If you are interested in the Broken Stone, investigate the Oracle; I saw glyphs very similar there when I was younger.
A dead end, I fear; it could be anywhere in Enbesa, but we made a copy of the glyphs for you just in case.
Perhaps there are answers to be found elsewhere? Rain bless you with guidance.
I do not trust those priests. This old library dig is probably a cover for something more sinister…
The sands swirl up.
What brings you?
I would welcome you better, but even the patient djat has deserted our island.
Waha Desher is old. Some of its beauty yet survives. Follow Abel, he will show you.
The whole of Waha Desher stretches from here, land and lore. Ask your questions, shema, and I will answer.
The Per-Iteru has stood, mysterious, for millenia — our river-temple, old as Enbesa.
When the sun first rose, the gods blessed the island-soil. On that land grew Issehds, eldest and tallest, the memory-tree.
Strangers built this camp long ago. Brought Tall-ships from the north, and many woes, but we remember, as Yara provisions.
The waha water is impure. Long ago there was beauty here, but now it is dust-sullied and scorpion-touched.
Floods no longer grace the waha. Saltbeds pile as the water dries up. As soon will we, like our fathers.
Tis time for guard duty by the Mecher, where Lord Ketema's provisions are stored. I leave you harbour-bound.
Our people know much. Talk to them and learn. If dismayed by our speech, come find me.
I remember tales of the kebeh, bringing water to the waha. A water-womb; life giver. Come, I will tell you.
There was fighting here long ago. Kashtan forces fled, bloodied by Ketema's host, now only ruins, memory-haunted.
A shedyet — a water well! Time clogged and lily logged, but hope for water still!
Barely had the shedyet been found then Ketema sent aid. A lord most trustworthy and care-giving.
The land is no longer used to water. It needs issehds to ward the threat of a wakh, a water-curse.
The issehds of the wasi died long ago, but there may be some on other islands, by deep-waters and cool-waters.
We are close to clearing the last of the rubble. Now comes the time to plant the issehd trees for water-holding.
A desehert no longer! Water flows, life-birthing and tempest-quiet — a miracle!
Ere we celebrate, the wasi of Per-Iteru must be repaired. It is dust-forlorn and poorly.
Work will start presently. We are thankful for your help, ever-stalwart.
We have very little without the Emperor's help. Perhaps some salt we could trade? Abel is wise in such things.
We work to prepare the mecher — warehouse — for trade, but we are resource starved.
We lack one thing for salt trading: seherut.
Our stores are salt-depleted, shema. Let us hope the fields do not barren prove.
Salt for livewood and fresh food — for now, Waha Desher survives. An auspicious start.
We are goods-thin once more, and in need of your generosity.
Pray hurry with your help! Some talk of leaving the island, lest we turn sand-eaters.
The ahku! It seems we will be starvation-safe for some time yet.
Waha Desher is phantom-hallowed and echo-haunted. Too many silent homes; time for us to make a returnless journey.
I gazed upon the pale walls and thatched roofs / And all that answered was silence, and uneasy hooves. Let us go.
Slowly life returns, but there is much to do ere we become a waha once again.
I provide them venison, but the children need iatet — goat milk. Perhaps the priests of Kidusi can spare us some...
The waha is a place of fire-sands and heat-pain. I know no awut who can resist such extremes, but perhaps there is such a breed...
The Ma-hedj certainly seems to be heat-content. A creature sure to be much-beloved!
No, this will not survive in the waha. Look further.
The djat is a holy bird, known for its insect-hunger and beauty. Bring a djat to the Waha, and our hearts would hope-fill.
Release the djat; let its blessed flight fill our dry skies with beauty!
The waha thrives again with soft-flight and moist-life. The ksar will live again!
Only a wise-one could restore the waha and culture-respect. With your help, Waha Desher and the Empire will grow greater.
With the Per-Iteru complete, come days of Mesyt - the feast of praise-giving. We want you as our honour-guest.
Mesyt is a rite of fertility, of life-celebrating. It is the heart of Enbesa, and we would teach you of it.
You have given much, only fair we be heart-generous in return.
As is told in legends, where waters springs so is memory unveiled. These soul-bonds we would give to you, as thanks.
You came to us a shema—stranger— yet learned to listen with heart-mouth and soul-words. You are one of us hamesy.
The season for the Mesyt is nigh— a time of fancy-flight! Did you bring enough so all goes well?
I beg of you, shema! These are not ruins, they are our heart. Our history. There must be some other way!
Waha Desher survives, but in what form? How much soul-loss, merely for our bodies to live on?
A pump? If the Emperor decrees it, of course, we must obey.
Grow indigo? But we cannot eat indigo! What shall we feed upon?
We turned to you for help and got iron-chain and industry in return. Waha Desher survives as a broken land, a soulless people. Tell your Emperor he has won.
The fire station has no access to water! If a fire breaks out, they will not be ready for it...

Janihoy, Janihoy! The goats — they are singing! It is a miracle, a blessing!
