Tomb Raiders

You are alone, seeking the fabled Lost Necropolis. A fable that seems just about credible when eyeing the pale golden shimmer of the windswept dusk from the seat of your camel. Somewhere out there in these wastes, beyond cyclopean basalt pillars, may lie the hoard of kings of old — and its greatest prize, the Vigil of Hor, a statue said to be made from the purest gold and inlaid with countless gems. Your stopover is a busy city on the delta, not far from the supposed site of the tombs. A young woman with an academic demeanour hails you as you cross paths in the national museum. "I have found something," she says, "and seek a responsible person to help the local museum recover it."
Agree to help out of the kindness of your heart.

You recognize the insignia of the prestigious House of Sands university on the young woman's lapel — an erudite scholar, no doubt. Explaining at great length that she cares little for riches and only wishes to see the history of her people returned to this museum, she lays a ragged, age-tarnished map on the delicate table in a musty back office. Strange symbols abound all over it, etched over criss-crossed lines that all lead up to a city facing a jackal's head.
'Assiout, as mentioned in the Book of the Dead. It reads: "Follow the Opener-of-Paths, Anubis — the divine embalmer, who holds the key to Assiout." We need to find where the trail begins!'
A god's followers pray to him at his temple, surely.

It is four days' peaceful ride from the city to the ruined temple of Anubis, further inland. Dark colonnades and intricate half-buried carvings tower silently over you, before you climb a set of elephantine stairs, leading to a colossal figure. Its head is that of a jackal, an unsettling light glimmering in its deep, red-gemmed eyes.
As you bow in deference before the long-dead god, you notice a pale serpent slither out of a crack in the wall beyond. Intrigued, you poke and pry at the stone blocks, until with a sedimented rumble, they give way! A secret cavity beyond reveals a room packed with animal-headed jars — the whole place bedecked with tarnished riches, with scrawling glyphs etched across the walls.
Attempt to decipher the glyphs

'This... this is the Book of the Dead! All of it — all 192 spells and incantations!' The young historian is ecstatic; evidently this is an unprecedented discovery. 'And see here... yes, it's near-complete! It reads "Follow the Opener-of-Paths, Anubis , the divine embalmer; embark through the ocean-of-a-million-years, where no life is allowed , and when the divine star rises from the dark waters, the City of the Dead will unveil itself." She starts scribbling furiously in her notebooks, copying signs and sketching vases, as you ponder this new enigma.
The ocean is the desert, and the divine star the rising sun!

Never mind the scorching days and long, chilly nights — there's precious little time to lose, as the two of you follow Anubis's red gaze to a small ledge beneath a mountain summit.
As your camp rises for a new day in the unknown, you turn to the pale horizon and send up a hesitant prayer. To what, you are unsure, but something answers.
Tall silhouettes flare out of nothingness, delineated by the fragile husky light of dawn: The Lost Necropolis! Dusk-clad pillars, strange pyramids, and arches span fathomless chasms of darkness.
At the centre of it all, casting a pale-green pall over the silent city, stands a mausoleum of godly proportions. Atop the grim entrance, several ominous signs are carved.
Ask the historian to translate the signs

The delight in her eyes at the wonder around her soon fades, replaced by a darker, more fearful mood, as her fingers trace the glyphs, her lips breathlessly shaping the arcane sounds within.
'Here rests Osiris Ounénnefer, by the care of watchful Anubis, until forever is no more and vengeance falls upon his foes. Within lies judgment, without oblivion, and all are his dominion. Come to him with a true heart, and join in the secret feasts of the Duat.'
Ignore the warning.

A long passage slopes down into the earth. Ornate paintings must once have covered every inch of the walls, but now only indecipherable lines and constellations survive — mere memories of what must have been a wondrously complex depiction of the night sky. 'Nout, the dusk-winged' whispers the young scholar, reverently. A narrow chamber lies ahead, empty but for a few scuttling black beetles. The paintings here are in a far greater state of conservation: human bodies with monstrous animal heads, cosmically vast landscapes and pagan offerings to name but a few.
Two lower passages head east and west into the darkness, below a set of arches covered in symbols.
Enter the passage marked <custom-entity tag="jackal_128px"/> <custom-entity tag="water_128px"/> <custom-entity tag="sunnny_128px"/>

She was but a few paces ahead of you, but all of a sudden the scholar has vanished! Perhaps something awful befell her, or perhaps... this is indeed the correct path, and she no longer has use of you. Ahead is a low-ceilinged hall surrounded by ornate dusky pillars. A sealed door, unadorned and heavy, is carved into the opposing wall. All around it stretches a masterfully painted scene: a set of giant scales, one bearing a beating heart, the other a feather. Anthropomorphic beasts take careful note of the proceedings while a ghastly, fiendish monster snaps at the heels of a line of terrified figures. As you look around, a strange and distant howling startles you. A hidden door is very slightly ajar, betrayed by the wind blowing over its threshold.
Stand the trial. Entrust your fate to Anubis.

A long silence fills the chamber, as your torch softly sputters out. The darkness comes quickly, and then.. the sound of softly lapping water near your feet. Something — several somethings — weave silkily between your toes — unseen monsters stalking, sensing, lurking...
You mutter in breathless prayer. Unexpectedly, perhaps your humility, your calm, has a positive effect. As uncannily as it came, the water seeps away, taking the strange entities with it. The path ahead is clear.
Press forward

Not daring to touch the door, you slip through the crack. The new chamber is colossal — easily tall enough to fit an entire temple inside. Long stone grooves trace the sides, filled with mummified animals, and multitudinous basins brimming with pale gold and jewellery. But despite the splendour, you have eyes for only one thing: a pyramid of black stone, carved with a set of steep stairs and bearing a chalk-white crown. Atop the pyramid, on an altar of midnight amber, stands the fabled Statue of Hor —He of the Thousand Thrones, Commiserer of the Penitent and Humble, and Purger of the Unworthy — there for the taking!
Wrap it up carefully and take it.

Perhaps Anubis deems you worthy. Perhaps he slumbers until "forever" sunders, or perhaps... he has seen the truth of your heart.
The statue is weighty, but easily removed from its pedestal. Uneasy at the silence and gloom, you make a hasty retreat out of the chamber, half-convinced that something stirs in the deep chasms all around. As you pull the Door of Judgement precautiously shut behind you, you notice a wan, lifeless face, shining out from the darkness beyond — the young scholar! Something is closing in upon her, like the night, claiming her for itself!

Despite this last, grizzly vision, you yourself are free of the tomb. And what's this? The Effigy of Hor is in your hands!
Leave the statue and plunder only the riches that surround it.

You decide to leave the pyramid untouched, but take whatever other riches you can from the chamber. Gold, silver, gems and jewellery of the most exquisite craftsmanship are shoved into pockets — a treasure-trove of kingly proportions!
As you make your difficult way back to the sands far above, you notice a pale, unblinking face in one of the deep trenches: the young historian. You go to recover her body, but something — a darkness — slithers over her, and she is gone.
You find yourself strangely relieved to have left the statue alone. The tale is wondrous enough for twenty fireside already — and who knows? Perhaps one day you will walk the streets of the Necropolis again...
Something lurks down there. A prize like no other.

You hold your pistol at the ready, and cross the threshold quietly. Water laps at your feet, accompanied by the sound of distant bubbling — crocodiles, you suspect. How do they survive down here? You may be about to find out. The predators slink through the water towards you — you need to act fast.
A crackle of shots is soon followed by the warm smell of blood welling into the water. After a brief moment to catch your breath, you strike a match, the flickering glow only briefly lighting the floating corpses of two colossal beasts — crocodiles of unholy proportions, their scales pale as bone. The crimson waters reassure you, however: if it bleeds, it can be slain.
Forge ahead

A high chamber stretches into the darkness around a basalt pyramid. At the pyramid's bone-white crown is a pedestal, bearing the fabled Statue of Hor. Standing before it is the historian. She seems entranced, her fingers inches from the statue's exquisite golden limbs. Her mutterings echo strangely, 'At last, they will know... Such opportunities... Never want for anything again...' Something draws your attention at the foot of the pyramid: slithering there, a patch of restless, and unworldly darkness.
The historian's hand reaches out towards the statue.
Run and grab the effigy from her.

You bound stupidly towards her, crying for her to beware, but billowing tendrils of mist wrap around her, as dark, many-coloured fumes spew from deep grooves around the pyramid's base. You plunge forward through the mists. It feels just like a sandstorm — like minuscule shards of glass tearing at you. A scream fills the chamber, inhuman and terrified — yours, hers, or something else. Rumbling shakes the ground. A chorus of ear-shattering whispers peels at your skin. Something within you breaks. Dissolves. Your eyes burn with a blazing white halo — a silhouette, great wings. The promise of wrath.

You wake up. Pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.
It's her prize now. Turn away.

Grim whispers echo strangely from the shadowy confines of the chamber. A swirling, cloying sensation almost knocks you over as something wakes. The historian's mutterings grow louder, deafeningly louder — painfully louder. A resounding crack follows, as if bones were shattered.
Then silence.

When your eyes open, the chamber is empty. The light from your torches flickers dully on the statue. Sand — great pyramids of bleak sand — piles high against the chamber walls. The historian is nowhere to be seen. Deciding it best not to linger, you wrap the statue carefully and respectfully before retreating gleefully out of the necropolis.
Enter the passage marked <custom-entity tag="jackal_128px"/> <custom-entity tag="desert_128px"/> <custom-entity tag="star_128px"/>

A trap! No sooner had you crossed the threshold than the door groaned shut, sprung by some age-old mechanism under your step. You pummel against it, but in vain. The path ahead leads to a minuscule chamber, barely tall enough for you to stand in. Slits in the walls point to where air vents must have been, yet now they lie utterly sealed. The entire place reeks with a husky, brittle air.
You start to feel light-headed — surely the air hasn't already run out? Figures on the walls appear to dance eerily in the torchlight. Suddenly, your torch flares out. You rasp for breath, and then — darkness, and the silence of the Necropolis.

You wake up. Pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.
Ancient curses are no trifles. Abandon the Necropolis.

There are powers beyond the reckoning of even the wise. Who knows what lies in the sandswept valley and tomb? Better to let the Lord of the Dead rest unperturbed.
As you make your troubled way back up the mountain, a hawk swoops mere feet away from your shoulder, startling you. As it shoots back up into the sky, merely a dark speck against the morning sun, you spy something in the sands by your feet: a cluster of tablets, joined with ancient reeds and covered in script — a priceless treasure in its own right. A gift, perhaps? Or a token of gratitude? Who knows what other mysteries slumber, no more than half-dead, beneath the sands of this strange land.
The ocean is the night sky, and the divine star the North star!

As soon as Polaris is seen shimmering in the sky you head off into the desert cold. Despite your best efforts, sleep soon takes hold, and you doze off as your camel paces unerringly forward in the night.
The next day, you're met with a glorious sight: a pyramid, sun-tanned and immense, blazing with aurorean light on the horizon! For four millennia — perhaps more — it's stood a quiet vigil over communities and travellers, untouched by the passage of time. Even the sands seem to hold still. You may not have found the Lost Necropolis, but you are safe. The smiling historian bids you farewell, and disappears into the slow bustle of the market.
Far above, golden-red in the light of the new day, a hawk glides down to a quiet roost atop the pyramid's alabaster peak.
Search the cavity for clues...

A glance is enough for the historian to tell you this alcove was a preparation room used in the mummification process. She warns you not to open the sealed jars, for your own sake. Beneath a mixture of dust and sand you find a scroll — a papyrus, relatively intact despite its age. You unroll it gingerly, finding it to be several feet long and covered with countless figures and signs. The historian points to a series of symbols: 'Here, the "Way of the King's Jackal"'.
It seems to be a procession: first the body is interred, and then at dawn, a series of offerings are made on a mountaintop — it's a journey of some sort, with the body in an oddly shaped sarcophagus, before undergoing a ritual of mummification?
You must have read it incorrectly. Re-examine the papyrus

On second glance, it seems obvious this text must be deciphered from right to left. It details a journey, perhaps not as metaphorical as you might have thought.
The opportunity is too great to miss: you hire a pair of camels, and prepare to ride across the desert.
Several days' journey brings you to a high mountaintop.
As the camp rises for a new day, suddenly a set of tall silhouettes flare out of nothingness, delineated by the fragile husky light of dawn: a vast necropolis, scattered with dusk-clad pillars and strange pyramids.
At the centre of it all stands a mausoleum of godly proportions. Atop the grim entrance, several ominous signs are carved.
Only the mummified can enter. Perhaps the jars will help?
Only the dead can find the Necropolis. Abandon your hunt.

A grave mistake. Taking one of the jars seems to have activated a hidden mechanism! You leap out just in time — a heavy slab of sand-gold stone slamming down onto the tiles where only a second ago your ankle had lain.
Doused by this unfortunate brush with a gruesome fate, you decide it is best to leave this place and its secrets to the desert. Some tales are best forgotten, and besides: who ever would believe you?
...No. Better to choose present riches than the promise of unseen gold.

There is something strange about the way the jars are slightly out of order — it's probably best not to disturb anything. There are plenty of other riches to choose from in the small chamber, anyway — bracelets, rings and diadems galore. Plenty enough to ensure a triumphant return back to ship. Even small trinkets like these will be sure to draw much wonder and praise!

The ruins of Assiout are barely visible under a shroud of sand and thorn-riddled shrubs. After two days of covering your faces from the scorching winds, you have happened upon a tall statue — probably one of the local divinities. It is unmarred by neither time nor wind, and seems eerily lifelike. Yet no sooner has that thought crossed your mind than you hear a sudden growl, low and threatening, seemingly disembodied. Surely not the statue...? As you contemplate retreating from these weird grounds, you sense movement behind the statue. Three black and gold jackals tread silently out from its shadow, shaking sand off their shoulders. Unnerved by their ghostly footfall, you turn to the statue; you could swear it is glaring down at you in judgement.
Whisper to the historian that she should create a diversion.

She is visibly terrified, and resorts to desperation. Stooping to pick up a fragment of the statue's broken pedestal, she hurls it at the brutes before breaking off into the ruins! One of the jackals yelps in pain as the rock strikes it's foreleg, and the trio of dogs give chase to the unfortunate girl. You will never know what becomes of her. As soon as they've left, you sneak out like a coward and examine the place from whence the creatures once came. After some excavating, your efforts uncover a crack in the tiles of a sand-clad set of stairs. A secret cavity beyond reveals a room packed with animal-headed jars — the whole place bedecked with tarnished riches, with scrawling glyphs etched across the walls.
(Risky) Attack the beasts

A quick, dextrous shot cripples one of the beasts' legs, sending its allies squealing. A further blow with the butt of your rifle saves the wounded animal from further suffering. Searching nearby, you note scuffs in the dust at the base of one of the columns, as if it has been moved. You give it a gentle push and sure enough it swings apart on a hinge, revealing a set of stone stairs in the floor.
Gingerly, you investigate the obscure cavity below. Narrow beams of sunlight from above reveal many animal-headed jars, and a room bedecked with tarnished riches, with scrawling glyphs etched across the walls.

You steady your rifle to take a shot but one of the brutes leaps at your arm, latching on with immense strength, while its companion bounds up and down on the spot, cackling maniacally. You attempt to push the beast off, but the weight of it sends you toppling to the floor.
The last thing you see is the creature's strangely calm face, gazing at the statue, as though its kill were some manner of offering... Your mind and vision race. Red eyes bleed gemstones in their thousands. A great feather held in a hand of shadow tickles you beyond suffering.

You wake up, pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.
Attempt to flee over the uneven terrain.

From your nervous glances, you're just about able to piece together a rough impression of the temple's structure. Hurling a pebble at the lead dog, you leap over a nearby wall, tearing through the roofless colonnade beyond with the creatures hot on your heels. You feel a set of fangs snap at thin air mere inches from your calf as you reach for a ledge and effortlessly swing over it.
Suddenly, the howling and yelping stops. After a short time, you survey the ruin. There's no sign of the creatures, but the thought they may reappear plagues your investigations. You give up on finding the Lost Necropolis, and return to sea to rejoin your crew. You hesitate, but decide it best to not let them know the strange names and words you believe you heard beneath the jackals' cries.

A fool's hope. The beasts know every passage, every shadow, and every secret of the sands. You weave through the temple ruin as best you can, but the jackals ignore every attempt to throw them off the trail. You are cornered, in a nook between two closed rooms, with no visible egress.
You lunge at one of the canines, but it hops aside, its manic laughter ringing insultingly in your ears, before it leaps and latches onto your upper arm. Its companions take the cue and bound into you too, sending you sprawling, as they close their fuming maws on your throat. Your mind and vision race. Red eyes bleed gemstones in their thousands. A great feather held in a hand of shadow tickles you beyond suffering.

You wake up, pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.
Examining the map should reveal the trail.

Hardly a challenge for a seasoned navigator. The trail points to an oasis at a crossroad between two mountainous hinterlands, where — legend has it — one of the entrances to the underworld lies, below the water.
Dark orange cliffs cast a soothing shadow over the oasis, accompanied by the joyous din of travelling merchants, wanderers and treasure-seekers. You look up to a high cliff, and can't help but wonder where a death-defying leap into the water would take you.
Take a leap of faith into the water.

You nimbly climb the burning rock. You take a sharp breath as you step to the edge of the cliff — then air rushes around you as you fall.
You zip into the cerulean waters below with barely a splash, fearlessly avoiding a series of cruel spurs that jut up from the shallows. As you open your eyes, a strong current drags you through a series of algae-clad passages, before a series of weird lights invite you to push upwards into an airhole. Your faith is rewarded. You find yourself in a shallow chamber, painted with a once beautiful depiction — a humble reed raft carrying the sun out of the rippling waters, and into the star-dotted sky. Two dark passageways lead further into the stone.
Ask the historian for her advice.

She spits water from her mouth, and clears her nose. Her usually quiet demeanour is overcome by passion as she examines the painting. 'They say the raft holding the sun travels between the lands of the living and the dead. See? Here, the raft emerges triumphant from the maternal waters. And there darkness takes it, and the journey underground begins. Do you see? The Land of the Dead, the Necropolis... they are one and the same! We must follow the journey as was ordained: westward, into the evening!'
Enter the corridor where the raft dives into the waters
Enter the corridor where the raft emerges from the waters
The raft dives into the water beside the left door, just as you dove to get here.

Interminable galleries wind across and over each other, spanning fathomless pits on spindly natural bridges. For hours you walk, with no sign of relief until — light! You scramble and dig, extricating yourselves until you come to stand on a small ledge above an incredible sight: a vast necropolis, scattered with dusk-clad pillars, strange pyramids, and cyclopean arches spanning fathomless chasms of darkness.
At the centre of it all, casting a shadowy pall over the city, stands a mausoleum of godly proportions. Atop the grim entrance, several ominous signs are carved.
As you rose from the water, so too does the raft by the right-hand door.

After some fumbling in the dark the passage starts to slope upwards. It is some time, however, before you come to a thin crack in the wall. You tear eagerly at the crevice, feeling it crumble easily under your hands. As you slip out, an ominous rumble echoes through the passage as it collapses behind you. Trapped! Before you, the quietly frothing waters of a hidden fountain, kept from human eyes for millennia, welcome you. Perhaps this is what the legends truly meant — life in the most improbable of places? You fade slowly...

You wake up. Pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.

The ascent is steeper than you had anticipated, and the sheer drop equally intimidating. You stare down at the waters, and a strange faintness comes into your heart. Your breath deserts you, as trembling seizes your limbs. The rocks surrounding the basin far, far below seem jagged and cruel, and you can almost hear them calling to you, yearning for a taste of your flesh, of your marrow.
Some time later, you find yourself struggling back down the cliffside. Stopping to take a drink from the waters, you realise how tired you feel, and decide it probably best if you rejoin the rest of the expedition.
Leap? From there? That would be madness!

You turn regretfully from the shimmering waters and journey back to reconvene with the rest of the expedition. They feel none of your disappointment at not having found the Lost Necropolis, and nor does it mar their enthusiasm when hearing of the many wonders and beauties of your journey, however fruitless it may have been.

The task is more arduous than it seems. After much befuddlement, you manage to find a point of convergence somewhere in the distant desert hinterlands. Gathering supplies, you hastily head into the desert, braving the scorching heat and dismally chilly nights in your quest for long-lost reward.
As you head further into the dunes however, you are swiftly sobered by the realisation that you may already be hopelessly and irretrievably lost, for how can you tell one dune from another in an endless sea of sand?
(Risky) Attempt to find an oasis in the desert.

No choice but to trust the instinct of the king of the desert. Hopefully, the camel will know the way to a nearby oasis. If not...
As soon as the beast's bridle is unlatched it darts across the sand, vanishing beyond cresting dunes at a steady amble as you rush to follow.
Fortune favours you! After some running and considerable cursing, you come to the bustling oasis of Awis, a natural spring nestled at a crossroads near some dark crimson mountains. Legend has it the waters hide a gateway to the Lands of the Dead. Perhaps hope is not yet entirely lost! It would only take a short climb, then a long, steep dive...

The land is harsh and unforgiving. There is little shade to be found during the day, when the searing rays of the sun glare down disapprovingly on you, and what shade there is turns out not to be safe. Exhausted, you fall asleep under an overhanging rock, only to awake to a sharp pain in your neck — two telltale puncture holes. The young historian is nowhere to be found. You wonder if the Lord of Sands will have mercy on you, however unlikely it may seem — he is not known for being merciful.

You wake up. Pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. The venom of an asp has taken you to the edge and back again.
Look to the sea, and the north. Let Polaris guide you.

The desert sky at night has a soothing, calming quality. Though the stars are strange and foreign, and many familiar constellations seem disconcertingly twisted, you chart a rough cartography of the skies as they correspond to the desert before you.
It is just a few days before you once again reach the desert's edge, and the familiar sights of a land where thirst can easily be quenched, and rest had for a nominal fee — yet it will be with no small pride that you will recount your strange experience among the dunes to the rest of the expedition.

The stars are strange and contrary. The familiar landmarks of the heavens seem oddly absent, as you scan the night looking for anything that might help you get your bearings. It seems something does not want you to find a way out of the desert. You steel forward to the best of your ability, charting vague patterns and routes across increasingly desiccated paper, but every passing day drives you closer to death and insanity. Perhaps a cautionary tale will be told of your and the young archaeologists' disappearance.

You wake up. Pale and dizzy beneath a great ceiling fan in a sweltering hotel room. It seems it was a bout of cholera that took you to the edge and back again.

Her scepticism shows plainly on her face. Grave robbers are found often in these lands, and doubtless she counts you among their number. You press her for support, arguing your good faith, but it only serves to distress her further. She holds the precious map to her chest tightly, fear in her eyes, and bolts into a nearby array of drapes, calling for help as she disappears amid the colourful weaves.
Before you can protest you innocence, several burly, sour-faced guards gather around you threateningly.
Claim the woman is the real thief.

The guards blanch. 'A grave robber, her? But she is one of the scholars studying at the House of Sands! If she is selling our heritage...' The guard pales at the implications, then streaks off into the streets furiously after the young woman.
Reach the House Of Sands before the guards

Fortunately, you sighted the House of Sands as you passed it by. You tread a swift path through the crowd towards its sun-dressed pinnacles, hoping the guards will be delayed long enough for you to get there first.
As you round a narrow alley onto the ornate steps leading to the entrance hall, you see the young scholar heading inside with a troubled look on her face.
Pulling her aside into a discrete alcove, despite her protestations, you urgently explain that rogues masquerading as guards are after her!
Offer to help her find the Necropolis before the map is confiscated.
Offer to take the map off her hands to draw the guards' attention

The city is a sprawling metropolis, and the House Of Sands could be anywhere. You try cobbling together information from broken conversations and fragments of your journey up until now, but to no avail.
You are dismayed to find that you have traced a path right back to the harbour where your ship berths — and where a mighty company of guards awaits. Despite your crew's protestations, they drag you off in chains, and it is abundantly clear — despite the language barrier — that they have no intention to release you for months.If the expedition is to continue, it will be beset by a heavy delay.
Retreat and rejoin your expedition.

The guards burst into scornful laughter. 'A respected scholar, a thief? You would need to be a better liar than even the sly jackal to make anyone believe that, stranger.' With a shimmer of death, blades are drawn. 'There is but one punishment for those who attempt to steal our history from under us.' It is from out of nowhere that your captain appears. "This... individual," he eyes you wearily, "is under the protection of Her Majesty the Queen. She will ensure they are brought to trial." Eventually, the local guards relent and turn heel. Whether they were convinced by the eloquence of your captain — or your crew, lurking daggers-drawn in the shadows — it matters not. You doubt your little excursion will go down well back aboard ship.

Whatever unfortunate fate awaits the young researcher, you cannot help but feel it will be her just deserts. Had she accepted your offer, you might both be spying the golden pillars of the Necropolis by now...
Best not to dwell on it though; doubtless once the guard has questioned her, he will come looking for you. Better for all if they find you long gone.
(Risky) Take no chances: shoot them first!

The guards are still eyeing you suspiciously when you loose fire from the hip, drawing your pistols before stealing the rifles from the fallen. As bystanders scream and run for cover, you make out the figure of the young scholar moving towards a side-alley. You bring rifle to elbow and fire one clean, precise warning shot over her shoulder.
She freezes, then turns with slow reluctance to face you.
Her choice, join you... or die.

'Hardly much of a choice, is it?' She scowls angrily at you. 'Very well — but know that I would rather die than see a thief lay hands on the statue.'
Barely trying to hide her distaste for you and your crew, she leads you quickly away from the chaos and into a low house, where she lays a ragged, age-tarnished map over a three-legged table. Strange symbols abound all over it, etched over criss-crossed lines that all lead up to a city facing a jackal's head.
'Assiout, as mentioned in the Book of the Dead. It reads: "Follow the Opener-of-Paths, Anubis — the divine embalmer, who holds the key to Assiout." We need to find where the trail begins!'
Tell her you'll take the map, even if it's from her cold dead hands.

Eyes blazing with hatred, she hands you the map before bolting off down the alley. Not bothering to follow, you quickly retreat to a discreet tea-house some way off and examine your prize. The map is ragged and age-tarnished, but readable. Strange symbols abound all over it, etched over criss-crossing lines that all lead up to a city facing a jackal's head.
A note, tied to the parchment with dry reeds, states "Assiout, as mentioned in the Book of the Dead. Follow the Opener-of-Paths, Anubis — the divine embalmer, who holds the key." Cryptic, certainly, but not completely unintelligible.
Release her under oath of silence and retreat to your ship.

Time is against you and you have little time to exact more information from her before inquiries about the shooting trace their way back to your ship.
Keeping your head stooped and your hat brim low, you thread a circuitous route back to the harbour upon the delta, and order the sails be let loose immediately.

A flash of searing pain causes you to crumple to the swirling ochre dust before you can even react. As your senses fade, you hear bystanders scatter fearfully as the guards fire a few celebratory shots into the air. It is much later that you hear, very softly, the familiar voice of the captain. "This... individual," you sense he is eyeing you wearily, "is under the protection of Her Majesty the Queen. She will ensure they are brought to trial." You drift back to sleep, and awake two days later to find yourself back at sea, your wounds treated. From the lukewarm reception, you sense your little excursion has not gone down well with the rest of the expedition.
Surrender to the guards

No map is worth dying for. Crestfallen, you find yourself clapped in irons and dragged off to a small cell, nestled in a ledge in one of the citadel's walls, some miles off from the city. When the sentence of several weeks is made known to you, you can take comfort only in the knowledge that it is but a few weeks of watery slop and bedding down in your own filth stands between you and being allowed to return to your ship, rather than months.
Decline, then secretly follow her in the hopes of finding the treasure.

"Well, it's been lovely meeting you — good day!" you say, before finding a secluded corner from which you can stalk her. Noting that your foreign garb will attract a great deal of attention, you nab a big hat and try to blend in to the living extravaganza that is the city. The deceit works wonders, and all manner of sellers, merchants and grifters brush past you like a nobody. The historian leads you to a sprawling complex of pillared halls: the great library of the House of Sands!
You wait for her near a heavily ornamented pilaster, before strong-arming her into a nearby empty alley as she passes by.
"Help me find the treasure!"
"Hand me the map, or else..."

Your attempts at discretion are hampered by your general ineptitude. It is not long before she notices you following her, and leads you through a tortuous maze of blind passages, right into the hands of a troop of guards! Before you can react, she whispers something to them under her breath and darts off into a side alley, as some of the soldiers draw their weapons and advance towards you.
Give up on the promise of treasure and return to the ship.

A grey feeling settles upon you as you give the order to unfurl and heave. The rigging cracks taut and sails fill to bursting with crisp winds, yet even the fresh breeze of the tide can do little to wash away the ambient morosity. You turn restlessly back, gazing at the distant shorelines to what you can still see beyond, tantalisingly out of reach: the promise of the adventure of a lifetime.
Continue your journey
You are now on board of your ship. Where do you want to go next?
Blessed Rains

Wide, sun-touched lands stretch out before you, long pale grass glittering with the night’s rain while a scattering of trees provides occasional shade from the already warm orange sun.
Unseen amongst the dense, matted grass, multitudinous creatures awake to the dawning day, nattering away gaily as the savannah comes to life.
A low dell not a mile away hides a blossoming waterhole, where numerous strange and foreign beasts are gathering before the day’s heat truly begins, nestled in the shadows of a set of monolithic spurs, looming high above the plains — surely with views worthy of a king!
Scale the spurs for a bird’s eye view of the savannah

The climb is arduous and long, but your topmen trace a forgeable path for the other sailors, using thick ropes and residues of flour hastily brought over from the camp. At last, you reach the topmost spur — a long slab of ochre red stone, worn by countless rainfalls and storms.

Endless wildlands stretch below you, dust-coloured and windswept. In the distance, rainclouds swirl over a patch of darkness, and a deep golden hush falls over the land, broken only by the slow ambling of strange, tall-collared distant animals. A low threatening growl suddenly echoes behind you, and you turn to face lions, territorially baring their fangs at your crew. You have trespassed upon pride land.
Shoot the leading male

One gunman shoulders his rifle and takes careful aim at a particularly large male, while the rest of your crew strive to stay as motionless as possible.
The shot echoes deafeningly against the surrounding boulders, and sends a threatening ripple over the lands below.
Cowed by the roar of the rifle and the sight of their pridemate slumping lifeless to the ground, the other lions slowly back away before turning tail and disappearing into the rocks overhead.

Whether owing to precipitousness or shoddy marksmanship, the shot misses the great creature by several feet.
Panicked, the would be hunter fumbles with the rifle’s lock, but an ominous crack signals the weapon’s reluctance to further use.
The lions take a slow step towards your huddled crew, hunger and wrath in their glare.
‘Someone hold them back!’ cries a sailor, before inching towards the first stone in the long series to climb back to the plains.
Order your two strongest to intimidate the beasts

Two colossi, nicknamed Ajax and Hercules by your ship’s erudite skipper, step forward.
One of them roars a challenge to the assembled felines, startling them a few steps back into the shadow of the overhanging spur, while the rest of you swiftly start the descent.
As the last of your men slip over the ledge, a low, feral snarl is heard some way overhead. A host of lions have emerged from various crevices and alcoves around Ajax and Hercules — a pride of such size that there is nothing even a hundred men might do to fend them off.
A burst of raucous song comes over the ledge in Ajax’s baritone, and the very next second you see Hercules jump to meet you.'Run!' he says.

Two burly southerners, thick-necked and ruddy, step forward hesitantly while the rest of your crew slip as discreetly as possible over the ledge and onto the path back to the savannah.
There is a long-minute’s hushed, precipitous silence, before you hear whispers of quiet, nervous conversation up above, followed by an ear-shattering shriek.
One of the men topples over the ledge, plummeting to the distant grassland, as the other becomes the first of many harried by cruel claws and sharp fangs in a fraught and fearful descent.
Every man for himself!

Years of experience are easily forgotten in the face of mortal peril. Your sailors push and pull at each other to be first to descend onto the lower ledges, and away from the rampant cats.
One man stumbles and falls with a sickening crack onto the stone, blood soon clotting his hair and pooling on the dark red rock.
The smell of blood inflames the lions, and what reservations they had are forgotten, pouncing upon the stragglers, rending them to pieces. Pride's rock is a name whose irony will not be lost on your expedition.
Throw the cabin boy to the lions

The captain knows he must do what is right. Do the lives of the many not outweigh the lives of the few — and are sturdy, aged hands not valued more in a storm than those of a youngling?
Yet the cabin boy’s wan, stricken face haunts him long after the garbled, bloodied crying — horrifyingly close, despite the distance — falls silent, at the claws of a merciful beast. None of your crew know untroubled sleep for many a week.
Intimidate the beasts with loud noises and gestures

Acting as one, your crew start stamping the ground rhythmically, battering the stone with such force that it trembles while fiercely waving their arms in large circles, concealing their terror as best they can.
Startled, the lions slowly edge backwards, their low growls no longer threatening but worried, and promptly disband, gracefully bounding up among the stunted prickly bushes where their den must be hidden.
Corner the den and smoke the beasts in

Dry wood and kindle abound despite recent rainfalls, and a series of short pyres are built around the lair’s entrance. Soon, bright flames cast deep shadows far back into the cave.
Rain-soaked grass and leaves are thrown onto the fires, spurting voluminous columns of creamy grey smoke.
There is a moment’s silence as the fumes invade the lair, before a powerful shape leaps through the haze — only to be caught by those lying in wait.
The lion roars its fury and anguish, to no avail, and your crew quickly return to camp, triumphantly bragging about their prize.

Finding kindle dry enough to start a fire proves difficult atop pride’s rock, especially with recent rains. You struggle to light small piles of damp grass and twigs, but your efforts only attract the lions’ attention. A female leaps toward a man struggling with a tinder box.
He ducks backward, narrowly avoiding a killing blow, only for blood to spurt to the ground as a ghastly tear appears in his jaw, his teeth visible through the wound. Your crew take cover behind what small, flickering torches they've managed to light, and start the achingly slow descent back to the plains, with their gored companion in tow.
Retreat safely back to camp

Preferring to err on the side of safety, your captain orders a swift retreat down the spur, while the pride is cowed and cautious.
Evening finds you all huddled around the campfire, exaggeratedly recounting the encounter with the pride to those sailors who had stayed behind.
A sudden cry of wild dogs is heard distantly in the night, and you wonder at the beauty and majesty of this foreign land, strangely satisfied with the bloodlessness of your expedition.

The pride is undeterred by your efforts to shout and stomp them away. Ignoring the increasingly high-pitched cries sallying from your crew, they prowl up to the edge of the overhanging slab, preparing to pounce. You look around at your crew, but the expedition up the spur seemed so harmless that none of them brought a rifle— save one lean and dark-faced young woman, who carries a narrow-barreled pistol model from overseas at her side. You feel entirely comfortable resting your odds of survival upon that. Cornering the lions when they land to subdue them might be easier, or repelling them with a hail of rocks?
Prepare to corner them when they land

You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.

One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
Order the woman to shoot, and hope that the gun works

Her face breaks into a dark grin as she draws the pistol to her hip with lightning speed. Sunlight glares off the silvery metal as rapid-fire shots flare from the muzzle with deadly precision and speed.
There is a moment's unbelieving, bated silence as four lions crumble to the dust, blood oozing from the small round wounds in their foreheads.
The woman smiles, satisfied, before returning her pistol to its holster with a flourish. A roar of whoops and cheers rises from your crew, and as they wend their way down from the spur, they crowd the sharpshooter to hear of her pistol — the last of the bolt six-shooters — and already, the legend of the woman who drew faster than her own shadow spreads like wildfire.

She draws the weapon with great haste, however, only one of the six rapid-fire shots hits its target. The lion roars, its mane matted by fast-flowing blood, while its companions furiously pounce on the young woman. Powerful jaws close with a sickening crack on her skull, bursting it open in a splatter of gore which sends surrounding sailors reeling and vomiting.
A famished growl is heard from above, before a newly woken group of slavering beasts jumps into the fray, rending with teeth and claw as your crew run for their lives.
Throw a volley of stones at them

You stoop hurriedly to grab a series of sharp rocks, pelting them towards the approaching creatures. They back away without breaking eye contact, clearly weathering the storm until there comes a chance to resume their hunt. Some issue low growls as the rocks hit their flanks, but most seem unworried.
Distract them with food
Much rather their stomachs be filled with this food than with you
Accept
Cancel

Some of your crew weep to see vital supplies tossed to the beasts, but all agree that they would rather lose food than become food.
The offering pacifies the pride long enough for your sailors to head quickly back down the spur — a terrifying encounter, certainly, but one that is sure to reward them with many an admiring drink in the pub back home.

You had expected to be back at camp by noon, and consequently brought very little food along — hardly enough to placate the hungering lions. Perhaps it is merely your imagination, but you think you hear a low rumbling run through the dark rock, as beasts from all corners draw threateningly closer.
Head to the waterhole

Your party edges stealthily through the high grass towards the hidden waterhole. As they reach a ledge where soft soil has fallen into the muddy water below, they gasp in wonder at the teeming life gathered here. Scores of creatures huddle by the water — tall-necked giraffes spread their legs awkwardly to lean down and lap the surface, while nervous meerkats and contemptuous gnus eye the waters warily — and with the suspicious profile of those drifting logs, it's not without reason.
Suddenly, the ground shakes. You wheel about to see a manifestly infuriated rhinoceros charging at your company!
Dodge the charge

Your crew scatter as one tall woman, made lean by years of working in the rigging, steps up out of the grass to face the charging beast. She straightens proudly, defiance flashing in her eyes, and waits for the inevitable blow.
At the last instant, she steps gracefully aside, sending the beast hurtling into the thick tree behind her. Stunned by the impact, the rhinoceros staggers slightly, shaking its head to extricate its horn from the torn flesh of the tree.
Attempt to capture it

Several sailors nimbly tie the creature’s legs together, carefully avoiding its thrashing head. The rhinoceros struggles against the binding, kicking out violently, but your men tug on the ropes and the beast comes crashing down on its side, motionless but fuming.
It takes considerable effort to drag it back to camp, but the dumbfounded look on the rest of the crew’s face is worth every bead of sweat.

By the time ropes are brought out to secure it, the rhinoceros has already struggled free of the tree and rounds furiously at the oncoming sailors. They attempt as best they can to bind its legs, dancing dangerously in and out of a flurry of rearing and kicking, but the massive creature proves impossible to subdue, and it's not long before it surges out of the encirclement, thundering off into the savannah, much to your crew’s disappointment.
Flee

A horde of gnus stampede past your crew, evidently alarmed by the thunderous attack of the rhinoceros, separating you from the beast.
Leaping upon the opportunity to escape the maddened creature and its threatening bulk, you promptly retreat back to camp, thrilled by your escape — and the impressively dramatic skills of the woman who deceived the rhinoceros.

Your captain singles out a sailor renowned for manoeuvring rigging in heavy storms, and orders him to lure the beast into a nearby tree.
The man stands nervously, his terror evident as the rhinoceros bowls right into his path. He tries to lurch aside at the last minute, only to be skewered by the beast’s impressive nasal horn.
A terrified roar rises from the nearby waterhole as the gathered animals sense the gore and panic, their anxiety soon turning into a stampede! The few crew members that do escape the terror-stricken beasts will be forever traumatised.
Climb up nearby trees

Years of seamanship, climbing the rigging of a moving, storm-tossed ship, makes scaling low, twisted trees only a minor challenge.
The rhinoceros tromps to a halt when it realises its quarry has vanished, looking around with dull, rage-shot eyes before retreating into the sun-worn high grass.
As the sailors ease down from their hiding places, they dejectedly realise that the creature’s tonitruous charge has chased all the animals from the waterhole, and there is naught left to do but retreat back to camp.

The crew scramble for low branches and scalable knots in the thick, tortuous trunks of the surrounding trees. Most find easy purchase and disappear into the dense foliage, but a few are left attempting to scale a young silver-barked tree; supple and tall, but clearly unable to bear all their weight. They tussle for a foothold as the rumble of the rhinoceros’s charge grows nearer.
A third man attempts to hoist himself up, but his companions push him roughly, only to see the chap tumble into the beast's charge.
Satisfied that it has repelled its attackers, the animal leaves, but only after consciously trampling the body in full sight of every crew member, a scene that will haunt them until their dying days.
Stay still and silent

It is well known among naturalists that rhinoceroses have limited vision, and the information is quickly doled out to your crew in whispers. Taking great care to avoid sudden movements, all move out of the creature’s immediate path and adopt resolute stillness.
The beast grinds to a halt when it realises its foes have vanished. It tosses and turns its voluminous head, eyeing the high undergrowth for any sign of life.
After a long, breathy moment of indecision, it finally turns away and tromps down to the waterhole, to take in long, slow draughts of water.

Your attempts to convince the sailors to stay motionless would have been more efficient had four thousand pounds of armoured, horn-touting, furious beast not been hurtling towards them. One lad, seeing the beast drawing ever nearer, gives in to fear and breaks into a mad escape.
The rhinoceros immediately turns towards him, and your crew seize the opportunity to retreat, desperately trying to ignore the fact that in order to escape, the young man's life will be forfeit.
Scatter!
Where to — it's charging!'
Flee as far as you can

Attempts to outrun the rhinoceros are futile. Turning to the stragglers, it singles out a limping fellow and bellows, before charging and skewering him with its horn.
As the body of their crewmate is tossed and broken underfoot, your sailors flee back to camp, haunted by visions of a dark, bloodied horn piercing through the man’s abdomen in a spurt of gore.
Encircle the beast to confuse it

Rhinoceroses are swift, but their bulk lends them poor mobility. Your crew dance in and out of the beast’s vision, leaving it dizzily turning from one evanescent figure to the next. As soon as it is sufficiently dazed, your men dart behind the creature’s colossal backside and run hurriedly back to camp, hidden by tall grass, fearing at every instant they might hear a furious bellow, catch a glimpse of grey armour, or feel the sharp end of that osseous horn.
Prepare to intercept them mid-leap

You order a loosening of the ranks — if the beasts pounce, they should immediately be surrounded —and not a moment too soon, as one particularly impressive male leaps into the fray. You prepare to corner it when a powerful fist crashes into the side of the beast’s head mid-leap, sending it sprawling, dazed, several feet away.
Surprised at the strength of Ajax, a surly but powerfully muscular gunman, your crew hastily retreat off the spur while the lion is stunned, and its companions cowed.
Tales abound around the campfire that night of the mighty feat of Ajax, without entirely making up for the crew’s sensation that they only narrowly escaped with their lives.

One of the lions pounces upon a young man in the front ranks. He ducks, hoping to avoid the beast, but sharp claws rake into his shoulder, blood spurting violently as the lad crashes down under the creature’s weight. His companions pummel the lion with their fists, but it barely seems to acknowledge the blows, and busies itself with goring the unfortunate lad. All pretence of resistance finally abandons your crew; broken, the sailors disband and flee back to the savannah, routed and haunted by the dreadful fate of their young comrade.
Make each bullet count

Guns are nervously loaded and trained on the creatures, when a sudden burst of rapid-fire shots sallies from the rear ranks of your crew. Three of the lions stumble before falling at your feet, heads bloodied by uncannily precise sharpshooting.
The remaining lions back away in terror as your crew wisely head back down the spur, gushing proudly about the young shooter’s skills, yet unpleasantly aware of how narrowly they just avoided death.

Your crew fumble to load their weapons, and a volley of haphazard shots crackles through the warm air. Without the proper time to aim, the marksmen miss the beasts by several feet.
Enraged, the lions pounce, ripping and goring those nearby with powerful maws, spattering blood through the air and onto the rest of your horrified party. Abandoning all pretence of bravery, they flee the towering rocks, followed by the dying cries of their comrades.

You can now build Docklands! Docklands allow you to export/import goods to/from global trade corporations, and build compact harbour modules with different functions.
The docklands can be built by accessing the artisan's harbour area construction menu.
The docklands must be built in your harbour's marked water area. The Docklands Main Wharf may only be built once per island.

Build modules to add features to your Docklands.
Some modules have functions you know already, like Depots and Repair Cranes. Here they are more space efficient however!

Modules can be built anywhere in your harbour area without needing a connection to the Main Wharf.
Modules directly connected to the Main Wharf (without roads) will, however, provide an attractiveness bonus.
Here on the Docklands Main Wharf's item tab, you can equip harbourmaster's office items, affecting anything within the building's radius.
Here you can manage and set-up Export/Import Contracts.

Here are your potential export goods.
Hover over one to see how much of it you have already exported: its 'Export Volume'. You've exported nothing yet, so the current Export Volume is zero.

Over here, you can see all of the available import goods.
Some are locked— hover over them to find out how you can unlock them.
And in the slot to the right, select the goods you want to import.
This is an Export/Import Contract. In the left slot, select a good you wish to export. The more complex a good is to produce, the more you will get in exchange for it.

The complexity of each good defines the exchange ratio for any given contract.
I will visit your Docklands at regular intervals to fulfill any contracts you set-up here.
This Pyramid shows your Specialty Exports— higher ranking goods get better Exchange Ratios. Export a good to increase its Export Volume. Do this enough, and that good will rank up.
With every trade, the goods increase their export volume. With enough export volume, you will improve your exporter level, which means better exchange ratios for those goods!
You've now filled every specialty export slot — very good! Remember: you can drag and drop goods around the pyramid to change their rank.

Hover over a locked slot to see the bonus to exchange ratio and Docklands module limit you will receive.
Note below the export volume required to unlock that rank.
You can drag and drop your speciality export goods down to lower levels of the pyramid, making room for other goods you've levelled up.
One of your exported goods is ready to level up! Drag and drop it to the next speciality level in the pyramid!
I will visit your docklands regularly, bringing imports for all current contracts with me!
Make sure you set up a minimum stock for these goods back at your trading post, if you want to keep some of them for yourself!

Underneath Captain Tobias's blustery exterior lies a fascination for things of the deep — a fascination that extends even to his ship, a curious, shark-shaped tanker. The lure of the abyss, the song of the sea... All of it hailing back to a memory long ago, and the tale of an encounter in the mists of the past.

From the deep darkness of the ocean she has returned — the great shark, Deep Blue, summoned to the surface by the echo of a call long-forgotten — a horn in the fog. A last, final blessing for Captain Tobias, who never forgot the wonder of that first encounter, and wishes for just one last glimpse of her — and, perhaps, a photogram by way of memorial.

News of Deep Blue's resurfacing has drawn the ghastly eye of hunters and trophy-seekers alike, each eager to claim the head of the largest shark in history! She must be protected at all costs, and escorted back to the edge of the abyss — the last wonder of the world, sinking slowly back out of memory and time, after a last chase and a last glimpse from the man who always dreamt of her.

Its call is a strange, rasping, bone-lonely sound.
Tea-stained blueprints for building an heir to the old shark-ship, Deep Blue.
Sultry sea's in the offing, it's a deal-and-trade day!
Ahoy and g'day!
Ready for a bit of the old haggle dance?
Mood's ripe for grafting!
We wobbegongs are swum north again.
Left home when I was young — the pull of the sea, distant shores. I'd serve on outfits of any size in those days - provided they had a proper billy.
Hogarth CC first eleven I was— pretty nippy with the ball. A bite from a blue eel saw to all that, but I still adore the sport.
There's a fascination to the sea. You miss harbour, of course, all the bustle and life, but out there? A secret. Something we've forgotten.
Comes a day when you find yourself looking at the sea from the shore for the first real time, and turn inland... I've yet to find that shore.
It's a joke, see? 'Cause a wombat's slow and... ah, forget it!
The ship was cheered, the harbour cleared...
It's not being drunk if you're part of the gintlemen!
She'll be right - long as the bludgers moor her tight.
... ain't no sirens left today, y'know. Drone of machines pushed them back to the Deep.
Dabbled in idealism long ago, but it's a young man's game. Flares and powder burn away at more than your lungs.
If you're going to spend your life on a ship you might as well make sure it's a damn comfortale one!
Some say sea's a mistress, a wife. But she's more of a... a book that changes every time you open it.
You can never own the sea, that's what I like. You're just... a traveller. A guest, listening to its stories.
Fit for the fight!
Better than ever!
Lob the shells!
Empty all tubes!
Quick, nab it all!
Secure the ship!
Into the blue!
Mind the narrows inland!
Trade winds steady!
Cargo secure.
Ready to barter.
Keep her close boys!
Scour the waters!
To the water lads!
Deep Blue... she's dying.
Steady as she goes.
Hold course!
Take her headlong!
Take her walkabout!
Air the portholes!
She's leaking!
Battered and bruised.
Nose sharp!
G'day there!
Stations all!
Mind the helm!
Deadset to snag that market then, eh?
Someone's been promoted up the batting order!
Ain't that a little ripper!
Colour me a twelve-sided puffin!
That stuff'll be the making of you!
You're the undisputed master of that avenue.
That's about as good a rate as you'll ever get!
You've really cornered that market, mate!
Y'can't go wrong with old keg!
Shines like a brushfire on a winter's day.
About time! Useful things when crossing meridians.
Sure to raise smoke, that!
Long as two people live one of them'll want something of the sort.
Nothing so lonesome as a pub with no beer.
Dip of coleslaw away from sausage heaven!
Sounds of the world in your home - even didgeridoo!
Dreadfully convenient and easy to ship!
Smoked the competition, you did!
Solid stuff, coffee. Insubmersible market.
Slick stuff, if inhuman to some.
One explosive arrangement, coming up!
Sweeter than a honey-ant, this deal!
Cull the herds and turn a certain profit!
Variety of flavour - nice change from roo and croc!
Not much of a socialite myself but Chanteuse chic is all the rage way south!
Used to have a mate who'd stalk the cook to know when Old Levant & Co. supplies were in. Mad about their breakfast conserves…
Takes a special sort to turn a profit from simple folks' fare, and while they might grind your gears, many a family would starve without FEEDL.
Board, chair, window, three-pronged barbie spike… KITEA have you covered. Solid stuff too- scandic sturdiness.
Ganymedia are all about gadgetry! Don't believe anyone else could peddle such… flamboyance and get away with it.
Qinsa drive a hard bargain on their ore - sharp minds, see? But there's no-one more skilled in all the East - or West, for that matter.
Powerful bludgers, that Promise Trust. Name holds well - promises as unbreakable as iron, but there's more than a whiff of sulfur there!
Never met a pie I couldn't love, but the Tattershire grub? No-one I'd trust more with a crust-and-filling!
Kasht'a Spice. Ambitious sort, real battlers - not surprised they they snagged the southern markets.
ENBE dabble in the smarter stuff - electrites and whatnot, right scientific. Damned if they're not the future!
Named - and designed - my ship after a shark, you know. A Great White by the name of Deep Blue - long story, for another day.
Strange things, Great Whites are. People fear them, and rightly so, but there's a mystery to them. A wisdom, you know, a memory of things we've forgotten.
Deep Blue here, she's a thing of today, latest innovations. But Great Whites… they haunted the deeps long before we came around.
Deep Blue - the shark - she was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. Like a ghost, a white memory in the vast blackness of water and time.
What I'd give to see her again… You recon you could help? I haven't much but I can share my ship's plans…
Foggy night it was, three decades past. Ship stranded in the dark fog and me alone on deck with the Foghorn.
Blared the horn out, so ships'd know not to run us in. Ever heard a Foghorn at night? Horribly, horribly lonely and yearning sound.
Perhaps that's what called her. The song of quiet millenia in the deeps, without a people. She'd heard the horn, and came in answer.
Wait, is that? It's her! Deep Blue, clever girl! Snap a picture of her quick!
Why'd d'you have to publish it? Now every darn poacher in existence is gonna be after her!
What've we done? And she the last of her kind! We must escort her to safety!
Oh, she's a right sight, ain't she? Last real wonder of the world. Farewell, old girl. I think, at last, we understand each other.
Dead… If I hadn't called her… I can't… Just leave me be. We'll talk at work.
Careful! She's the last of her kind!
Another missed opportunity, another regret, another day.
Mind you use it well. It's old and fragile.
Novel business this is, so let me show you how to arrange Trade Contracts and build up your Docklands.
So, Trade Contracts! The rum of it is that the more often you use the same Trade Contract, the more profitable it becomes.
There, your Trade Contract has grown more profitable! Look to your Docklands, you'll find you can expand them now.
Batter this old cobber, what a sight!
Reminds me of a city I knew - lovely red lights.
Efficiency over comfort, eh?
Can't go wrong with taller and wider.
Right beauty of a place you've made this harbour!
Lump yer 'ead back in and stop scribblin' Jozef!
What the saggy mold-eaten son of haggis-tuba is this?
… nastier temper than me da' these birds - see the scar? One peck - one!
…miles and miles of desert and this huge red rock just standing there, like the egg of a forgotten god…
… ginger wine. Ginger! Lord help me, I need a drink.
The Mariner, whose eye is bright, whose beard with age and hoar…
… what was it made 'im think I'd be happy ending up like him?
… he said "whaddya gonna do?". I said "anything but this".
Roar of the chains, crackin' of timbers… That's a melody.
Knew a welder named Jock. Damn finest voice in the shipyard!
… dashing around the rooftops with a cane and white tails, I swear!
… Ten more and bit of nosh and I'm your man!
… then there's goat cheese, and cow and moose and pig…
... Huge and slimy, wrapped around some kind of monolith…
… red moon, the inn was called, but there were only five survivors…
Garlic snail sandwich in a closed, top-floor office. Really?
… days' work, out the bally window...and all the way down...
... the number of hats I've seen tumbling from top-floor windows... You wouldn't believe.
... had to fire him, he wouldn't stop dropping coins from the twentieth floor!
File the report tonight and send me a report on the filing tomorrow.
Setting sun over the city is a thing to behold. More than makes up for working late.
… upstairs? Well, well, well, that's your ticket then!
Imagine a giant gorilla climbing up here.
…rookie numbers, I told him he's gotta work harder…
It a bird - it's a blimp - it's a… panda?
For the last time, we're not having cereal for dinner!
Why do they keep changing aisles every other day?
I'd like to talk to the manager please.
Who even needs twelve sorts of spoons?
... and this device here finds wayward stockings in the most recalcitrant drawers!
If it is so expensive, what is it for, after all? It looks like a cross between a swordfish and a lute...
What strange manner of contraption is this then?
… can't stay, I'm afraid. The chaps want me at the club in ten.
Oh the arcades are all very novel - the light, the sheen of oddments and inventions!
Cheese, cheese everywhere!
Knew a bloke once - brave as fire, heart of a mountain - claimed he started steel-running age twelve.
Sky-dancing they called it - the ultimate test of bravery.
Dancing? Great big steel beams and three hundred feet and they call it dancing?
I hear the name was given to 'em by people looking up from below.
Looked like a whirl of ghosts or gods, dancing at the edge of the world far up there.
Swore I could've heard them sing and laugh as the wind shook the rafters.
Think they en't afraid, like? Some kind of spiritual connection?
Nah. If anything I reckon they're more afraid - or better. They respect the danger.
I've known blokes from all parts as could rivet a beam with a half-mile fall below e'm.
But that bloke, he danced with the open sky, keepin' time with it. He listened, see.

The tourist's eagerness to discover your city's culinary culture is undampened by the limitations of the current menu. Having eaten well, she is now insisting upon a tour of your restaurants' wholesale food suppliers, with a particular interest in sustainable and naturally-sourced ingredients.

Though she doesn't doubt for a moment the talent of your fleet of chefs, the Tourist finds your restaurants' culinary repertoire rather limited. She has summoned you in the hopes of putting your heads together to invent a new, daring recipe.
The Tourist is eager to let the world discover your most recent culinary creations. She asks you to supply your restaurants with the recipe as soon as possible.

The moreishly over-sweet flavour of your doughnuts has reminded the Tourist of the excellent pastries she'd been enjoying on her cruise to your city. A disturbing sharpness spreads to her smile and eyes, as she "suggests" you take her to the ship, so she can procure more elaborate recipes for your restaurants.

A silver lining of the well-proportioned chef's absence is that the Tourist has "procured" the cruise ship's book of recipes. She now urges you to return her to her hotel, so that she may examine it at her leisure.

According to the Tourist, the masterful chef's cookbook lays out a veritable smörgåsbord of fresh ideas to enhance your café menu. She urges you to acquire the necessary supplies to start producing novel and flakey pastries.

A meal is not simply sustenance: it is flavour, an experience — an exaltation of the land and its people. A rich main course is essential. Intricate gastronomic ideas are expected, yet dinner guests must also have the sensation of a warm and comforting hug from their first mouthful. Savoury aromas, textural contrast, ideally with a meaty heart — do you understand?
Meaty? There's game and cattle aplenty here!
Meaty, you say? What of seafood? A healthier option, surely.

Excellent! Now, to mellow the palate, a dash of sauce and garnish.
Game, once the bones have been removed, is ideally suited to a fine crusting of breadcrumb and herbs.
Other meats may be better coated in a sweet, fruity mantle of a sauce, for example — something unctuous and rich, bringing out the natural sweetness of a stewing cut. Which of these possibilities is leaping out at you?
What about marinated meat, bobbing in a vegetable gravy — with sweetcorn?
Herb-crusted venison it is then, with a side of buttered vegetables.

Mmm! Now that is an interesting refinement! The surprising pop of New World sweetcorn in this stew truly elevates it! I hear this is a popular dish among Bohemian and Muscovy communities, where they call this elegant variation a Stroggof Goulash!
Crusted deer — wonderful! Beautifully turned vegetables and a deep, dark sauce to bring it together — Heaven! I think your Venison en Croûte will sell like hotcakes.
Unlock Recipe

Excellent idea! Maybe with a side of something tangy, a note of sourness — smoked, perhaps? Unless you'd rather an actual fish rather than seafood, in which case I'd recommend something sturdier, like mashed potato, or durum wheat pasta.
Fresh fish — lovely! With crisp fried potatoes and a fine slice of lemon.
Enbesan lobster. Smoked under a cloche, with a dash of lemon.
Lemon, you say... With potatoes — why, yes, of course! A quaint sort of Fish and Frites, from across the channel! I should have known...
The fragrant aroma of sweet braisé lobster... The cloche lifts like a theatrical curtain for the magical reveal! A perfect Lobster Cheminée!
All pastries need plenty of flour, but the elephantine palmier also needs some musky sweetness. Do you have anything like nutmeg? Or something similar perhaps...
A sweet boozy kick of rum would do the trick.
Cinnamon might make a nice replacement for nutmeg.
Some unground grain, for bite and texture?
Rum? Well, the sweetness usually comes from the spices and — ah, of course! Cinnamon, that's it!
Ah yes, of course! Cinnamon is the perfect ingredient for that sweet-and-spice perfume!

Grain? Interesting texture, certainly, but not remotely sweet...
(The Tourist glances at the glass of wine standing between you).
It ought to be something spiced, almost like the hot winter wines of the northern regions....
(She pauses for a moment to think.)...
Of course, cinnamon! I'll add it to the recipe.

Now for the Eclair — my favourite! We need flour, of course, and... confound that sea spray! The rest of the page is drenched — the ink's all run! It's unreadable! Perhaps reading on the deck was unwise.

Let me see... Perhaps I can conjure one up in my mind's eye to see what's missing. Mmm, yes — there it is! An Eclair whose rich, dark chocolate filling oozes out upon separation; a breathy choux crust... and that underlying sweetness! That's what's missing! Any ideas?
I really do think rum is the thing to add.
Sugar, surely?
Why not coffee, to complement the chocolate?

I'm afraid I must disappoint: the harshness of the rum has absolutely no place in a classic chocolate eclair — I really rather think the sweetness comes from the sugar. Why not try simple refined sugar? It should do the trick.
Of course, how did I not think of that! Into the recipe it goes!
A clever innovation, but won't it embitter the mixture? Unless... Why not add sugar! Into the recipe it goes.

Long has the Queen heard your city praised as the 'Crown Jewel of the Empire', but the Tourist's latest ravings to her friends have convinced Her Majesty to entrust her latest magnum opus to you: raising a colossal steel tower — a marvel of engineering that will stand testament to the Empire's industrial and cultural importance!

Her Majesty has extended a list of requests to ensure the inauguration proceeds in the best possible circumstances. Particulars include securing a hotel suite next to the Iron Tower and providing light reading for Her Majesty, as well as a maidservant to attend to the Queen's toilet.

One last momentous task remains to ensure the inaugural celebrations will be worthy of this historic event: preparing the banquet. What better way to crow such a feast than with the greatest, most glorious national pudding ever built? A challenge the Tourist is unwavering in her desire to take up.

With inauguration day drawing ever nearer, Sir Archibald has started to worry that security is not up to snuff. He insists there need to be more police patrols near the monument, to apprehend miscreants, rabble-rousers and in worst case, those looking to commit deadly treason.

Your investigations into potential security issues has unveiled yet another possible threat of assassination against the Queen! Most dull and tiresome! It is vitally important that you squeeze the worker for all he knows of this plot!

Having uncovered a member of a conspiracy threatening the public humiliation of Her Majesty with hurled fruit and veg, you have decided to bring the villain to the Queen's dedicated aide, Sir Archibald, to ensure the threat is de-escalated.

Having successfully managed to corrupt the worker into sell out his associates, you must now hasten to the harbour where they are all gathered ahead of their planned attack on Her Majesty's dignity. They must be arrested and delivered immediately to Sir Archibald, so he can assess their true threat.
All is set and ready - the Iron Tower built, the grounds secure, the people gathered... At last, the Queen has decreed the inauguration is to proceed and has invited you as guest of honour.

The splendour and pomp of the inauguration ceremony are such that even the revels of the great kings of old would pale in comparison— History will doubtless remember this moment as a turning point, the beginning of a new age! And what better way to commemorate such an historic event than with some equally regal photography?

The inauguration ceremony has left the Queen quite famished. She is now eager to discover the menu at Restaurant 'La Reine', the three-star establishment at the foot of the mighty colossus that surpasses all others in its quality of fare. Let us hope you choose her dishes wisely!

The Queen wishes to impress upon you her appreciation of your efforts in preparing the inauguration. She has a particular thank you in mind but insists it must be kept a surprise while she prepares it.

The Queen requested an impressive trifle for dessert, one worthy of the Iron Tower! Let us start with a bit of backbone, so our great pudding will not slump and sag!
Sponge cake should give it texture and body, n'est pas?
Fatty Tallow should keep the whole thing clumped together.

The skeleton is now there, but we need a daring touch to take it over the cusp and put it firmly in the kingdom of deliciousness. Some audacious signature that will ensure the pudding is festive enough for such an event!
Her Majesty probably likes a good bit of booze in her trifle— rum, perhaps?
If in doubt, add thinly sliced meat...
There, the signature element is in! Now— and importantly— something that gives the wow factor to any pudding.
Um...sugar?
Coffee, as with tiramisu, is weaponised flavour!

Of course, of course— naturally! One last thing then: the trifle must celebrate the Queen, and her indomitable Empire! Should we celebrate its reach or its resilience? What one ingredient of any good trifle is still conspicuously missing?
Something that is resilient and elastic: like jelly!
Something exotic and grand, from a distant colony: like bananas!

Wonderful — everything is assembled and settling into place! Into the ice cellar it goes... and now we wait for a time!

So, the banquet! As a warm up, an aperitif...perhaps something fruity? A generous dab of fine liquor canonically makes for great effect— one of those effervescently aristocratically-named spirits, if you have them.
Daiqiri Tropic (Rum, Sugar, Banana)
Black Muscovy (Coffee, Rum, Schnapps)
Montmartre '75' (Sugar, Champagne, Citrus)

For the main course, pray avoid anything too reminiscent of the sea. Her Majesty came by airship expressly to avoid such features of nauseating and dreary holidays. The dish should be contemporary, striking in appearance as well as flavour— a colourful ode to travel!
Archduke's Schnitzel (Pig, Tallow, Bread)
Stroggof Goulash (Meat, Paprika, Corn)
Fish and Frites (Fish, Potato, Citrus)

And now for the finale we have all been waiting for... dessert! I do love a good patriotic trifle. Tell us, did you succeed in completing the masterpiece we asked for? I have been asking every day for news about it, jumping up and down on my four-poster-bed like a little girl again, trying to imagine what it could taste like.
Your Majesty, may I present...(a mere trifle m'am I assure you)... the Trifle Tower!
This is the Trifle Tower dessert. It... hopefully... tastes better than it looks.

Her Majesty has insisted on traveling with a limited retinue. A duly vetted handmaid will consequently also need to be provided to attend upon her every whim, courtesy of you, Her loyal subject.
