The Tourist asks you to build a Tourist Mooring, so that she and her friends can take a (possibly) well-earned vacation on your island. The Public Mooring isn't nearly welcoming enough for those wanting to make a longer stopover — it does not scream luxury holiday!

The Tourist asks you to build a Hotel, and to connect it to the harbour by bus for her convenience. In her own words: "Travel is terribly tiresome you know, and one must have an omnibus at one's beck and call to deliver all the luggage to the Hotel, and take one around all of the nice and interesting places, while avoiding all the squalid and sordid ones the likes of which one always seems to encounter on foot."

The Tourist asks you to build a Variety Theatre, and connect it to her Hotel by bus. Taking in a show, you see, is one of the first expectations of the overnight traveller wishing to absorb the cultural highlights and footlights of any given surround.

The Tourist asks you to build a Restaurant, and connect it to her Hotel by bus. A Tourist expects to wine and dine every evening, somewhere different than the place they're supposed to sleep. Hotel food, you must understand, is barely edible after the hour of nine in the morning when the breakfast service ends. After that, it's nothing but deathly-dry hunks of meat, overboiled vegetables, and dense, over-reduced sauces.

The Tourist asks you to build a Zoo, complete with enclosures containing rare and impressive animals, and connect it to her Hotel by bus. In her own words, "When one is able to relax happily in a new and undiscovered place for a long time, one finds oneself craving stimulation of one kind or another. In particular, anything with those jolly animals who are all on holiday from their homelands too."

Restaurants are a new building type. They act like public services, but consume input goods! The input goods depend on the chosen recipe.

When selecting a Restaurant, the green street overlay shows you where it can fetch recipe input goods from.
Make sure you have a warehouse within range of it!
Currently, this Restaurant has no active recipe. Open the recipe book to choose one.

Here you can see all the available Restaurant recipes. There's only one available right now, but you can unlock new ones later.
Click on the first recipe to jump directly to it.

In principle, Restaurants act like public services, but consume input goods. As long as a Restaurant can produce the selected recipe, it will fulfill the Tourists need for a Restaurant, no matter which recipe you select.

Depending on a recipe's ingredients, a Restaurant will need different input goods.
So make sure you have a warehouse with a stock of those goods nearby.
Apart from the effect on us Tourists, a recipe also has a beneficial effect on your local residents near the Restaurant. Local residents do not require a bus connection, however.

So, remember what counts for Restaurants:
1. The bus network decides which Hotels can reach a Restaurant.
2. The green street overlay shows you where input goods can be fetched from.
3. The circle shows which local residences will benefit from the chosen recipe.

Production buildings require a workforce, right? Well, Restaurants require us Tourists as customers in the same way.
If a Restaurant has too few customers, the need will not be fully supplied, and the benefit to regular residents will be reduced.

We Tourists are very picky! If we are unhappy, filling our basic needs will not attract as many Tourists as it could.
In other words, only when you make us fully happy, will you start to have full Hotels!
Check the happiness needs tab to find out more about why some Tourists may be reluctant to visit!

Right now, we are unhappy because this island is not attractive enough.
Build attractive buildings like Zoos and Museums, and with more exhibits! Only then will more of us move in.

Defeat the attacker or end the war altogether! Only then will more of us move in.

Build better hotspots and make sure that they are not too far away by bus to improve this! Only then will more of us move in.

Increase production on the ones listed here! Only then will more of us move in.

Regal Gala Parade
An entire day dedicated to the glory of Her Majesty, the Iron Lady, the Preserver of Peace, waving to the cheering crowds that bask in her royal presence.

A benefit of an increasingly globalised world, is the joy of fusion. Take East Bohemian goulash— already a beloved dish among artisans— and regard how humble Señorita Maldonado elevated it with the mere addition of New World corn.

A rather commonplace Friday evening delicacy in the territories, albeit with the potatoes often suffering the slings and arrows of far-too-astringent malt vinegar. To lighten the flavour profile, a citrus substitute would better appeal to continental tastes.

The pastry exterior remains crisp thanks only to a thin pancake, acting as an absorbent buffer to the meat. The end effect is a celebratory pink, and not-at-all-rubbery, centrepiece to commemorate any jaque-booted cross-channel contretemps.

It's that first dramatic reveal, as the cloche floats away, and a great plume of subtle smoke fills the nostrils. Then the eyes perceive a silhouette, an alien — a sunset exoskeleton, demanding to be prised open for the white meat within.

A light lunch for café-goers. To some, eating raw meat is repugnant; to others it is the epitome of delicacy. After all, molecular gastronomers may argue that exposure to any form of heat can do nothing but damage the quintessential flavour of an ingredient.

The banana is a mysterious and exotic gift that this dish only desires to celebrate. Festooned with sprinkles of cinnamon, the real and genuine surprise here is the uncompromising hit of sour, goaty savour that comes with the goat milk.
The very definition of a stiff drink. The ice, they say, comes directly from the larch forests of the frozen north, where dark-bellied bears loom on their hind legs behind every towering timber.

Left bank, right bank, nobody's sure... either way, it's a drink for thinkers, or those that like others to think they're thinkers. Crisp and clean in its profile, this cool drink became a classic from the moment it was first shaken into being.

Thick, oleaginous clouds swirl up through this magnetic polar blend. Some report having seen the aurora borealis shortly upon drinking; others merely sensations of comfort and warmth, as well as temporary immunity to the push and pull of the sea.

Though rather a typical image of Enbesa, dawn is indeed a magical and dreamlike time there. You may even find the Elders in a good mood after their morning purge, filled with bright hope for the strictures of a day yet to come.

A conceptual dish whose inventor intended to celebrate hundreds of years of ocean-going exploration. The elements are gathered from the four points of the compass, deconstructed and then reconstructed to represent 'the journey' above all else.

In an attempt to reconciliate with Sir Archibald Blake in strident mood, the cream of Enbesan chefs created this provocative marriage of surf and turf to represent the powers at play. Time will tell if these two elements can ever sit in harmony on the tongue.

Fluffy, buttery brioche on both top and bottom can scarcely contain the West Atlantic strips of meat within. Is it fine dining? Well, it's a statement, that's for sure — and that can count for a lot at the high end.

A dish to really give people something to choux on, this narrow strip of morning ecstasy may disappear down the gullet in a flash. Forget all the pretenders — a filling of rich and velvety dark chocolate is the only way to go.

Crack apart a palmier, and a whiff of all-too-buttery spice perfumes the air. It's easy to make a pig's ear of these delicate treats, but they're said to look like so many different things, it's become part of their appeal. A props game over coffee!

A cabaret cocktail, this drink is a statement burlesque. It takes bottle to order one of these, and it ain't for everyone. But for those who can own it, this boudoir sip, jam-packed with colour and fantabulousness, is the night incarnate.

With a wobble intended to convey the quaking majesty of empire, this charming blob of a pudding represents all that is right and yet so dreadfully wrong about its island home. A showstopper, surely, for even the grandest of banquets.

Popular with locals, this homely dish may underwhelm with the casualness of its presentation. Yet, for Tourists, it may well be the first choice on the menu — stating a commitment on their part to sample only the most authentic food of the region.

The Fourré is the sum of several scarcely-distinguishable 'solid donut' strains. Rarely does the absence of nothing cause such controversy as with a donut without a hole, yet when that centre is richly jammy, what fool could possibly complain?

Rum, Sugar, Bananas— not a foot put wrong across the white sand, between coconut husk, pink crab and driftwood, the sun plummeting towards cool night and the gentle sway of melody. Isabel Sarmento rarely has occasion, but if she did raise a glass...

Introduction
Tourists

Tourists are a special resident type who stay in Hotels in your city, and have various basic and luxury needs. Rather than provide workforce like other residents, Tourists are customers who visit Restaurants, Cafés, Bars and other Tourist Hotspots in your city.

Tourist customers are represented by the suitcase icon.
Tourist Mooring Upgrade
Your existing Public Mooring will have to be upgraded to a Tourist Mooring before Tourists can visit your island. Click the upgrade button inside the Public Mooring building to upgrade.
Hotels— Introduction & Needs
Hotels — Happiness & Hotspots

Hotels do not count as residences, and therefore cannot be upgraded.

To keep Hotels full, you should strive to keep your Tourists happy. You can do this by improving your city's attractiveness, fulfilling luxury needs, and connecting them to Tourist Hotspots by bus. Tourist Hotspots are cultural attractions like the Zoo and the Museum.

Tourist happiness is also affected if the island is at war, or you receive bad press in the newspaper.
Impact of Happiness

Tourists are pretty picky and have five categories of Happiness for you to keep in check: Attractiveness, Island Peace, Hotspots, Luxury Needs, and the News.

If an unhappy red face is visible on a needs meter, this will limit the maximum number of Tourists who can reside in the Hotel.

Be sure to keep your Tourists happy, as they will be quicker to leave than other resident types.
Limited Needs
Buses
Buses — Step-by-Step

Buses take Tourists from the Tourist Mooring to their Hotels and other places of interest. Plan your network of Bus Stops carefully so that Tourists don't have to travel too far. Tourists expect Food & Drink Venues and Cultural buildings to have nearby bus stops.
Bus Networks

Select a Bus Stop to see the highlighted buildings which fall within its service radius.

Other Bus Stops in the same network will also be highlighted, with the green street overlay showing if they're connected.

The Bus Stop building menu indicates the level of access Tourists have to Hotspots in that Bus network. The further a Hotspot is from a Hotel, the less it will meet the Tourists' need.
Places to Eat & Drink
Venue Types

Restaurants, Cafés and Bars are Tourist Venues that function like public services, but consume input goods! The input goods required depends on which Recipe is currently active at the venue. You can switch the current recipe in the building's menu, selecting new ones from the Recipe Book.

Tourists will enjoy every dish, no matter which you pick — but each recipe has different effects on regular residents nearby.
Sustained by Tourism

Rather than workforce, each venue needs Tourist Customers in order to function. A lack of customers may mean Tourist needs are not being met, and in turn, recipes may have a reduced effect on regular residents living nearby.

Select any Food & Drink Venue to check if a Warehouse is within reach to supply recipe ingredients. Some of the required goods will need to be imported from other regions.
Orchards
Multifactory
Different output goods can be produced in your Orchards by choosing from a variety of trees. Orchards work similarly to the lumberjack's hut, and can also be built in the New World.
Choosing Output Goods

The Orchard Catalogue functions similarly to Recipe Books in Tourist Food & Drink Venues. Accessed from the Orchard building menu, it allows you to select your preferred output goods.

No input goods are necessary — just make sure there's enough space to plant trees!
Chemical Plants
Chemical Plants allow you to choose from a variety of industrial products as output goods. Chemical Plants work similarly to factories.

The Formula Codex functions similarly to Recipe Books for Tourist Food & Drink Venues. Accessed from the Chemical Plant building menu, it allows you to select your preferred output goods.

Make sure to have a warehouse in range to supply the required input goods.

The building can be improved with electricity.
Effects

Recipe books allow you to pick which goods you want Restaurants, Cafés and Bars to produce, from a selection. Multifactories such as Orchards and Chemical Plants have an Orchard Catalogue and Formula Codex that follow the same principle.

They can be accessed from each buildings' respective menu.
Navigating The Recipes
Monument - The Iron Tower
Introduction
Restaurant "La Reine"

The acme of architecture in the industrial era, The Iron Tower is the final building introduced with Tourist Season. As with all Monuments there are several phases of construction, and only one Iron Tower can be built per island.

On completion of the monument, a special restaurant will open known as Restaurant 'La Reine'. This functions like any other restaurant, but its extravagant recipes require four input goods rather than the usual three.

As a result however, you can expect stronger recipe effects.

You can assign surplus Tourist customers to further increase the radius of the recipe effects within the Monument building menu, but all other Restaurants, Cafés and Bars have priority over the Iron Tower.
Tourist Hotspots
Tourist Needs

Since Tourists are very picky, their basic needs can be limited by their Happiness.

If your Tourists are unhappy, a red sad face above the Needs bar will indicate the maximum fulfilment currently possible.

To discover what's limiting your Tourists' Happiness, you can hover over the Needs bar.

Hotspots are Tourist attractions in your city, like the Zoo. Hotspots must be connected to Hotels by bus. The further a Hotspot is from a Hotel, the less it will meet your Tourists' needs. Check the Happiness tab of your Hotels to see how well-connected they are to your Hotspots.

Unique buildings like the World's Fair are exceptions, and are always well-connected, no matter the distance. The attractiveness of certain buildings, such as Zoos and Museums, also affects need fulfillment. Add modules to increase attractiveness, better fulfilling your Tourists' needs.
First, build a Bus Stop near a Tourist Mooring, ensuring the Tourist Mooring is within the Bus Stop's radius.

The Index displays all Recipes at a glance, as well as the active recipe. You can show or hide the required input goods and recipe effects, or jump to the recipe page to find further details.

Some recipes may be locked, and require you to complete a Quest or fulfil certain conditions to unlock them.
Next, build Bus Stops near each of your Hotels, ensuring the Hotels are within a Bus Stop's radius. Multiple Bus Stop radiuses may freely overlap.
Lastly, build Bus Stops close to any other buildings you want Tourists to have access to — Restaurants, Variety Theatres, and Zoos, for example.

Select any bus stop to see its reach via the green street overlay. Bus stops must have overlapping overlays for them to be considered connected. If you see gaps in the overlay, add new bus stops in those spots.

New dawn, new day, new dishes!
How about a canapé?
I know the waiters personally, wait a moment…
What's your poison then?
Surely you'll join me for a small one?
Your usual today, or something more exciting?
This latest brew is quite the thing, I assure you!
Tell me your mood and I'll tell you your drink!
Plenty here that'll spoil if it's shut too long!
Catering must be rather exhausting, I suppose.
Perhaps they're flipping the menu?
Down to a simmer for a bit then?
Slow cook for a while?
Time to let the dough rest?
Flambé, not 'burn it all down!"
Fire in the kitchen?
Can it have been the seafood?
I knew it tasted undercooked...
Staff seem... overwhelmed today, don't they?
They must be understaffed: no one sends the porter to deliver a dish!
Staff are on hand but stocks are low.
Fresh produce is running dreadfully low!
The stuff won't magically stock itself on the shelves!
No warehouses? So they just leave the food... in the street!
It's not just the food itself, it's the crowd, the culture, the flair and elegance of it all!
Oh I've worked alongside the very best chefs! I've tried B. R. Ekfest's breads, for example.
The painting on the wall? Well, sometimes a penniless artist comes in for coffee and you want to do them a favour, so…
There's coffee and pastry at home, but the whirl of colours, people, drama? Not like this...
My tutor used to say all the great classics had two things in common: a backroom at a local speakeasy and a series of stiff drinks!
You'd be surprised how many bad drinks a bartender can pour if they're a good listener.
The pastry chef - Honoré - is something of a culinary saint!
Studies have shown the flavour is exalted by the high altitude and thin air!
Can't cook without electricity!
Power's off, food's going to waste!
The pier is such a long way away!
I'll not walk from pier to hotel! I have standards!
Pity the place is too far from bus routes.
I tried, the omnibuses just won't go there!
Must fetch Jemima and sample this new dish!
Ah, fresh flavours! Delightful!
Now this is what this journey's about!
Once more unto the dish, dear friend!
Make a reservation, Jemima, we're dining out tonight!
"Opening soon"? Well that sounds promising!
"Coming soon: new dishes"? Intriguing, intruiging!
Closed… Still working on the menu, I expect.
High dining in the most literal sense!
I hope one day they'll do my truffled trout... simply terrific… usually!
I've heard the cellar alone is worth millions!
Couldn't keep away from the soufflé, could you?
Just in time for the hors d'œuvre! Pull up a chair!
No transportation is hard enough, but no road?!
I'm by no means an expert, but aren't roads essentials to, well, any industry?
Time to put the cutlery back in order!
Set the tables, light the candles! We're coming in!
Lady Hunt is formidable, a model in her own way. But hers is the power of a caged thing, trapped by norms and rules. I want so much more!
I wonder: if she'd had the opportunity, do you think Her Majesty would have chosen this life? I just… ah, never mind.
I heard a story about old Nathaniel not long ago. Chilling, it was, but it may just be true. There's an edge, a strangeness to the man.
Isabel's is a tale of tragedy. Imagine what a woman with her mind - what so many women like her - could have done in other circumstances?
Bente and I have a long history, you know? We've not exactly met, but I like to think we have a special connection. Women of the world, freedom-minded souls.
I attended one of Mercier's lectures, in the last days of his tenure. The fervour, the passion… I almost signed on there and then.
I'm a godly sort enough, but the Elder's faith? It's dry. A creed of museums and dusty halls. It doesn't feel… alive.
One day I'll take the roads north, join the Explorers. Seek my fortunes, make a name for myself. You just wait!
This La Fortune fellow… there's something in his eyes. A shadow, tantalizing, thrilling almost, but dangerous.
I understand Anne Harlow's anger, but surely there are better ways to fight back than murder and plunder?
A pied-à-terre, at last! Breakfast at nine, I assume?
Transportation means travel, travel means adventure! Onward!
A variety theatre? Who knew you had such a flair for the audacious!
One does tire of hotel food, however convenient. Time for some gastronomy, I think!
At last, a temple to flavour and taste! Let us pay our devotions then!
I would like to know if the food I am enjoying at the restaurant is fresh produce.
Come, where do you normally take all your foodie tourists, show me!
Oh, I see. Very well.
Excellent choice! Oh my, the wine— I do believe I've overindulged! But that vine, that vintner.. Simply delicious!
Tall, crisp, sturdy fields of healthy grain; a sight for sore —and famished— eyes! Oh, the dishes this will make...
Fine spirits! Strong, gold, with character and... is that peat, I smell? A seal of quality, right there!
Do you mean to say your food is processed? Ugh, that has put me right off!
It's not that I oppose meat per se— I mean that would be hypocrisy— I'd just hoped to see something less fleshy. Vegetarian, perhaps.
The fish is fresh, certainly, but it's more than a little bit whiffy around here, gutted fish innards and all.
Industrial fodder? But what of the dedication, the love, the devotion to the culinary art? And I had such high hopes!
A meat factory? And here I was hoping for cuisine, art...
So many fresh products and just one dish on the menu? That won't do! Come now, let us stew the broth of imagination!
Why waste such quality spirits on poor fare? Come, grab a bottle, let us call upon Dionysus' fecund inspiration!
Excellent choice! I shall inform your cooks immediately!
Wonderful as the Archduke's Schnitzel is, I can't have it every meal! Come, we must improve this menu of yours.
Come, punters ought to be trying our new creation! Supply it to all your best restaurants!
A roaring success for a simple enough course, don't you think? Ah, I'm eager to plan our next culinary wonder!
Come to think of it, the cruise ship should still be around. You have to try those pastries! They churn up so many memories.
...mostly memories of that bronzed adonis of a chef... perhaps he will finally melt and tell us all his culinary secrets. Imagine how his buttery pastries could enrich your cafés!
Oh well, sorry for thinking people came on holidays to have fun...
Shall we? You'll see the pastries are simply scrumptious, much like the cook himself!
I didn't see much of the pleasure decks. I was too busy lounging and eating in the restaurant.
The pastries were succulent, but I'll confess the cook himself was something of a treat on the eyes as well.
Not that I'd see him much - too busy with the pastries, of course. I'll confess I fantasized a chance meeting in the dancing hall once or twice but in vain, alas.
Oooh, I'm all a-twitter! Do you think he'll remember me? Well, anyway, shall we?
I shan't be long! Do help yourself to the bar in the meantime - the cocktails are simply splendid!

I am especially sorry to say Chef was no longer there...but...I found - well the captain sort of offered (what a sweet soul!) a book of the cruise company's recipes! Let us depart so I can study it in peace!
A bit of light reading on holiday, just the way I like it!
There's something in here about a... palm tree? Ah, no, palmier! A biscuit of sorts - interesting!
And here... Yes! the Eclair! A special favourite of mine, especially with the chef's unique... touch.
A delightful journey all around! And I'm certain the destinies of the Chef and I may still be intertwined. Shall we?
Those two recipes would certainly be a great addition to your menu, but we need to verify that you have the right ingredients. Take another wine with me!
As fine a café menu as I've ever tasted!
You've a decent palate, and fine eye for presentation! It's definitely been a memorable stay. Here— by way of thanks.
Your insight proved wiser than I'd expected! A connoisseur like you will surely appreciate this excellent vintage!
Any decent afternoon stroll needs a stop by the café, a lounge in the sun with pastries and tea!
This book is a manuscript full of handwritten recipes. And it's signed... James Cook! The name of my sweetheart Chef. At least I am not leaving empty-handed!
These donuts are all about the filling! If you had had some other pastries I might have scoffed them too — like the little creamy and curvy ones aboard the cruise ship...delicious!
The chefs have talent, I must say the Archduke's Schnitzel is delectable. I presume other dishes are soon to follow?

Now I've entered and won my fair share of bake-offs, and this is no mere trifle! Rather it's the trifle to end all trifles, a 'zuppa inglese' of the culinary gods! Come, I feel the creative sugar rushing!
It's over! It's done! The trifling masterpiece of a lifetime, an ode to colour, texture and taste and - oh, I'm all atwitter!
It's all wrong! The texture, the flavour, the fragrance... It's nothing like I had expected! Sorry I couldn't be more help...Oh, what'll Her Majesty say?
I think that you need to hear about it, but I have heard terrible whisperings from crows around the tower. As we well know, heads of state have frequently of late been targets for assassination.
Murmurs of the Queen and other terrors in the same sentence, I fear some rebels are preparing a coup d'etat or some other dreadful thing for the inauguration.
Oh, look yon to the horizon! The Royal Airship is approaching! Let us strike up the fanfare!
What an occasion! The splendour, the pomp! The royal guards parading are so proud... and also attractive!
I'm thinking of putting on a small dancing revue - I'm quite the competent dancer myself! - but I'll need your help.
I had such hopes, such aspirations...
None of that drab old ballet; this would be audacious! A tribute to fine art and food! But a show needs dancers. Distinct hues and characters, I think, like a fruit salad.
Crimson berries - shows character, daring. A fine addition to this fruit bowl of a revue!
Purple vine, lounging in the sun, the face of an angel... That sense of Bacchic bliss will do wonders!
A perfect complement to our crew - sharp golden lemon, sweet of temper, zesty and dazzling under the right light!
What a lovely ensemble! A colourful, bright, sweet, exotic... Marmelade of sorts! Yes, that fits nicely: the Marmelade Revue! We'll have the audience on toast.
This venue won't do! We need something far grander, worthy of the Marmelade Revue! A place for hundreds, thousands!
You've certainly outdone yourself! The Marmelade Revue will take the city by storm - or rather skirts.
The Marmelade Revue must have costumes worthy of its name! I was thinking... Lemons! Lots and lots of lemons sown together!
I think that should about cover it. Well, so to speak - it is a revue after all.
Oh it was a roaring success! The praise, the applause... Even fan mail - here, read it!
My dear Cook was here! I told you the sea would toss him back to me. Here, hold on to this. It's the least I can do for your help. I've no doubt all my fellow Tourists will go wild for it.
The lemons, at last! Shall we?
We've not met before, have we? I am a Tourist - a holidaymaker, if you will - and I've plans to spend my vacation here!
Such a quaint place you have! It could be such a success with people like me... But you'd need to expand your public mooring - it's a tad drab for Tourists.
We Tourists are a demanding lot, but I'd be happy to help you navigate our needs, if that'd help.
Every Tourist loves a good variety theatre, but we'll ignore any venue not properly connected to the bus network.
A Tourist's concerns are two things: is the venue interesting, and can I get there without walking?
Say, how about a restaurant? But we'll need a omnibus to get there - couldn't have us walking there, now could we?
Well, enough lounging about! Let's see what the city's bus network has in store!
Goulash always was a labourer's meal - hardly dignified, too rich. But the addition of corn? Someone must congratulate this obrera!
I had tried this when I was young, but the vinegar everywhere.. ugh. Citrus is far cleaner.
I worried transportation from the Arctic would damage the meat's quality, but it's simply unctuous!
What surprises me is not that a scholar came up with this - them and their smoking. It's how delicious it turned out!
I'd expected strange things when they opened a post office in the frozen wastes, but venison? At least someone got creative from it!
So this is what comes when Enbesan tradition meets New World curiosity? Ooooh my!
Just a slurp and you can simply tell it was made to keep you awake! Tut-tut-tut, those investors.
A dash of coolness on a warm afternoon. Very left bank, very bohemian.
I'm surprised, the whale oil doesn't taste entirely terrible in there. I suppose the captain did say it was good for warding off scurvy...
Imagine a drink capable of making Enbesan Elders doze off in the sun before a service. Now that's a drink!
It's a concept dish. A beautifully presented twist on everything explorers have ever had to survive on!
They made it especially for a royal banquet in Enbesa but apparently... one of the guests stormed off, so the whole thing had to be cancelled!
Is it supposed to be a likeness of Her Majesty's sovereign head... God Save The Poor Girl if her face looks that fleshy!
Now I have it! The Eclair! After hours of baking practice. The memories of the cruise and that filling... Ah, I simply had to try it myself!
Love hearts? Pish. The Palmier's inspiration is elephant ears, see? Supposed to remind one of the old country - story goes a girl came up with it for her ailing Enbesan grampa.
A recipe inspired by a cabaret revue? Well I certainly can't let that go untried and untasted!
I was sceptical any dessert could truly convey the splendour of The Iron Tower, but this Trifle Tower dessert... A frightening extravagance worthy of a Queen!

My most loyal subject, I have an idea! Something that can stand for, perhaps come to define our present era,— a marvel to draw crowds from all the world! An Iron Tower impossibly tall. Think you can do it?
Oh, so you won't dedicate an Iron Tower to me? Well you aren't the first to snub one... imagine what it's like trying to get a bill through parliament...
Wonderful! Now choose an island worthy of bearing such a monumental and historical work!
Ah, a promising start! We look forward to the inauguration!
Skeletal, but perhaps in exactly that sense, it has all the makings of a true Wonder!
A bright dawn is coming, the opening of a new era! All must be perfect and regal - a suitable tribute to Our will!
Ah, the ingenuity, the intricacy, the sheer daring of it! We looked to the skies and claimed them for our own, that all may know: look upon Our works, and praise the Empire!
The Inauguration will be upon us soon. We trust you will satisfy the following requirements with due expediency.
We trust it needs not be explained that the fulfillment of these requests is essential to ensure our presence at the Inauguration.
Perfectly suitable. We trust there is a view on the Tower? Capital!
Ah, excellent choice! Adventure, glory...and most importantly, romance! I shall no doubt dream of my love-to-be tucked away in his distant court.

Ah, excellent choice! Bente Jorgensen we have heard from the keeper of the scrolls, is a distant distant relation of mine, and there is such enthusiasm and brightness in these travel recollections, we may faint!
An intriguing choice, certainly. I am not sure it is ideal holiday reading, rather macabre if anything.
Too long being an administrator! This selection is... dry, dreary, dull! We are supposed to be at holiday!
Is this what we are supposed to read during our stay?
She seems eager to please, competent and discreet. Essential qualities in a maid. Good show.
What an arrogant little so-and-so you've chosen, like my dreadful mother telling us how to dress... Well, if she can pour tea I can still take her.
We've better sense than to take on a maid driven by selfishness and whimsy! We shall be forced now to make our own arrangements!
Well now, let us review. Invitations? Sir Archibald will provide. Accommodation, staff, the reception...

Oh dear, we forgot the banquet! Never fear. You, dear steward, will provide. It must be grandiose, worthy of the Iron Tower! And of course a mighty finale: a patriotic trifle of momentous proportions!
Something intricate and festive, unforgettable! The world will remember this day - let your pud commemorate that - the Trifle Tower of pastry!
The day of departure draws nigh, but We fear dear old Archie stills frets for Our security. Your city is secure, is it not?
A misunderstanding cleared up, a secure ceremony, cleaner streets... An all-around wonderful job!
At last, the moment of truth approaches! Our stratospheric saviour of burnished iron awaits! To the Inauguration!
What a splendid venue! The perfect shrine for this momentous occasion. Let the Inauguration... begin!
Ah, the fervour of a loving throng's adoration! What monarch has not dreamed of leaving such an imprint upon the ages of Time? Today, We make History!
Pray, commemorate the moment - let all future times remember this instant!
Perhaps it is time to open the banquet? We do start to feel peckish. Tell us, what have you concoted to honour this grand occasion?
You simply must tell Our palace chef your secret! This meal was truly divine!
Seldom have we eaten so well. Improvements could be made, certainly, but that dessert? A marvel indeed!
Perhaps we should have entrusted this delicate task to someone better suited to cooking than an administrator. Ah, well...
It is Our pleasure and honour to declare this restaurant... open! Let all savour the splendourous dishes concocted here!
We have requested Our chefs deliver the recipe for Our favourite dessert. This should should help your restaurant regain some... repute.
Before We leave, pray provide Us with some cloth. No, no questions - it is to be a surprise, a reward!
The quality is exceptional, naturally?
And now, fresh off the looms, our tribute - our thanks for your service, your diligence and your loyalty!
A fitting tribute to the architect of such masterful works - this city, its glories and triumphs... The world deserves to know your quality, my loyal servant: the highest of all!
Duty calls, I fear - but next time I stop by High Clarence Hall for tea, I’ll ask Archie to send you an invite!
Do you like my airship? Splendid isn't it?
It has a special exterior design commissioned just for this occasion.
We must say the ariship has been entirely to our satisfaction when it comes to appliances and amenities.
We're only waiting for you to come to the ceremony. Do you really want to make your Queen wait?
Now, count to 3! 1...2... and 3! Unveil the surprise, dear Subject!
… I'm telling you, the butter… the butler... the butler did it!
Another one, please - and I want you to shake it this time, rather than stir it!
… called me an uncultured trout! For dipping croissant in coffee!
Look, there's a heart in the coffee foam! Do you think she did it just for me?
Oof, I couldn't possibly! Could I? Oh, very well, one more slice!
Oh! And er...a carafe of the expensive sauvignon, there's a fellow!
… create a distraction and I'll nab one of the spoons for a souvenir!
…the first wave is truffles, yes, but then… is it garangal or ginger?
There's a line, yes, but I know someone who knows someone...
One of the beams is actually gold and only painted iron!
It would be a great and humbling honour to be chosen to be Her Majesty's maid...
Rather knocks you sideways with the peatiness, this one— pass me the spittoon if you would.
… no, they're of a mind to outlaw all the speakeasies back home. 'Dry state' they call it…
I do believe I may be ever-so-slightly tipsy!
Well I'm partial to both tweed and silk, if you understand my meaning.
… took my placard and wanted to lock me up! Fortunately sister dearest was there to smooth things out.
One more for the road? —at least we'll be walking home in straight lines!
… not leaving until the closing bell tolls!
It goes like this: a Coronian lord walks into a bar…ouch.
Put it on my tab, will you? We'll be coming here a lot.
I'd no idea there were so many strains of bean!
No no no - milk before the tea!
… oh yes, and a whopping great whirlywhip of cream on top, if you have it!
Dip your hat, quick! There he is again at that table soixante six.
(coughing) Oh Jemima! That was the salt you buffoon!
It would be like strata— one palmier, then filling, then another palmier!
We'll take it strong, I think! All ready for a day on the tour buses!
The combination looks… intriguing. Might I have a bite?
That sauce is lip-smackingly… [blissful sigh]
Ah, but you cannot leave yet! You've not tried our famous pudding!
I wonder… might I change my order? That dish over there looks far tastier.
No table? But… we're practically regulars! It's us, you know us!
Ugh, the nerve! They could at least make an effort to learn the language.
"You are a tourist, he is a holidaymaker, but I am a traveller!"
...A nice gesture that bread comes gratis.
We breathe out, trees breathe in, they breathe out, we breathe in...
I love the feel of the crisp bark wrapped inside my arms.
Funny...we chop down trees so we can build a place to plant them again.
This way, we can give a tiny bit back to the rainforest.
I can't cut it down... I can't— it's too beautiful and it's ages old.
Strange sort of smell in there, isn't there?
.. I'm telling you there are corporate interests you don't know about at play...
... Well sometimes, yes, but I prefer organic and natural myself.
Tube 54 is empty! You didn't mix it into the solvent, did you?!
... nip in and see if that's their latest line, there's a girl!
Oh, I doubt my sister could see herself eating here. She's always so dreadfully humble.
… white for fish, red for venison, sauternes for dessert - unless you…
... don't worry about the bill, I've opened a credit line in Father's name…
… think the chef would object to an offer of employment to replace Teddy out at The Grange?…
… no, it's bad form! Better leave the bottle unfinished and order a new one for each dish.
I don't suppose we could take this food away with us!
… thought I might try it myself once! But I'm more of a critic than a craftswoman, really.
… think of it: without this tower, this restaurant, hundreds would be without employment!
How long before they build one back home for sheer spite?
What of the birds? They'll fly straight into it!
Two hours queue! Be a dear and fetch me a drink, will you?
… and they could fly around it with a great banner, and…
I heard they employed special workers, from the New World - unafraid of heights, you see!
How far do you think they had to dig to make it sturdy?
Imagine your hat blowing off up there!
How… many… more… steps?
Ladies and Gentlemen, welcome to the Phantom Tour!
See the city's strangest corners and hear its dark legends!
First stop, the infamous plaza where…
Built at the turn of the century, it was rumoured…
This one is much older, dating back to annotiquity…
And if you turn left you'll notice a dark smudge of the smoke is still there.
… where Humphrey Smidge, Lord Hunt, infamously buried…
… a frantic collector of all things Imperium, including a peculiar theatrical mask…
It was torn down and rebuilt, but the stones still remember the weeping…
If you crane your necks down that street there you'll notice…
Now if the two gentlemen at the back would let us resume…
… where celebrated composer Erich Zann was last heard fiddling in the night.
They say she was fleeing witch-hunts in her native Corona, and so came to this street quite destitute.
When it was torn down they found ruins below the cellar, far older than…
That window, over there? It opens onto a room that doesn't exist. Can't be found from inside the building.
Beyond that wall there stretched Old Maggie's Garden. Now she was rumoured…
Scientists debate how the stones were brought from so far away, but legend goes…
And last but certainly not least, the notorious…
This concludes our tour. If you enjoyed it please do remember your guide. I ain't doing this free you know.
Oh and here we are, could someone wake the two gentlemen at the back?
The first thing I would do is attempt to transform those grotesque clothes Her Majesty always seems to wear...
The Queen's Maid, my goodness, I can't wait to see my stupid friends' jealous faces.

The Gazebo Plaza is an ornament belonging to the Luxury Park category. Open the Classic Tab of the Beautification Menu to find it. Donald Bader’s tastes are highly specific and he will accept no other ornament.

Obsessed with the Shopping Arcade’s promise of profit, Donald Bader tasks you with commandeering office space amid the existing Engineer apartments for a so-called ‘market research lab‘. He wants to develop new patents there — or as he calls them, the needs of tomorrow!
With the office completed, and Miss Jenny (who told you she is in fact called Theodora) hired, Donald is extremely pleased with himself, and rewards you by letting you choose the very first patent.
Due to the theft of the required goods for the patents, your research has come to a halt. It seems things will remain that way until you deliver the new goods to Miss Jenny (Theodora).

My guru, here’s a pitch: customers are demanding, but gullible — that’s great for us! They’ll have you think they want convenience, luxury, quality... but what they really want is to be led to what they want. We had them on toast with the toaster! I say exploit the moment. Use it. The suckers are salivating for a new gadget, so let’s provide one!

Cunning, right?
Electrifying. The Galeria Baderette sings modernity. Add another machine!
I think the Galeria should be a place of glamour! We need something luxurious!

Ah, great minds, my guru! So, another culinary gadget! They've had a toasty slice, let's provide them a whole darn meal! Everyone’s got to eat!

Let's get their stomachs grumbling, then offer them a gadget to sate their hunger! But, what could that be...?
A new gadget? A convenient cooling device for those without room for an ice cellar!
Switch it up. We've built towers, now people need a convenient way to clean them...
Replace the icebox with a Refrigerator! Of course, my guru! I see the potential! A gadget that opens its doors to a whole new set of culinary products – the bigger we make it, the better!
Agree to develop the refrigerator patent
Of course, my guru! We’ve built the real-estate — now we get to sell the suckers Vacuum Cleaners to deal with the additional hassle! Ha, wait for the thank you cards their wives will send me!
Agree to develop the vacuum cleaner patent

Luxury! Yes, my guru — we model the opulent lifestyle, and they’ll labour under the illusion that they can have it all — if only they work hard enough. Hilarious!

What did you have in mind? The toaster numbers surely speak for themselves — something culinary?
Or something complementary? People need something to eat off after all!
If we want to sell luxury, we need business accessories. A high-end bag?

Oh, Crockery! Yes, why reinvent the wheel when we can just slap a new coat of paint on it and sell it! Let’s make it a staple piece — the good china for special occasions.

They’ll need to be of the finest material, of course — the more they break, the more we’ll sell!
Agree to develop the crockery patent

Maybe a Briefcase? I could certainly use one for all these darn documents I have to lug around... Why not be a little self-indulgent for a change!

I do love a product that sells itself — every bag hanging off an arm is a walking advertisement!
Agree to develop the briefcase patent

Mr. Bader has convinced a group of bemused citizens to take part in what he calls a 'marketing survey'. He hopes these survey subjects can unearth the next lucrative patent for him. He’s invited you to his office to hear their survey responses and determine the best course for business.

The marketing survey did not go as Donald intended. But, knowing little of scientific rigour, he is unbothered and wants to you to analyze the results regardless. As long as there’s a product at the end he can sell, he’ll call it a success.
With the vanity screen chosen and the poster distributed, Donald demands that you start production!

A vandal is tagging the vanity screen posters around the city, with a red and white logo of a falling man! Mr. Bader will not have his property defaced, and has tasked you with apprehending the criminal.

The market research survey results are in! Where did Miss Jenny put my darn notes... Oh well, don’t need em'! We had some really dull responses. I cherry-picked the data:

maybe 80% want fancy furniture, 75% like luxury stuff, and 20-odd percent just want a drink.

So, my guru, what do you think will make us money?
Furniture, quality, and a drink?... Um, a mini bar?
Actually, I'd like to hear what Theodora has to say about the results.

Ha-ha, I like it! Not everyone has a Miss Jenny around to get em’ a Gin and Tonic, huh? This is a very good ratio, by the way. Miss Jenny, do you think people want a mini-bar? Speak up, what’s your take? No wrong answers.
Listen to Miss Jenny

What do I think? Well, I must say the 'method' of analysis skewed the results, so I'm intrigued by the percentages you uncovered, Mr. Bader! Well done.

If we consider our survey responses, I’d say they want a product to help them personalize their skyscraper apartments, and provide a little privacy, while others perceive the Galleria as rather uninclusive and would prefer a range of affordable products.
Maybe a Vanity Screen. It’s decorative, grants privacy and, well, affordability is relative.
A Vanity Screen? That seems rather specific. Maybe for some that could be a fit, but...
It’s hard to define a single product. Maybe our focus should be personalization and affordability.
Yes, we have a very diverse customer base. I could write a patent proposal and...
Continue

Miss Jenny, there’s no pleasing everyone! We’re here to make a product that sells, and I’ve run out of talk time!

My Guru, you’ve taught me to follow my instincts, so let's just go in hard on the Vanity Screens! Decorative, perfect to hide behind, and really, we don’t want every kind in our Arcades now, do we? So make it pricey!
Unlock the vanity screen patent

Well done us! Now all we need is a flashy poster and they’ll be craving a vanity screen in no time! My guru — we need a slogan! We could play on a sense of luxury or fun — make it rhyme!

'Galeria Baderette... ‘
”...the height of etiquette”
”...life is a cabaret”

Ah, how creative! They’ll love it. Now all that’s missing is a picture of the vanity screen...

Miss Jenny would you... no not that one! The other one! Yes. Good...
See the poster
The height of etiquette!
Life is a cabaret!
“What kind of products would you like to see in our stores?” That’s broad... Well, I moved into a skyscraper apartment. The view is nice and all, but the interiors all look the same...
“How could your current situation be improved?” Right now? A drink! Sorry. err... Look, I work in an office, and we’re shoulder-to-shoulder in there. There’s just no privacy...
“How do you perceive our brand?”How can I put this... It’s very fancy and grand, but... it’s also expensive and intimidating? I feel a little out of place in that swish Arcade...
A fellow with red and white paint, you say? Yeah, I saw one. Heading down to the docks. He had a proper moustache, too.
Lying on top of the crates is a bundle of clothes. Among them you find a sizeable fake moustache, a brown wig, and a long blue dress...

Someone with a moustache? You'll need to be more specific... See, I saw a red-haired woman a little earlier wearing a beautiful blue dress — I wish I had one like it! Now that I can recall! She was feeding the birds.

The flock of birds is pecking away happily. As you shoo them away, you discover a note placed beneath their feed. It reads: “Mr. Bader, looking for me is like trying to find a needle in a haystack. Give up and go back to sleep in your furniture store.”

There is a pile of red and white paint buckets. One of them has a note stuck to it. It reads: “Take the paints. This is all futile — your conceited product will see the light of day anyway. Enjoy your shallow victory while it lasts. Regards, an angry worker.”

Miss Jenny should be in her office, somewhere near an Engineer skyscraper.
Just wait and listen to Miss Jenny until she meets with a mystery character.
Mr. Brokeman, Donald's lawyer, left his suitcase behind before boarding a cruise ship. You'll likely find it at the harbour.

Mr. Bader has been made aware of inconsistencies in the office’s budget reports. He suspects that Miss Jenny (a.k.a. Theodora) might be using the money for her own purposes. Not only would she be disobeying his instructions, but he’s also worried that she might be leaking industrial secrets, endangering the worth of his brand. He's asked you to spy on her.

You followed Miss Jenny to a private meeting with a mystery man by the name of "Mr. Brokeman." There you uncovered that he had promised to supply her with goods for a secret patent project she appears to have undertaken without permission. Taking a picture of the meeting would be the perfect proof of her deception for Mr. Bader.

Having caught Miss Jenny (real name Theodora) red-handed at her private meeting with a broker, she implores you to hear her out before reporting anything back to Mr. Bader. You may as well listen, as either way you have photographic evidence of her secret agenda, and if you still aren't persuaded, you can always grass her up afterwards.

Miss Jenny – or rather, Theodora - has persuaded you that her female-oriented product could help modernise society, and provide a much-needed first step towards female emancipation. She’s asked that you provide her with the oils she needs to complete her patent — but you'll have to hurry and deliver them before Mr. Bader catches you in the act!

Donald is outraged that his employees would have the gall to make deals behind his back — with his own money at that! But he's got a plan, the first step of which is to cut Mr. Brokeman's holiday short, and bring him into the office for a chat. He's delegated that task to you.

Seeing as his money has already been spent on the research, Mr. Bader has decided that he might as well try and finalise the product. He intends to recoup any monetary loss by having Mr. Brokeman issue a brutal lawsuit against his employee, Miss Jenny. To file the suit, you first have to prove your loyalty to Bader by locating Mr. Brokeman’s briefcase, which contains the necessary documents.

Secrecy was my last resort! I pitched my patent to Mr. Bader, used reasoned arguments — said this would attract women; customers! — in their droves to the shopping arcades... But he flat-out refused. He said it was an empty market!”

Well he’s wrong. It’s only an empty market because women have yet to be allowed in! This product would be a gateway for us!
Keep listening

I’d hoped the prospect of a whole new customer demographic would sway him, but this could be so much more...! Men shouldn’t hold a monopoly on the modern. Modern conveniences can be tools for social emancipation. Products like mine can normalise women running their own budgets, having agency in the world of commerce.

The projected sales figures might yet convince him, but I desperately need to finish the prototype first. Will you help me?
You're damn right Theodora, something needs to change. I'm in.
Miss Jenny! Using Mr. Bader’s funds for personal gain?! I have to report this!
I must hurry! Oh, I do hope the harbour was a good spot to pick...
It really would have been preferable to acquire the oils on my own terms, but he seems trustworthy.
For someone so focused on modernisation, Mr. Bader is peculiarly blind to the future. ‘Women don’t shop!’. Well, I wonder why?!
So much on my mind, and it’s all spilling out... Come on, Theodora, take a breath and hurry along! It'll all be over soon...
Psst, 'Dora!
Oh, Mr. Brokeman! There you are! Very punctual...
Dora... Please, forgive me. I... I don’t have the oils you asked for.
...Mr. Bader's doing, I presume?
Yes, I... he’s having me watched. I can feel it. I want to help, but I can’t lose my livelihood over this... You understand?
WAIT, WHAT WAS THAT!? A CAMERA FLASH!? OH NO... Theodora, you were followed!

I knew Bader'd be furious but... sweet mercy. I yield! I promise, I’ll spill everything!

Just get me out of the water!
Drowning was his idea of a joke? My poor heart... You know, I can’t say I’m surprised. He always has had his own ways of dealing with insubordination... At least I'm still alive. That's something.

There are five factors influencing a population's happiness: goods satisfaction, pollution, peace, working conditions and the news. Alter those to achieve the desired increase in happiness.
Temporary modifiers that decrease your workers' happiness due to your earlier decisions may be active right now. Waiting for them to time out may also help you reach the desired happiness level.

The success of the Galeria Baderette Shopping Arcade has set a precedent for the future of consumerism — a founding myth for a new era, its daring promise of endless growth exemplified by rising sales and towering skyscrapers. To ensure his place in history, Donald Bader dreams of a unique monument: the gigantic Skyline Tower. And he has entrusted you with making it a reality.

With the construction of the Skyline Tower underway, some of the workers have expressed a fear of heights. Mr. Bader wishes to avoid construction delays, and has asked you to knock some sense into them.

Following reports that some workers at the Skyline Tower had expressed a fear of heights, you promised to find brave volunteers in the city to help them safely though their shifts on the higher levels. To fulfil this promise, you need to find replacements before the workers' shifts start. Failing to do so could end in considerable disappointment.

The lack of basic security measures at the construction site led to a tragic accident: a worker fell and suffered serious injuries. His fellow workers are demanding to speak to the person in charge, and Donald seems to think you might be the best one to handle the conversation.

Following the recent accident at the Skyline Tower, your workers have been asking serious questions about your health and safety measures. To ensure the emergency services can react fast in times of need, you've promised to build a hospital close to the construction site. Your workers welcome the idea — if indeed you follow through on your promise.

The vigilante that's been interfering with Donald Bader's plans has stolen some materials from the construction site, leaving yet another ominous note behind. Mr. Bader believes it can only be a worker causing the mischief, and intends to make an example of them by teaching them a lesson. You still have time to find a more delicate solution.

With the strikes causing delays to the Skyline Tower's construction, Bader suggests you negotiate with the workers to get them back on track. A nice, generous gesture might increase their happiness, even if it’s just a temporary boost to the spirit.

The workers in your city are very unhappy with the way they’ve been treated, and have organised a strike at the Skyline Tower construction site. The only way to compel them to resume their work is to increase the general happiness of your city.

Miss Jenny (a.k.a. Theodora) insists that checking the integrity of the Skyline Tower is a vital step in the construction process, yet one which Donald Bader seems determined to ignore, whatever the risks. Now that she has your ear, though, you should be perfectly capable of making an informed choice for the project by yourself.

Theodora’s concerns were well-founded! The structural integrity of the Skyline Tower has been compromised by its height and weight, and cracks are forming on the lower levels! If only the chief investor hadn't been so stingy in sourcing quality materials! Theodora, however, believes that if you act fast, the Tower can still be saved. She sees a couple of possible solutions.

Theodora was right! Having heard strange groaning noises, the workers discovered more signs that the tower’s structural integrity was failing, as it transpires some of the columns are starting to bend! Theodora implores you to act fast, as the tower's core structure must be strengthened.

Your recent choices have culminated in a worst-case scenario: The tower is now highly unstable, and Miss Jenny is nowhere to be found. In his time of crisis, Donald turns desperately to you, demanding a solution.

The security measures you implemented were vital in preventing complete disaster, but the tower is not yet saved. Theodora has contacted you. She’s working on a plan to strengthen the structure — but to implement it, she requires your help.

Theodora’s predictions have come to fruition once more — the Skyline Tower has reached a height too great for its structure! Donald faltered at the groans of his wavering monument and, in the absence of Miss Jenny, has turned to you for an inexpert solution!

With the tower threatening to fall at any moment, Donny J. Bader is frantically searching for his Miss Jenny. He is concerned that his lead engineer and all-round crutch might still be in the tower. Convinced that she is his last hope, he charges you with making sure that, at the very least, she is not in immediate danger.

You found Theodora, surrounded by workers, near the crumbling tower. She seems uncharacteristically out-of-patience with Donald, and curses his blind ignorance — an ignorance that even prevented him from seeing who she truly was all this time. You should give her the chance to reveal her true identity.

Theodora, having revealed herself as a humble worker-cum-engineer (defying the social ladder) — and also the vigilante who's been trying to stop Donald's irresponsible construction practices during the Skyline Tower project — has come through for you once more. She's been preparing a last-minute solution to stabilise the wobbling tower once and for all. To implement it, she's going to require additional materials from you.

The Skyline Tower is a momentous achievement that will forever define the skyline of your city — yet its construction was subject to many issues and incidents. Theodora insists that you take stock of the many mistakes made along the way, so that any future construction projects won't suffer the same.

Look, it’s not like we ain’t used to the heights — we are, more than most — but that means we know how dangerous it can get. One mis-step can change everything... This tower, it’s higher than we’ve ever built.

And that brand logo... it's unlucky — it's spreading fear! We don’t need a reminder of it plastered on the walls... All it takes is one fall...

The Skyline Tower’s making history — the heights Mr. Bader envisions have never been reached before! But such a construction is unprecedented. I fear the structure isn’t strong enough to support its own weight, or withstand the adverse wind conditions up there. The architect had all the solutions for these issues, but Mr. Bader knew they would cost, so he's taken several shortcuts instead.

I strongly advise conducting a survey to verify the building's structural integrity. That way, if my fears are well-founded, we can act.

[AssetData(137516) Text]

Here's a summary: the lower levels are showing wear, and some cracks have formed near the entrance. We’ve also had a partial cave-in on the fourth floor. The weight and winds have combined to weaken the foundation, and with every floor we add, we compound the problem.

We must strengthen the base by adding shoring devices — a wooden support system to provide additional load-bearing support. But I’ll need quite a lot of wood to make it work, and Mr. Bader certainly isn’t prepared to pay...

We must strengthen them! We could fortify them by cementing the base, effectively doubling their size, or by adding structural support through shoring devices.

I think neither option will be the end of our woes, but they might at least buy us some time!

I’ve taken the time to gauge the situation. I’ve talked to workers and passing citizens, and there’s a lot of contention surrounding the Skyline Tower. Due to its immense height, the workers have felt that, throughout the construction, their safety has been at risk. A lot of citizens, too, are unhappy with the shadow the tower casts across the city.

In their interest, we want you to undersign a bill to guarantee a limit of one Skyline Tower per city. This is a non-negotiable demand.
Continue
One per city? Ha, and here I thought I was making a unique tower! No, of course! It’ll be a hit in every city, and so long as my name's on all of them, I’m in. Where do I sign?
Agree to the limit of one Skyline Tower per city

Good. But there’s more. Skyscrapers are a true wonder, of that there is no doubt. They are a symbol of modernity and advancement, but they're also an ode to money and power. They reach far above any other residence, public place, or church... and our fear is that by elevating one part of the population — those with means — the already existing divide within our society will only deepen.

The Skyline Tower should stand for something. By virtue of its uniqueness, it has the eyes of the world on it, and we have the chance to make use of that attention. We demand the Tower be dedicated to a single cause.

My Skyline Tower, a messenger for a good cause? Well surely such a — what’s the word — philanthropic move would get people’s attention? You know, that could actually be a good advertisement for Galleria Bader... Er, well, anyway...

How about something to do with... poverty? Sickness? Erm, maybe it'd be better if you chose the charity?

A local investor has big dreams of building the city skywards. The invention of elevators has filled him with excitement, and he’s eager to join you in paving the way towards skyscraper construction.
With enough elevators in stock, nothing is standing in the way of building your first skyscraper.
The keen local investor sees shopping arcades as the next big investment opportunity. A department store would be the perfect start. Others will surely follow.

Who wouldn’t be disappointed when looking out their 14th floor windows just to face a brick wall? Having a panoramic view of the city makes for a much better view, and would certainly attract more people!
You've built first level skyscrapers, but why stop there? Donald wants you to go even higher!
Any Engineer or Investor residence can be upgraded into a skyscraper. They only need to be fully populated.
The Department Store requires the input goods for its design patent to be within range. Make sure you have a warehouse nearby. The green street overlay shows you where input goods can be acquired.
The green street overlay also shows you which skyscrapers will have their shopping arcade need fulfilled.
Skyscraper residents like to have an unobstructed, panoramic view when looking through their windows.
Having smaller skyscrapers nearby supports the "Panorama Effect". Skyscrapers that are taller, or of equal height reduces the effect.
To achieve an intense Panorama Effect, build five level 1 skyscrapers around one level 2 skyscraper.
As soon as a skyscraper, whether Engineer or Investor, is fully populated, you can upgrade it to the next level.
Engineer skyscrapers can go up to level 3, while investor skyscrapers can go up to level 5.
For skyscrapers, you need elevators. And elevators are produced in the assembly line, a new multifactory.
In a Multifactory, you can choose the industrial patent it'll produce.

In Multifactories like the assembly line, you can change the product being produced on the fly.
But Elevators are exactly what we need right now, so let's just leave it as is.

Here you see all assembly line patents. Right now, only one is available, but you can unlock new ones later.
Click on the first patent to jump directly to it.
Here, you can see which input goods are necessary to produce this industrial patent. Choose the Elevators now.
Shopping Arcades are a new building type: they act like public services, but consume input goods! The input goods required depend on the chosen design patent. Start with a department store.
When selecting a Shopping Arcade like the Department Store and choosing a new design patent, you require different input goods. So, make sure you have a warehouse within range!
Currently, this department store is not selling anything. Open the shopping catalogue to choose a design patent.

Here you can see every Department Store design patent. Right now, only one is available, but you can unlock new ones later.
Click on the first one to jump directly to it.

In principle, all shopping arcades act like public services, but they consume input goods. As long as the selected design patent can be produced, it will fulfill the skyscraper residents' need for this type of shopping arcade, no matter which product you've selected.

Depending on a design patent's ingredients, a Shopping Arcade will require different input goods.
Make sure you have a warehouse nearby, that stocks those goods.
Aside from fulfilling the need for a Department Store, it also has a beneficial effect on any residents that live nearby.

These tips apply to Shopping Arcades:
1. The green street overlay indicates where input goods can be fetched from.
2. The green street overlay also indicates which Skyscrapers will have the need for a Shopping Arcade fulfilled.
3. The circle indicates which residences benefit from the current patent.

Skyscraper residents like to have an unobstructed, panoramic view when looking out their windows.
Having smaller skyscrapers around them supports the "Panorama Effect"; skyscrapers that are taller or of equal height reduces the effect.

The stronger the "Panorama Effect", the higher the population within the skyscraper will be!

When you select a skyscraper, smaller skyscrapers are colored in green.
Taller or equal height skyscrapers are colored in brown.

Click on the "?" in the skyscraper menu to get more information on the Panorama Effect.

GOING UP!

LUXURY BRAND GETS BRANDED!

Tree juice on tap! This viscous and versatile substance is harvested by cutting a groove into the bark of a tree and collecting the sap. The trick is to leave enough behind for the tree to heal itself and produce more.
A coveted raw material for crafting beautiful furniture. With its rich colouration, it's sleek but sturdy to the touch — difficult to work with, but rewarding to a master. A carpenter’s delight!

This sticky gunk is just one in a long line of adhesive materials — whether it be birch-bark tar, pine resin, or beeswax, there has always been a need to stick one thing to another. So, apply, connect, leave to dry and... Oh no! I put the wrong sides together!

The shiny finish of lacquer often comes in a wide array of colors. Applied to a surface like wood or metal, it provides a glossy or matt protective coating, adding more than a touch of quality and luxury.

A pure form of alcohol, ethanol is fermented, distilled, and stored by the barrel, and as a universal solvent, has a wide range of applications beyond recreation — as an antiseptic, or fuel for example.

Thankfully, the use of celluloid has now replaced that of elephant ivory in the manufacture of billiard balls — a shapeshifting, chemical wonder! Simply liquefy, pour into any mold, wait, and ta-da — dolls? A mantelpiece clock? The only limit is your imagination!

This sticky, sugary, elastic snack is infused with the sweet and spicy flavors of cinnamon — for a little while, anyway. The medical advisory board of High Clarence Hall advise that it should be spat out once the enjoyment has passed, to avoid the agglomeration of indissolubles in the lower abdomen.

An engineering marvel that makes every new feat of skyward construction possible— I say, imagine having to take the stairs fifty storeys! Here's hoping the bellboy isn't rude, the muzak is innocuous and you aren't trapped in there for three days with a dishcloth salesman...

This portable, click-clacking quill-and-ink-substitute stamps perfectly-formed pigmented letters onto crisp office paper. So, cheerio spidery scrawl, like hieroglyphs to decipher! — that handwriting business was so dreadfully 1800!

Uniform in shape, size and taste, these afternoon delights tumble off the assembly line in their dozens — and if they survive the landing, soon disappear off in their boxes. Keep out of reach of children, or else you might end up with just a handful of crumbs!

Ah, toys! Look at her, for instance — chubby face, rosy cheeks, angelic locks! Simply the perfect gift for itsy-bitsy grandchildren. They will be delighted! Most of them, anyway... Some might be terrified.

This fully automated breakfast machine is, apparently, calibrated perfectly for the toast that’s ‘just right’ — simply pop in a slice, wait, and soon you’ll smell the delightful scent of perfectly toasted bread! If you like your bread rare or well-done, look elsewhere.

Feel good about having guests again! Set the table for any occasion — a cosy breakfast, a quick lunch, a fancy dinner party — then leave the dirty dishes for the next day! Or the one after that... Or just throw them out and buy some more!

No more sweeping things under the rug! This machine removes dirt in no time. Five minutes until the guests arrive? No problem! It'll huff and puff and leave the apartment clean as a new dime. It can even tackle the bigger stains! Sick of the cat, the kids, the wife or husband? You know what to do!

Tired of going up and down the stairs to the ice cellar at garden parties? Dashing to the iceman for your icebox, or worse still, waiting for that big snow? Imagine ice every day, all year 'round! Spoiled food? Yesterday’s worry! A perfectly iced glass of summer strawberry and cucumber? Coming right up!

A superior leather attaché for people with all-too-important business to attend to. Perfect for legal documents, top secret papers, diamonds, and cash bribes — all the essentials in one place! But for goodness' sake, don't leave it lying around.

What an electrifying design! An elegant and well-made brass stand with that distinctive emerald glass shade we've all come to associate with serious work — simply tug the pull-chain switch, adjust your glasses, and pore over the case notes.

A divisive piece of furniture to compartmentalise sections of a room, ornament, act as a windbreak, or indeed, afford you the necessary privacy to change out of your trousers. Princess Qing swears by it! Simply fold and move as needed!

The centrepiece of any office is surely also the most important. Fashioned of wood that is rich, imposing and solid, it is adorned with fine brass knobs that give the desk a rather severe countenance overall — although they do say life's best friendships thrive on tough love...

Capriciously soft and inviting, this regal restbunk's drapes are in fact a practical consideration: they keep out the cold in drafty towers, offer privacy in shared bedchambers, and shield late risers and vampires from the morning sun!

These chic leather loungeables will enhance the look of any office or living space — your guests won't even need to sit on them to understand how important you are! But when you do sit, you'll feel every cent of the luxury they promised — whether it's a quick siesta, or that lengthy late-night business chat.

For optimal use, apply this carbon-based black paste to your teeth twice or thrice a day and scrub vigorously with a brush! You can even brush your tongue if you wish, though we'll leave that decision entirely up to you...

A synthetic surfactant, this all-rounder is the cleansing agent to remove blemishes big or small. Whether you mop, scrub, or wash, it’ll smell citrusy fresh — and take your skin off if you're not careful!

A portable splash of fiery red for the perfect cupid's bow. Once the preserve only of actresses and undesirables, lipstick now heralds a new era of emancipation for women — suffragettes walking arm-in-arm — who have the freedom of the arcades!

A moisturising lotion that conjures images of groves of citrus and pleasant afternoons, it's soft and gentle on the skin, and promises the secrets of eternal youth — long-term effects unknown, please read the small print, terms and conditions apply, may contain traces of nuts.

The discerning gentleman has a duty — nay! — an obligation to the upkeep of his hair, real or otherwise, and the concealment of the first sign of the dreaded grey... Apply liberally to shape, hue and style your moustaches too! For removal, a companion detergent is available at all respectable retailers...

Corky Jr. getting the better of you again? Don't worry, it's not the cognac! What you need is practice, old sport! So chalk up your cue and get set with this heavy-set game table with a fetching green baize. Ivory-free balls means more tusk on the walls!

A beautiful, shapely wooden instrument to play when you're feeling blue — play it well, and it may produce breathtaking melodies; play it badly, and well... may you benefit from your neighbour's energetic percussion through the paper-thin wall!

This fine-flavoured brandy requires only a select strain of grapes. The acidic, thin wine they make is virtually undrinkable — but give it two loving years to age, and the result is romance in a glass. Warm, flavourful, digestive!

Skyscrapers

Both Engineer and Investor residences can be upgraded to skyscrapers.
This is only possible once they have full population, and all basic needs have been fulfilled.
Engineer skyscrapers can have up to three levels, while investor skyscrapers can have up to five levels. Each level brings with it new needs for their residents.

Skyscrapers have significant maintenance costs. Manage your income and expenditure accordingly!
Building Skyscrapers

Select any Engineer or Investor residence and click on the button to add a skyscraper level. This will require elevators, which can be produced in the assembly line.

You can also remove skyscraper levels, eventually turning the skyscraper back into a regular residence.

Once built, you can change the appearance of each level by clicking the brush icon.

Tip: Hold while having a skyscraper selected to see all skyscrapers at the same level.
Panorama Effect — Benefits

Skyscraper residents like to have an unobstructed, panoramic view when looking out of their windows. With this in mind, you can create Panorama Effects on skyscrapers.

The Panorama Effect of a skyscraper increases the population that can live in it, and reduces its maintenance cost.
Panorama Effect Strength

There are, in total, five different strengths of Panorama Effect, all of which increase the population of a particular skyscraper.
The effect grows in strength based on the number of smaller skyscrapers around it.
Note that you will not be punished for maintaining no Panorama Effect: the skyscraper will still have the regular population amount.
Panorama Effect — Radius
Skyscrapers in a Radius

Each individual skyscraper counts other skyscrapers within a certain radius when calculating its Panorama Effect. The higher that skyscraper is, the bigger its radius will be.
Regular residences are not taken into account!

Calculation of the Panorama Effect
Select different skyscrapers to see how and which neighbours are tinted with colours.
Select different skyscrapers to see which of those around them are highlighted.
Example with Level 2 skyscraper: the starting value is 2, and the sum of all modifiers is 4.

Green:
Smaller skyscraper, acts like a +1 modifier.

Brown:
Taller skyscraper, acts like a -1 modifier.
Skyscraper of equal height, acts like a -1 modifier.

No colour:
Is too far away, has no effect.
Is not a skyscraper, has no effect.

The sum of all modifiers determines the Panorama Effect that the selected skyscraper will get.
This will never go below zero, or above five.
Assembly Lines
Assembly Lines are multifactories that can produce industrial patents.

The Parts Catalogue allows you to switch the industrial patent that's being produced on the fly. It can be accessed from the building menu. Different input goods will be required based on the selected patent.
Artisan Workshops
Artisan Workshops are Multifactories that allow you to produce artisanal wares.
The Craft Catalogue allows you to switch the artisanal wares being produced on the fly. It can be accessed from the building menu. Different input goods will be required based on the selected patent.
Orchards
Orchards are Multifactories that allow you to produce natural products from trees, similar to the lumberjack's hut.
The Orchard Catalogue allows you to switch the natural product that's being produced on the fly. It can be accessed from the building menu.
Chemical Plants
Chemical Plants are multifactories that allow you to produce chemical formulas.

The Formula Codex allows you to switch the chemical formula that's being produced on the fly. It can be accessed from the building menu. Different input goods will be required based on the selected patent.
Shopping Arcades
Store Types

Shopping Arcades function like public services, but consume input goods. The input goods required depend on which design patent is currently active in the arcade. You can switch the current design patent in the building menu, selecting new ones from the Shopping Catalogue.
Impact on Residents

All Skyscrapers within the green street overlay range of the Shopping Arcade have their need for it fulfilled.

For Skyscraper residents, any active design patent will fulfill their need for the respective Shopping Arcade.
Depending on the chosen design patent, there are a variety of beneficial effects on residences within a radius of the Shopping Arcade.

Recipe books allow you to pick a single active product for Shopping Arcades from a selection. Multifactories such as Orchards or Assembly Lines have catalogues that follow the same principle.

They are accessed from the respective building's menu.
Monument — The Skyline Tower

Behold the modern Skyline Tower — the final building introduced with The High Life. As with all Monuments there are several phases to its construction, and only one Skyline Tower can be built per island.

The Skyline Tower also has significant maintenance costs. Manage your income and expenditure accordingly!
The Ultimate Luxury Residence

The Skyline Tower is, in principle a residence just like other skyscrapers. Thus, an exorbitantly high number of investors can live in it.

Skyline Tower residents simply cannot do enough shopping: the wider variety of shopping arcade products there are available, anywhere on the island, the more the tower’s population will increase.

Take note though, that the Investors acquired from shopping arcades do not consume any other goods, so are essentially "free".
Changing the Output
Make sure you have a Warehouse in range to supply the required input goods.
Make sure you have a Warehouse in range to receive the final products.
