Assiduous as always? I too am rather swamped with work. You know how it is, money won't move itself around.
You must come across your fair share of tiresome people? Freeman is heralding a bear market again, but you and I know, a 10% decline is no true bear. The bull will come charging back!
Know why my investments are so profitable? I follow two simple rules. One: when investing I don't lose. And two: I never disobey the first rule.
Chaps at the bees club have lost the damn bet. You can quite clearly see from up here no curvature of the earth whatsoever...

If I find it only satisfactory, imagine the poor chuffs on the ground floor.
Society's grafters are up in the rafters.
Just like old Skyline, I've always been a head above the rest.
The Skyline Tower is getting top billing.
Blue-chip, blue sky, if you're one of the Skyline brigade.
Boredom is rare, now we have a little Skyline luxury.
There's no-one that isn't looking up to me now. Except birds, perhaps.
Daddy's little place up on Mount Olymp.
I've risen to the top...the absolute top. All that's left is to stay there now...
A towering inferno!
We have flown too close to the sun!
It's those unwashed window monkeys, spreading disease through the glass.
Close the boardroom doors! Stop the commotion and the gawking! I am owed my rest!
The board will suffer your baroque misconduct no longer!
This tower is the capstone of your failings, I refuse to parley! Speak only to my lawyer!
The View? Sterling! I spy my house in the countryside, the little veranda, the dogs, gazebo three.
Here's a spot of advice. Anticipating people's needs is impractical - unpredictable as stocks - convince them they are in need what you have on offer. Let the money come to you.
I heard of a chap, raving about a mile-high skyscraper he plans to construct, but something tells me the record of the Skyline Tower will be safe for quite some time yet!
Care to join me for cognac out on the skydeck? Although, mind you, that pesky elevator might be out of order again, so you may have to slum it up the stairs...
First Elevators, now Metal Frames! Skyscrapers are key to this city’s otherwise worthless future— sky’s the limit I'd say— a business venture ripe for the both of us!
Sorry, you've probably heard of me— Donald Bader, call me Donny. They say don't brag, but who has time to be coy? I'm the best Investor this city has, apart from you of course— my guru!
Our elevator plants are cutting-edge. Time to get production off the ground!
We have the elevators, so let's elevate our ambitions— sky's empty, so we fill it. We'll be kings in no time, looking over our beautiful kingdoms.
So proud we laid the first stone. Keep it up— plenty of real estate up there! My rivals are trying to keep pace, which is so funny to me, because they are all failures.
Nifty gizmos these typewriters— save time and money, both of which I need. You know, my lawyer's handwriting was unreadable, but now I can get typist monkeys punching all that profit in.
Behold, The Galeria Baderette! Now, sacred halls have to have product worthy of worship. Get the suckers leaving with their arms full.
You know, your catalogue is pretty skinny... It's ok, Donny has some ideas to fatten it up— I already put notes in the margins.
A Toaster! The perfect trap. Pipe toasty smells out and put the suckers in mind of breakfasts surrounded by family, childhood camping trips...all weak spots we'll target.
Toasters are selling fast! Imagine the profits if we had more types of products in our stores!
Found this note on my way back from brunch— really bizarre. An artistic sort of a threat— get this all the time. Here, go ahead, if you want a laugh!
Someone likes a crystal ball— If I wanted foreboding notes, I'd go see my cardiologist— Only no hopers hate change. Can we expect you up on the skydeck for lunch?
Time to brew up tomorrow's trends! I’ll uncork the bubbles! This catalogue will be bursting in no time, and with a fat profit! I take it you're not turning down the co-opportunity of a lifetime?
Knew you’d be onboard, oh wise one! To kick off we have to invest in R & D – a bore-chore – but we delegate. Once we've built them their lab we can get on to the real stuff.
Scared? Happens to some...I'd better find another industrialist to idolise.
Boring! We’re shaping the future of consume, here! The outside’s drab— has to show off what happens inside. People like gardens, right? Slap a gazebo next to it!
Not too shabby! Should be a breeze now for Miss Jenny, my house help here, to get to work. We do the big picture, she'll do the nitty-gritty.
The whole darn island? Tough business! Well, this patent is dead. We'll have to relocate, if we want Miss Jenny to get working for us.
No lab, no research. But don't wait, find some new real estate and build Miss Jenny a place to busy herself.
Miss Jenny, be a dear, I have a cup here with no coffee in it— Now, to business: Our first patent! You've earned the executive decision, partner, what'll it be?
The wife will be thrilled! Though the noise is intrusive— how will I enjoy the sunday paper? During testing, Miss Jenny will want to get vacuuming and find a way to keep it quiet.
By-! A device that keeps food fresher, longer. Miss Jenny is good with groceries, great even, with time she might think up the ideal base temperature.
A staple we can get in cheap and ship out at a price. Miss Jenny! Let's get us some blue inks and add the company logo— that’s how they’ll know it’s genuine Bader!
Yeah! Miss Jenny will get sewing right away. Has to be a statement piece, out of materials that speak to luxury. We’ll set price accordingly.
Stupendous! Well partner, I’ll be in contact once the lab have finalised the patent.
You were out, Miss Jenny? I thought your work was your life— well, but can you still continue our research?
Darn it, this is stalling us. Wasted time, wasted money, Miss Jenny— my partner and I will have to look at your salary, won't we?
Perhaps you can replace the missing goods, guru, you know, keep up your side of the bargain? Not sure I trust Miss Jenny to do it on current form...
Likely an eager rival trying to tweak his odds. I'm used to slander, it is part and parcel of the business, but that a peer would stoop to thievery. Embarrassing.
Ah, how I relish working with a professional! If only that was the norm, wouldn’t you agree Miss Jenny?
Effective and fairly silent, a winning combination. I may yet keep miss Jenny on!
Cold and calculating miss Jenny, as usual. I think we can shut the door on this one, guru.
The difference a brand makes, an immediate mark-up. I must admit Miss Jenny you have a keen eye for domestic detail!
Striking look! I might just grab one for myself, special one-time edition, don't mind if I do. Make it so Miss Jenny.
I’ve coaxed a few citizens into a so-called marketing ‘survey.’ Your input is appreciated, can you stop by the office?
A whole bunch of demanding so-and-sos in that survey. How you put up with them on the daily is beyond me. Let's skim the results, pick our best-seller!
Two birds one cartridge: A brand-new patent and a dazzling poster advertisement! While Miss Jenny runs the posters round town, us big dogs can crank up production to meet a deluge of demand!
The posters are up— can't be missed! I gave Miss Jenny some time off, she didn't look her usual self...
What a debacle! Our promising posters have been defaced by some deviant boheme. Look here, it's all over the papers!
Vanity screens ready— great! We’ll know how divisive our marketing campaign was once the numbers are in. I'll be sure to pass them along, but so you know, I already put the Champagne on ice.
Miss Jenny'll make sure the vandal gets it in the neck! Hey, Miss Jenny! Miss... I forgot, she’s off work. Well it's civil disobedience in your city— don't let our little venture take the hit...
Time's a wasting! Every poster that's been got at is a dent in our profits!
Ha! You can drop that case! The scandal the vandals hoped for was the proverbial bad publicity we needed to top out our sales!
Angry worker you caught, was it? Predictable. But I have half a mind to thank him for his work pro bono! Worked wonders for our sales, you know!
The "vanity screen with the red and white logo," is the talk of the town! Well, I’ve decided to follow their model. I've made that graffito our new brand logo!
Failed to catch 'em? No harm done— this is your initiation in the big dog ad campaign club. Go ahead, my treat— take the poster as a trophy.
You really came though for us with these posters. I knew you would. Here's an original for you to keep— your design after all!
Accounting found discrepancies. I don't like to point the finger, but sounds like Miss Jenny's spritzing our budget on personal endeavours. I think you're more discreet than me, think you can check?
These are changing times, partner. Industrial secrets are worth their weight, and I’m not about to chip away at my worth.

Who’d have thought funny little Miss Jenny could be so daring? Wait, is that Brokeman!? That's my lawyer! Well, you give 'em an inch and they take a mile— seems the guy used his vacation to grow a spine...
Pretty sure my lawyer grows weary of his vacation— can hardly be relaxing with treason on his mind. Cut it short would you?
I recall him mentioning a fancy cruise ship. Looks like his next item on the docket is a surprise pick-up.

Bit of a surprise you kept your involvement a secret, guru. You think her kind can be big players in the world of commerce? I suppose I'm going to have to hold up my hands and trust your superior instincts.
Bit of luck this lipstick stuff is a goer, and a bargain! The lab has found ways to produce it more cheaply than expected.
Ah, Mr. Brokeman, how was the vacation? Miss work? You must have— got yourself into a bit of a muddle with my assistant, didn't you?
Well Brokeman, now you have unique insight into this conspiracy against my company, you can file the case against her. So, get your papers together and show me whose side you're on.
Misplaced? Astounding, I should commission a study on the adverse effects of holidays on worker morale. My partner will find your briefcase no doubt. In the meantime, start writing the complaint!
Ah, I see you too uncovered what Miss Jenny and my lawyer were working on in secret— new patents without my consent! But the money’s spent... so, development may as well conclude now!
I doubt it will make a splash, but I might get some compensation in marginal profits. The rest I’ll collect by means of a lawsuit against Miss Jenny via Mr. Brokeman.
Splendid! Mr. Brokeman can finally earn his wages. Miss Jenny will be notified of the hearing arrangements.

We settled out of court. Miss Jenny could not afford a lawsuit. She’s agreed to forego her vacation and work overtime on our patents! This should make up for the time we lost to her bid at independence.
Yes, this is how a business should be run— I lead, everyone else follows! I'm the one with the nose for profit!
Hey guru, look at the skyline we shaped— what’s missing? A massive tower to shame the rest! The suckers will call it hubris, and we’ll be spitting on their heads from the top.
Stupendous! Oh, the envy they'll feel – let’s get it done, faster the better!
My Tower! Unfinished and already dominating the skyline! Once built they’ll be looking up at it and chanting our names!
At last, my tower stands! The true gold standard! Let the fools try and surpass it, it’ll be real fun watching them fail. Oh what a legacy!
Another weird note. This one landed on my desk —someone’s gonna answer for that — care to see what trash they came up with this time?
Well, this is getting to be darn annoying. Keep an eye on my tower, will you?
Too late for record time, but at least we’ll still smash the height record.
An Hour already!? Just wrap it up, will you? I hate waiting!
This should have been a sprint not a damn crawl. Maybe I bet on the wrong horse.
Some of the workers are scared of heights. What in God's name did they expect? This stunt is wasting us money, any ideas?
What damn risk assessment? No Miss Jenny. Why go out of your mind looking for problems when there are none!?
A Priest? Good God, with that superstitious lot, all they need is a wing and a prayer.
Wait, there are workers milling around who aren’t on my scaffolds? Can’t have them miss the view of a lifetime now, can we?
Safety harnesses and equipment? Well, if you feel like burning money you can go right ahead.
It's important to be able to ignore people. If you give their kind a finger, they'll grab the whole darn hand!
Spot of bad news. A worker lost his balance, had a tumble – terrible accident. The others could be trouble now... they’ll be wanting to talk to us.
A doctor? What’s his name? Either way, always better to get a man on the job you can trust to patch things up.
A hospital? Isn't that an overreaction? Besides think of how goddarn awful it’ll look next to my tower— sickness, death— boy, what a downer!
A risk premium? Well, then I darn well deserve one too. Clearly, I’m at the risk of your questionable choices.
Ignore! Put your fingers in your ears! Always works for me! If push comes to shove, we can always hire more.
Ugly. You can still remove it. I know a good demolitions crew. Miss Jenny will give you the contacts.
No dismal Hospital! Always keep the other side guessing! Join me for a drink on the skydeck – the Champagne is perfectly chilled.
Stolen steel beams— from the site! How!? Of course, no one saw a thing! And look, there's even one of those damn notes!
This pathetic joke’s been dragged out long enough, time we gave it a swift punchline, make an example of these workers— they've just got to be in on it!
Good, time to stop playing nice! The only way their kind learns is a crack of the whip.
A mistake! You’ll never hear the end of it – they’ll cook up more trouble and come running back to you expecting a handout.
The goddamn construction site's shut down— the workers are striking! It’s disrespect— against us! Take care of it, will you?
Surely you can finagle something— my lawyer would kill for your negotiation skills! Get these workers back— kicking and screaming for all I care.
A free ticket to the zoo! Wow! That's basically their natural habitat!
Yes, a barbecue bash! Stuff their bellies with beer and sausage, til they're too sluggish to care anymore.
Oh, great! Steep investment with no return— workers don’t spend their money in the shopping arcades— you know those people don't even eat toast?
Oh, finally! Let’s just hope you’ve not been spoiling these guys. They’ll need to put their backs into it, if we're going to plan to make any good on the time they’ve wasted!
No surveys! I hate surveys! This isn’t the first - or last - tower built in my name. Just make sure those workers aren’t slacking and get me a coffee. Gaelic.
Bending columns? They’re made of steel for chrissakes! I'm the ace when it comes to construction and I say that’s goddam ridiculous.
Oh, don’t go catching Miss Jenny’s paranoia! I pegged you as immune to this nonsense. But, I know you’ll bounce back, just make sure my tower's finished.
My guru, steadfast as always. When one is in pursuit of a great goal there’s no time to let fools distract you!
What the hell was that noise? It didn't come from the tower?! I refuse to lose face in front of this city!
Something must be done - Miss Jenny! It’s her goddamn job to have ideas! Where the hell is she?
Yes. Strengthen the pillars... maybe that could stop this wretched creaking? For once I’d be glad to have Miss Jenny here yapping away about some crazy solution!
Shoring. Sounds good. Think I’ve heard Miss Jenny use that term. For once I’d be glad to have Miss Jenny here yapping away about some crazy solution!
Guru, if you’re out of ideas...so am I. For once I’d be glad to have Miss Jenny here yapping away about some crazy solution!
Help me! Get over here quick! – God, I’ve never heard a screeching so terrible. Make it stop for chrissakes!
The whole thing’s breaking! Goddamned - How!? For all our sakes, what will we do?
What will you do!? You’re in charge, find a solution! —You always do! This can’t be it... this tower can’t fall!
God, that sound is driving me crazy!
Sweet Jesus it will fall. Like a house of damned cards... What have we done? We need Miss Jenny...
But... where the hell has she been this whole time? Not in the lab...? Oh wait, she's not in the tower, is she!?
Miss Jenny, what the hell is this? Is this your idea of a joke...
You can’t be... are you truly the one who’s been interfering all along? But why!? Why?!
Miss... Theodora. I can’t fix this. You’re... right, you’ve been right. This tower is a crumbling mess. Get us out of it, please. Help me?
Goddamn...that was close.
So it does. Thanks to you...Theodora. Well, I’d say it was high time we wrapped this up... I can’t wait for this tower to be finished with me.
But that's nothing compared to what Theodora and the workers accomplished. So, well done. I might disappear for a drink.
Theodora... You were obviously much wiser than I thought... I beg you: please fix the tower— do it for the workers! I can't live with the shadow of such a catastrophe.
Miss Jen- Theodora! You're not fired, you know! I could keep you as my advisor. Increased salary, vacation. It'd be my honour.
What’s this? Did we discuss halting construction? Well, better pick it up fast!
The islands lost!? And with it all our progress! – I better go find another guru.
Where's it gone!? Did it cross your mind to give me some kind of warning? – Oh I hate starting from scratch...
Right on time – Just as ordered! Despite all the hassle you finished the Skyline Tower in good time! Here a have a treat, with regards from all of us at the Galeria Baderette.
Unstoppable – my guru! Despite all that hassle you finished the Skyline Tower in no time, I’m stunned. Here a special present for the best, with regards from us all, at the Galeria Baderette.
Fashionably late? Given the issues we faced I guess it’s fine. I already had this wrapped anyway so here take it, from all of us at the Galeria Baderette.
Immortalize our victory! Let all know who built the highest tower of the era! – All that trouble must be worth something!
The world won’t forget what we all achieved! They’ll remember us as pioneers!
Finally, the work’s done! We can move forward with the construction.
Production will take time, so let's diversify our portfolio— The Arcade could cater for the furnishing of empty office towers.
A hit! Of course my Galeria Baderette is the best. Let’s keep it that way, the lamps are old news, we need a new best seller! We could even ask the customers...
This weird loser's really obsessed with me! I mean I’m impressive, takes a lot of work to look like this. Are you into grooming? Cosmetics and such?
Well, if people aren’t all smiles! A perfect advert! But something’s off– I know the mouth-breathers are buying but the numbers don't add!
A Drug Store hit! With so many arcades we need to fill em’! Build bigger towers. Attract some whales.
My guru, city's really grown! Lots of rich people, lots of very wealthy people. But I was here first, I'm the original, the biggest whale. I think they need a reminder...
It'll be a heck of a view! Don't make me wait. Really, I hate waiting. The faster you build the bigger the pay-off for you.
Keep in mind, without a marketing office our partnership will come to an end!
Oh, so you’ve decided to outsource to another island? A shame.
I know a thing or two about construction investments and let me tell you elevators and skyscrapers are on the rise! I can offer insider info, if you like.
Done. Time to get the Elevators up and running. People want better views— why not turn a typical residence into your very first skyscraper?
Ah yes, Shopping Arcades! Heralding a new era of consumerism. Time to welcome eager patrons into the halls of luxurious promise!
Surely a higher skyscraper surrounded by lower ones would provide the best panoramas of the city?
A truly intense panorama of the city! Reserve an apartment for me at the top, I'd love to be the envy of others!
So, what next?— Surely you weren’t about to stop here? These skyscrapers can go even higher, and if they can, they should!
Up to you how and where these towers grow, just make 'em grow real high. I can smell your ambition!

Who am I to deny the working class? They’ve seen us eating off china at the club, and now they want the same. Let them! — all they have to do is pay for it!
Splendid! Cleaning all these floors is hard work, I should know, I pay the bill. With this machine I can slash the staff!
Engineers, a restless bunch! Even on an ice cream break, they think up the next thing - And I do prefer my scotch on the rocks and my meat unspoiled.
Yes, Jr. has a classmate from Enbesa, young chap, jaunts about with a sleek leather bag. Passing the shopping arcades, he’s practically a walking advertisment!
I’ve heard the oriental exhibition at the zoo is a hit. haven't been myself but, a vanity screen with a thematic print might be the perfect souvenir.
Clearly a quality lamp needs a quality writing desk to stand on, however else will our customers work through the night to afford both. Rather illuminating wouldn’t you agree?
Yes, maybe with quality bedding – something warm and soft from up North, like eiderdowns – people would require fewer hours of rest and could go shopping!
People enjoy listening to the wireless together? Well surely, we can provide comfort with the appropriate seating. They’ll have to work to afford the leisure time of course...
In meetings with Avery I like to gaze out of the window – contingencies are a bore – but there was this nasty spot on the glass obscuring my view. I can’t have that!
The wife’s taken a liking to the cabaret – beats me – but feels that among the glitz she can’t shine. I tell her, 'darling wear something bold, something the others can’t afford.'
The museum’s new exhibit is rather ill received by my peers – the icy rooms you see, make their skin turn red! Face cream, with some whitener, should appease their antiquated standards!
The wind up here makes having a tipple a chore. We need something to set the hair. Jr. spoke of a wax-based hibiscus hair mask from Enbesa, let’s brand it for the regional market.
Wasn't it you who called your client a ‘nosy neighbour’?
Someone died?
Let me guess, all that witchiness had you spellbound too?
Witches make lousy cooks?
Doesn't take witchcraft to predict where this is going.
Word is you've tried your hand at extortion?
Is that so?
From your humble perspective as a...?
And Hayes just let you walk? The end?
Once in a blue moon. You?
This is the one who mangled his victim and tossed her in a river?
Yet here you are.
Think you could have done something?
But you know who did it...
The secretary? I saw her pretty little face in the papers.
She must have be traumatized...
She ever tell you her motive?
Little you can do for her, I imagine.
Oh, and this was the pulp writer? Wrote about the 'Phantom Detective'?
So, the squibbler skipped town because his creative trail had gone cold?
You solve it?
Dragon-green ink?
Once. Nice Painting. What drew me in was the marvel of the crowd.
Didn't the press speculate it was an inside job?
Help the kid steal the painting.
And the kid-thief, does he know?
So the kid wants the Curator to deal directly with the mob?
You're there when the trade happens?
What a shame. I was hoping the Don would be caught.
I went to see an operetta that night, ‘The Merry Widow.’
Really, they were out that night?
You were at the hearing? I heard people arrived before daybreak for a chance at a glimpse of her.
You really think she killed the sultan?
The press called her husband a monster.
None of her past was mentioned in the press!
You were tasked to find them?
You were to obscure the truth?
Some say he may have been framed?
So he puts his arsenic to use...deadheading...
So what was different this time?
They both survive?
You contradicted a reality she was convinced of.
I make a living.
What other kind is there?
Likely she knew on some level, but chose to believe otherwise.
Another private eye?
He liquidates their assets.
Like a pair of ruby earrings.
Humans made this! ...I mean just look at how measly we are in comparison!
Look up there, the flag! Are we supposed to put our hand to our heart?
There's a foreboding feeling in the air, hell I even saw lightning strike the needle once!
Oh it's a mighty tower, don't get me wrong, it's overpowering. But, from out on the farm it's a spike on the horizon next to mountains.
Darling look! All the way up they are, cleaning the windows! Hanging on by a thread!
Helen was adamant that I didn't need to get her a present. A little too adamant so...
Scuse me, would you kindly point me towards the lavatory?
A toaster? Would you say it comparers to roasting bread over fire?
The wife told me to 'simply grab some spoons' on the way home, but there so many variations!
five, twenty, thirty, thirty two and... wait how much did you say it was again?
Go on, I must inspect this sofa. I'll sit down for a spell, determine if it's snug enough...
The finishing looks rather dull does it not? Everything in the catalogue looks so... glossy!
What? You expect me to carry the cabinet!?
He heard it from a friend, who’s brother's wife's sister knows a bloke from newspaper row. It's factual— refrigerator paint's full of lead poison.
She went and invited the lot, they're to arrive at seven and we're still four walnut chairs short!
Trust me, a pinch of nutmeg, works like a charm...
I took three just to be sure. Now I am feeling rather drowsy...
In my professional opinion the whole side effect business has been steamed up.
...and then he got up and walked again. I'll ya' that medicine is our saviour, reborn.
All these fancy products when a good scrub with soap and hot water will do...am I right dear? ...Dear?
You have my attention until the elevator reaches my floor. That's five minutes, so shoot!
I avoid the lower floors, I abhor the feeling of going down.
"I care for a lofty lifestyle" - is that actually something people say?
All inclusive: Living spaces, offices, shops, entertainment. Soon the city will be brimming with smaller cities.
As a fellow Investor once said 'plant trees that other men will sit under,' and look at the shadow this tower provides!
They do know we have stairs? The party is tonight and I needed those drinks yesterday. Have them carry the crates up.
David, this isn't about us merely competing, we have to dominate!
I have to say the novel view of the city even elevates the chore of bookkeeping, for a while anyhow.
Charles is appraising the property as we speak, a new get-away. I grow tired of the countryside.
Wallace was droning on about some supposedly useful invention, what a bore.
Well yes, I have heard murmurs about rent pricing— but give the buggers an inch and they'll take a mile.
I instructed Hall: we settle out of court. Hook or crook, Janice, hook or crook.
The skyline is reminiscent of the stock market, you never know which district is about to rise an which about to fall.
I assure you the real estate market will switch from square to cubic meters. There's simply room for growth.
After a fashion the skyline mirrors society. The lows and highs.
My hypothesis predicts that the 'high life' will suit me— I've always been squirreled away in attics.
A source of extreme vertigo!
Teetering on the brink!
Integrity is failing! I predict complete collapse!
All that optimism comes crashing down!
Someone has pulled the cut-off switch on us up here.
Don't for a moment imagine ivory towers...
Height provides no innate additive value to my research.
My concerns require concrete solutions.
This tower is quantifiably deficient.
This building is an echo chamber.
The foundations of something are there...
Our peer review shows this construction to have room for further refinement.
I have identified a number of small tower issues I would like to raise.
I have revised and annotated a version of the skyscraper blueprints.
I don't consider myself especially needy, not compared to the investors in any case...
To this tower is come an influx of great minds.
No glass ceiling to obstruct me from fulfilling my potential.
I have been having elevated thoughts.
I am experiencing a heightened sense of productivity.
Breathtaking— yet the altitude hasn't dented my brain power one bit.
An ivory tower without the ivory, it's fairly near perfect.
Another summit of ingenuity for our species!
The story of the engineering behind tall structures is fascinating, I quite recommend it.
Quickly, form an orderly queue by the fire escapes!
No, never ever the elevator! Always the stairs!
This tower is very densely populated, the spread must be contained!
Open-plan offices increase the efficiency of viruses too...
Since we were crammed into towers, our discontent has spiked!
The pressure will only build unless you make concessions to our demands!
There you go, coffee with milk— I use powdered. Sugar is over there - oh! careful! it's the one on the left. To the right is Lead acetate. Sweet, but toxic.
Yes, I am often transported to unexpected floors too...I am presently working on a equation that will calculate the elevator's sequence of priority, and roundtrip time, based on traffic.
Are you aware that a typical skyscraper fire escape suffers many shortcomings? I have prepared a 'fire shute' concept I mean to share with architects and those ethical persons of business.
Have you considered any alternative names for the skyscraper? The term could be easily confused, since the appellation formerly indicated especially tall horses, ship's masts and ladies' bonnets.
Yes, the details are within my purview. One footnote, my name is Theodora – although Mr. Bader seems to prefer Miss Jenny— an honor to make your acquaintance.
Very well, Mr. Bader, I’ll see to it...
Mr. Bader, there's a problem. While I was out this morning someone broke into the office. The piston pumps have disappeared.
Mr. Bader, there's a problem. While I was out this morning someone broke into the office. The oil for the cooling system was stolen.
Mr. Bader, there's a problem. While I was out this morning someone broke into the office. The paints for the brand logo have been stolen.
Mr. Bader, there's a problem. While I was out this morning someone broke into the office. The bags of cotton have been stolen.
I am afraid not. Without these materials I cannot move forward with the prototype.
Are you certain we should use these goods...?
Indeed Mr. Bader. I too wish that were the case.
Good news, ingenuity has prevailed. The prototype successfully passed testing, is fully functional and is ready to enter into production...
Oh, he sent you... Please, at least allow me to clarify the situation before you report back to Mr. Bader.
Such a relief! I had a feeling you might be of open mind. Mr. Bader, of course, thinks you two are like peas in a pod, but then he only ever sees half the picture.
I'm no longer surprised Mr. Bader thinks of you as one of his betters. You're all the same as far as I'm concerned— do what you must.
Mr. Brokeman had agreed to supply specific oils I required for a new patent I'm developing. As you know, he did not deliver, and without them I am stumped...can you help?
Time is of the essence, now. Mr. Bader's already suspicious, and if there's any hope of making this product on my own terms... it must be underway before he is alerted.
Phew, just in time! I will use it right away— it was only meant to be the last little tweak to finish the prototype...
My newest patent! You’ve earned a look – The Lipstick! Now, to persuade Mr. Bader... Once stocked at the Drug Store, it can fulfill its intended purpose!
Catastrophe. Mr. Brokeman was right to be worried, Bader had him watched. They finally got to him and now he’s gone and revealed our plans...
Oh good, are those my oils?
With the expected height of the Skyline Tower, we must assume that any hazards will be of proportional magnitude. A risk assessment is vital in helping us react should anything happen.
I implore you to act! With each day the risks become greater. It’s paramount that we check the state of the lower floors and the columns...
What a relief! I'll get to it right away. You won’t regret taking the time to do this, thank you!
Mr. Bader truly has found his mirror.
It is as I feared: Cracks are forming on the lower levels. If they expand, the integrity of the tower might be at stake. We must act fast!
Very good! I will coordinate the installation with the workers. It will take some time, but it will be worth it.
This is gross negligence! There’s evidence that the tower's unstable and yet you refuse to act!
An emergency! The workers heard cracking noises from the structure. Some columns can’t bear the weight— they're bending! We must strengthen them, or they might not hold!
Better later than never! I'll provide the workers with materials, and we’ll encase the main columns. This should buy us some time.
Better later than never! I’ve ordered the shoring devices. They’ll arrive soon. Installation will take some time, but it might save the tower!
I am rendered speechless.
You’ve been looking for me? I’ve been very busy! I... Look, I might be onto a possible fix. But there’s not much time and...I’ll need your help to make it work.
Thank the stars! – okay, we must hurry. I'll finalize everything at the office and then hopefully set it all in motion before it’s too late...
I see. You may be able to live with yourself ignoring this, but I can’t. So, leave me to my work!

It’s never been Miss Jenny, it's Theodora, 'Donny'! And honestly, I should have quit after the first note I sent. but somehow, I thought ‘he can’t be that dense!’ Well, here we are. This crumbling mess, it’s on you!

You had ample opportunity to change: The tarot card, the posters, the letters... you laughed it all off. I thought you’d be deterred by setbacks; all I ever wanted was for you to be more responsible – but whatever disguise I took on, I was always beneath you.
I’m done playing charades. I’m not Miss Jenny, not your secretary, not your engineer – very different jobs by the way! Let me show you who I am.
I’ve been the one trying to stop you all along. I’m one of them lot. I applied for this job hoping to improve working conditions, safety, but no-one listened! You really are two of a kind.
I’ve been the one trying to stop you all along. I’m one of them lot. I applied for this job hoping to improve working conditions, safety, and found someone in your partner, Donny, who actually cares!

Here’s my plan: I’ve returned those stolen materials. We'll repurpose them to join the existing pillars to provide loadbearing support - what Donny should have been willing to do all along— and we'll need more!
Do you have the lacquer?
The workers and I will take care of it. We'll let you know once it’s done.
Good god, it's done! The danger’s passed and the behemoth lives another day.
Me too. Once it's done, we'll need to have a talk, all together.
I don't feel the need to apologise, but I will say this, that the Skyline Tower at least has a vision behind it— it'll change the skyline forever.
Let's gather together. The project didn't go without a few major hickups, and I'd like to address a couple of things before I leave you to your tower, Donny.
I'm done with this Donny. I'll get back to my own projects now...

I'm not fired? I'm not fired!? How about this Donny Bader— you work for me from now on. I run the company, and you get me the cash. I get an office at the top of the tower. You can start by getting me a coffee. Gaelic.
It won't take long.
It will only take a few hours!
The work is done, the construction can resume now.
It is probably for the best.
Dizzying is it not?
Up here my good soul, the stars are just around the corner.
To further science is to stand astride the shoulders of giants, or... simply take the elevator to the top.
Do you think the upstairs neighbours might be more accommodating? You see, I need to test this at altitude...
Precisely— the great feat of engineering is translating the measurable into the immeasurable.
The risk is due to the vertical build you see, fire moves upwards.
I have said it before and I will say it again, zoning restrictions are the death of creative construction!
Would you mind skipping my window? It helps me to gaze out across the city when I'm stuck on a problem.
Are you aware the soap you are using to clean the windows, is a feat of science too?
I despise animal cruelty, but that pigeon coop must go, I have not slept a wink!
Sure, the elevator is a grand feat of engineering— rising easily to the top, even— but much ingenuity is less overt— take the flush toilet!
Shameless! Read the second paragraph, identical in every regard— even the semiconductor junctions! Martha, they've stolen my design!
For heaven's sake close the blinds Harold! The light will damage the samples!
Get me the binoculars— it's those neighbours acting up again.
Honey, who would we call? Of course I know how to fix a stuck window, I'm an engineer for chrissakes.
Surely we should take the stairs! It will feel like ascending a mountain!
Look! From up here the other skyscrapers look itsy-bitsy!
Louise, tell me true is it my imagination or does it resemble a giant needle?
There she is, the Skyline Tower! A beacon for all the world to behold!
She is a marvel!
I feel as though each day there's a new piece in the papers on some elevator mishap. There's just so much to go awry on the way up or down...
You know Marcy, one spark might turn that spire into a towering inferno...
I recommend two sets. At least! For everyday use and for special occasions. But you'll also want a backup, for when the good china breaks.
Yes, the pantry has changed considerably since I've started taking care of the shopping. The supply is dictated by my demand.
That's wrong Alice. This once for white, this once for red, this once for sparkling wine and well this is an eggcup... who's been stocking these?
Was I here this morning? Yes well, there were a few more things I needed to get, so I thought why not pop back in and browse for a bit.
Oliver used to do all the shopping, but since it has become fashionable for us to shop, I've gladly taken over.
Put that desk lamp down. You already 'work' too many nights as it is.
Oh no, look part of the upholstery is torn, you think they'll give me a discount?
There’s Alice, Abby, Agatha, and Angela - she's new - and, well used to be Anne, rest her soul, so you see I’ll need a bigger bed.
Yes, well, I know we're lost, we passed that revolting lilac cabinet fifteen minutes ago!
I do appreciate a change of scenery when shopping, but the way the stores are made to look, it does feels like I've just entered another apartment.
Ruth you must get this lipstick, the shade of red is so daring! I love it.
So this why Mary's been looking less pale of late! It's the rouge. And here I was speculating that her health had improved.
Eric's depleted another tin! His Handlebar moustache has drooped into a horseshoe.
Judy vows the tincture did wonders for her complexion, and the itching's only minor.
Ingrid dear, I recommend this. With all your woes, it's never too soon to ward off wrinkles.
I expected Rory to be part o' this one...
You know whut'? Them lofty heights they dream of, they'd be nothin' without us to raise em' up.
You ever consider the odds?
So, what do you family say about this job?
Every time we start with a fresh patch o' dirt, it's impossible to imagine the monster it'll make.
Good weather won't make the fall any shorter.
Send em' up the scaffold. They'll soon learn those who ain’t afraid don’t make it.
By the way they be looking down on us workers you’d think they're the ones whiling away in the skies.
...they start pointing fingers!
Sure thing, still heatin' em up.
Did you make it to Mike's funeral?
Yeah well... Hey! Look at that scraper down there! I worked that job a few months ago, ha, thought it was the highest ever...
Yeah, almost done. What do you reckon they'll do for the opening?
Used to be I could count the family I had working in the sky on one hand. The old man, my uncle, grandfather Joe...
In the end we can only build the best from the materials we're given...
How can the people enjoy the delights of arcadia without a road?
I thought it might be nice to lay a small road to the shopping arcade?
Of course shopping off the beaten track is wonderful...
Please, peruse! It's like a museum to craft, but you can take things home!
The arts and crafts movement can be the consolidation of practical and decorative, behold!
I must ask you not to touch if you do not intend to purchase.
Certain components of our vacuums are handmade you know...
...and the toasters even, to a degree, are very well made.
Keep the body afloat so the mind may create.
Welcome to the Drug-Store. We are happy to hear your complaints.
A tincture for all nature's little blemishes!
Come, cover your eyes with cucumber and your face with cream.
Pull up a chair, make yourself at home.
Soft surroundings and myriad movables!
Yes! Please do take a seat!
Admittedly, some of our furnishings may divide people...
I sincerely apologize, for we are currently closed.
The arcade will throw open its doors to patrons again tout suite.
Oh! We're closed for refurbishment presently.
Candle-light flickers in carpenter's grottoes once more! The arcade is open again!
Ah yes, there's the wonderful chime of the cash register.
Then, my life among the aisles and shelves must resume!
Close the arcade?
Yes, you're right, enough of social interaction!
They seem to be closing down the arcades everywhere.
The wooden shelving is alight!
Fire is sweeping the arcade!
A malady creeps through the arcade! Bar the doors! Stop the spread!
It can only be the consumption!
Down with consumerism! Restore what is beautiful!
We are the shop front! We are the shop front!
Capable hands are low in stock.
Just some willing to arrange the bouquets here and there.
Mam', I regret to inform you, this product appears to be out of stock.
Between empty shelves I see customers wandering, searching, yearning!
Oh, can it be as tedious as a warehouse?
We await a delivery from a non-existent warehouse.
Women shopping in the arcades is the first bud of liberation. To purchase a good is to take ownership, after all.
Not at all— I relish inquiring what our customers truly seek. Toasters, yes, but what lies beyond that base craving for a crisp slice of bread?
I ponder, do Arcades influence our perception of the self? Are we less what we do and more what we own? Do we consume these goods or do they consume us? Um...would you like a bag?
Browsing is the finest part! The way our wares present themselves is everything— we take great care— and besides once you've paid, all virtue in them dies.
Would you like a sample treatment? Although, I must preface the long-term side-effects are not within our purview.
Have you seen the traveling elixir show? A lovely lie turns snake oil into a miracle cure. The crowd was wooed, but I was struck – Am I the same? Dressing tinctures in empty promises.
One ensures a pale complexion, the other adds a vibrant flush of colour. A dichotomy, but a healthy mind can withstand dissonance.
Consider bartering. Our Products, unused, are inert but when applied produce a chemical reaction – by virtue of the user they come alive, thus the price should vary.

It is a wonder. In a single building we have created a multitude of faux habitats. A Livingroom here, an office yonder, and a bedroom over there. None of them lived in, but all of them, so convincing!
Homemaking is a primal act – vulnerable beings seeking shelter from a hostile world – but what of aesthetics? Is the abode our refuge for the corporeal and beauty our refuge for the soul?

I’ve taken to decorating the store – look, there’s flowers in the lounge! A beautiful vase is it not?... in my home all fragile things end in shards. There lurks a black furred monster when I am gone.
I can assure you the comfort and luxury of our furnishings is sublime. I'm forever having to dislodge customers falling asleep upon our lounge collection.
These wares are made equal in darkness.
Without electricity the arcade is as like a wolf without lungs.
While my mind feeds on ideas, these shelves do not.
An empty arcade fulfills no purpose.
Customers are seeking goods, but we have naught to offer.
A dandy choice!
This is sure to please many customers.
A fine piece of craftsmanship.
You’re looking for a Mr. Brokeman?... Well that's me. Mr. Bader needs to see me? I-is it really so urgent, I’m on holiday…
I normally give Mr. Bader space when he's having one of his little tantrums. It’s the reason I’m still his lawyer and I’d like to keep it that way. Are you sure I need to see him now?
I’m unsurprised my vacation's being cut short... Mr. Bader is choleric at the best of times though usually not without cause...
Dora’s idealism is rare. Maybe I was hoping that, by helping her, I could reclaim some of my own drive. I'm tired. Really tired.
I knew Mr. Bader would never appreciate the virtues of this product. Immediate gains are his sole measure of success, blind to other kinds of worth, not like Dora...
Well, the only way out of this is through...
Of course, it’s just... well, before boarding the cruise, I misplaced my briefcase. And the papers you requested...they're in there...
You’re the reckless one but, we’ll be the ones dealing with the consequences...
Boss, if we’re to start work on the upper levels on the morrow, we’ll need them new set o’ hands mighty soon!
Those new lads seem capable! Up here confidence is key, the price of an indecisive step is steep... and they’ve just arrived in time!
The Lads and I were counting on not going upwards today. Wish we’d had some time to prepare... that kind of uncertainty can be fatal.
A priest? Well, maybe some of the lads can find solace...
Ah, that’s great boss! The lads and I appreciate you takin’ action.
There’s anger brewing on site...shouldn’t expect anything else by the way you’ve been treating us!
A whole hospital? The closer the better! Quick action can be a lifesaver. Thomas will be relived.
Nice to know there’s help close by – makes me worry a tad less about the lads, but let’s hope we don’t need it!
You really hold so little regard for our lives? We got no safety on site, no hospital close by... it be madness on our part not to be scared!
One doctor? Will he be around for a bit? You never know what’ll happen tomorrow...
That's good! The risk won’t be gone, but if something does happen... well, it’s quite a bit! It could pay for little Emmi’s education...
You’re serious about this? I saw the lads come back from the quartermaster office - injured! You realize, the money you’re takin’ from them is food off their family’s table!
It makes a grand difference to us boss! Very good of you it is, we’ll raise a glass to you at the pub tonight!
A visit to the Zoo? That’ll be a change o’ pace and little Emmi’s gonna be chuffed to go!
Can’t go wrong with a hearty feast. It’ll be nice to have a carefree night, help the lad’s take their minds of things.
That’s quite something boss! It’ll last us a stretch to be sure. Might even get us something nice like one of them fancy toasters, or a new toy for Emmi.
Right, we’ve decided to get back to it. It’s our work after all and we take pride in it, just remember we ain’t interchangeable and if we don’t feel valued, we can go back to striking.
Dear god the tower’s swaying! There’s no time! Get word to the lads we must evacuate everyone – Now!
A case this clear cut makes you wonder... do the rest just avert their gaze? Scared to be branded snitches, or worse...

And like the cops I damn near dismissed her. No-one likes folk who stick their noses into other folks' business— I should know— and the picture she painted of the couple next door was made in pretty broad strokes... Her curiosity was piqued when the wife asks the Landlady if she can make a little casket-sized space in the basement.

No, not yet. He's still out and about, but his wife's there knitting her mourning cap, lamenting his short life. Nosy neighbour's convinced herself the wife’s a soothsayer of doom— a Cassandra. I tell her if 'you want an exorcism, you're tooting the wrong ringer'!
A quick look might not have taken me long, but I fell down the rabbit hole. Took a few twisted arms, but I began to notice our neighbours couldn't help but mention the wife's 'dinners'.
Ha! Well, I dug around. Not a month ago a hefty life insurance was made for the soon-to-be-late husband— then I discovered our would-be-widow was widowed before. Several times.

Yeah, that’s when the other kind of digging had to start. With the help of a friend I unearth the plain facts from six feet under: there's no arsenic in the ground, but plenty in the remains of our four unlucky suitors.

As for the fifth...well, he makes it. Barely. The cops, for once, have an open ear and get our witch weighed fast. If there's any kind of lesson, it's he oughtta think to cook his own dinners from now on...
Allegedly. You know me— I'm an amicable sort. I try to stay clear of trouble, but it has a tendency to seek me out.

I was headed to a juice joint, when I see a car tailing a young nurse— bad part of town. The car speeds up and I'm thinking I don't need this one on my mind and push her aside. But, the car turns, drops a briefcase and rushes off. I go to inspect...
That's when Detective Hayes emerges from an alley. Says I've been caught red handed and takes me for a drive uptown. Heard of Donoghue? Big shot surgeon. He's been getting calls...

They'll throw 'acid in his kisser' if he don't serve up ten grand by the end of the week. Now the doc's a handsome fellow, but any self-respecting blackmailer should have threatened to burn his hands...

Scapegoat. I'd wandered into the handover, the real culprit— a no-show. The cops are puzzled, but it's an open case. Hayes should consult the gossip column once in a while, then he'd know the doc's business gone bad. Botched an operation on a starlet.
So, I rip off the Band-Aid for 'em. It's a ruse, Donoghue wants to leverage his alleged victimhood for a spot of good press. My diagnosis is met with denial.

Like I said, I am an amicable sort— and there's a press conference tomorrow. Donoghue will get to show off his acting chops and I intend to be there. See the show, ask some compelling questions. Of course.
You go to church?

Growing up, but I dropped the habit... ...Hall told me he pled insanity. Stood, his back like a lightning rod, the accused, as if preaching to his congregation. You know that right after he killed her he went and delivered a sermon?

God' spaketh to him and said: 'make a sacrifice.' ...You know I thought about skipping the roof today, the new speakeasy downtown looked so inviting. Simmering with the booze tinged troubles of its flock, the promise to drown among them nearly turned me around.
...I think we may have crossed paths, back when I was still raking muck. I was downtown for some silly news story when I passed this baby church...

A young priest was out front, I think I asked him for a divine light, and we talked. He seemed too polite. A young girl had just gone missing in the area. I was too busy with my notepad to add two and two together.

I think a lot of people could have. There were questions when he was ordained, complaints in every parish. But everyone just passed him along, like he was someone else's problem. So did I, in a way. Anyway, they found the poor thing buried at the back of the church.
For a moment I thought Agatha would know peace. I should know these kinds of secrets always end in the grave.

We were rivals, in a sense, although she was always better. Had a skilful way of dissecting my work at a glance. While she published truth, I dug up dirt, my lines riddled with lies before the ink could set.

When I quit the paper, she ordered us drinks. When I told her I planned to strike out as a private eye, she ordered more. I'd hoped she'd believe I was finally stumbling upon something true. Now here I am, failing to close her case...
Hearsay from ex-columnists in dingy offices downtown is nothing in court. The only one who had any power to turn the tide is gone...

Yeah, they were pretty pictures. They called her beautiful. I was dead on the case, no solid lead to speak of, and she walks in, guilty-eyed, a story to tell. I could see in the set of her jaw, the words of hope waiting to be spoken, but someone had scared her.

She was already working for Agatha weeks before the big story broke. How I wish Agatha had snuffed the piece in it's crib, but, as you know, it was published. And like all of her work it hit true— mobsters dragged under the spotlight.

A week later Agatha gets the response she wasn't looking for, and the girl was there to see it. Remembers the thud at the door, hiding under the table. When the poor girl left my office that day, I could see blood, dried at the soles of her shoes.
She had that far-away-look... and all I could do was go and make a promise I knew I couldn't keep, that I'd make sure she was safe. The same damn lie I told Agatha.

She’s dressed in yellow, stands out in the dismal place like a flower growing up through concrete. There’s a resolve on her face, she harbours no illusions, innocent or not, her judgment is made. So, I forego preamble, and ask did she stab the counsellor.

The popular story is she did it for the money. They were seen in the club, him flirting, her dancing. Some say they left together, others say he followed, she led. The next time they saw him he was dead, bleeding out in a side-street.

She agrees she did it. But points out for me that his wallet remained untouched. They don't want to know her real motive— bad press. But make him out to be a martyr? What a legacy. Hours before the funeral his second has already picked up the mantle.

She just smiled. Like it's done now, and her words won’t raise the dead, so she’ll take it them to the grave. And anyway she says, who am I to deserve such a secret? So, I talk to my client, the owner of the dancing establishment, and she cares. I arrange for the two of them to talk. For once I wait outside.

This case is out of my hands. I made sure to hand my client a list of trustworthy lawyers, for whenever she might need to inquire. Now she got a taste for spilling her secrets, she tried it on me, but I stopped her at 'my father was poisoned'. It’s not my story to tell, and as things stand, I don’t need more ghosts haunting my mind.
The landlady is simply shocked no-one’s out looking for the young man. At first, I think her concerns lie with the state of her property. But turns out she relishes the young writer's work.

Yes, more than a little derivative, if you ask me. Although by the looks of it, he wasn't a great fan of his latest efforts either. The chimney was packed with the remnants of charred notebooks and flame-eaten papers. The room's a mess, there’s burns on the carpet— it look like he packed up and left in a hurry— and there's a pot of dragon-green ink spilled on the table.

Maybe he wrote something? But there doesn't seem to be a note. Then I find something strange: money stuffing up a tea box— why leave it? I start snooping. His contact at the magazine tells me the ‘Phantom Detective’ was doing swell but its writer was slow to deliver...

Yeah maybe. I try and get mine on track by spending the evening at his favourite haunt in the hope of gossip. The place is like death, lacks the seedy flair or a downtown juice joint, or the glitz of a snazzy uptown gin mill.

A few excitable friends of his invite me for a drink. One is fascinated to know my procedure, adamant he knows how ones like this always get solved. Another suggests an artistic quarrel drove him out of town. A third reckons he got in with the wrong crowd. After the fourth drink they mention his financial troubles. After the fifth it's the mob, the scorned lover, wild dogs and I'm tired of contradictions.

So I make some guesses of my own, like which of their jolly crowd might work as a likely suspect. That's when they fess up. They got a strange letter— night their friend disappeared— a riddle they've been failing to solve, and it hurts their pride.
I didn't bother. In my experience real crims rarely pen riddles and this one happened to be in green ink.
Uh-huh. Turns out he's grown bored of the 'Phantom Detective' and is working on a new story. One he wanted put to the test.
Ever see it up close?
When I arrived at the scene all that was left was the empty frame. It lay on the floor all gaudy, a hushed silence suffocating the room.

It was. Three days after, the curator walks in my office and confesses. I give him directions to the closest church, but he persists. He says a week before the crime he's confronted by a young man, tries to extort him, fails badly. They get talking.
The kid's desperate, begs the curator for his life. He's gotten in with the mob and the Don wants him to steal a masterpiece as a present for his wife. The curator gets an idea.
Almost. He can't imagine the Don will think to have the painting inspected, so the night of the theft he makes sure there's a fake on the wall.
No, he thinks he's gotten the real 'woman on rocking chair', 'til the day he gets a letter. The Don's wife's real discerning and had someone take a look. Now they want the real one plus reparations.

So it seems. But the whole thing feels off— after all the mob rarely correspond by mail. Anyway, we pen a response, naming a place and a time for a trade. The Curator'll bring the genuine piece, and two more.

He's aghast— steal two more with the cops crawling the place!? Well for once I'm not working solo, I call up Hayes, who loves that I might need his help, but agrees. We get two pieces 'on loan' so to speak.
Young man is nabbed red-handed. Didn't exactly trust the curator's charity after the first time, and besides, wanted to cream a bit off the top.
Then you might have spotted the pair up in the balconies.
Yes, Mr. Hall neglected to mention this in his defence, although that wasn't the most pertinent information about the princess he omitted.
Five days in total and I was there for the lot— still nebulous to me what truly transpired.
Shot him three times. They were alone, and the door to the hotel room was locked. Hell, they had to knock it through to reach 'em.

It was easy for Mr. Hall to cast him the villain and her the damsel in distress. See, there's more to the princess then meets the public eye. She made her initial foray into the limelight as a dancer, then upped her paygrade to an escort and ultimately, as you know, rose to become foreign royalty.
Vested interests ensured that it wasn't. Before she met the Sultan she had a short but heated affair with a duke. I was hired to make sure the lovers letters are kept out of the limelight.
She holds the Duke's responses as leverage to get someone like Hall on her side. I was to make sure there no other clues could be uncovered.
It pays the rent. I convinced myself it had nothing to do with the murder. Well, shows what I know. Hall send me a card, a job well done.
In his defence the solicitor said Rowse made a habit of carrying phials of arsenic in his pockets, to kill off the dandelions outside his house. This was in the dead of winter.

They make the argument that the central plaintiff is his rival. But then again, said rival was poisoned over some chit-chat and a cup of yellow tea. And Rowse owed him money, money his business was no longer bringing in.

Not for the first time. There was an inquiry made six months ago— about his wife. She'd been gravely ill but recovered at a countryside hospital. When she returned home she was dead inside a month. I looked into it at the time, but the physician was convinced she'd relapsed— In some sense he was right— shouldda insisted on a thorugh examination of the body.

Rowse grew sloppy. He likely poisoned his wife over months, maybe years, but his rival wants him to pay up, fast. First he sends a box of chocolates to the house. But the sister-in-law receives them and gets peckish. That night she falls ill.

Plan B is the invitation to yellow tea and cake I mentioned. Rival barely accepts. Then it was "'scuse fingers" as Rowse hands him a slice of death. The attending physician is the same one that attended Rowse's late wife and he gives me a call.
With a little luck. Meanwhile the coroner is exhuming the wife's body for the trial, for some reason she was buried with an oriental Noh mask on. Ugly scenes.
When I delivered the news that her husband was faithful, do you know what he did? Spat at my feet, accused me of being a con.
The more truth I uncover the lighter my pockets seem to get.
You sell a version of the truth.

The empirical, the one many don't wish to hear. She gave me a conclusion and I was to evidence it. A strange woman accosted her at the mall. Tried to steal her ruby earrings, calling her the thief, and when she told her husband, he tried to downplay it all.

A week later the earrings are gone from her dresser. Her conclusion: Her husband took the earrings for his jilted lover. As for mine: I won't deny one can make a living off the dead...but the mortician’s wage hardly explains his wealth.

Ignorance was prudent to her lifestyle. Anyway, I stakeout the coroner's office, trying not to doze off until I realize I'm not the only sorry ass wasting away in the sun— and if anything the wife has a knack for describing people, because who I'm seeing is the alleged assailant from the mall— a young woman.
She doesn't spot me. I wait 'til she leaves to do some digging, and there's plenty to be suspicious of. Seems most of the dead died without family.
And keeps their belongings.
What he doesn't know is the dame he stripped them from had a quick-witted niece, who I'm thinking of introducing to his lovely lady wife.
Yes, it is in the Beaux-Arts style, but at the upper levels the decor is less pronounced. A perfect marriage of aesthetics and pragmatism.
Everyone's praising it, calling it a grand success, but I had a friend working top side and he got stories to tell that make you shudder...
...and I said, no way in hell could they build such a behemoth so fast, and now they're done even sooner! I sure hope it holds up.
I for one have a bad feeling about the Skyline Tower. They neglected to skip the 13th floor.
Whatever the architect designs next, it will always have to live up to that there Skyline Tower.
Ed was positively howling with laugher! I only ever asked if he reckoned I could save up a Skyline Tower apartment...
Imagine it, waking up to a view from up here. What a high life that would be.
Oh no I feel weak in the knees just looking up - Is the tower swaying in the wind?!
If I send the patent office the plans for my baseball-catching-device, who's to say they won't steal it?
No, there's a stain on it see here? I was about to polish it with my jacket, how would I even fit this plate in my pocket!?
Well yes, the refrigerator cost us an arm and a leg, but then, one really does like ice in ones scotch.
I think I will take to the customer lounge, I must consider this purchase over a sweet cup of tea.
Do I need a new bag? Well, I don't know about that. But I certainly don't have one made of leather. Yet.
Oh! This mirror is rather beautiful— or is it just the face in it...
What do you mean it's part of the store? I thought all the furniture was for sale.
Honey, I know the armchair is an heirloom, but look at how tasteful this one is!
I would love to test that armchair but I think he’s fallen asleep...
Well, I told Arthur those mustard drapes were awful. No wonder she left...
You know it does make me think of the tincture that agitated travelling salesman offered us... I think I'll stick with cod liver oil.
I see them judging me, it's the third bottle I've had to buy that man this week.
Certainly, it's basic hygiene, I brush my teeth twice a week.
Well it's rather crafty, I heard she used the arsenic in rat poison and honestly...
Do you by chance know how well detergent takes care of blood stains?
You haven't heard...?
Just castles in the sky ain't it?
Nah, if I wanted better ones I'd enlist.
Blimey, if me Ma' knew I was walking iron she'd climb up here and pull me down by me ears. Poor fool mom thinks I work in the offices.
It's gonna change the look of the city forever.
Rained last night, better take care not to slip...
Had some rude fella trying to tell me it's the perfect job for fearless workers like us.
It’s a matter of perspective ain't it? Down there they look like ants to us, up here we’re ants to them.
You know what bothers me? We do an excellent job no one mentions it, something goes bad...
Poor old us huh! Haha... Toss me em' rivets!
...didn't get the day off.
Looks like you broke your own record!
Give us the day off. We ain't fancy enough to cut no ribbons, but can't say I'm complaining. Hey, I like my kids!
I know exactly what you mean. Was my brother who started it for us, but now there's a familiar face walking iron in every corner of the city.
Yeah, sometimes it sure does feel like they expect us to spin gold out o' straw...

Scenarios are standalone missions that you can access at any time from the Main Menu. They involve unique challenges and mechanics to test your strategic skills. They're usually harder than your typical Anno game, too.
Objectives and Rewards

Each scenario has three tiers of objectives for you to fulfil — bronze, silver, and gold. Achieving an objective tier provides a unique reward which you can access in the main game. Unlocking a higher tier reward automatically grants all the lower ones, e.g. achieving gold will also grant you the bronze and silver rewards.
Milestones
Some scenario elements persist through subsequent playthroughs. Even if you fail one attempt, you may find some of your items, buildings, or units still present once you start again.
If you wish to start a scenario again without any persistent elements from your previous attempts, press the Reset button to clear all milestones and start the scenario from scratch.
Scenarios
Changing Seasons

The weather in this region lurches dramatically from dry summers to wet monsoons. Within this pattern, there are variations: individual summers and monsoons may be milder or more intense. These seasons will have different effects on your economy and people — check the list of effects on the right hand side of your screen. Furthermore, later seasons are accompanied by optional events, themed according to the seasons.
Irrigation

The monsoon seasons bring heavy downpours of rain. Construct basin buildings to collect and store this rainwater. Then, by connecting canals to basins, you can create areas of irrigated land in which crop fields can grow.

Each basin can hold a limited amount of water. This amount directly corresponds to the number of canal tiles it can support. In this image, the basin is currently supplying 20 canal tiles, but can support a maximum of 32.

Basins refill during every monsoon season. During the summer, the amount of water they contain (and thus the number of canals they can support) slowly reduces. Remember: moving a basin will empty any water you may have collected from the monsoon, so plan carefully!
Silver Deliveries

The king — well, more likely one of his dreadful sycophantic minions — will demand regular deliveries of silver goods from you. These demands will grow, both in terms of the quantity and type of goods required, as you progress through the complicated silver production chain.
Failing a Delivery
The king's staff are a corrupt bunch, and always amenable to bribery. If you fail to make a delivery, you may be able to negotiate a way to save yourself — at a cost.
Silver Production

After you've extracted silver ore from a silver mine, it must be purified using cyanide. Cyanide is produced at the ammonia plant, and requires dung. To acquire dung, place an animal farm within range of the ammonia plant.

By the pale light that filters in through the boarded windows, you can see what remains of the church. Sallow plaster hangs limply from the walls; cracked floor tiles shift beneath your feet; rows of worm-eaten pews lead up to a pulpit without an altar.

Beneath the pulpit sits the collection box, conspicuously devoid of dust. Gently prising it open, you see the glint of copper coins.

What do you do?
Loot the collection box.
Close the box and leave.

Forty réis are now yours.

Amid the humid heat of the rotting church, the coins are cool to the touch. You stroke one softly, rolling your thumb across it, feeling the features of a sovereign you do not recognise. As the rest of the coins are lifted from the box, you see a message scratched into the wood:

Wealth is worthless on the day of wrath; but he who follows me will be delivered from death.
Leave the church.
Look in the well?
Deep in the musty well — far beyond your reach — something glints in the sun.
As the monsoon rains pour into the well, it begins to overflow. A case of schnapps floats to the top — yours for the taking!
The well is empty now, and little use to anybody.
The chair provides a direct view of Deserto de Prata, and the mountain which looms over it.
There is nought left in the vegetable patch but weeds and shrivelled roots: the only testament to a futile attempt to coax life from this place.

...the next day he came again; and though he squinted against the sun, having dwelt so long in the depths of the mountain, he saw us — truly saw us — and knew our sins.

And he told us of those who had come before — showed us the bones in the riverbed, the marks carved into the cavern walls, the scraps of metal that once were tools.

He told us, too, of those who would come after us. This is where they will pierce the rock, he said, and ran his hand along the unblemished cavern wall as if tracing an old scar.

Now we stand before your judgement,
And we see our errant ways,
Raise our hands in supplication,

Seasons of Silver
SEASONS OF SILVER

By order of King João, Third of His Name, His Most Faithful Majesty, Emperor of the Crown Colonies, Appointed by the Grace of God and the Unanimous Acclamation of the People; Granter of Mercies, Upholder of Dignity, Scourge of the Corrupt, etc.


Vasco Oliveira, for your failure to retrieve the Sceptre of Capon, you are hereby stripped of your position as Chief Aide to the King.

By order of His Imperial Majesty, in consultation with his most esteemed and incorruptible ministers, you are to be sent to Deserto de Prata, where, by way of atonement, you will establish a silver mint, and extend the beneficent hand of His Gracious Majesty to this most stubborn of regions.

May you bear your punishment more productively than you have borne your duties.
Vasco Oliveira has been exiled to a remote island. His task: to establish a silver mining operation, while dealing with extreme weather and punishing deadlines.
Complete the final delivery
Complete all other deliveries

Regain Vasco's lands, titles, and honour.

Are you sure you want to reset the scenario?
The hacienda will begin in ruins; quest reward ships will be gone; harbours on other islands will be removed.
In this scenario, there are no items available. Only proper planning will save you here!
The monsoon rains will not irrigate your islands — the soil is simply too dry. You must build basins to collect the rainwater that comes during the monsoon seasons.
Once your settlement is established, seasonal events will appear. These are always optional, and allow you to make potentially useful trade-offs.
Each summer and monsoon season has slightly different effects — some will help you, while others will hinder you. These effects are detailed on the right-hand side of the screen.
Failing a delivery is not necessarily the end for you — though it is highly inadvisable.
Besides Deserto de Prata, there are two nearby islands which can provide useful resources and fertilities.
Some of the ruins on the island can be removed with the demolish tool; others will require workforce to remove; others can be renovated.
And thus was Vasco Oliveira's debt to the crown repaid; a Viscount once again, though a chastened one. Congratulations!
And thus, the downfall of Vasco Oliveira was complete; a man forever banished from his home. Perhaps you might want to try giving him a happier ending next time.
Most Gracious King João,
I have considered your offer to reinstate me as your Chief Aide. I have had plenty of time to think in the nine months since I returned from Deserto de Prata — and I am afraid I must decline.
A man's value lies not in his titles, or his position, or his holdings. It lies in his ability to overcome hardships.
I have proved my worth to myself, and that is true redemption. Now, I shall tend to my estate, and enjoy the reassuringly temperate climate of my homeland.

Yours humbly,
Vasco Oliveira
Ten years have I languished here.

This wasteland has somehow grown even bleaker with our presence. The dust mingles with the searing stench of cyanide; the ground is strewn with broken equipment; the only novelty here, the latest shipment of exiles to hack away at the mountain.
The silver veins are dwindling... but the mountain’s appetite for the miners is undiminished. Every week, it takes another.

I ask myself daily where I went wrong, where I could have refined the production process, what more I could have done.

If only I could try again.
P.S. I was sorry to hear that your Most Faithful Actuary, Edmundo Vara, has been unable to produce even a single bar of silver for you. He has my warmest regards.
