What is this curious ritual?
Rage weighs heavy on the soul; better to let it out.
These people need to learn to bear their suffering with dignity.
A man can hardly be expected to keep it all bottled up inside, eh?
The people want a sacrifice to be made.
If it will inspire their fervour... Let the water be spilled.
If it will inspire their fervour... Break the basin.
What do we have to lose?
Agh, this infernal heat. What are we to do about it?
For now, we redouble our efforts; the coming rains will feel all the sweeter.
No point exhausting ourselves in this wretched heat.
Better that these blazes come at a time of our choosing.
Ah, the Season of Reaping — time to settle our favours.
I am a man of honour, after all.
For once, I receive what I deserve.
Nautical knowledge — now that's priceless.
What is all this commotion? Let me through!
We've all felt it — there is something, deep within the mountain.
Cast aside these superstitions! There is but one God!
Why so quick to turn to superstition? The human body is more resilient than you credit it for.
The sound of rain on the hacienda roof... I think I'll miss it.
Odd company, these exiles — but none of us would have survived here alone.
The empire is a rotting husk, with vultures like Vara picking at its fetid flesh.
I can't say I miss life at the royal court. The soft sound of the waves, the whispering breeze: this is all the company a man needs.
I wonder if there's a more effective way to put all this water to use.
Don't let a drop go to waste!
A much more efficient design.
Crops need all the help they can get to flourish here.
The people are terrified by these winds. They need guidance.
I will not allow these petty superstitions to prevent my homecoming!
Demon or no, one can't be expected to work with this racket.
If this is what it takes to placate their fears...
It is customary to exchange favours during the Season of Sowing.
What kind of man just leaves this lying around, anyway?
We all deserve a taste of the finer things in life, no?
You will receive your reward in time: you have my word.
What's this commotion? Do these people never tire of their bizarre rituals?
We all must face our sins.
Enough of these processions. Back to work!
Admission is the first step towards atonement.
It's all here. You and your little friends at court seem to have underestimated me.
There, take it. You've no idea of the toil that went into this.
All of the very finest quality, I assure you.
I really don't have time for this.
Little else to admire in you, I suppose.
And what does that make you, then?
You are nothing but a parasite.
Vara, how do you expect me to maintain quality with these ridiculous deadlines?
Oh, I'll see you again – when I denounce your crimes before the king.
That's Viscount Oliveira to you.
Ah, I do love bureaucratic interference.
Forty days since I was cast into exile...
Banished to the bleak backwaters of the empire, along with a wretched band of other exiles and dissidents.
I see it now: Millay Picchu, cradling its riches.
A mountain of silver, amid a pile of dust.
I can feel the quiet malice of this place.
Others have come before, and all have failed.
Every governor and geologist, every miner and missionary; all of them, lost.
But I, I shall overcome. I shall take the mountain's bounty; reclaim my honour; and I shall see my home again.
Finally, a break from the heat — though I fear these rains might interfere with our work here.
I really should have brought some different clothes.
A thriving settlement in this, of all places. I'd like to see Cousin Vicente achieve that.
The habit is not to my taste... but chewing gum seems to help the miners stay hydrated.
The empire is infested with these loathsome bureaucrats. How they captured the ear of the king, I'll never know...
From unyielding rock to burnished silver: the first coin!
By my reckoning... that should be the last coin.
This land is hostile to our presence.
No wonder these troublemakers ended up in exile!
They say the sickness stems from the mountain. Poisoning the entire land...
Give your silver unto me, mighty mountain.
May we fare better than those who came before.
A residence befitting a man of my stature.
If this venture doesn't go well... I can always take a swim in the cyanide vats.
So many mouths to feed, so little arable land...
The summers here are punishing, but the rains that follow are plentiful. If we can build a basin to collect the water, we could have irrigation all year round.
This dry soil is useless! We'll need to keep the fields on irrigated land.
Since this soil won't hold a drop of rainwater, we'll have to collect it ourselves.
Aha, the rush of cool water!
The foreman says we've already extracted a hundred tons of silver ore. Fine work.
We'll need cyanide to get the silver out of the rock. I might leave this part to someone else...
Let me check those rubber moulds — we must make sure King João's image is properly represented.
Let's get these shiny lumps hammered into something more appropriate.
And the sea gave up the dead which were in it, and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them — and they were judged, every man, according to his works.
Said He: see, I have refined you, though not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
Five times shall he come, and five times shall you say no, beast, begone! I will not barter with you!
Lucas! Lucas! Has anyone seen my son? He never returned from the mines!
No greater pain... than to recall times of happiness in times of misery.
Take me home, Santa Maria; take me home, across the waves...
Funny, isn't it? I get caught stealing a loaf of bread, and end up sharing the same punishment as Vasco Oliveira himself.
I said to the judge: I have every right to distribute my pamphlets. It is not treason to call for the empowerment of local assemblies!
By order of King Joao, Third of his Name, His Most Faithful Majesty, Emperor of the Crown Colonies... and so on, and so on...
Vasco Oliveira, for your failure to retrieve the Sceptre of Capon, you are hereby stripped of your position as Chief Aide to the king.

By order of His Imperial Majesty, in consultation with his most esteemed and incorruptible ministers, you are to be sent to Deserto de Prata, where, by way of atonement, you will establish a silver mint, and extend the beneficent hand of His Gracious Majesty to this most stubborn of regions.
May you bear your punishment more productively than you have borne your duties... Oh, for heaven’s sake.
How very gracious.
You think you can handle the weather here... or the people?
Onward, then. Bear us home, and don't look back.
My pleasure. Now, my ship awaits.
You… You can't make me do that, Vara. My debt is fulfilled.
Most Gracious King João, I have considered your offer to reinstate me as your Chief Aide.
I have had plenty of time to think in the nine months since I returned from Deserto de Prata — and I am afraid I must decline.
A man's value lies not in his titles, or his position, or his holdings. It lies in his ability to overcome hardships.
I have proved my worth to myself, and that is true redemption. Now, I shall tend to my estate, and enjoy the reassuringly temperate climate of my homeland.
Yours humbly, Vasco Oliveira.
P.S. I was sorry to hear that your Most Faithful Actuary, Edmundo Vara, has been unable to produce even a single bar of silver for you. He has my warmest regards.
Ten years have I languished here.

This wasteland has somehow grown even bleaker with our presence: the dust mingles with the searing stench of cyanide; the ground is strewn with broken equipment; the only novelty here, the latest shipment of exiles to hack away at the mountain.
The silver veins are dwindling... but the mountain’s appetite for the miners is undiminished. Every week, it takes another.
I ask myself daily where I went wrong; where I could have refined the production process, what more I could have done. If only I could try again.
You might want to tie your hair up before you go clearing the dung.
Hacendados y hacendadas! Gather round, and hear my tale of the Great Corn Blight of 1792.
Just make sure you brew the rum in different barrels to the hot sauce.
A new age for agriculture, and we're at the forefront!
It says it right here in the almanac: when grass is dry at morning light, look for rain before the night.
You've succeeded? What a pleasant surprise.
I believe we have a deal.
You remember Commodore Pinto? This is one I confiscated from him.
This all looks... quite satisfactory, yes.
What a desperate situation you find yourself in.
Cash for mercy? That's my kind of deal.
Excellent work, Vasco. So good to see you've kept your chin up.
And I thought your cousin was the reckless one!
The imperial prisons are fit to bursting with convicts... I'll send some your way.
Enough to cover the king's demands, and fair recompense for my services too.
Your concern for the happiness of these exiles is so very touching.
Human capital — it's one of my favourite kinds of capital.
Bring me the silver, Vasco.
On the contrary, dear Vasco, your success delights me.
Sounds like you were left out too long in the sun, Vasco.
You are a most dedicated man, Vasco.
Oh dear... But then I suppose you're rather used to failure.
You should be glad that I'm such a gracious man, Vasco.
You chose to take the sceptre this time? Progress.
Bad luck, Vasco. You do seem to attract it.
I'll be merciful — this time.
You disappoint me, Vasco.
You will make this up to me, Vasco.
I have other ways to get what I want.
Your latest disappointment.
A less gracious man than I would not be so merciful.
We all have to get our hands a little dirty from time to time.
I thought you'd have got the hang of this by now.
I'll take this, and this, oh, and some of your mining equipment...
Go on, Vasco. Let them see what kind of man their leader really is.
Falling at the final hurdle? How terribly tragic.
That's all settled, then.
Even with all these goods on board, I should have just enough room for the silver. Tick tock, Vasco.
Your time is running out, Vasco.
Don't make me wait, Vasco.
Where is my silver, Vasco?
You have my silver?
Here as promised, Vasco. You know, the king often comments on my perfect punctuality.
Wit as dry as this barren soil.
Such a desolate place... Who would come here but sinners and outcasts?
Vasco, Vasco... I am your salvation. Your guardian angel. Through my grace, you may yet step back into the light.
I do look forward to our little meetings, Vasco. Quite the profitable enterprise we have going here.
Parasite? I was not born noble like you; never had my father take me to dine with the king; never gained a position on the back of my family name! I worked, Vasco — I toiled, as you now toil.
How heartening to see these sinners put to productive work.
I don't believe that's my problem to solve, dear Vasco.
Ah, Vasco — it really saddens me to think that this could be our last meeting.
You truly think the court will listen to you, the disgraced exile?
I never knew you'd be so suited to working down the mines, Vasco. I think I'll increase your next quota.
Oh, do be aware that your next quota has been slightly increased. There were certain... unexpected shipping costs.
You know, Vasco, with all this silver, we intend to build a grand new armada: an armada of airships. Naturally, we won't be entrusting this one to any members of your family...
Good news, Vasco: the next quota will be your last. Let's make it a challenging one, eh?
I am Edmundo Vara, Actuary to King João, Collector of Royal Dues, Inspector of Crown Revenues. Such a pleasure to meet you, Vasco.
Get used to Vasco. Now, I am here to ensure that your work proceeds efficiently.
Collected your luggage?
Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear...
I call it effective oversight. I shall return periodically to collect the king's dues — have the first quota ready for my next visit.
Listen not to this foolish preacher! His god has no power in the realm of Supay!
Supay, whose halls are of silver, whose throne is of silver, whose claws are of silver, who brings the swirling storm and searing sun alike!
So bring your offerings unto the mountain, and pile them high, or your life shall be the price!
Her skin, it turned blue! Ramon says it's the silver dust.
Don't forget to bring your offerings tomorrow. The mountain is in an ill mood...
They exiled you for dissent? What a worthless crime to be banished for! You should at least have stolen something.
What kind of person brings their child here? Better left in the orphanage at Port Real.
I tried telling the judge: I'm not an arsonist, just a terrible cook! But he sent me here all the same.
And thus was he born, a child of the mountain, and lusted for silver ever after.
In his hands are the depths of the earth; and so too are the peaks of the mountains.
You're a resourceful man, Viscount Oliveira. Your lands and titles are hereby restored.
You know, none of us ever truly thought you’d get this operation up and running. Now that it’s producing so much silver... Well, it really should be entrusted to someone more responsible.
Giving orders is among my greatest strengths. You may depart.
Thank you ever so much for signing, Viscount Oliveira. Your lands and titles are hereby restored.

Ah, but here’s the thing, Vasco. Now that you’ve got this operation up and running — a fine feat, by the way — it has been placed into my capable hands. And I couldn’t think of a better administrator to install here than you.
According to this pledge of service you just signed, I can.
Farewell, Vasco. I’ll be taking your ship, since you won’t be going anywhere soon.
Scrub those walls clean, we have guests coming!
New edict announced today: all alpaca wool must be assessed for fluffiness by a royal inspector before sale. Good citizens, take heed!
So they all go inside, talk for an afternoon, and when they come out, there's a new edict we have to follow? Pah, I think I'll become an anarchist.
Take off that tatty old poncho. You're a hacendado now!
The patrón wants to use his new airship to spread fertiliser. Crackpot...

A staple of the New World diet, corn has persisted where great empires have risen and fallen.
Not technically beans, but rather seeds, the potent pips of the coffee berry are a blessing for tired workers, weary travellers, and flagging writers alike.
“Tapping” seems a rather tame term for the process of knifing a tree until it surrenders its milky white blood.
Tales are told of a Mesoan emperor who dined on nothing but liquid chocolate, frothy and bitter and sharp. Today, inhabitants of the Old World seem to prefer it sweet and solid.

The potato is a remarkable thing: it contains an extraordinary variety of nutrients, more potassium than a banana, and hearty amounts of Vitamin C. It can be fried, baked, mashed, roasted, or stewed. But as we all know, its main use is to make Schnapps.

Dr. Reginald Bosworth, chief medical advisor to the Queen, writes that "the desire to seek out spicy foods is indicative of a volatile personality, and individuals exhibiting such behaviour ought to be barred from public life". His theories remain unproven.
With wheat, one can make both bread and beer: a complete diet, as far as certain nations in the Old World are concerned.
Rum has gone by many names: grog; demon water; kill-devil; navy neaters; pirate's potion; mariner's merriment; seafarer's swig; captain's crutch. I only made three of those up.
Once upon a time in the Fertile Crescent, somebody had the odd idea to ferment grain rather than baking it into boring old bread, and humanity has been happier ever since.
A delightful drink made with finely ground corn flour, atole is best served warm. It can be enlivened with spices, fruit, or chocolate — or tequila, if you're having that kind of day.
Some are carried through this industrial revolution by their fervent belief in a brighter tomorrow; for others, it's hard liqueur.
These little bottles of fermented chilli paste provide the perfect accompaniment to an unexciting meal.

Hacienda

The hacienda is a special building that can only be constructed in the New World. It functions as a central hub for a number of unique production buildings, and allows you to enact island-wide edicts. Only one hacienda can be built per island.
Hacienda Modules

The hacienda has a number of optional modules which expand its functionality. These include the highly productive hacienda farm, additional storage buildings, space-efficient residences, and the hacienda brewery, which allows you to produce goods previously unavailable in the New World. To function, these modules must be within the hacienda’s range and be connected to it, either with regular roads or hacienda pathway/paving tiles. The hacienda’s range expands as you increase your population.
Hacienda Production
The new Hacienda Farm and Brewery modules allow you to cultivate a wide range of different crops, and process them into valuable goods.
The brewery allows you to produce goods previously unavailable in the New World. Hacienda farms offer high space efficiency, requiring fewer farm modules than their standard counterparts.
Both buildings must be in the hacienda’s range to function properly.
Production

To start production at the hacienda farm or brewery, select the desired output from the list of available products. You can produce any crop at the hacienda farm, regardless of whether the island has the requisite fertility!
Fertiliser

Fertiliser is a new resource that boosts the output of all crop farms. To use it on a farm, construct the appropriate module in its building panel. The farm will start consuming fertiliser, increasing its productivity.
Producing Fertiliser

To acquire fertiliser, you must construct animal farms within the radius of the hacienda fertiliser module. The animal farms will provide dung, which is required to make fertiliser in the fertiliser works. The fertiliser resource will then be transported to your warehouse. From there, you can use it on your island’s farms, or transport it to other islands.

Postal Service

Post offices allow you to fulfil postal lifestyle needs for your residents, providing additional income and residents. There are three types of mail: local, regional, and overseas. The latter two require airship transport and related infrastructure, but also provide greater bonuses.
Collecting Mail

Local mail is collected by post offices or post boxes. The efficiency with which these buildings collect mail increases with the number of residents in their radius. These buildings also store the mail. You can increase mail storage capacity by building more post offices, post boxes, or airmail sorting offices at the airship platform.
Mail Routes

To create a mail route, click on the airmail sorting office and select 'Your Trade Routes'. Then choose the destination, select the quantity of local mail to be loaded, and the airship you want to commit to the task.

When you're done, press 'Create Route'. Upon arrival on another island in the same region, mail will become regional mail; upon arrival in another region, mail will turn into overseas mail.

Local mail can be consumed on the same island on which it was produced. To obtain regional and overseas mail, you need to send local mail elsewhere using airship routes established at the airmail sorting office of the airship platform.

Regional mail is created when local mail travels to another island in the same region; overseas mail is created when local mail travels to another region.

Note: airmail routes are not like regular trade routes. Mail is not intended for manual loading/unloading or trade. If you choose to remove an airship from a mail route, its mail will be automatically removed.
This good will be destroyed if unloaded manually!

Scholars (Land of Lions DLC) can boost their science output with a unique mail type, New World reports. To gather this, recruit the New World Science Reporter specialist at the research institute, and equip her in a town hall with a post office in its radius.

Arctic reports can also be generated if the Arctic Science Reporter specialist is equipped in an arctic lodge with a post office in its radius (Passage DLC).
Item Transfer

Airships can be used to quickly transport items and specialists between islands and regions. Build an item transfer depot at the airship platform and move items to a free slot in the shared storage section. After a cooldown, these items can instantly be accessed in the item transfer depot on any other island.
Capacity and Storage

The more item transfer depots you build, the more items you will be able to add to the shared storage. Note that the higher the rarity of an item, the longer the cooldown before it can be accessed from the shared storage.
Aerial Warfare
Some airships can be used to attack enemy airships, using their mounted guns. They can also attack enemy harbours and naval units, using bombs.
Combat Airships
Only armed airship models are capable of targeting other airships with their mounted guns. Note that armed airships cannot directly target ground targets, including naval ships and buildings.
Drop Goods
Airships can be equipped with various drop goods, which can be deployed from the air. These are produced at supply factories.
Anti-Air Defences
Flak emplacements can now be built, which can target airships from the ground. Likewise, the new flak monitor is able to target airships. Note that flak guns are useless against non-aerial targets.
Bombs
Bombs can be used to damage enemy harbours and ships. Any other enemy targets in the area of a bomb drop will not be damaged, in accordance with the laws of war and all that.
Sea Mines
Sea mines can be dropped into the open sea, ready to explode on contact with enemy vessels.
Pamphlets
Airships can drop propaganda pamphlets over neutral or enemy islands to reduce their happiness and productivity, and increase the chance of a riot.
Care Packages
You can drop care packages over friendly or neutral islands. These increase happiness, productivity, and morale.
Fire Extinguishing
Use water drops to quickly and efficiently quench fires.
Initiating Drop Actions

Loading drop goods onto an airship will unlock the drop action button. Clicking this will allow you to plan a drop action. If you have multiple types of drop goods aboard, you'll first need to select which type you want to drop.

Next, load your drop shafts. The more drop goods you load for a run, the greater the strength and length of the run. To initiate the drop run, select 'Set Drop Target', then choose the target location for the run, as well as the direction the airship will head in after the run is completed. Drop runs will be automatically performed as long as the target is viable, or until a new order is provided.

Lifestyle Needs

Lifestyle needs are additional goods that can be provided to your residents, which grant bonuses and extra residents if fulfilled. They work like regular needs, except for the fact that fulfilling them is entirely optional! In addition, residences provided with lifestyle needs will not become abandoned if you fail to provide regular needs.
Consumption Lock

Once available, you must manually decide whether to provide lifestyle needs for each resident tier on each island. This is done via the lifestyle needs tab in the residence menu, and allows you to make sure that the resources remain available where needed.

Paloma Valente, inventor of the rigid airship, is impressed by your achievements and thinks the two of you could accomplish great things together. Would you like to help her?
Despite high praise for her airborne inventions, Paloma Valente isn't resting on her laurels. She intends to use her airships to spread joy and help those in need, and you're going to assist!
Paloma informs you that a ship carrying mail has been sunk by marauding pirates! She asks you to help her recover the mail before it's lost to the waves.

One of the parcels you recovered from the destroyed mail ship is proving particularly difficult to figure out. Paloma asks you to help her investigate, so that the parcel can be reunited with its intended recipient.
Your investigation into the origin and intended destination of the parcel leads you to believe that its owner is to be found in the New World. You ought to head there.
Your investigation into the parcel wasn't conclusive, but from the various clues you found, you've been able to draw up a list of likely owners. Take a look around!
Your investigation into the parcel allowed you to find the name of its intended recipient — even if you did have to take a little look inside. Go reunite Benison Silva with his childhood toys!
The Queen has made an unexpected appearance and demands your attention. It won't do to keep Her Majesty waiting — best you go talk to her as soon as you can.

The Queen — ever eager to outpace her continental counterparts when it comes to technological innovation — has requested that one of Paloma's new airship models be made for her. It never hurts to gain a royal favour, eh?

The Queen is pleased with her new airship... mostly. For this craft to satisfy her refined tastes, it will need to be properly furnished. Sir Archibald Blake can take care of the task, but he'll need you to bring him the necessary materials.

Paloma brings news of an artisan, so deeply stuck in his state of melancholy that a whole string of psychiatrists, doctors, priests, jesters, and one or two veterinarians have failed to shake him out of it. Paloma suggests that you go visit him — and bring an airship along.

The artisan, worn down by the repetitive monotony of existence, is entirely lacking in inspiration and unable to write a single word of literature. Paloma, however, believes that a journey among the clouds might reignite his enthusiasm.

The depressed artisan already seems to have perked up at the prospect of experiencing a flight on an airship, but he isn't quite rid of his malaise yet. Take him on a short journey and give him a new perspective on life.
The artisan was so thrilled by the tour you gave him that he's positively bursting with literary inspiration. Set him down at the next harbour so that he can begin work on his masterpiece!

A young worker's attempts to console his sister have gone awry: after he sent her some postcards illustrating the fictitious adventures of her lost stuffed penguin, the girl ran off to follow the itinerant bird!
Supremely confident in your keen eye and quick wits, you decided to look for the worker's lost sister on your own. Best bring your airship along — the aerial views will be useful.
If you're going to find the worker's lost sister, you're going to need as many clues as you can get your hands on.
Since the postcard showed Quinn the penguin out at sea, it makes sense that the worker's sister might have gone down to the harbour. You should check for further clues there.

The latest postcard seems to show Quinn amidst some potato fields. A curious place for a penguin to sojourn, but nonetheless, there's a decent chance that the worker's lost sister has also been hanging around with tubers.

After a difficult search, you and Paloma found the worker's lost sister playing on Sir Archibald Blake's island. The absent-minded ambassador had apparently failed to notice her at all! You and Paloma ought to approach her.

The worker's lost sister wants to make a postcard for her brother, just like the ones he made for her. Put aside the strangeness of a prestigious trading company's director turning photographer for an errant youth: the sooner you get this done, the sooner you can get her home.
You successfully located the worker's lost sister, and fulfilled her wish to make a postcard for her brother. Now, it's time to get the juvenile journeyer back home to her brother.

Paloma revealed that she hasn't seen her brother in years. In the dark years when La Corona desperately attempted to maintain control of her home island, repressing any dissent, her brother fell foul of the authorities and fled. You should talk to her.
Paloma has written to the Queen, requesting funds for an expedition to the Antarctic, where she hopes to find her long-lost brother. For now, there's nothing to do but wait for a response.

The Queen — a little bemused by Paloma's desire to journey to the sparse Antarctic, but willing to help nonetheless — has agreed to fund the expedition. She's even offered a choice of additional supplies.

The Queen has an outpost in the Antarctic. Whether its purpose is scientific, military, or political, you don't know and don't ask. In much the same way, the contents of the lettery she's asked you to take there are entirely mysterious. You could always refuse.

Inspired by the sibling reunion she facilitated, Paloma has made another attempt to complete a task which has bedeviled her for years: finding her brother, whom she hasn't seen since she was a child. She recalls that he wanted to be a scientific illustrator, and loved playing out in the snow — so she's searching for him in one of the few places she hasn't yet looked, the South Pole.
As monarchs are wont to do, the Queen has arrived unannounced with some urgent matter on her mind, judging by her tone. You'd better see what she wants from you.

The source of the Queen's distress is neither a pressing political matter, nor a crisis for her lowly subjects, but rather the theft of her airship. You aren't sure whether to be flattered or concerned that she's chosen you to deal with the malefactors responsible for the act.
The pirates who stole the Queen's airship are demanding a ransom for its safe return, and they aren't messing around. The Queen has deputed you to deal with the situation.
You decided to agree to the pirates' ransom demands — they seem like reasonable chaps after all, just a little light-fingered. Load up an airship with the ransom and send it their way.
You delivered the ransom to the pirates who stole the Queen's airship, and are now awaiting its safe return. This is all going rather smoothly, isn't it?
You declined to negotiate with the pirates (probably wise — they hardly seem like good business partners), and in their anger they've decided to attack you and the Queen. You'd better prepare.

You failed to properly defend the Queen from the pirates, though she at least escaped unharmed. She needs a new airship to replace the one she lost — and, of course, it's only right that you provide it.

The destruction of the royal airship resulted in a deluge of debris and poorly spelled anti-monarchical leaflets over the settlement. To rescue her reputation, the Queen demands that you drop some care packages there.
The Editor of the Daily Courier wants to talk to you about Paloma Valente, and he seems to be unusually excitable. Head over to the post office where he's waiting.
Paloma's brother is waiting in the New World to talk to you.
The Editor of the Daily Courier is involved in planning a grand reunion for Paloma and her long-lost brother. He's asked you to send her to the New World with a special parcel.
Everything's in place for the grand reunion! Paloma is waiting at the marketplace, and you've got an airship full of unsent letters from her brother, ready to rain down like confetti.
Finally, the pirates have returned the Queen's airship. A happy resolution to a sorry affair, eh? The airship is waiting in your harbour — time to go and reclaim it.

I never thought I'd see these again! You're an angel, Miss Valente!
The same sights, the same sounds, the same scents, day after day. How can a man be expected to create art amidst such drudgery?
If you insist, I suppose I shall come along. But it will be for naught, I tell you...
How beautifully the crops move in the wind — like waves in the sea! Let me grab my notebook...
From up here, this is no mere mine, but a bleeding wound in Mother Earth's side, her entrails dragged out by the cartload. Ah, I sense the beginnings of a novel!
Even this illustrious abode, furnished by the munificence of the Queen herself, seems like a child's doll house. Ripe material for my treatise on the human condition!
Thank you, Miss Valente, for this priceless gift — I am overcome with inspiration! Please, drop me off at the nearest harbour, so that I may begin my masterwork!
I can't find Quinn anywhere... But this is where he was on the postcards!
I think I understand... Well, I want to send him a postcard as well! Can you take my picture?
Brother, you won't believe the adventure I had! Paloma told me about the postcards.
You're safe! Oh, I should have just told you that I couldn't find Quinn.
No, I enjoyed the postcards very much! Please make me more — I promise I won't run off again!
Looks like you found us, Your Maj. But if you want this little beauty back, it'll cost you. Otherwise, your citizens might get some unexpected deliveries from the royal airship.
Well, ain't that sweet of you. A deal's a deal — one airship, coming right up.
Archie, I have requested that my new airship be delivered here. Be a dear and pay for it, would you?
Of course, Your Majesty! Always a thrill to have a mighty vessel glide its way into one's port.
Just applying the finishing touches, Your Majesty...
I moved a lot when I was a boy, you know. Papa took work wherever he could find it...
Do you prefer wheat or corn? Me, I like both.
I don't trust postmen. It's those fancy hats...
Couriers are just too expensive these days. Better to find a friend who can take it with them.
Thank you for the help! Please, take these letters — I wrote them to Paloma over the years, but never knew where to send them. When she gets to the market, drop them from the skies like confetti!
Hold on a minute — we've got one last gift for you! You're going to enjoy this.
You lost the letters? Good thing they were just copies! I've got more of them here.
Definitely not mine — I refuse to have anything to do with post!
Not for me. Nobody ever sends me anything — I've been legally dead for 11 years!
Is that my copy of Corn Farmer Monthly? No? Not interested then.

I have gone to find Quinn. He left me lots of clues so I could follow him.

It will be easy to spot him because he is a penguin and there are not many penguins around here.


Anna

An old parcel, battered and browned, has been moving around for years. It's been stamped and stamped again by dozens of puzzled postmasters, and by now, the addressee's name is illegible.

You need more information. What's the best course of action?
Write to a philatelist who may be able to identify the old stamps
Persuade the company which owned the wrecked ship to provide further information
Write to a palaeographer who may be able to decipher the old handwriting

It seems that the oldest marking is a hand stamp from the New World, pre-dating the invention of adhesive stamps.

An interesting start, but you'll need more information to track down the intended recipient. What do you do next?

Sufficiently persuaded by your financial sweetener — and bemused by your interest in this odd package — the head of the shipping company tells you what she knows about the parcel.

It was 'inherited' from a now defunct shipping company. The parcel has been moving back and forth for years, befuddling scores of postal workers and customs officers, and picking up numerous stamps on its futile travels.

Bad news: it's the most common name in the continent, Silva.

The worker explains that his little sister recently lost her stuffed penguin toy, Quinn.

To placate his distressed sibling, the worker has been making postcards about Quinn's travels, pretending that they were from the peripatetic penguin. He purchased a stack of postcards, then painted on the penguin.

Now the sister has disappeared, leaving only a note. Well, you'd better read it for yourself...
Look at the note

The worker says that he sent his sister more postcards, but he can't find them at home — she must have taken them with her.

Paloma looks wistfully into the middle distance as she recalls her brother.

You've not known her for long, but this pensiveness seems most unlike her. Perhaps you should talk to her.
Ask Paloma more about her brother

Paloma sighs.

'I've tried looking for him, but I just have so little to go on. He was great at drawing, I remember that much — wanted to be a scientific illustrator, in fact.'

How do you respond?
Ask if there's anywhere she hasn't looked yet
Ask if she remembers any places her brother particularly liked.

Paloma shrugs.

'I've looked everywhere, pretty much. Well, except for the Antarctic. Too dangerous, too expensive. And why would he even be there?'
Point out that for a would-be scientific illustrator, the Antarctic is a fascinating destination!

A slight smile crosses Paloma's lips.

'He was always fascinated by the Antarctic. Loved playing out when it snowed — he used to say, "Just think: there's a place that's nothing but snow!" But nobody lives there, right?'
Point out that there are numerous Antarctic research posts — the sort of place a scientific illustrator might end up...

Paloma's face lights up.

'Hey, you're right! Well, it's a long shot, but as I recall, I've recently acquired a royal favour. I'll ask the Queen to fund an expedition to the Antarctic!'
Contact the Queen

Paloma's face lights up.

'Hey, you're right! Well, an Antarctic expedition will be expensive — but once I've finished that airship for the Queen, I'll have a royal favour to call in.'

The Queen generously offers you a range of supplies for your travels to the icy south.

If you have a better idea, you could simply keep the Queen's gift and take something else along instead.
Accept some basic supplies
Accept some materials to build a new airship for the expedition
Accept the services of a skilled specialist

In true monarchical fashion, the Queen has delegated the delicate task of resolving this issue to you.

You could cough up the ransom demanded by the covetous corsairs, or prepare to defend the Queen against their wrath if you refuse.

Paloma and a small team start surreptitiously making their way through the snow. It soon becomes apparent why this location is unpatrolled: the ground is treacherous, the snow concealing deep cracks.

A sudden scream halts the crew’s progress, as an engineer’s leg slips deep into a crevice. The group pull him out, but his leg is broken and the crew beg to return to the airship before anyone else gets hurt.

Paloma nods, her spirit shattered like the engineer’s bloodied leg. The journey is over.

Once you've produced the requisite materials, you can begin constructing your first rigid airship at the hangar. You can filter your airships by whether they are armed or unarmed. Armed airships are equipped with weapons capable of targeting other airships. They are fast and dangerous, but offer less cargo space than unarmed airships.

First, local mail. Simple: this is mail that's both created and delivered right here on this island.
Next, regional mail. When you take mail to another island in the same region, it becomes regional mail. You currently don't have any, but we'll see to that soon.
Finally, overseas mail. When you take mail to another island in a different region, it becomes overseas mail. It's the most valuable kind of mail, providing the most bonuses!
Shopping Arcades will produce luggage if a passenger kiosk is nearby: these luggages can be consumed as a lifestyle need in the New World.

You can create a new airmail route from here. Airship routes can only be established between islands that have airship platforms. Load local mail on the trade route, and it will automatically become regional or overseas mail when arriving on another island.

When mail arrives at another island within the same region, it will automatically become regional mail. If it arrives at another island in a different region, it will become overseas mail — the most valuable kind! You can think of delivering mail like a step in a production chain. Check your airmail sorting office to see how much mail of each kind you have on your island.

Be aware: mail routes have some unique rules compared to regular trade routes! Mail can't be manually loaded or unloaded, only added to an automatic route. So if you remove an airship from that route, any mail on board will be immediately removed.

Probably shouldn't be allowed to handle explosives, but she gets the job done.
Knows the dirt.
A dung devotee.
Balloon popper.
Does the rounds.
Squeezes every last drop.
Keeps the gas pressure steady and the pilot's pressure low.
Wields her wrench like a painter's brush.
The cargo bay is his kingdom, and you'll arrange the crates as he commands!
Has an aptitude for altitude.
Wind speeds, air pressure, altitude, temperature, velocity — countless factors swirl inside her head as she steers effortlessly.
A highly respected scientific authority, apart from that one article on the medicinal benefits of ingesting mashed parrot.
An accomplished penguinologist.
Commands his team of burly unloaders with the discipline of an army drill sergeant.
"This way to your room, ma'am... No, we don't offer separate accommodation for your hound."
Knows the dirt.
A dung devotee.
Highly persuasive.
Just try not to set it off near your own gas bags.
Detects underwater metal objects — ideally mines, but people keep dumping steel beams into the sea...
Filled with flammable arctic gas.
Equipped with anti-air weaponry.

Soggy, but mostly legible.
An excitable philatelist tours your post offices, interrupting the work with his enthusiastic questions.
A despondent artisan in need of inspiration.
Far from exhausted by her travels, the little girl eagerly presses her face to the window.
Stamped with the royal seal, and filled with orders far above your station.
A set of valuable sketches, to be delivered to an author in the New World.
Countless letters written but never sent, from one lost sibling to another.
An old map of another research camp, provided by the penguin researcher. He's marked the main office with an X.
A good luck charm, supposedly. It certainly has an enchanting aura...
All who look into its eyes are instantly charmed.
"We will turn your pots and pans into airships and cannons, rifles and rockets."
Postmen snap into action at the sight of it.
The modern world moves fast, and so must one's mail.
"Advertising is based on one thing: annoying people until they buy something."
"Oh, I have slipped the surly bonds of earth, and danced the skies on laughter-silvered blimps..."
"Oh dear sir, it appears you're over the limit. Now, if you'll just pay a little fee..."

Contrary to its reputation, airship food is actually rather good.
It's not your ebonised oak chair and sturdy mahogany desk, but it'll do.

A place to gather with other passengers, tut loudly at delay announcements, and anxiously examine pocket watches.

Package Received
Drenched!

Well well, it seems that I'm famous. But I'm not in this for the kudos — my dream is to connect the four corners of the world. So I'm making my designs available to everyone — your good self included.
It's almost magical, flying among the clouds. I've been thinking — I want to spread some of that magic. Want to help?
Much appreciated. I've got piles of requests for my help — let me sort through them, and I'll get back to you.
No problem — I'm sure you have your hands full with all those production chains.
Our first task, my friend: a mail ship has been sunk by pirates. Would never happen with an airship, of course. Anyway, let's retrieve that mail before it's lost at sea!
Fantastic, I'll get these parcels delivered straight away. But this one here seems a little difficult — could you take a look?
Wondrous, no, the joy that a single act of kindness can bring?
Monarchy isn't my style... But royal approval makes for great publicity.
I've been told about an artisan afflicted with a melancholy so powerful that even the most radical psychiatric treatments have failed to uplift him. We ought to pay a visit.
I think he’ll be amazed what a simple change of perspective can do for a despondent disposition.
There's always wonder in the world — even if we sometimes need help to find it.
Another request for our help: this young man's little sister has gone missing.
Hello, little one. Your brother sent me. You see, he couldn't find your penguin — so he made those postcards, to make you happy.
A photographic masterpiece. Now, let's get you back home.

Ah, siblings reunited. I haven't seen my brother for years. Got in trouble with the authorities back when La Corona was still in charge, slipped away before they could grab him, and we never saw him again.
I've tried looking for him, but I just have so little to go on. He was great at drawing, I remember that much — wanted to be a scientific illustrator, in fact.
I've looked everywhere, pretty much. Well, except for the Antarctic. Too dangerous, too expensive. And why would he even be there?
He was always fascinated by the Antarctic. Loved playing out when it snowed — he used to say, "Just think: there's a place that's nothing but snow!" But nobody lives there, right?
Hey, you're right! Well, it's a long shot, but as I recall, I've recently acquired a royal favour. I'll ask the Queen to fund an expedition to the Antarctic!
Hey, you're right! Well, an Antarctic expedition will be expensive — but once I've finished that airship for the Queen, I'll have a royal favour to call in.
When did dwelling in the past ever bring anything but disappointment? I should get back to my workshop.
This parcel has no address, and it's barely sealed... It's full of sketches!
Is this... Some sort of message for me? Follow the penguin again, I suppose.
All of these are addressed to me! From... my brother? Saulo, you found me!
I'd almost given up hope... I guess when you spread a little kindness, some of it must make its way back to you.
Release the mooring ropes, drop the ballast, vent the ballonets — we're taking off!
Well worth the effort.
This could be a problem.
What to do now?
Difficulties are made to be overcome.
Why, would you look at that...
This looks promising.
I've faced worse.
Just need a little courage.
One way or another...
I can do this.
Onwards.
We keep searching.
We press on.
We're close, I feel it.
We'll find him, I know it.
We'll find him, I know it.
Helium is essential for safe airships — but to get it out of the ground, we're going to have to pump something in.
And so begins the age of aerial warfare. No turning back now.
Strange-looking stuff, bauxite — but with a little magic, it can give us the lightweight metal that we need.
Once that hangar's assembled... Ah, what a sight it'll be!
An impressive structure, I must say — befitting the wondrous craft that we're going to launch.
Lightweight, flexible, durable... The future will be built from aluminium, and we're going to need a lot.
Magnificent, isn't she? Sturdy, reliable, capacious too — plenty of room for post, passengers, cargo...
Sleek, streamlined, powerful... These will revolutionise tactical thinking.
What goes up must come down.
A modern economy needs all sorts of gadgets and gizmos — not to mention experts and engineers. Now you can transport them across your empire at record speeds.
One step closer to connecting the world.
Get another one of those up and running, and your workers will be able to live on one island and work on another.
Think of all the letters that will flow through here; all the drama! Love reaffirmed, rivalries stoked, reunions arranged...
A beautiful structure, no? And what joy it's going to bring, distributing letters from all over the world!
A loquacious bunch, your people — the mail's already starting to come in, ready for you to deliver it!
I knew air mail would be the next big thing.
Extraordinary, no? Voices can travel across continents for the price of a stamp!
Wonderful — now your residents will have the chance to experience the thrill of flight for themselves. Let's sell some tickets!
There's a clamour for fast international travel, and we're going to provide it.
A new era of cosmopolitanism; of truly global cities!
I should finish repairing this airship before I start competing.
Good as new.
Not a bad base of operations, but I need to get my mailing operation set up before I start competing.
I love a challenge. Who have you got for me?
Glad we're all having fun.
Let's see what we have here... "Dear Miss Paloma Valente, we are delighted to invite you to the first Grand Postal Derby."

"This special competition — organised and exclusively covered by the Daily Courier — promises to be the greatest competitive event in the history of humankind, surpassing even the 1806 Sausage-Making Championship."
"Victory will require a dedication to deliveries, a mastery of mail-routes, and pre-eminent postal prowess!" Who on earth writes like this?
"We at the Daily Courier have no doubt that your airships will thrill the public, and provide stiff competition for even the slickest of mail delivery operations."
"We eagerly await your arrival. Yours sincerely, the editorial board of the Daily Courier." Well, I do love a challenge.
Pleasure to be here. I'm looking forward to showing what my airships are capable of.
Well, isn't that sweet of you. Speaking of competitors, who am I up against?
Ah, so that wasn't a heavily armed pirate cove I spotted on the way in? And a whole string of anti-air cannons?
Well then, I'd better get started. That trophy is mine.
They... love stamps?
This is the strangest competition I've ever heard of. I can't wait.
Thank you, thank you – careful with those fireworks, though.
I'd say that was a pretty conclusive demonstration of the power of my airship designs.
Flattered, Your Majesty, but I think I'd rather stay in charge of my own business.
Sort out your pirate infestation, and I'll consider it.
Give my regards to your colleagues at the Daily Courier – I’m looking forward to reading the final report!
"Dear Miss Valente, your friend at the Daily Courier here."
"I thought you might enjoy getting an advanced look at the final write-up before we go to press."
"Victorious Valente Vanquishes Monarchical Mailmen!"... My word, he really does love alliteration.
"The Grand Postal Derby came to its thrilling conclusion with airship pioneer Paloma Valente pitting her skills against the Royal Mail itself."
"Undaunted by the challenge, Valente and her airborne fleet triumphed magnificently, conquering not only the skies, but the hearts of countless spectators."

"Despite the unexpected incursion of some local pirates (whose presence and acts of criminal damage the Daily Courier accepts no liability for), the event went smoothly, showcasing the potential of the rigid airship to bring humanity together."
Couldn't have put it better myself.
These technophobes are going to slow down my operation — but I reckon I can help them out.
Welcome to the modern world, my friends.
I'll make sure to have the airship frames checked more regularly.
Or too unprofitable — these financial records are a mess!
This may require some reorganisation...
A 'psychiatric curiosity', or so I read in the Sunday Inquirer. Not that I prefer your competitor, of course.
And high standards — some of their reviews are absolutely vicious.
You wouldn't happen to have an aspirin, would you?
Seems he was setting up a mail company. I hear that connecting long-lost relatives is his speciality.
Should have stuck to dynamite fishing.
Well, she seems lovely — pleasure to meet you, Mrs O'Mara!
I'm beginning to think she isn't such a nice gal after all...
What kind of competition is this?!
I really think you should read the entry forms more carefully next time.
Have you seen these attack ads she's putting out? "Valente's airships are piloted by drunkards, thieves, opium addicts, and dogs." Scandalous!
Ever think you might enjoy alliteration a little too much?
That arctic weather seems to follow them around — I'm suddenly freezing!
I'm starting to wonder what I signed up for...
I still can't believe you let them compete!
That's okay, they've only got an entire state behind them.
Better luck next time, Your Majesty. Now, time to go collect my prize.
I wonder who this belongs to?
No harm in taking a little look...
Now, who should get this one?
Now, who do I know with award-worthy facial hair?
Might make a nice story for the Daily Courier.
Plenty of lost mail lying around here. I wonder what I might find...
I'm already airborne.
Watch the skies — I'll only be a minute.
This will be a breeze.
Permission to dock?
Ready for your delivery?
How does this look?
Another time.
A nice journey, nonethless.
No problem — I'm not lacking for storage space.
You see? Air mail is the way forward!
More glamorous than a cargo steamer, eh?
One of my fastest deliveries yet.
My airship designs require some unique and complicated materials. Would you like an introduction to their use?
First, we'll need a hangar — and a big one at that.
Unlike the blimps that came before me, my airships aren't simple gas bags: they maintain their shape with their lightweight aluminium frames. We'll need to produce plenty.
Along with using it for airships, we'll need aluminium to build their platforms too.
That's one island set up — but if we really want to get things moving, we'll need to build an airship platform on another.
Now, the second key thing we need is helium. It's going to take a while to produce enough to fill an airship, so let's get started.
Here, a little something to help you start filling up that storage space.
As it happens, I've got a few letters that need to be delivered here. Let's distribute them.
Now, we're going to need some post boxes for your people to drop off their mail.
So many people across so many islands, all keen to send each other post. We'll need to set up a mail route.
One thing I won't have to explain is gravity. Bombs, mines, pamphlets, care packages — load up your airships and let them rain down.
You are in the presence of royalty.
These flying machines are utterly fascinating — I must have one for myself! Send it to Archie when it's done.
Splendid work! The furnishings lack the requisite regality, however. Archie can fix that, if you'll provide him the materials.
Much better! When King João sees this, he'll scuttle back to his mouldy old flagship in shame!
Thanks to your magnificent airship, I am the envy of the continent! It is only right that I repay you, however odd your proposed expedition might sound.
Oh, and if you have the chance, please do deliver this letter to a small outpost I have stationed there.
You there! I require your immediate assistance — my old airship has been stolen!
After my airship disappeared, I received this grammatical mess of a ransom note.
A queen does not negotiate with pirates... But you can. Go and recover my airship, posthaste!
How impertinent! I shall not even consider stooping to talk to these reprobates.
Rewarding criminal behaviour? I hope you don't expect this ransom to come from the royal coffers...
Ah, my property has finally been returned.
What on earth...?!
Those wretches! Showering my people not only with debris, but with scurrilous slurs about their rightful sovereign! This must be rectified.
I do hope you know what you're doing — you can hardly expect the pirates to fight fairly.

Not the finest hour of my otherwise glorious reign, but at least I still have my life. A show of generosity will be needed to refute those scurrilous pamphlets — and the royal fleet will require a new airship.
That seems to have been the last of those hoodlums. Now, a show of generosity will be needed to refute those scurrilous pamphlets.
A shambolic affair, but a happy resolution in the end. Take this token of my gratitude and let us never speak of these events again.
If you beat me, I shall have you arrested for treason. Only joking — that isn't going to happen.
Do keep up, Miss Valente.
Don't worry, dear — I'll make sure to mention you in my victory speech.
I wouldn't know, of course, but I imagine it's rather thrilling to be defeated by a queen.
How can you possibly expect to beat me? Half the stamps have my face on them!
I expect a proper effort from you, Miss Valente, despite the stupefying effects of my regal splendour.
Unacceptable! I need someone to blame, immediately!
A conclusive demonstration of the incompetence of my Postmaster General! Now that his position is shortly to become vacant, how would you like a job, Miss Valente?
Where to?
What'll it be?
Airborne and ready to go.
Skies are clear.
Lift achieved.
Ready to fly.
Onward!
On our way.
Sky's the limit.
Nose forward.
Adjusting for winds.
Engines engaged.
We're taking fire!
We're in peril!
Bail! Bail! Bail!
We're going to crash!
We're airborne.
Taking flight!
Following.
We'll keep an eye on them.
Initiating drop.
Deploying.
Make it rain.
Bay doors open.
The inspector is coming today, so get sorting.
Strange thing, an airship under construction. Like a beached whale...
Hold on to those ropes — she'll be arriving soon enough!
Another ingot, coming right up!
'As parent birds, when first their callow care, leave the high nest to tempt the liquid air...'
Fire up the rotary kilns!
First class or second class, sir?
What on earth have you been ordering, Mrs. Johnson? This weighs a ton!
Affix the gondola!
Careful with those gas cells, I don't want any leaks!
Weird looking stuff, isn't it?
Load up the carts.
You live on one island and work on another? Why, that does sound grand.

Grand Postal Derby

In the Grand Postal Derby, competitors are placed into groups. Beat two rivals in your group to progress to the next stage. How do you beat them? Well, you'll need to prove your postal prowess by delivering stamps to local collectors!
Stamps, Mail, and Island Charters
Stamps

So, how do you get those stamps? First, construct post offices to generate mail. Then, when your residents consume the mail, they'll return the stamps to you, which you can collect and deliver like any other good.

Local mail (generated and consumed on the same island) will get you local stamps. Airmail (generated on one island, consumed on another) will get you airmail stamps.
Island Charters

There are rules to this competition, don't you know? One of them is that you can't settle a new island without an island charter. Island charters are given out as rewards for completing a stage of the competition. Spend them wisely — the Daily Courier might not have printed enough for you to settle all of the islands in the region...
Competitors

There are many rival companies participating in the Derby! You can choose which rival from your group to take on. Challenges will always consist of delivering a certain number of stamps, but each competitor also has their own unique objective that you'll need to complete — and unique negative effects that you'll have to deal with for the duration of the challenge!
Competition Stages

After registering for the Derby, you'll be placed into a group with three rival postal companies. To get through the group and advance to the next stage, you'll need to challenge and defeat two competitors. Go through three such stages, and then... well, rumour has it there's a special finale in store.

Note: don't take too long to start challenging your rivals, or they might win the group ahead of you!
Reward Buffs

Each rival company you defeat will give you a special buff that's activated in the grand finale. You can collect all the bonuses, or only choose ones that you think will give you a winning edge in the finale. Anyway, we shouldn't be telling you about the finale...

My Good Sir,

I gained much from your recently published treatise, Puppets on Strings: Civilisation and its Overlords, in which you so brilliantly articulated the ways in which governments treat societies as if they were mere games, and their people simply automata. The metaphor is so accurate that I almost wonder whether it is in fact the real truth!

But I must disagree with your advocacy of propaganda of the deed, on the grounds that one can never predict the consequences of such actions. I shall give you an example. Let us say that one of our young comrades, hot with fervour, proceeds to destroy a sausage factory owned by a notorious strike-breaker. Certainly, one damages the holdings of our anti-trade-unionist enemies — but at what cost to our cause? After all, we must aim to bring onside as many workers as possible, but if we are seen to cause a sausage shortage, the disgruntlement of the local population will surely be turned against us, rather than the true oppressors.

I keenly await your response,
Peter Pelloutier

To the aliens living in the sea,

My name is Professor William Warburton, and it is my great pleasure to make your acquaintance. None of my colleagues believes in your existence, but I shall prove them all wrong!

Let me tell you a little about our species. We are bipedal, hairy in varying degrees, and experience a range of emotions including dejection, exasperation, and wrath, such as when a colleague disparages one's carefully-considered theories. Some radical theorists proclaim that we are descended from apes, though I think it more likely that we stem from almonds or peaches. We subsist mainly on fish and sausages, and are a fairly placid lot, although a schnapps shortage is considered a fair cause for civil disobedience.

I do hope you'll consider emerging from the unexplored depths to greet us land-dwellers, and usher in a new era of inter-species friendship.

Dearest Rachel,

My hard work here bears fruit — already I have been promoted to Senior Editor. Our publishing house goes from strength to strength, providing fine literature throughout the continent.

But such news will give you little comfort, I know. Every day, I ask myself whether I made the right choice in leaving you to come here, and every day I grow more certain that I made a grave mistake. Whatever wealth I may gain, whatever fine projects I may complete, whatever goodness I may spread, what does any of it mean if I am without you?

I am not as brave as I once thought, and I readily admit it. I am no lone genius, but a soul split in two.

Tell me to give all this up, and come be with you, and I shall do so in an instant.

ON THE LOST TREASURES OF ENBESA

For the intrepid explorer, Enbesa is a land of great opportunity indeed, with many ancient treasures still to be uncovered. It is rumoured, for instance, that a golden staff, passed down by generations of Enbesan kings, lies buried beneath the great well at Durame.

Travellers to Enbesa are advised to bring plenty of potable water, lightweight clothing, and some method of protection against sunburn. For the latter purpose, a recipe consisting of the following ingredients, well-mixed and strained, is recommended:

Two drachms borax
One drachm Roman alum
One drachm camphor
Half ounce sugar-candy
One pound ox-gall

A lost page from G. T. Herbert's Guide to Exotic Treasures.
Select to read.
A golden staff? I sense an adventure! I love claiming precious ancient artifacts as personal possessions, because I am rich.

The judges carefully considered the smoothness, cleanliness, softness, size, shapeliness, and — most crucially of all — the density of various famous beards, and concluded that yours was worthy of the prize.

Pah, I only want awards for my inventions! Tell you what — I know an old jornalero with a lovely set of whiskers, try him.
Oh, no boss, I'm just a humble man — don't need any awards. I heard the Emperor of Enbesa was visiting, though — would make a fine gift for him.
Much appreciated, young lady, but it would not be appropriate for me to participate in such frivolities. I would suggest taking it to that hardworking editor.
How very pleasing! Do you think it would be unbecoming of me to write an article about my little victory?
You know, I was going to shave the whole lot off, but now I think I'll keep it! Thank you!
Alright, alright, give it here. Is there a trophy in it? Maybe I can melt it down for scrap...
Well, maybe the grandkids will be excited to see it. Gracias!
Well, it is nice to be appreciated for my facial hair. People usually pay more attention to my hat.

You found the Beard of the Year award lying around — unfortunately intercepted before it could reach its intended recipient, it seems. There are various bearded fellows present in the region — whom do you consider most deserving of the award?

Why, this is a pickle!

It seems that none of the bearded boys around here wants to accept the award, for one reason or another.

The fate of the Beard of the Year award rests solely in your hands! What should be done?

RULES OF THE DERBY

Registration
— All participants must bring their registration form, and one stamp, to the Daily Courier Office. Don't forget the stamp!

Competition Rules
— All competitors are assigned to a group. The winners of each group will form a new group, and so on until only one remains!
— To win your group, challenge and defeat two competitors!
— According to the wishes of our generous and very reasonable sponsors, the Royal Philatelic Society, all challenges will involve stamps!

Stamps
— Get stamps by delivering mail to your residents. They'll gladly give you the used stamps.
— You'll be delivering these stamps to stamp enthusiasts here in the arena!


RE: All Those Lost Letters
There's a lot of lost mail around here. You won't get any extra points for collecting it, but your help tidying up the arena will be much appreciated. Besides, you might find something interesting!

The Daily Courier insists that you hire some of the elderly postmen, just to make things fair. Now, let them tell you how things were done in the old days...
A set of regulations aimed at ensuring postal airships don't explode. Unions, eh?
Enthusiasm for post has been dampened since Last Mile Co-op started inundating you with copies of Potato Planter Weekly...
The march of progress is relentless, and occasionally confusing.
Trust Wibblesock to flood the mail system with spam, scams, and general drivel!
These reviews are sickening — literally!
Aarhant has whipped everyone into a frenzy with his promise to reunite long-lost relatives!
Scores of pedantic customs officers have descended upon you, insisting on double-checking everything you send. O'Mara has nothing to do with this, naturally.
Hordes of ruffians, hooligans, and guttersnipes are milling around and raising hell! O'Mara has nothing to do with this, naturally.
Occurrences of cooking fires, overturned candles, and improperly discarded cigars have suddenly and suspiciously increased!
Are those... Pyrphorian flame ships?
"Valente's postmen steal money from birthday cards, draw crude images on love letters, and smuggle narcotics in old ladies' parcels."
An inundation of preposterously heavy packages, straining your poor postmen to the limit!
A rancorous legal dispute about the original patent for lighter-than-air craft has begun; until it's resolved, airship production has been halted.
An unseasonal chill is inbound!
All those pirate ships? Why, they're just here to celebrate a birthday party. Lots of pirates are born around this time of year, you know?
No pirate's birthday is complete without a reckless discharge of munitions. Any damage to your buildings is entirely accidental.
The royal actuaries are out in force.
A very mean declaration, filled with all sorts of slights on your employees.
Archibald Blake's crack team of seasoned customs officers ensure that every item gets thoroughly probed.
Privateering has a long and noble tradition — you should be honoured to be hunted down by such illustrious fellows.
The hardy old postmen are pitching in.
United Postal have devised new, efficient airship regulations, saving on maintenance costs!
The Last Mile Co-Op have brought fresh produce from the heartlands along with their postal rounds.
The experiment has borne fruit, offering new insights into efficient work organisation.
Everyone's amused to hear Wibblesock's tales of how he was suckered by a scam letter from a fake Enbesan prince.
The travellers have brought some obscure medical treatments back from their journeys, to make up for their earlier toxicity.
A tide of long-lost siblings, estranged children, and misplaced parents has arrived — and to thank Aarhant for reuniting them, they're ready to help.
O'Mara has provided some of her expert smugglers to serve as navigators. Sorry, not smugglers — just very shy helmsmen.
The friendly chaps at Blazing Fast Mail have given some helpful seminars on fireproofing.
Kahina's years of shipping experience allow her to give valuable insights to your warehouse staff.
Pole-to-Pole Postal are bringing in some express mail the long way round. The really, really long way round.
Who better to give you some tips on brawling than a pirate?
An extensive and mostly incomprehensible form, the main purpose of which is to divest the Daily Courier of all responsibility for what happens next.

A CLASH OF COURIERS

Dear Miss Paloma Valente,

We are delighted to invite you to the first Grand Postal Derby. This special competition — organised and exclusively covered by the Daily Courier — promises to be the greatest competitive event in the history of humankind, surpassing even the 1806 Sausage-Making Championship.

Victory will require a dedication to deliveries, a mastery of mail-routes, and pre-eminent postal prowess! We at the Daily Courier have no doubt that your airships will thrill the public, and provide stiff competition for even the slickest of mail delivery operations.

We eagerly await your arrival.

Yours sincerely,

The editorial board of the Daily Courier.

The Grand Postal Derby
The Grand Postal Derby

Dear Miss Valente,

Your friend at The Daily Courier here.
I thought you might enjoy getting an advanced look at the final write-up before we go to press.
VICTORIOUS VALENTE VANQUISHES MONARCHICAL MAILMEN
The Grand Postal Derby came to its thrilling conclusion with airship pioneer Paloma Valente pitting her skills against the Royal Mail itself.
Undaunted by the challenge, Valente and her airborne fleet triumphed magnificently, conquering not only the skies, but the hearts of countless spectators.

Despite the unexpected incursion of some local pirates (for whose presence and acts of criminal damage The Daily Courier accepts no liability), the event went smoothly, showcasing the potential of the rigid airship to bring humanity together.
Congratulations, felicitations, bravo and hooray! The Grand Postal Derby has a worthy winner! Now, time for the editor to take a well-earned rest...
Oh dear! Not the outcome you were hoping for, eh? Well, there's always next year...

Scenario Quest
Every string a mystery, a woven piece of history. Malching snagged this from Paloma, ooh... several years ago now.
The revolution's first blow was struck with this blade, but fate cruelly determined that the enemy, under Admiral Silva, should then claim it as a trophy.
This Mesoan god was far from toothless. No wonder it spoke to Margaret Hunt, who, rumors suggest, still smiles with all of her original teeth.
A simple envelope. But what does it contain?
Something is rattling around inside.

Kassandra Hisna Nalaoui,

How I rejoice that you have chosen to write to me again.

I know I have caused you much grief, but I can say in all honesty that it never crossed my mind to take the idol you sent me for, and now you know the truth.

I, being the fool that I am, did go to Prosperity, but upon reaching it, I was tied up and shipped to the Old World like a parcel.

But let us speak no more of this.
If Hunt has it, it is within our reach. I have asked one of my friends to make inquiries among her servants.

I must warn you, though, that I was not the only one to take an interest in the past.

We did have our initial suspicions, as you knew the Pyrphorian symbols, but you soon proved your innocence.

You are impeccable in your manner; the wealth you have amassed has only added to your reputation.

She, on the other hand, cannot afford a single misstep. Her niece's rebellion has greatly infuriated Her Majesty.

While searching her drawers, our common friend has stumbled upon an interesting document.
It concerns one Edmundo Vara, and includes some fairly detailed numbers and charts.

While I cannot make sense of them, I doubt Hunt kept them hidden for no good reason.

I was able to learn a little more about our mystery man: loud, brash, curly hair, calls himself an artist.

He has been talking to witnesses of the Pyrphorian crisis, trying to assemble a list of stolen items.
Among them was a certain idol, bearing the likeness of Hueyaca.

When he's not sniffing about, he seems to be spending ample time with Miss Paloma, who likes to leave her doors unlocked.

The circumstances allowed us to procure the blueprints of her famous airships
While they are undoubtedly valuable, I do not know if a sale would pass unnoticed.

She knows what you're after, and will be on her guard.

I do hope you'll be careful in confronting her - remember what she did to Isabel and her people. Even unmasked, she still has cronies that will do her bidding.

I have placed the drawings you sent in the hands of a talented young artisan. The result is remarkably accurate - I doubt the untrained eye could tell that it's a fake. All you need now is an opportunity to make the exchange.

Speaking of opportunities, one of our friends has gained access to Hunt's finest liquor.
The finest minds in the New World have been getting tipsy on her wares. You need only say the word...

Dear Madame,

Ever since you arrived in the New World, your name has become a synonym for exquisite taste.

It is no secret that you deal in some of our greatest treasures. While this practice is perfectly legal, we regret that our people were unable to place a bid for what is rightfully theirs.

We, the Artista Collective, want to encourage the repatriation of these objects and hope to enlist your help in this matter.

Rather than intrude on your time uninvited, we have an offer to make - one that is well-suited to your talents as a trader.

We await your presence at the Atelier Insólito, graciously hosted by the Yaosca Research Centre.

Respectfully,
