Festivals
Electricity in the New World

Power plants can now be constructed in the New World. Supply a factory with electricity and you'll boost its productivity - but supply a New World animal farm with it, and its pastures will produce bonus goods! These powered pastures require no street connection - goods produced this way instantly move to your warehouse.
Secondary Products

Providing electricity to animal farms in the New World allows them to produce secondary products in addition to their regular produce. Pastures do not require a street connection to deliver secondary products - the transfer is instantaneous.
The Dam
The Dam is a unique monument that can only be built on the Great Island of Manola. It is a self-sufficient power plant that requires no input and provides the entire island with clean energy.
Advanced City Institutions

City institutions can now be upgraded. Their upgraded forms require additional input to operate, but are fully automated, sending out all available units whenever an incident occurs. They strongly reduce the chance of an incident occurring, and have a higher street range than regular city institutions.
Advanced Volunteer Units

Advanced units have reduced unlock requirements and automatically respond to incidents. Once the advanced institution they belong to is no longer supplied with the goods it requires, they will behave like ordinary units, responding to incidents, but never heading out in full numbers unless prompted.
Stadium
The stadium can host sports championships that award influence and trigger festivals on the island that's hosting the event.
Starting a Championship

To host a championship, select one of the three available tiers and provide the stadium with the required goods. Once preparations are complete, you'll be prompted to choose a reward chest and claim the influence you've earned.
Football Festivals

After hosting a championship, a cooldown will trigger, during which the residents of your island will gather to celebrate the winning team. The effects of this festival will vary depending on the scope of the championship you hosted.
Public Services - Samba School & Cinema
Service Production Chains

Samba schools and cinemas are new public service buildings that require specific goods to function. In exchange, they have a higher street range than regular public services, serving residences that are further away.
Public Services - Beach

The beach is a special public service building. Its range can be increased with the use of beach ornaments. You can place them according to your preference, with each ornament contributing to the range of all beach buildings on that island.
Pride & Peddlers

In this scenario, your task is to establish a trade empire by staying abreast of an ever-changing market, always adapting to supply and demand. You are not pressed for time, but your resources are limited, so use them wisely!
Making Money

All of your residents in this scenario are volunteers, working for the Artista Collective in exchange for food and shelter - but they pay no taxes in exchange for the basic needs you provide. You can, however, make a fortune by selling goods to other traders. Your residents could perhaps also be tempted to pay for more exclusive goods, such as those which might be obtained on the Black Market...
Time to Trade

Six trading posts are scattered around this part of the world, all of which have unique offers and demands. Note that the goods you sell there will be sold at the current world market price. All traders will stick to their islands - the remaining islands are yours to explore.
Relics and Riches

In order to win, you need to build a museum, and equip it with the lost treasures of the New World. The greatest of these treasures need to be purchased from other parties - but who knows what you may find if you set sail for new horizons...
Ebb and Flow
In Pride & Peddlers, your mines have finite deposits - so eventually, they'll run out. Trade your ores wisely, and settle new islands to increase your supply.
Unexpected Events
As your population grows, certain trade-related events may occur. Some may reduce your profits; others might provide an unexpected boost to your economy. Stay flexible and best your competitors!
Boosting the Economy
Most traders sell rare items that can boost your economy. You can also maximize your agricultural output by making good use of tractors and fertilisers!
Annopedia

Though a hangover from colonial times, the Empanada has lately been reclaimed by the independent peoples of the New World. The fragrance of traditional Mesoan ingredients survives the ocean crossing, as these unassuming crimped pastries yield to reveal rich and savoury centres.

The effects of Green Fairy upon the drinker's bodily health are something of a cause célèbre - except, that is, to Jacobins and poetic types, who appear only to thrive on its corrupting bitterness. Indeed, the drink is so bitter, it comes to the customer complete with its own dedicated sugar spoon.

There is fun to be had with this dessert. Couples can be seen spooning it into each other's mouths and dissolving into fits of giggles, much to the ire of stiffer patrons. The names of many a pastry chef have been made on the quality of their quenelle scoops - a smooth pod formed by quickly passing the ingredients between two spoons.
Portable and pressurized - the ultimate water-based solution.
The sight of justice being delivered can be most arresting.
Burnished and fired, ground to paste, here's a way to steal the color of the sky at sunset - the blight of any artist's wallet.
An orchid a day keeps the doctor away.
Pictures in motion, all wound up. Experts appreciate the natural film grain of carefully crafted celluloid coating. Flammable, handle with care.
Modern problems require modern solutions - preferably the ones that do not spontanenously combust. Click the “Select Formula” button to commence.

Aarhant congratulates you on your latest catch.

ON FISHING: PESCATORY PRACTICES PECULIAR TO MANOLA

A Precis: Manola's waters play host to a singular collection of marine species that, once having developed sufficient trust, appear to delight in human company.

The first species this study is concerned with is the Manta Ray, which frolics between Manola's three peaks.
The second, as-yet-unidentified creature, was sighted in the shadow of a local mountain.
The third, by all accounts a larger animal, is thought to prefer the oily western shores of the Manola archipelago.
A fourth specimen appears drawn to the old battlefield, but why, we cannot yet say.
The fifth and final known example watches over the bay, thereby keeping its distance from sharks and manta rays.

This last creature appears very rarely, responding only to the sound of the horns used in the sieges of Fort Björn. If they were to be used where she dwells, she might become less shy. Once caught, and the customary introductions made, it's only right to toss our new friends back into the water. (The rest of the treatise is rather dry and over-reliant on unsubstantiated scientific and climatic data)

Artista
Interesting!
An enticing prospect!
Another step forward.
A bold statement!
Beautiful!
Great minds think alike!
I will paint a mural of you!
You're an inspiration.
You push the limits of the possible!
A fellow visionary!
They'll talk about it in the next era!
I could burst like a bubble!
I toast your generous heart - and wallet!
Always wanted to try that!
My pleasure.
No harm in trying.
A tragedy.
I'm lost for words!
Wrath and ruin!
Such a waste.
Crikey!
You play with a broken string.
A pasodoble of poverty and pettiness!
D'you need a coffee?
You worship the void!
All hail the King Vulture!
What you call mania, I call ecstasy.
Last night, I dreamt of a city built entirely of obsidian, shining under a jaguar moon.
What we perfect with no one directing us - that is what we are.
Sleep? And miss the stars as they come out? The drums, the beats, the silver streets?
I would draw you like a Mesoan god: with the body of an ocelot and the head of a snake.
Critics? Hah. Those poor people cannot paint, and resent the fact.
The obreras shied away from those dreams that they thought too daring, too dangerous - but to take that leap? That, is where you start to feel alive!
The Mesoans were masters of their craft. Ah, what I wouldn't give for a chance to watch them work.
You call it the New World, but it's only news to you. This continent already existed six hundred queens ago.
I visited the Old World once. She seemed to me like a beautiful widow, proud and serene, her smile hidden by a veil of rain.
Isabel Sarmento never picked up a paintbrush. If she had, I bet those artworks would have made you weep: so expressive, so brave, so true a woman.
La Fortune is a man willing to pay the ultimate price for his freedom - as we all should, though we seek freedom in different ways.
The start of something beautiful.
Heartbreaking.
Scorch marks on my soul!
Such passion, wasted on banalities.
Oh, go grind water.
You cannot silence the damned!
The blistering plaster reveals the mould!
How can there be beauty in suffering?
Even the quetzal has lost its plumes.
Like swallowing a cane toad.
The pen scratches, but the ink's dried up.
I feel... thin, like paint spread on too much canvas.
A tango with feet of lead.
I see a lot of potential here.
How about adding some highlights?
The glass is... who cares, pour some more!
It never rains to everyone's liking.
A still life without grapes.
So bored, I might just lay an egg.
Happy as a kinkajou in honey.
Like a frog in sweet, summer rain.
Good vibes!
The pleasures of the body and the mind, so happily entwined!
I'm a lightning rod in a storm of ideas!
Dance! Dance until the night collapses!
The privilege of watching my dreams take shape!
Like music, joy is infectious!
Drunk on dazzling delights!
Beauty speaks to me, and now I know how to answer!
Call me a hedonist if you like — I'm too happy to care!
Such freedom of expression!
My soul has learned to soar!
I feel... invincible!
Behold the happiest man alive!
A splatter of joy, a touch of compassion, and layers, rich layers of life!
Hold this, I'm going in!
My instruments! My operatic scores!
Help, the handle is melting!
Where books burn, no one is safe!
The flames of greed consume us!
This is more than a hangover...
Do I look green to you? I feel green...
If I must die, let it be for love.
The owl cries... and my soul must answer.
Last chance... for an autograph...
You can't arrest an idea!
Our passions turn to revolution!
Stand back, or stand with us!
We must stay true to our convictions!
We will not go silently!
I feel the jaws of the jaguar closing in...
I thought we had moved beyond the need to kill one another.
This will throw us back years!
You can't tell me anyone is winning this pointless slaughter.
A true leader would know better than to place their people in harm's way.
The lights flicker, the organ beckons... after you, I'd say.
To follow the music, we must learn to let go...
Basking in the sun, that is where the words find me, and remind me how lucky I am.
Welcome to the age of enlightenment!
This will be our peaceful battleground: a stage for our passions; a home for our hearts!
Though I've found my wings, gravity means that I still walk the streets.
I feel so disconnected, as if no path led anywhere.
The road to success is paved with hardship... Or... not paved at all...
A city with no streets? What's next, tamales without meat?
The road less travelled by, is still, you know, a road.
Behold, the beating heart of change!
Fancy a tour?
The walls are sturdy, the possibilities... endless!
Ready to rumba.
A glass of juice, to moisten your throat?
Look, my sense of direction is a little, ehh... How about a road?
Don't make me get mud on my shoes, I'm going dancing in these!
The road to happiness is... What, where did the road go?
It is not enough to see it - you must feel it!
Ahaha! I like it, I'll glue it in my collage!
...and if I ever refuse free cake, you'll know it's an impostor!
There's a trick to it, watch...
No sketchbooks at work, they said...
Uh-oh. That's gonna be expensive.
Bring buckets, pumps, hoses, anything!
It's getting out of control!
Work later... Doctor now...
It was just a little cough this morning!
The last drink I had... was bad...
Man the barricades!
Here are our demands in e minor, written for maracas, baritone and pianoforte.
Hold the line, my friends!
I'm a man, not a squid. A little help?
It's lonely in here, can I have a pet Macaw?
I feel like a single ant, doing the work of an entire colony!
We used up everything we had - except our imagination.
Our supplies are gone - and I didn't take them!
I read a story about a man who built cities out of dust, but I think that was fiction.
We need a warehouse!I don't want the monkeys stealing all this!
If we leave it out here, the colors will fade!
I won't be able to fit any of that in my workshop.
This place is like my bedroom - stacked all the way to the ceiling!
Can't fit another needle in this haystack.
The shadows grow long...
You cannot rush perfection...
I'll need more coffee to survive this.
Time to tinker about!
Nearly finished this chapter!
Hours spent with subtle conversations... finding inspiration...
The lights are out, I repeat, the lights are... Ow. That was my toe.
I don't like to be kept in the dark...
We seem to have... eh... lost our spark.
That's not how I envisioned it.
Why won't it work?
We're shortselling our potential!
A spanner in the works...
This is humiliating.
Time for us to fill the silence!
...120 verses isn't actually long, it's just detailed...
Anyone interested in reading my manuscript?
I could have had a lie-in!
If you don't need me, I'll be at the docks. I like to paint en plein air.
I could probably use a nap.
Oh. Already?
Stuttering back to life!
The show must go on.
The waters, pristine, paint a promising scene, but think of the rush of the fall!
Energy is never lost, you see, unless you work in accounting.
What happens if I push this lever?
Alright kids, follow me, but don't tell anyone I let you in.
More calamari for me.
What do you mean I can't eat all the chocolate?
First of all, I'd like to thank all my loyal fans.
The only thing honking in here is a pair of geese.
I... smell like my abuela. This entire place smells like my abuela.
Much like skin, silver bromide is sensitive to light.
Look at me, it's a perfect fit!
A powerful solution.
...quick, help me get out of these, before the boss sees...
Who would've thought such a silly little plant could have such interesting effects...
Safety goggles - so fashionable right now!
Come in, but be ready to duck!
Let us unravel the mysteries of life!
Technically, we are all components...
Hola! Hope you have good insurance!
Whatever you see, don't try it at home!
I've finished the inventory! It's... a lot!
You could hide anything in here...
Don't get lost, we still haven't found Mario...
Now the creative juices are flowing!
When life gives you lemons...
Come in and try a sip!
Which passion to pursue?
I have a million ideas, but you'll have to decide.
We'll need a recipe - at least, if you want it to work.
The Muses need a champion. Can we count on you?
I thought you might like what I had in mind.
I just can't get this idea out of my head. Could you help?
A kindred spirit.
My heart feels so light, it's a wonder my feet are still on the ground!
This is thrilling!
Reality is absorbing... but we mustn't lose track of what's truly important.
You should hire a secretary, you know, so you don't get trapped in the day-to-day business.
Without your help, this dream will never come to life.
Great ideas always seem intimidating at first.
Such an excellent opportunity is not likely to be repeated!
A symphony... for the deaf.
All artists must be willing to suffer.
Do we call it a failure or... an unhappy little incident?
An obstacle is no reason to surrender.
Ready to present your work?
I'm just dying to find out what you've been up to.
Did you bring something for me?
Oh, I just can't wait!
Can I have a look?
What have you got there?
You have proved yourself both imaginative and resourceful.
Couldn't have done it better myself.
That must've been quite the adventure!
A kindness in exchange for a kindness.
I would like you to have this.
Not at all, my friend, not at all.
Welcome to the most magnificent meeting place of the New World!
I can already hear the crowd, the chanting, the cheers!
All of this is so terribly exciting!
Just finished the warm-up routine!
Let's not delay the opening ceremony!
Can't wait for the ranks to fill up!
Be sure to reserve me a ticket!
Tremendous fun!
Ooh, a chance to present my new anthem!
Can't wait to breathe in the ambience!
It'll be the talk of the Old World, and the New!
It's all about finding the fun in... fundamentals.
One step at a time - cha, cha, cha.
It's becoming even more beautiful, now that it's real.
But what of our game?
At this rate, we'll just be kicking each other's shins!
Now I can't tell who's winning!
It's pandemonium in here!
A disaster with terrible timing.
Prepare for the most eagerly awaited match of the year!
Time to find out if the Alpacas can beat the Nandus!
If ever a crowd was ready, this one is!
Remember to play a beautiful game!
Let the games begin!
It's a boiling pot of emotion in here. Neither team seems willing to relent, and... is that a tortilla costume?

And that's another beautiful save, woo! And to think she just stepped off that tourist ship this morning - you'd think she's been doing this her whole life! Better give that lady a long-term contract!
Please bear with us while we remove the capybaras from the playing field.
Let me draw your attention to this unique cloud formation, notice the swirling patterns - oooh, hang on, d'you see that white speck over there? Is that.. the ball?
Goal! Gooaal! What a shot, what a risky move. Now I need something to wipe my eyes...
Can I paint you with one of these?
Hold it up high, so all of us can see!
Ah, the magic of this moment. Victory, camaraderie, t-shirts miraculously disappearing!
All of them! All of them would do nicely!
Here's a trophy to outshine all precious jewels - a hard-earned win!
There's been a disturbance at the stadium, and it wasn't me!
The game had to be interrupted!
Can't we for once just enjoy ourselves?
Oh, don’t make me invite him to the tertulia – he’s such a bore!
I write and I write and I write – I stay up all night, writing – and then the next morning, my publisher changes his mind!
Go on, tell her you love her!
Paradise? I think it will be some kind of infinite library.
Run along now, and I'll take you out for ice cream when I get back from work.
This city really comes to life at night.
Ostrich on the loose!
Can we walk along the beach for a change?
Coming to the concert this evening?
I feel so alive!
Ah, nothing better for the constitution than sea air.
Hey! That gannet stole my churro!
These seagulls are vicious!
A bold artistic choice, letting the screen remain black for two hours… Wait, what do you mean they forgot to turn the projector on?
No, no, don’t you understand? The chinchilla was a metaphor for his depression.
Ugh, so many sequels. Have they run out of ideas already?
It's her greatest work yet!
He does all his own stunts. Well, he did until he fell off that bridge.
A masterpiece!
You’d better sharpen up before the carnival!
Relax those knees; keep them soft!
2/4, please.
Lovely form, Miss Rodriguez!
Don’t tell me you left your tamborim at home again?
10 to 1? That’s my kind of bet.
50 on the team in red and blue. I like their shirts.
Inverted wing-backs are the future of tactics, I’m telling you!
Here, you take this envelope, and United get a penalty in the 90th minute. Simple.
He must have a foot like a traction engine!
Eeeeeagles!
The magic of the cup!
Goals change games.
Good feet for a big man.
He's got a wand of a left foot.
Liquid football!
It's such a pleasure to meet you at last! I've been waiting in the wings, now I will join you on the stage. Would you care for a proper introduction?
I have slightly altered our production buildings, merging tradition with our vision. Connect them to your power grid and be prepared for an electrifying performance!
Have you ever felt like you needed a breather from formalities? Advanced city institutions are here to protect your city without trespassing too much on your time. While stocks last, anyway.
It's a lovely day. Think of what life could be, lying in the sun and staring out to sea! Let us go to the beach and look at these blueprints together.
Our public services offer the most delightful distractions from the daily grind. But who wants to be a mere spectator? We'll need to put some costumes on if we're to join the fun!
Imagine two teams meeting on a perfect turf, cheered on by thousands, vying for glory. It'd be the pride of any city - a temple of entertainment, instilling your people with the spirit of champions.
Have you heard of Manola? The big island - hidden gem of the South? They say a drink from its waters grants the gift of true insight! It sounds like a wonderful place to settle down...
Manola, land of the falls and shimmering rocks! Now that you've made yourself at home... when can I move in?

So... I went hiking the other day, watching the water plunge into the deep, and... I slipped. But after I hit my head, I had a fabulous idea, one that will require... alas... a little help. Would you be willing to spread the word?
At last, time for our big reveal! There's hundreds of liters going over that ledge every second, that's enough to spin a turbine, or two. You could build a dam here, just like the one in La Xultuna!
Our work here is done, open the gates! Adios the dirty powerplants!
It is so very beautiful! And it works, too... you know, not that I ever doubted it, we did try it out in my bathtub. I wonder if I could have a picture, a little something to remember it by?
Thank you, for all your efforts - for helping us preserve the beauty of this place.
Solid groundwork, that's what I have to say - and there's more to come!
The shapes, the structure! If only I could freeze it in time... but don't let me distract you, keep up the good work!
A choice of our future artworks, and a chance, Madame, to do some good in the world.
Welcome, oh, welcome! Do take a look around!
But I don't understand... I did send them an invitation...
Did we not?
Ah, but even a thief may have a sense of honor. I am sure she knows, deep down, that she's taken something that cannot be replaced...
Come now, Madame. The Mesoans miss their god. You have until midnight to read my letter... and return the relic.
Please, Madame, these people are thieves.
There's no end to what they will take... with their cannons and coins, and their clever little deals.
We've left them unchallenged, and this is what we've come to. A Mesoan god, used as Hunt's paperweight.
We are proud to have you at the helm, Madame. I know you will put these scoundrels in their place!
The warehouse awaits, Madame. Our people are ready to load the boats.
We came from nothing, but now we have taken the bull by the horns!
Each knot is a record. Can you imagine? It's like holding a warehouse in your hands!
There it was, a puzzle piece of our past, safe at last from thieving hands.
Madame, you are a force of nature! Not even Admiral Silva can match your stride!
The sword! The sword of Sarmento... What a feat, what a glorious day!
Sarmento was the first to raise his weapon for the Movement... but by far not the last. His sister, forced to watch him die, freed so many others. My papá would have loved to see his sword return.
The Lady Hunt, hard up! And to think she called us a band of beggars!
Toast to you, Ma’am, and, whatshisname, god of the... Mesoan god. It’s got a... a real thing to it, a... you know, like it is real and I’m not.
I dream of a place worthy of housing our history.
Chapter 1: Ahem. The independent artist - how I found my first client, and other adventures.
When I write of Jornaleros, I think of my Papá, toiling under the sun. He never said what his role in the Movement was... but he always spoke highly of Simon Sarmento.

Our cause attracted many fine young minds, bursting with ideas... but Madame did not seem much taken by them, always distracted, always gazing out to sea. I was sure it had something to do with those letters.
Chapter 3: Growing suspicions. Thanks to Kahina, our mission was rapidly gaining momentum. It was beginning to dawn on me, however, that she had a mission of her own.
The stage was set for a grand opening night. We had but to retrieve the last missing pieces...
It was imperative that we find the perfect spot for our exhibition, no matter the cost.
It was a pleasure to talk business with Miss Paloma, who has a curiosity to rival my own. Though she did absolutely refuse to hand me any of these mysterious letters.
Chapter 5: Friends and Foes. Yaosca had been a most generous hostess, and it felt good to repay her kindness.
Isabel's cause was close to our own hearts, and trading with her did nothing but reinforce these bonds.
Chapter 2: Leaving Port. You should have seen Kahina climb the rigging, nimble as a fox, up, up and away.
Though these ship had left our shores behind, the forests still bore the mark of their memory.
Our first triumph secured, we were approached by a private collector willing to pledge his treasures once our exhibition opens. Oh, you should have seen the Curator's tap dance of celebration.
Prologue: Science and Art have quite a lot in common. The pursuit of mysteries, respect for history... and high coffee consumption.
Madame, I fear we have been living above our means. In fact, I'll soon be selling my shoes!
News from home?
You just smiled. A pleasant surprise?
At this rate, you should get your own pigeon.
Someone out there must be fond of you!
Madame, I'm told this charming young woman has a letter for you.
Madame, your popularity is reaching new peaks! Miss Paloma has another letter for you!
Oh, you're not going to read that? I could never resist the temptation...
So, this is your offer? Empty frames and painted promises?
They're leaving. They took a gamble on our treasures, thinking we would sit down and play.
A Mesoan god... Such a sight has never graced my Emporio.
Perhaps I could do with a challenge. One last wager. One more chance to feel the wind in my hair...
Pardon?
Sit down with thieves, and you'll leave with your pockets empty.
Ruining my reputation, risking my assets, to help you out trade my richest customers?
For now, I shall greet them with a smile and offer them my wares. It would be rude not to let them contribute to their own demise.
How very... rustic. But at least people will know where to find us.
The bully, I should say. Never liked his style.
Fascinating. I'm told von Malching wore it as a scarf.
He may have his sea legs, but I know how to climb.
Careful. It's sharper than you.
Poor Margaret was never taught to be generous.
Yes, yes, it does appear to be genuine. But do let me take a closer look... this won't take a minute.
We depend too much on fickle favours.
He never could resist a tempting offer.
The Admiral never does anything he does not think to his advantage. Try not to change his mind too soon.
The Lady Hunt is contributing to our cause. What a noble gesture.
I have always been fond of oysters... at least they know how to keep their mouths shut.
No more need for candlelight dinners.
Once upon a time, it took courage to see the world from above.. I am not sure if I like these contraptions. They make it too easy.
The world is getting so motorized, I wouldn't be surprised if you had steam coming out of your ears.
I prefer a smaller weapon, the kind you can tuck in your hair. But each to his own, I suppose.
Just a receipt.
A pleasant certainty. I do not much enjoy surprises.
I already have enough birds to feed, and they sing the most curious songs.
I feel that you should not be so fond of standing behind me.
"Dear Madame, ever since you arrived in the New World, your name has become a synonym for exquisite taste. It is no secret that you deal in some of our greatest treasures."
"While this practice is perfectly legal, we regret that our people were unable to place a bid for what is rightfully theirs."

"We, the Artista Collective, want to encourage the repatriation of these objects, and hope to enlist your help in this matter. Rather than intrude on your time uninvited, we have an offer to make - one that is well-suited to your talents as a trader."
"We await your presence at the Atelier Insólito, graciously hosted by the Yaosca Research Centre. Respectfully, The Artista Collective."

"Dear Madame, I am surprised, just as you must be surprised to find my handwriting on your correspondence. It seems we've both been taking liberties with other people's property - but it goes without saying that you're the more talented thief".
"For your deeds, many would see you in chains, but that would be such a terrible waste. I have a feeling we will need gifts such as yours if we're to end the illicit art trade.
"In exchange for the timely return of the idol, and your continued services, I am willing to forget what I just read. Your friend, the Artista."
"Hunt is the only one who knows, and she cannot expose you without revealing her own, far greater crimes".
"I believe that she loathes the thought of public rejoicing even more than she would the truth: that the museum displays a masterful fake, and the idol of Hueyaca is yours at last."
"As such, the world will never know who negotiated the sale of Prosperity. Or how Edvard came to be acquainted with the enemies of the Queen."
"You may rest at ease that waters have calmed, even at home. Awaiting your orders, as ever, your faithful servant."
"I can't believe it, that little critter left me a note! Snooping around, reading my letters... I'll wring his skinny neck!"
"Blackmail. And based on, let's see. "Hunt is the only one who knows"... Well now she bloody isn't, you absolute genius... Great. Wonderful. Brought down by two morons with a mailbox. "

What do you do with the time you have left here?
Dig through the rubble blocking the passageway.
Make casts of some of the carvings.
Just look around.

Using their tools, your crew begin to remove the rubble blocking the passageway.

The reverent atmosphere is broken by the sound of shattering pottery, as a crewman's pick strikes a ceramic jar buried in the rubble.

Looking at the broken jar, you are surprised to see some seeds that had been sealed inside. They look like they could still sprout!

As you exit through the main door, it seals shut behind you!

What will you do with your discovery?
No time for experiments! We'll take these to the village for analysis.
We'll try planting them on La Xultuna.

Carefully, you pour the liquid rubber and begin to make the casts. You reflect that even if this place were to be lost to the elements, at least something of its beauty will survive.

After the time-consuming process is complete, you leave through the main entrance — which slams shut behind you!

Yaosca will surely be interested in these carvings from the now-sealed pyramid.
I'll take them to Yaosca.

As you explore the cavernous interior and marvel at its mystical atmosphere, you reflect on what will remain of your own work for future generations.

Using your photographic equipment, you take numerous pictures of the staggering structure.

As you box up the negatives and leave through the main entrance, it slams shut behind you!

You hope that the prints you plan to make will inspire the workers.
We'll show the photographs to Yaosca's people.
The photographs you took of the pyramid carvings inspired Yaosca's people.
Not only did you save the flailing birds, your efforts also cleaned the water.

No map — just this riddle! If I can figure out which constellation to follow, I should end up at the right island. What do you think?

"I am no ox, but bear soft horns;

I am no magpie, but leave silver in my wake.
Follow me on a starry night, and find what you seek marked with an X."

Dear Isabel,

Thanks to you, the Pyrphorians have been driven from our region; but their legacy remains.
The generator they left behind — the generator we were forced to build during their loathsome occupation — is polluting our land.

My people depend on the electricity the generator provides, but it is killing our island: our rivers are choked with filth; the smog-filled air drives the birds from the trees; even the soil suffers a slow poisoning.
But we have a plan: a hydroelectric dam! My people have the knowledge and the skill, but we need your leadership to build a new, sustainable town for the workers, and help us complete the dam.

With dearest wishes,
Yaosca Rodriguez.
Defeating the Pyrphorians was but the first step for The Movement: now, we must help those who have suffered under their tyranny to rebuild.
With this dam, we can defy the hegemony of the Old World; we can proclaim our ingenuity, our self-sufficiency, our vitality.
It is rumoured that before they evacuated the island, the Pyrphorians hid some crates of resources...
La Xultuna is covered with ruins left over from the Pyrphorian occupation. Remove them to help the island heal faster.
Crop farms of the same type placed close together create a monoculture effect, negatively affecting the soil quality. Diversify your crop farms for a positive polyculture effect.

The Herbarium — a collection of botanical knowledge and samples — is a new resource required to craft valuable items and train specialists at Yaosca's Harbor. Find Herbaria in the world, or solve Maya's quests.

Decision events will trigger if your eco values get too low; if your resident needs remain unfulfilled; or if your treasury balance becomes negative. Beware: events triggered by critical eco values may have permanent effects!
The Relocate tool is disabled in this scenario. Plan your expansion carefully!
This region hides many mysteries. Explore the surrounding islands with your flagship, and search for rare plants to compile in a herbarium on La Xultuna.
Resource deposits are limited in this scenario, but they can be replenished with items crafted at Yaosca's harbour.
Legendary items can be used in every run: if you craft them once, you'll find them in your harbour when you load your next game!
There are three new buildings which actively combat pollution: the aquafarm, water purifier, and forester. They must first be unlocked by crafting their blueprints at Yaosca's harbour.
Fish shoals can be depleted, but they will regenerate over time. The rate of regeneration depends on your water quality.

Most of your production buildings have a negative environmental impact. Try to counter their negative effects with items crafted at Yaosca's harbour, or the new mitigation buildings: the aquafarm, forester, and water purifier.

Do we truly expect to be able to create an Eden, a perfect world? Perhaps not.

No solutions are ever perfect – certainly the hydroelectric dam built by Isabel Sarmento and Yaosca Rodriguez wasn’t. It disrupted fish migration, caused unintended damage to the ecosystem, increased the risk of floods.

But if we must choose between imperfection and inaction, there can only be one answer. We can always improve our designs and implement mitigations – what we cannot do is sit idly by while our world collapses.
What Isabel and Yaosca did represented a bold step forward. With the knowledge and technology we possess today, we can do so much more — and it would be inexcusable not to try.

Yana Rodriguez

Scenario Overview
Scenario Details
Ecosystem
La Xultuna is a living island that directly responds to your actions. The buildings you construct and the decisions you take will affect its fragile environment.
Eco Qualities

There are three parameters indicating the condition of the island: Water Quality, Soil Quality, and Air Quality. These gradually change depending on the pollution and exploitation caused by your buildings. All qualities are equally important — if one of them drops to zero, you will lose. You can replay the scenario and learn from your mistakes as many times as you wish.
Countering Pollution
It's important to make sure that your impact on the environment remains positive. Some buildings and items can counter the negative impact of your town with their own, positive impact.
Soil Quality

Planting a single type of crop across a large area will lead to harmful monocultures. When one type of crop is clearly dominant, it creates a monoculture that negatively affects soil quality, and may lead to you losing fertilities.
Calculation

All farms interact with other farms in their direct proximity. If two farms of the same type are too close, they will create a monoculture and begin to negatively affect your soil quality. The strength of this effect depends on their type and size. On the other hand, building a variety of different farms together will provide positive bonuses to your soil quality. Plan your crops wisely, and check the Eco Balance Overview for a detailed breakdown.
Proximity

All farms have a range in which they strengthen the effects of monocultures. If two farms of the same type are too close to each other, they will magnify the effects of monocultures on the island. On the other hand, different types of farms placed close together will have the opposite effect, creating polycultures and boosting soil quality. You can also build aquafarms to erase all influences — both positive and negative — around them.
Air Quality

Heavy industry buildings pollute the environment in proportion to their productivity. The harmful chemicals and fumes they emit reduce the air quality, decrease the productivity of animal farms, and may cause even more severe effects.
Green Lungs
Reforestation directly increases air quality on the island. Trees do not regrow by themselves, however. After they are cut down by lumberjacks, you must use forester’s huts to plant new ones.
Water Quality

Animal husbandry can negatively impact your water quality, depending on the size and amount of your animal farms. The penalty is proportional to the productivity of the farms. The worse the water quality is, the higher the chance of disease for your residents, and the slower your fish will repopulate.
Fish Shoals
Fish shoals are now limited in size, and overexploitation will quickly deplete them. Pause production at your fisheries to let the fish repopulate, or move your fisheries elsewhere.
Non-Renewable Resources
Resource deposits, such as iron veins, can no longer be exploited infinitely. Each deposit now has a limited amount of resources that can be extracted — once it runs dry, the mine becomes inoperable.

Build new mines on different deposits, or use items crafted at Yaosca's harbour to refill the deposits. Refillers, such as dynamite and excavators, can be activated at any time from any storage menu. Remember though – in this scenario, the Move feature is disabled! Plan your expansion carefully.
Pyrphorian Ruins

La Xultuna is covered with remnants from the Pyrphorian occupation. Clearing these ruins will gain you construction space and building materials, but the operation will require time and effort from your workforce. All Pyrphorian ruins which you remove will reappear in subsequent playthroughs, except for Jail, Barracks and the Pyrphorian Factory. To reinstate these, you must reset the scenario.

But we have a plan: a hydroelectric dam! My people have the knowledge and the skill, but we need your leadership to build a new, sustainable town for the workers, and help us complete the dam.

A project like this could reunite my fractured people.
Leadership is a heavy burden. I don't know how you manage.
You won't heal the land without our help.
Do you just want to chat, or are you going to get down in the soil and help us?
I’ve been working this land since I first learned to walk.
I’ve seen droughts, plagues, famines, blights – the Pyrphorians were nothing I couldn’t handle!
I’ve always said that messing around with machines would lead to no good!
Yaosca may trust you, but it takes more than a big reputation to convince me.
I don't want my grandchildren to grow up in a blasted wasteland.
Optimism is useless to me. You’ll get nothing done without hard work.
Treat our island with care. This was home to my abuelo, and his abuelo before him, and his abuelo before him.
Yaosca? Hmm, I'd rather a leader with a bit of dirt under their fingernails.
Yes, we worked the land for the Pyrphorians - that way we could make sure it was protected!
Some of those Obreras practically begged the Pyrphorians to come here. Blame them for this!
Everything I have is going up in flames!
Another fire! There is something very wrong on this island!
I... I'll work on the dam later. Right now I need the doctor.
Mi estómago... It hurts!
Maybe build a road before you try to build a dam.
Is a road really too much to ask?
Good luck building that dam when you can’t even provide for our basic needs!
Is this how you treat your own people?
At least the Pyrphorians kept us fed and clothed!
Life is hard enough – you just make it harder!
I don't ask you for much, Isabel.
All work and no reward... Some leader you are.
We’ve got everything we need to get to work.
I have everything I need – now focus on the island.
You know how to keep us supplied, I'll give you that.
Care for our island as well as you care for us, and I'll be happy.
No complaints from me... For now!
Me? Oh, I’m doing fine.
We’ve run dry!
Sorry, it’s empty.
Nothing left here. Nada!
Good luck getting that to grow here!
That might have grown here before – not any more!
Plant as much as you want, it’s not going to grow!
Ah, bien - I was getting thirsty.
Still plenty of time to save the island.
We’ve got a bit of breathing room.
Keep the island healthy and I won’t complain. Well, no promises.
My grandchildren can still play outside, so I guess we’re doing alright.
If the island is well, so am I.
I’m not too worried yet.
Not so nice around here these days.
I don’t enjoy seeing my homeland looking like this.
We’d better save the island before things get really urgent.
This island is changing, and not for the better!
Never thought I’d live to see my home die a slow death like this.
Things were looking a lot better a few weeks ago...
My home... What a wretched mess!
The end is upon us!
The land... it withers and dies in my hands!
In all my years, things have never been so bad!
I am ashamed to pass this land on to my grandchildren.
Hell on earth!
Foundations are done. Let me know what's next.
That’s the first part done... now, let me just rest a minute.
We need this concrete giant just to power our humble village?
I don’t want to see a block of concrete ever again!
It's finally done. My back is killing me!
I hope all this was worth it.
Eh? Who are you? Wait... Isabel Sarmento? The howling wind, the swirling storm herself!?
I could use your help, your, er, your eminence. I need wood to grill my fish. Fish is raw, fish tastes poor; that's my motto.
Some wood for your humblest servant?
Aha! A fish on the grill is the sweetest thrill, that's my motto. Come, feast with me!
Ah, Miss Sarmento! Help a poor fisherman, would you?
When the Pyrphorians came, my dear Ignacio buried his wealth. He did not survive the Years of Fire... but I found these obscure directions to his belongings.
Let's see where this leads us.
This has to be it! Thank you, Miss Sarmento - now, to dig!
No, not this way... Ah well. The sea reveals what it wants to reveal.
Ah, Miss Sarmento! Any more thoughts on the map?
Come, Miss Sarmento. I'd like you to be with me when I uncover Ignacio's belongings.
Here goes...
Ah, a wooden box! And inside it is... Another note?
Oh, Ignacio, you beautiful, beautiful man!
Alive, he's alive! I'm coming, Ignacio! Farwell, Miss Sarmento — and thank you!
Some of the fish we catch go straight into these pools.
Ah, the Wacah Chan. Its trunk is a caiman that turned to stone while upright. You can still see the scales!
Anything to get rid of this Pyrphorian mess.
It has to be thicker at the bottom than at the top - deeper water, more pressure, you see?
I said fifty bags of concrete, not fifteen!
This thing is an eyesore.
We're going to live downstream from this? Are we sure it's safe?
We need this huge thing to power our little village?
I've been eating fish every day for 23 years!
I never thought I'd get out of that Pyrphorian work camp alive.
I think this time would be better spent praying.
The Lord will judge us for what we've done to this land.
When the Pyrphorians came for my nephew, I hid him under the floorboards.
The Mesoans would clean the chultun with aquatic turtles. Now that's real ingenuity.
It shouldn't be this hot, not at this time of year.
Oh yes, tell me again about how brave you were during the Years of Fire.
If we have to leave... well, I don't even want to think about it.
Francisco says this is a test, a test from the Lord! We harmed his creation, and now we have to fix it.
I went up to the ruins to look over the island. I can't believe what we did to this place.
I can't sleep at night. Visions of fire...
Then, everything changed when the Pyrphorians attacked.
A little rum in my atole, to get me through the day.
Red sky at night, jornalero's delight.
Keep your head down, focus on your work, just like during the Years of Fire.
I don't think Sarmento knows what she's gotten herself into.
If we survive this, I'll ask her to marry me.
Chorizo! Chorizo! Has anyone seen my dog?
I'm glad I'm not the one who has to make the decisions here. It seems there's just one dilemma after another...
It came out of the forest! Looking for food, I think.
It's been a long time since I went swimming. The water here... I'm not touching it.
Have the nightmares stopped for you yet?
Before you go accusing me, why don't you explain all those extra rations the Pyrphorians would give you?
A building with wings? Hmm.
That must refer to the treasury. Unfortunately, it's empty...
I never knew Mesoan water technology was so advanced - I can see how it inspired the planners here.
Or at least that's what they told her... There's a Pyrphorian note here, ordering their minions to hide in the village everything that they couldn't evacuate. There must still be caches...
The barracks for the wretched souls who were forced to work on the generator. There's a note pinned to the door...
The headquarters? It must be located somewhere here on the island - a place with access to the sea, certainly...
The headquarters? They must be referring to the research centre.
The headquarters? Just like in the note from the jetty. A building with wings, it said...
Yaosca's disgust for the generator is matched only by her need for its power.
She loves her people - but I wonder if all of them trust her.
Something for the settlement!
This was worth the effort!
A diversion from the dam, but a worthwhile one.
After all they stole, I'm happy to take from the Pyrphorians.
No shame in stealing from thieves.
I'll make better use of this than they did.
I can't see from here.
I need to get closer.
We need to sail closer.
This looks like a recent wreck.
A shipwreck! Pyrphorian, by the look of it.
I remember these Pyrphorian steamers. They look much better dashed on the rocks.
What curious plants... I ought to take some samples.
More Mesoan ruins. I ought to take a closer look.
Mesoan ruins, over there!
The entrance is shut. But knowing the ingenuity of the Mesoans, there must be a way to open it...
Aha, that did it!
I found something!
This corridor leads deep inside...
Quite the adventure. Now, back to Yaosca.
Someone is living in this strange little place...
Those clothes - he's a Pyrphorian castaway, for sure. Pitiful...
Look at that ship - split apart and left to bleed its cargo. Oh, those poor birds!
Another outpost, abandoned by the Pyrphorians as they scurried away. Maybe I can find something of use.
An old Pyrphorian outpost. Looks like the rats have fled their nest.
The Pyrphorians left this place in a hurry. I wonder what they left behind.
More scrap. Is there no corner of these lands untainted by the Pyrphorians?
What's that in the debris? A message in a bottle...
Manuel...
This monkey... she looks desperately sad.
In their haste to flee, those vile Pyrphorians couldn't even let this monkey out of its cage.
The little one still seems to know its way.
They left these for me?
No doubt that little one was destined for the animal trade.
What a strange pattern...
That has to be the island the fisherman was looking for. I ought to tell him.
Farewell, brave voyager.
Look at this beautiful place... strewn with Pyrphorian debris.
A turtle, trapped in the nets! It barely has the strength to struggle any more. I ought to take it somewhere safe.
It’s alarming how often the people here get sick.
These people suffer from illness so frequently.
The people and the island suffer alike.
Extra supplies are always useful, but I think we may have over-produced...
Despite the problems we face, the ecological measurements seem acceptable for now.
I'll need to offset the pollution caused by all these factories.
It pains me to cover so much of this land with fields, but I need to feed the workers.
With all these fisheries, I'll need to make sure I don't deplete the shoals too quickly.
And so the first factory rises, and our work truly begins.
If we can plant more than we hack down, I’ll be happy.
For all their scepticism about the dam, the Jornaleros are working hard.
Keeping all these workers supplied is going to be a challenge, but we’ll need them to complete the dam.
Nothing left in this deposit. We’ll have to find another source.
The village is certainly fascinating. I wonder if any of their techniques could be applied on a larger scale.
The project is proving costlier than I thought - I have to maintain our finances!
The ruins in the town aren't half as impressive as those the Mesoans left behind...
That's a lot of fields. We'll have to make sure to diversify the crops we plant in them.
The same crops, row upon row... I hope we don't damage the soil.
The deposits are emptying faster than I thought they would.
The air doesn't seem so fresh today - I should keep an eye on the measurements.
The water isn't looking so clean any more - I ought to be careful.
The latest soil samples are beginning to concern me.
The environment here is beginning to change rapidly.
With these workers, we can really start to make progress.
The fishing shoals grow thinner by the day... We may have exploited them too heavily.
The forest is dwindling. We need wood, but the island needs trees...
This wretched smog! I should never have let the air grow so foul!
The water should not be that colour. Something’s gone very wrong here.
The soil is degrading faster than I expected – I should have taken more precautions!
Defeating the Pyrphorians was but the first step for The Movement: now, we must help those who have suffered under their tyranny to rebuild.
With this dam, we can defy the hegemony of the Old World; we can proclaim our ingenuity, our self-sufficiency, our vitality.
It's going to be huge. And unsightly...
The build-up of sediment could be an issue...
It's too late to stop now.
All I'm saying is, how are the fish going to get through?
The curvature will send some of the pressure to the rock walls.
I didn't think we'd make it this far. We're so close.
Eavesdropping again? Old habits die hard for a Pyrphorian informant, I suppose.
Make sure you boil the water, it isn't so safe these days...
We never found his body. I think the Pyrphorians must have burned him.
He told me he's given up the rum - only atole from now on.
The chlorination experiments seem promising - we could really improve our water filtration.
We need bold solutions! Think the unthinkable! Not you, obviously - you can't even deal with thinking the thinkable.
She won't even talk to me any more. I think she's too ashamed.
My son wants to study ancient history. I wish he'd choose a more practical subject.
When the guano runs out, artificial fertilisers will be the way forward, I'm telling you...
He doesn't comprehend the difference a few degrees can make. I tried to explain!
Red next to black, jump way back; red next to yellow, cuddly fellow.
I know I missed your birthday, I know - all I can think about is the dam right now.
I need to get back to the forest garden.
Yaosca looks so tired these days. No wonder she needed help...
The wretched baby was howling all night. I would too, if my father was a Pyrphorian.
It's called a kinkajou - it's like a cross between a monkey and a raccoon.
Up close, Isabel looks nothing like what I expected.
I never had the chance to tell her I love her. The Pyphorians came in the night, and...
All this effort put into the dam... Wind power is the way forward, I'm certain.
He begged me to forgive him. The dirty collaborationist rat...
We need to be precise with these measurements - Isabel is counting on them.
She works night and day on the encyclopaedia - trying to finish it before the birds disappear entirely...
I don't talk about the Years of Fire. Especially not with busybodies like you.
We should have started measuring the fish population sooner!

The Jorgensen family tree already's got a group of genealogists sleeping next to it!
The dawn of a new era!
If ye can trust the crew, ye can trust the ship, too.
We would never have made it this far without you!
Here's to another year of adventures, be they on these shores or far, far away!
This exhibition spells out what we so easily forget - the extraordinary tale of ordinary people. Today we bow to patience and perseverance, courage and kindness.
I cried a bit during the opening ceremony.
A lovely scene of Schladming through the mist, in the upper gallery!
All the Annobility is here!
Together they’ve stood through centuries, a band of pioneers, each pursuing a dream. Did you know that, after all this time, you deserve a place among them?
Much merrymaking marks this year's Annoversary - a grand Silver Jubilee. Stay a while, and reminisce on old adventures.

Creative Note: Although incidents no longer occur, Hospitals, Police Stations and Fire Stations can still liven up your city.

Creative Note: Income restrictions will no longer keep you from creating the most exquisite cities. You can't be defeated or go bankrupt in this game mode, and you can always get a new flagship for free.
Creative Note: Unique buildings from the campaign or additional content you may own can now be found in the ornament menu.
Creative Note: Diving trips with old Nate have been cancelled, but he will still craft items at your request. Replicas of the Salvager can be built in Steam Shipyards.
Creative Note: Bureaucracy has been overthrown. Scholars no longer require permits and there is no limit on major discoveries.
Creative Note: Residents will move in more quickly in this mode, and residences will never revert to ruins of their own accord.
Creative Note: Who needs a Workforce? In this game mode, factories will always be at 100% productivity, no matter what.
Creative Note: Bay Areas just doubled in size, allowing you to create even more extensive harbour areas! Bathing at own risk!
Creative Note: Zoo Modules can now be placed as ornaments, with a wide array of wildlife to choose from. No animals were harmed in the making of this game mode.
Creative Note: No news is good news. The Editor is taking some deserved time off and will no longer approach you with drafts.
Creative Note: Build a monumental masterpiece - you can now instantly upgrade monuments with the upgrade tool, no need to wait for materials or workforce.
Creative Note: Let all good things grow! In this game mode, fertilities no longer impact your farms or forestry buildings.
Creative Note: Combine and conquer! Special buildings are no longer restricted to a single region, mix and mingle at your own preference.
Creative Note: Time to tell your own story - quests are disabled in this game mode. Call it an aesthetic adventure.
Creative Note: Paradise or Dystopia? You can use the downgrade tool to downgrade buildings to their ruin state - provided they have one.
Creative Note: You can use ornamental fields to fill up cliff edges and make your island bloom.
Creative Note: Feel free try out new city layouts and create stamps for your sandbox games. Note: Some ornaments are limited to creative mode.

In the wake of your father's alleged treason and death, your uncle Edvard seized control of Goode and Sons, leaving you and your sister Hannah to fend for yourselves. Hannah put everything she had into purchasing a small island, but it's in a bad state. Ruins from the tin rush litter the place, and before you can start afresh, you'll need to demolish them.

Clear:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount]
Hannah encourages you to get to work on your new island.
Hannah asks you to clear the first ruin, in order to discover the island's potential.
Hannah is pleased with your work and encourages you to continue.
Hannah reminds you there is forestry work to be done on your island.
Hannah mentions there are small ruins on the island which you can get timber from.
Clear any small ruin for Timber
Remove the old ruins to clear the area for the new buildings.
You can also remove smaller ruins to get additional timber.

Hannah noticed that you're running low on timber, but she knows a quick way to stock up on it. It just so happens that there are still several ruins scattered around Ditchwater that you could demolish for materials.

The island Hannah bought for the both of you. Ditchwater is still a diamond in the rough; the ruins of a tin rush town must be demolished and cleared before the potential Hannah saw in this place can be realised.
Hannah prompts you to keep on cleaning the island.
Remove the old market ruins to have more space for your village to grow.
You can also remove smaller ruins to get additional timber.
Ditchwater has almost become what Hannah once dreamed it could be for the pair of you. Only a few more ruins now stand in the way of building a shipping company worthy of your father's legacy.
Hannah advises you to demolish the next set of ruins, which are blocking your expansion.
Remove the ruined church to have more space for your village to grow.
Edvard is baffled that you would remain beyond the funeral proceedings.
Hannah feels this island has potential.

In the wake of your father's alleged treason and death, your uncle Edvard seized control of Goode and Sons, leaving you and your sister Hannah to fend for yourselves. You have your own company now, but there's plenty to do before you can think of building ships and a shipyard. First, you'll need to build a small settlement to house the loyal people who followed you and Hannah to Ditchwater.
Hannah asks that as a first step, you provide housing for your loyal followers.
Hannah emphasises the importance of having more people to clear the island.
Hannah reminds you to provide housing for your followers.
Hannah is glad you are managing to produce timber already.
To attract farmers you need to build farmer residences.
You farmers need to live close to a marketplace. Build one near their residences.

Uncle Edvard seized control of Goode and Sons and left you and your sister Hannah fending for yourselves. But you have your own company now, keeping your father's dreams alive. Still, there is plenty to do, before you can think of ships and a shipyard. Producing timber, for example.
Hannah wants you to start producing timber.
Hannah reminds you to start producing timber.

Now that Uncle Edvard has seized control of Goode and Sons, you have to start your own company from scratch. Still, there's plenty to do before you can think of building ships and a shipyard. Clearing the ruins on Ditchwater took a lot of effort, and your people are hungry! The town needs a stable supply of food!
Hannah urges you to supply food to your farmers, who are tired from the demolition.
Hannah urges you to feed your farmers.
Aside from building residences for them, you need to provide for your residents' needs in order to attract more citizens.
Build a fishery close to your Trading Post to provide fish to your farmers.
You're keeping your father’s dream alive, as he always hoped you would. Still, there's plenty to do before you can think of building ships and a shipyard. Housing your people, for example.
Hannah asks that you support the influx of settlers with housing and amenities.
Hannah reminds you to give your people the houses and amenities they need.
Hannah congratulates you on building a settlement that may soon attract workers.

One of your cousins writes from Bright Sands, the island now owned by your Uncle. He speaks of a climate of instability surrounding Edvard's administration. Find him in the vicinity of the Great Exhibition foundations, and he may be able to help you gather some followers among the rioters.
Find your Cousin leading a mob in the vicinity of Edvard's Great Exhibition construction site
Your cousin informs you that workers are rioting in Bright Sands.
Hannah says people in Bright Sands are unhappy with Edvard, and urges you to seek out your cousin.
Hannah urges you to contact your cousin about the worker riots in Bright Sands.
Go to Edvard's harbour south-west of your island. You can also click on the quest in quest tracker to move the camera to Edvard’s harbour.
Find Edvard's church in the harbour district. It has a high bell tower. Your sister also remembers that your cousin's house has a purple roof and a campfire in the backyard.

Having saved the unhappy workers from your Uncle Edvard’s regime, your town must grow to accommodate them. With suitable housing, more workers will soon flood into your settlement, giving you the manpower to build your first shipyard.

Upgrade to:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount]
Hannah asks that you upgrade your houses to accommodate workers.
Hannah reminds you to upgrade your houses for workers.
Fulfill all the basic needs of a farmers' residence to reach the maximum number of inhabitants.
Fully populated residences can be upgraded to the next level by using the upgrade tool.

You finally have the workers on your side, but you'll need many more of them before a shipyard can be built! Your city needs to grow if you want your company to become an attractive choice for workers.
Hannah says you must have more workers before you can build a shipyard.
Hannah reminds you to expand your city and workers.
Hannah is pleased that you have enough people to build a shipyard.
Get more Workers by upgrading more residences or by fulfilling more needs.

You've cleared most of the island, but a few stubborn ruins remain. Luckily, you now have workers living in your city. They're skilled enough to take care of them for you, and aid in the final phases of making Ditchwater the perfect place to grow your new company.
Hannah advises you to remove the more robust ruins on the island.
Clear Worker Ruins

With your Uncle's debt finally behind you, you are now free to start your shipping company. Your first shipyard and ships will take you and your sister to the bright future that your father would have wanted for you.
Hannah is excited to see your first shipyard built.
Hannah is desperate to see the shipyard you have worked so hard for.
There is a whiff of salt on the breeze. With your first shipyard and ships, it will surely be a matter of time before you eclipse your ghastly Uncle.
Hannah is keen to see sails manufactured.
Hannah thinks you should make sails a priority.
Hannah discourages you from opening your Uncle’s private letter.
Hannah is shocked by Uncle Edvard’s letter and suggests you take it to Sir Archibald.

Hannah has recognised Edvard's prisoners as your father's most trusted associates, and the documents make it clear they may have been wrongfully accused! Your sister believes a higher authority like Sir Archibald Blake ought to intervene in the matter.
Hannah urges you go to Sir Archibald and show him Edvard’s devious letter.

OR:
Bring Edvard's Political Prisoners to Sir Archibald Blake
If you decide to take the political prisoners to Archibald Blake, move your ship close to his lighthouse.
Workers will migrate into a city, not into a village. You need to expand your small town.
Hannah asks you to build housing for migrants.
Hannah reminds you that new farmers need proper housing.

Since your Uncle Edvard doesn’t trust your father’s former newspaper editor, perhaps it is an opportunity for you to employ his services instead. Rumour has it he is a loyal fellow, even a little too loyal...
Aarhant wonders if your father’s former newspaper editor would be willing to work with you.
Aarhant reminds you to find the Editor in your Harbour.

Aarhant reminds you that people need a place to drink, rest and celebrate to recover from all their hard work after clearing Ditchwater's ruins. A bit of schnapps and a local pub should keep their spirits up.
Aarhant thinks Schnapps can motivate your people to keep going.
Aarhant reminds you to schnapp to it.

Provide your farmers with schnapps to keep them happy! In order to produce schnapps, build a potato farm and a schnapps distillery close to each other, then connect them to a nearby trading post or warehouse with a road. Finally, build a pub close to your farmers' residences, and put a smile on your farmers' faces!
You can also build more schnapps facilities to satisfy your farmers' needs faster.
Aarhant alerts you to an emergency lifeboat in your harbour. The survivors aboard are dressed in prison uniform, and no doubt have some tale to tell.
Aarhant alerts you to the arrival of an emergency lifeboat in your harbour.
Aarhant is sure the lifeboat survivors in your harbour are of interest.

Talk to:
Survivors on [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Object]) Text]

You rescued your Uncle's prisoners as they were being transported to Eli Bleakworth's prison, but they claim that Edvard has forged the charges against them. Aarhant has found some sealed documents amidst the wreckage that may prove this, if you dare open them...
Aarhant dares you to open your Uncle’s sealed letter.
Aarhant encourages you to oppose your uncle Edvard.

OR:
Open Sealed Document on your ship
If you decide to open the letter, you'll find it in your ship.
Eli wants Alwin, a former prisoner, found, so his investigation into your father's death can proceed.
Eli Bleakworth invites you to investigate the circumstances of your father's death.
Alwin admits it was he who killed your father, and made it look like something else.
Eli is concerned the security of his prison is compromised, and will speak to you later.

Dear Governor Bleakworth,

More of the traitor Samuel’s conspirators. Crimes and sentences as follows;

Ernest Sterling – Use of foul language – 16 years with hard labour.
Verity Goodheart – Impersonation – Transportation to the Antipodes.
Elias Noble – Writing a threatening letter – Life imprisonment
Honora Decent – Character assassination – Life imprisonment
The judge saw very well my view, that any lack of proof they conspired with a traitor was, in itself, evidence they hide something. All things considered, his verdict could have been far worse. Sincerely
Edvard Goode

Wormways Prison— A first terrible night!

My island, Prosperity, is sold. That is all I can puzzle of my arrest, and present circumstance, shackled between these cold grey walls. Tomorrow I resolve to make my case again to Mr. Bleakworth, who today so cruelly refused me a proper explanation. Now I must try to sleep, and can think of nothing but my poor Hannah, and the other, so far distant.
Wormways Prison – Light through the bars.

With daybreak comes clarity. Prosperity was sold to the infamous rebel 'Sarmento' – and I must be the last to have heard of it! The Queen, the nation, is up in arms, that the jewel of the new world is lost!

The guards, from whom I heard all, thought me playing some trick! Yet it is I who am tricked; duped of my island by persons unknown! Although it can only be the same persons that came to me one ominous day, masked and embroidered with eldrich symbols. They pressed me towards a sale. But I shut the door hard I tell you, and bid them good-day!
Wormways - A third night, and alas not the last.

I have today begun the process of gathering evidence in my defence. Hannah was here, though they did not let her stay long. She gives me hope that a full and unmitigated pardon is possible. Years of loyalty count in my favour, but the very idea that I may have betrayed my Queen weighs heavily upon me. Even if the dark clouds of scandal pass, they may forever have damaged our family’s prospects.
Thomas N. Ticker sees no purpose in trying to impress your father now he is dead.
