Isabel tells you to keep on expanding La Isla for the obreros.

Isabel's comrades were taken hostage to coerce her into working for the Pyrphorians, but she's confident that you'll be able to rescue them from their humid cells on the western archipelago. Evading the Pyrphorian guards, however, will not be easy.
Isabel has received intelligence as to the whereabouts of her abducted comrades, and asks that you free them.
A hostage is deeply grateful for your actions.
The Pyrphorian hostages are ready to come aboard your ship.
Isabel trusts you after bringing her comrades back.
Rescue Pyrphorian hostages from [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition ExecutionObject]) Text]
Deliver [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition CurrentDeliveryObject]) Text] to [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition ExecutionObject]) Text]
Deliver [Conditions QuestCondition Amount(ObjectiveIndex)] [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition DeliveryObject(ObjectiveIndex)]) Text] to La Isla
Isabel expresses her gratitiude for bringing the missing people back home.
There are Pyrphorian patrol ships inside the island atoll. Don't get into their sight radius, or else they will attack you.

Isabel is under attack! The Pyrphorians have discovered that she's been working with you to save the people of Prosperity, and have sent a fleet to burn her island to the ground! You have to stop them!
Isabel needs your help to fend off the Pyrphorians.

Destroy:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] that attack Isabel
Isabel pleads for your help one last time.

Only Prosperity's contract of sale can prove that it was not your father, but an impostor who sold the island to Sarmento, and that she herself was coerced into making that deal by the Pyrphorians. You must hunt down the thieves and retrieve the contract to prevent a war between the Queen and Isabel...
Isabel realises the Pyrphorians have stolen the Prosperity contract.
Complete Expedition [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
To start the expedition, go to the World Map and click the expedition named "The Contract".
Once the expedition has finished, wait for the ship to return, then select the expedition ship to collect the reward.
Isabel tells you bitterly how your father's actions have harmed the rebels' cause.
Isabel mentions that she somehow still trusted in your father, and believed he meant well.
Isabel suggests that the best way to start your investigation would be to find the contract of sale.
The magistrate tells you that the contract is still in his former house.
Isabel transfers you the magistrate's home island.
Isabel gives you the freedom to govern this island, to encourage the magistrate to come back.
The magistrate oversteps the mark by asking for a zoo.
Hannah waves off his inquiry.
The Queen transfers the island rights to you.
The magistrate officially revokes the island's sale.
La Corona thanks the Queen.
Hannah can't wait to confront your uncle upon your return home.
Isabel thanks you for saving her and her people.
Hannah wonders why Isabel has yet to hand you the Prosperity contract.
Sir Archibald Blake announces that the Queen's fleet is ready to reclaim Prosperity by force.
Hannah believes the Prosperity papers will prove that Isabel is not the Queen's enemy.
Isabel admires your audacity.
Hannah is proud of you for retrieving the contract in time.
Isabel fears the Pyrphorian ships approaching her island.
A Pyrphorian threatens Isabel for contravening their orders.
The Pyrphorian orders an attack on Isabel's island.
Hannah shares a letter she has received from a small boy.
The Pyrphorians threaten you and demand you leave the region at once.
Isabel warns that your presence here has not gone unnoticed.
Progeny of Samuel, you know not with whom you meddle.
Leave, if you value your life, else all shall burn.
The Pyrphorians will not let you meddle in their affairs.
An obrera cries for help.
Isabel alerts you to the danger on Prosperity and of settling other islands.
Isabel believes you have better odds at hiding them from the Pyrphorians.
Please, take us back to a safe place...
The final evidence that uncle Edvard is in fact the guilty one.
A flame-throwing weapon? Really?
Refugees from Prosperity
Hostages of the Pyrphorians, Isabel Sarmento's people
Written by hand
Edvard was the one behind the unlawful sale of the oil-rich Prosperity.
Hannah congratulates you on getting the final proof and wants you to deliver it to the council.
Hannah urges you to bring photographic proof to the council.
The Queen snatches away the photograph.
Bring to the Queen:
The Pyrphorians persist with their schemes. More fires are raging throughout the settlement, spreading fear and danger. You have to arrest the arsonists and stop this madness!
Hannah is frightened that more Pyrphorian arsonists have snuck onto your island.
Hannah is relieved that you apprehended the arsonists.

Having returned from the New World with conclusive evidence that it was your uncle's treason that sealed your father's fate, Hannah is eager to finally confront Edvard in Bright Sands and settle things once and for all.
She cannot wait to arrive at Bright Sands and confront him.

Deliver:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition DeliveryObject(ObjectiveIndex)]) Text] from your Trading Post to Edvard
Edvard asks what your business here is.
Sail a ship to your main island's trading post, and transfer the Prosperity contract to it.

Some people managed to escape the great fire of Bright Sands through the city's sewers! You must come to their rescue! But beware - Pyrphorian patrols have the place heavily guarded. If you're spotted, all of their lives will be at risk…
Hannah begs you to evacuate Bright Sands.
Slip past the Pyrphorian patrols to the Bright Sands Sewer Exit

Deliver:
[Conditions QuestCondition Amount(ObjectiveIndex)] [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition DeliveryObject(ObjectiveIndex)]) Text] to your island
Theodora Ticker is thrilled you have come to their rescue.
Hannah is appalled that you could not help the people of Bright Sands.
Hannah asks if the Bright Sands refugees are ready to disembark.
Slip past the Pyrphorian patrols and deliver [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition CurrentDeliveryObject]) Text] to your island
Don't get into the patrols' line of sight, or they'll attack.
The smaller and faster the ship you use for this, the higher your chance of success. Try it with a gunboat.
It is over. The Pyrphorian army has been overcome, but at great expense. Before you can move on, the dead must be mourned. Meet Hannah at the church cemetery in Bright Sands for your Uncle's funeral.
Hannah would like you to be there for your Uncle's funeral.
Select the church with a cemetery in Bright Sands
The Pyrphorians have infiltrated your island, and are causing widespread chaos by setting your buildings alight! Hurry up and catch the arsonists before it's too late!
Hannah asks you to arrest the Pyrphorian arsonists on your island.
Hannah believes in you.
Hannah worries you let the arsonists escape.
Search for hooded figures with a torch in their hand. Zoom in to see them better.

Now that you've finally delivered Bright Sands from the Pyrphorian terror, Hannah hopes you can resurrect the city closest to her heart. It was your father's dream, your childhood home; it will take a lot of work, but you have the power to dream up your own vision of Bright Sands now!
Hannah has something ambitious in mind.
Hannah asks you to rebuild Bright Sands.
Hannah entrusts everything to you from now on.
Demolish the ruins in Bright Sands, or renovate the individual buildings you want to keep.
With the demolish tool selected, hold Shift and drag to demolish all the buildings.

Attract to Bright Sands:
[Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]

Her Majesty has placed Edvard under house arrest in Bright Sands, where he awaits his trial for treason. The Queen has appointed you to host his trial on your island, for which you will need to erect a suitably imposing Court of Justice.
Sir Archibald Blake announces you are to build a Court of Justice to hold Edvard's trial.
The Queen admires your Court of Justice.
Finish the first phase of the Court of Justice
Finish the second phase of the Court of Justice
Finish the last phase of the Court of Justice
A Court of Justice that the Queen ordered to be built. The trial against Edvard Goode is due to be held here.
The Queen is impatient to see your Court of Justice.
Sir Archibald Blake reminds you to finish preparations before the Queen's arrival.
Place a warehouse close to the Court of Justice, and produce the required goods for it.

The Pyrphorians have taken over Bright Sands! They were the ones pulling the strings behind your Uncle Edvard's betrayal, and now they threaten to turn the Empire to ashes along with everything you hold dear. No matter how dreadful their army, you have no choice: they must be stopped!
Sir Archibald says protecting the Queen is of the utmost importance.

Destroy:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] at Bright Sands harbour
Take your time to build a large fleet. Equipping powerful items on your ships can make them much more formidable.
Target one enemy ship at a time with your whole fleet to minimize their numbers as quickly as possible.

Sir Archibald wants to support your fight against the Pyrphorians by sending you supplies from the Queen. His shipments will need to be escorted, however, in case they should run into Pyrphorian patrols.
Sir Archibald requests an escort so he can send you supplies.
Sir Archibald is relieved you received his supplies.
Sir Archibald fears you cannot afford to lose his next batch of supplies.

Protect:
Royal supply ship until it reaches The Queen's flagship
Don't underestimate the fervour of the Pyrphorian attackers. Bring strong military ships to flank the royal supply ship.
You will earn important supplies upon completing this quest, which will help you in your progress with the main quest.
Sir Archibald Blake asks if you're ready to receive the royal supplies and munitions.
Sir Archibald announces the launch of the next supply ship, and wants you to protect it.
Aarhant has the feeling a darker threat is looming over the horizon. He asks you to prepare for whatever may happen by improving your harbour defences.
Aarhant feels you must prepare for an eventual attack.
Edvard repents and warns you of a greater enemy.
Hannah is determined not to forgive Uncle Edvard.
The Queen acknowledges your efforts to protect the Empire.
The Queen seems rather ambivalent about the trial.
Aarhant is surprised at the Queen's... assertiveness.
After taking over Bright Sands, the Pyrphorians are coming for you! Prepare to fend off their attacks!
Aarhant alerts you to an incoming Pyrphorian attack.
Hannah asks you to put an end to the Pyrphorians.

Destroy:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount] approaching your harbour

Now is the time to blunt the Pyrphorian blade! Aarhant prompts you to attack the Pyrphorian patrols that are roaming the seas, and decimate their numbers. Any cargo they carry might also prove useful if used against them…
Aarhant advises you to cripple the Pyrphorian forces by raiding their patrols.
Isabel encourages you to break the Pyrphorian supply lines.
Aarhant advises you not to lower your guard against the Pyrphorians.
Aarhant advises you remain wary of the Pyrphorian menace.
You will earn strong military items upon completing this quest. These items will help you with the main quest.

The Pyrphorian fleet is huge, and a great and final confrontation seems inevitable. Aarhant has long-since anticipated such a battle, and makes his recommendations on how to counter the Pyrphorian threat with a mighty fleet of your own.
Aarhant suggests which ships you should build for the great battle ahead.
Aarhant believes these ships capable of defeating the Pyrphorians.
Having two shipyards at work at the same time will increase your output of ships. The same goes for weapon factories.
You can also buy weapons at Isabel's island in the New World.

Your island's defences are sufficient to guarantee the Queen's safety, and the Court of Justice is ready to hold the trial. Her Majesty and Sir Archibald Blake await your welcome at your harbour, before taking their place at the tribunal.
The Queen expects a royal welcome.
Welcome the Queen to your harbour
Preparations for the trial are complete, and it only remains for the defendant to be removed from house arrest and led to court in chains. Sail to Bright Sands and fetch the pitiable Uncle Edvard.
The Queen is ready to see Edvard for the Trial.

Pick up:
Court summons from The Queen's Flagship
Arrest Edvard with the court summons
The Queen wants to hand over the court summons for you to issue to Edvard.
Sail a ship with at least one cargo slot free to within range of the Queen's flagship.
Once your ship draws close to the Queen, accept the request she has for you.
Aarhant is hardly surprised to hear Edvard was behind this all along.
Hannah is furious about Edvard's treason.
Aarhant pities Edvard.
The Queen expects your Court of Justice will serve the Empire well.
Sir Archibald believes Isabel Sarmento will be an important witness at the trial.
Isabel Sarmento agrees to testify at Edvard's trial.
Isabel sympathises with you.
Sir Archibald announces the Queen's arrival.
The Queen waves off Archibald's overly formal introduction.
The Queen is keen to start the trial.
Isabel Sarmento presents herself for the trial.
Isabel Sarmento hopes her testimony will absolve her people.
Aarhant is horrified to see the Pyrphorians take over Bright Sands.
The Pyrphorian Grandmaster threatens your family.
Isabel Sarmento vows to fight with you against the Pyrphorians.
The Queen is determined to end this fighting.
The last Pyrphorian acolyte dies.
The Pyrphorian Grandmaster threatens and ridicules you.
The Pyrphorian Grandmaster belittles you.
The Pyrphorian Grandmaster refuses to accept defeat.
The Pyrphorian Grandmaster vows to return and get revenge.
Theodora Ticker is finally reunited with her husband.
Thomas Ticker is relieved that his wife is safe and sound.
Aarhant toasts your victory over the Pyrphorians.
Hannah is full of praise for your victory over the Pyrphorians.
Hannah is excited to be welcoming the Queen to Bright Sands.
The signature was forged by your Uncle. Your father is innocent.
A document summoning Edvard Goode's to trial.

Since you managed to settle the potentially catastrophic dispute over Prosperity, the Queen has decided to entrust the island to you. Isabel Sarmento hands over the keys to the golden gates of Prosperity, an island that evokes only bad memories for her and her people.
Isabel dismantled all of her rebel structures on Prosperity. The island is all yours now.
Isabel Sarmento is happy to see you once again.
Isabel Sarmento is travelling to the Old World to be principal witness at the trial against Edvard.

Select in the New World:
Prosperity Trading Post
Bright Sands
Prosperity
Ditchwater
La Isla
Islands vary greatly in their riches. Examine the fertilities and deposits in this overview to help you choose where to settle.
Islands vary greatly in their riches. Examine their fertilities and deposits before you decide where to settle.
Sail to the coast of the island you want to settle, and build a trading post there to claim it officially.
Select the trading post blueprint in the desired location, and give the order to build it.
Sail in any direction to discover new islands to settle.
Select the trading post blueprint once you're ready to place it.
This is your construction menu. You can select your marketplace, residences, roads and everything else you need.
Start with a marketplace. As the heart of your city, it needs to be placed in an open space, so your people can live around it.
Nobody will be able to reach your marketplace until you build a road to connect it to your trading post.
Housing people is essential! Make sure to build their residences near the marketplace and connect them via roads so people have access to goods.
Select a residence and observe how farmers slowly move in because you fulfilled their need for a Market!
You can choose to build farmer's residences, marketplaces and roads from the construction menu.
Your people need to live near a marketplace, otherwise they'll not move in.
People will only be able to reach your marketplace if a road connects it to your trading post.
All residences need to have a marketplace nearby, else no-one will move in!
Residences need to be connected to a nearby marketplace by a road.
Residences need a marketplace nearby. You can select it from your construction menu.
Drag and drop to lay down roads after selecting them from the construction menu. You can also click once to set a starting point, and a second time where you want the road to end.
All production buildings need to be connected either to a warehouse, or the next building in their production chain. Make sure they're close enough!
Warehouses can store and deliver all your goods, but they come at a cost. Be sure to lay out your production buildings as efficiently as possible to make best use of them!

Some production buildings require an input of raw materials or intermediate products. These can be sourced either from a warehouse, or directly from the production building itself. The final goods, on the other hand, can only go to a warehouse - so be sure to build the final building of your production chain near to one.
Storage is shared across all Warehouses on the same island: once a good is delivered to a Warehouse, it becomes accessible to the whole island.
Every marketplace, warehouse and public building needs to be accessible from your trading post!
Every marketplace, warehouse and public building needs to be accessible from your trading post!
Your farmers are hungry! Build a fishery by the sea!
Every fish they catch needs to be delivered to a warehouse or a trading post. Be sure to lay a road between them!
Fisheries can only be built by the sea, and must be connected to either a warehouse, or your trading post.
Once delivered to a warehouse, goods become accessible to the general population. Make sure your markets are kept well stocked!
Your population's access to a marketplace, and the amount of stock you own determines their level of satisfaction with their goods.
Your people's demands will grow along with your city. If their needs are not satisfied, they might move out!
Start by opening the timber production chain in the construction menu.
Place a Lumberjack's Hut in the forest to start producing Wood.
Place a Sawmill near the Lumberjack's Hut, and connect them with a road. The Sawmill will consume Wood to produce Timber.
Don't forget roads! The Sawmill workers need to be able to access their input good!
Timber needs to be stored in either a Trading Post or a Warehouse. Make sure the Sawmill has a road connection to one of these located within range.
All warehouses need to be connected to a trading post. After all, you can't sell your goods if you can't reach the trading post!
Every production building can be found in the construction menu.
Your sawmill requires wood to produce timber. A lumberjack's hut will be able to provide it.
Your production buildings need to access their input material either directly from the source, or from a warehouse. Similarly, they need to store their output in a warehouse.
Your balance is the difference between your income and your expenses. Keep it positive! You don't want to go bankrupt.

You can sell any excess of supply to other parties to earn extra money. Click on the resource in your trading post menu to set how much you want to sell, and the trade will be fulfilled automatically.
Your residents need more than just goods - they also require certain buildings. A pub will increase your residents' happiness, along with the income they generate.
Fully equip your finest ship, and send it on an expedition of discovery to unlock the New World!
Select an expedition to access the expedition menu, and assign a ship to it.
Equip your ship with goods and items to prepare for any potential threats the expedition may encounter.
Morale determines your expedition's chance of success. Stock your ship with hearty rations, and make sure your sailors leave port with as high a morale level as possible.
Once your ship is ready, you can launch your expedition, letting them weigh anchors and take off into the world map!

Every time your expedition stumbles upon an unexpected situation, they'll ask you for the best course of action. Their attributes determine their chance of success at certain actions, so make your decisions carefully.
All farms require fields. Select the farm, and then select the fields. Fields need to be adjacent to the farm and to each other.
All animal farms require enclosures. Select the farm, and then select the enclosures. They need to be close to the farm.
Refineries are modular buildings. You'll have to place oil wells on deposits in order for them to function.
Once your farmers' needs are completely satisfied, you will be able to promote them to workers. Select a residence that is ready and activate "Upgrade" in its menu to renovate the building.
You can upgrade a house by selecting the corresponding button in the house menu, or by using the upgrade tool.
Upgrading a building requires construction materials, so make sure you can afford it first!
A residence can only be upgraded once it has reached its maximum number of occupants.
Harbour defences are essential to protect your island from attack. You can find several options in the harbour category of your construction menu.
Your influence increases along with your global population. You can check your current available stock here.
Your quest book contains all the information you'll need about quests - and sometimes, even hints!
Happiness is impacted by many factors, for example the access to luxury goods. Find all factors in the residence menu.
Schnapps makes your people happy, and will give your income a nice boost! Start producing some from potatoes!
The schnapps distillery will process potatoes into schnapps.
You can deploy additional units to overcome an incident by selecting the option from the relevant institution's menu.
Now you can build a shipyard and construct your own ships! Use them to trade, fight, and explore the world... The possibilities are endless.
Select which ship you'd like to start building from your shipyard's menu.
Tourism is a great source of income when your city's attractiveness is high. Build a public mooring so guests can dock.
Left-click on your ship to select it, then right-click wherever you want it to go to.
Left-click on the dynamite to select it, then left-click where you want to throw it.
Right-click on the fish to pick it up.
Whenever you want to sell a ship, sail it to the buyer's harbour and click on "Sell Ship".
Click this button to see the buyer's offer. Accept the offer once you're happy with it.
Hey, guv. I've this drill from me late uncle just laying around the house, thought you might find some use for it. Go ahead, take it!

You can equip items in the Trade Union that will affect every production building in its range in very interesting ways.
Build a Trade Union close to your Clay Pit to try out the item you just received!
Select your trade union, and click on any slot to choose the item you want to equip.

My baby Black Beard used to be so adorable, with his eye patch and his buccaneer bicorne. Who would have thought that my tiny little cub would grow into such a magnificent beast! I love him with all my heart, but there's just not enough room for him at my humble workshop... Give him the life he deserves, I beg of you!

Poor little thing. Talk about underestimating him... He clearly wouldn't survive a single day in the wild. The best thing we can do is build a proper enclosure for him in a zoo. I'm sure people would love to come visit this huge, cuddly fellow.
Select your Zoo to see more options. Build an empty enclosure next to the main building!
Now select the empty enclosure and equip it with our big fuzzy friend. He will be very happy here.
Equip an empty enclosure with the black bear.

And that is the story of how my great-great-great-grand-uncle left the convent to become a comedian. My nana used to tell me all about her old uncle Hilarius; his was such an unbelievable journey. His works were not only entertaining, but they were extremely significant for their time as well! I believe you will find this extremely enlightening.
I didn't know what to make of it at first, but pal, I think this piece has some serious historical value! Why don't we build a museum, and display it for our people and visitors?
Select your museum to see more options. Build an empty exhibit next to the main building.
Now select the empty exhibit and equip the artisan's gift. I am sure people will be very eager to learn more about that old monk!
Equip Illuminated Manuscript on Empty Exhibit
Some residences are ready to be upgraded! Once we do so, we'll be able to welcome people from a new social class into our city.
Nobody enjoys a life surrounded by pollution... You can check your island's contamination levels in your city's attractiveness menu.
Each production building requires a specific type of workforce. We should always house enough of each to keep our industries running.
Heavy industries produce at a slower rate. You can... temporarily adjust working conditions to increase productivity.
The editor will ask for your opinion before publishing every edition of the newspaper. With enough influence, you'll be able to... tamper with the truth to impact public opinion.
We can finally send expeditions out into the world! Open the world map, and have a look at the different possible destinations.
Here you have a quick overview of the currently available expeditions.
Storage is shared throughout all Warehouses: once a good is delivered to a Warehouse, it becomes accessible to the whole island.
La Fortune might be a pirate, but he's a reasonable man. Try to deal with him, and he may surprise you.
It may be hard to deal with pirates, but gaining reputation with them could be very beneficial. Harlow might be more open to signing off trade rights, or even negotiating peace if she likes you.
Sir Archibald Blake is the Queen's representative. He always has interesting items and goods for sale at his harbour.
Isabel Sarmento is the courageous leader of the New World's Movement. You can find many interesting items and goods at her harbour.
Old Nate is a despicable scavenger, but his bad habits do garner him quite a curious array of items for sale. Although I hear he only settles deals in an eccentric foreign currency...
Eli Bleakworth prides himself on running the prison with an iron first. All kinds of useful people seem to land in his cells. Bail them out, and they'll gladly join our company.
Madame Kahina knows every route going for exotic goods and items. You can find almost anything you can imagine at her shops, for a reasonable price...

Bente Jorgensen is gentle young woman with a passion for exploring the world. Like you, she has just started her own company. She'll be more than happy to interact and deal with you as her company grows.
Princess Qing runs her family's subsidiary in these parts with as steady a hand as she can muster. She'll be glad to interact with you - just make sure your intentions don't get lost in translation.
Willie Wibblesock founded his company very recently and quite out of the blue. Nothing is lost by talking to him.
George Smith seems to be experienced in everything life has to offer. Grumpy though he may be, he will gladly deal with you as long as you show a similar strength of principles in your actions.
Beryl O'Mara is a self-made woman, though her methods are not what one might call conventional. She is a ruthless rival, but if you deal with her you might find she's not without a heart.
Carl Leonard von Malching is obsessed with making his name heard again, and he seems to be achieving that for all the wrong reasons. Don't let his attitude get to you in negotiations.
Artur Gasparov thinks of himself as the greatest architect of our time. Keep that in mind every time you need to strike a deal, for it is the only thing that truly interests him.
Alonso Graves is the most dangerous, unpredictable man this side of the ocean... Tread very lightly around him.
Admiral Vicente Silva serves a rival empire. His mind is set on conquering the Old World. Diplomacy is not his strong suit, but he does have a couple of weaknesses you could exploit.
Lady Margaret Hunt is one of the most influential members of the Royal Council. Be very wary of her, and don't let her play you.

La Fortune has dedicated himself to piracy to survive, so be careful not to let your ships fall into his hands. Still, if you play your cards right, he might agree to lay down arms and trade with you.

Beware of Anne Harlow. She's not interested in expanding her island, but her pirate ships will hunt our traders down unless we pay a fee... You may be able to trade with her, if you can manage to get on her good side...
There are many new construction options available in the New World.
Refineries will pump out the oil that power plants require to generate electricity.
Oil wells can only be placed on top of oil deposits, so make sure you build your refineries nearby.
Refineries can only deliver oil to the oil harbour. Don't forget to build a railway connection between the two once they've been built.
Power plants consume oil to generate electricity. As such, they require a railway connection to your oil harbour.

Power lines run alongside your streets. Electricity will revolutionise productivity and residents' lifestyles, but the better-off will demand a connection, and some production buildings will not function unless they have one.
Press this button to sell your ship to a nearby trader.

Now that we have a zoo, wouldn't it be nice if it had more wildlife? I can only dream of what unknown species our expeditions may encounter — and I've certainly heard a few menacing growls while walking around Madame Kahina's Emporium... I'm sure some of our friends would express their gratitude with pups were we to help them out!

You can find all the details about your cultural buildings in their respective menus. There you will find additional information about the animals and artefacts you have in your zoos and museums. And who knows — maybe one day, we'll gather all we need to complete one of the sets!

We now have a museum to showcase every interesting artefact our expeditions encounter on their travels! I'm sure many of our friends would be happy to donate to our collection were we to help them out. We should also keep an eye out for interesting merchandise next time we browse Kahina's Emporium!
Access a detailed breakdown of your financial situation by clicking on your Balance.

This building has been constructed as a blueprint! This happens whenever you don't have enough construction material or money to complete the actual construction.
Select the blueprint to finalize it whenever you're ready.

Mind your buildings' processing times! Processing times are displayed as a tool tip when you select a production building in the construction menu. One Clay Pit can supply two Brick Factories at once; open up a second factory to optimise production!
Upgrading your trading post will increase your island's storage.
Depots are also useful when it comes to expanding your island's storage capacity.
Warehouses can be upgraded, too. An increased number of loading ramps will reduce transport delays.
Your power plants need to be connected to your oil harbour by railway.
Oil can only be transported by railway. Build tracks between your refinery and oil harbour!
The sole purpose of Oil Stores are to increase your island's maximum oil capacity.
Windows are a valuable construction material, made out of sand from the coastline.
Trees take some time to grow, be patient!
Limestone is extracted from quarries to create concrete, an essential construction material.
Fire risk is increasing! Build a Fire Station before there's something to regret.
Your population is feeling restless. Only the police can restore order in the event of a riot.
As your population grows, so too does their chance of falling ill. A hospital can prevent sickness from spreading, and treat your residents when they're feeling unwell.
Clay Pits need to be built on top of existing clay deposits. Look for one on this island.
Clay will be processed into bricks at a brick factory.
Missing a certain fertility? You can easily set up trade routes from this menu to automatically transport goods between different islands.
Your residents will ask for goods that can only be produced in the New World. Set up trade routes to ensure a steady income.
We have discovered a new region! You can select it in the World Map.

You don't need to produce everything, you can also buy goods from other traders!
Select the good you'd like to purchase in your Trading Post, and set up the trading options for it. Visiting trading ships will automatically sell it to you.
Artisans are asking for some goods that aren't available in this region. If you don't have a way to produce, or import them, you can always get them from Madame Kahina.
Some of your production buildings require electricity to function. Make sure you build a power plant close by, as the power lines will run alongside your roads.
Your people need new clothes. First, you'll require a supply of wool from sheep farms.
The framework knitters will weave the wool into work clothes.
Steel beams are the foundation of industrialisation. We need iron!
Weapons are essential to the construction of military ships and buildings.
Better safe than sorry. Prepare your island's defences in order to repel any enemy in the event of an attack. Place harbour defences along the coast to protect your trading post.

Define districts and bend the rules with administrative buildings (Town Hall, Harbourmaster's Office, Trade Union). Equip them with powerful items and specialists to impact both your economy, and your population in very interesting ways.
Your advisor, Hannah, greets you.
Your advisor, Aarhant, greets you.
Aarhant is here to help you.
Hannah urges you to make some renovations.
Your advisor suggests you regularly visit the traders.
Aarhant directs your attention towards the newspaper.
Aarhant advises you to find a suitable island to settle.
This is where it all begins. Find a suitable island for your first settlement, and claim it by placing a trading post.
Build: [AssetData(1010517) Text]
Hannah stresses the importance of having a good marketplace.
First and foremost, you'll need people to work with you. All they need to start moving in is a market, and a roof over their heads.

Hannah reminds you that every residence needs a road to a marketplace.
Your residents need to live close to the marketplace, or else they won't move in!
Connect [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] to a marketplace
Hannah urges you to connect your production buildings to a warehouse.

Your production buildings have a limited storage. Once their stores are full, if they can't deliver their output to a warehouse, they'll simply stop producing. Make sure they have a road connection to a warehouse in range.
Connect [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] to a warehouse
Hannah points out that some buildings can't access your trading post.
Every marketplace, warehouse and public building requires a road connection to your trading post to be able to access your island's storage. Don't forget to pave the way!
Connect [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] to the trading post
Hannah urges you to take care of your people's basic needs.

Your people have certain needs, and the most basic of them is food! Farmers will be content with a stable supply of fish for the time being. Pay attention to your residents' needs, or they may start moving out of your city.
Build [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Hannah is preoccupied with your timber supply.
Building a flourishing new settlement requires a lot of construction materials. You won't get very far unless you start producing timber.
Primary Resource: Build a [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Construction Materials: Build a [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Goods need to be delivered to a warehouse. An island's Trading Post counts as one, but you'll need to build warehouses within range of any more distant production buildings.
Hannah worries about your company's balance.
Money is key to your progression, so you'll want to avoid going bankrupt at all costs. Try to improve your balance sheet - there are many ways to reduce your costs and increase your income!
Make your balance positive.
Settle your debt.
Aarhant recommends you build a pub.
Your residents need more than just the basics! They will be much happier — and generate more income — if they can enjoy a drink at the pub in their spare time.
Build [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Hannah encourages you to expand your settlement.
The larger your settlement grows, the more options you'll have in your construction menu. Attract more residents to unlock new buildings!

Attract:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text] [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount]
Aarhant is looking forward to reaching the New World.
The New World is waiting for you! The only way to set foot on their shores is to send a discovery expedition.
Send an expedition to the New World.
Hannah points out that your farms lack fields.
Farms require fields and enclosures to function. If you want to grow plants or raise herds, you need to set them!
Set Sheepfolds
Set oil wells
Oil refineries require raw oil extracted from oil wells within range. Don't forget to build them on top of oil fields!
Set potato fields
Set grain fields
Hannah says you're now ready to house your first workers.
Once your farmers' needs are completely satisfied, you'll be able to promote them to become workers. Select a residence that's ready, and click "Upgrade" to renovate the building.
Upgrade to [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Hannah warns that you're lacking workers.

Different types of production buildings require different types of workers. Workers are able to operate heavy machinery in mines and factories, but only farmers have the required sensitivity to tend to farms and craft certain basic goods. Watch your workforce and make sure you have enough people to operate all of your production buildings.
Increase your workforce balance.
Hannah advises to import the goods you cannot produce.

Sometimes, you'll require certain goods that you can't produce on your island. In this situation, you'll have to find a way to import it, either by trading with other parties, or by settling on another island where you can produce it. Don't forget to set up a trade route if you want the goods to reach your main island regularly!
Hannah reminds you that certain buildings require electricity.
Electricity isn't just a major improvement - in some cases, it's an essential requirement. Some of the heavier factories cannot run unless they can plug their machines into an electrical connection.
Provide electricity to your [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
A worker has something for you.
Hannah suggests you build a trade union to put your items to good use.
Trade unions allow you to equip unique machines, specialists and other items that will have various beneficial effects on every production building in their vicinity.
Build a [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Equip an item at a trade union.
An artisan wants to give you something.

An artisan got himself a bear cub and thought it would be hilarious to call it Black Beard, dressing it up as a romantic pirate. However, it seems he can no longer take care of his tame but frankly gigantic pet, so he's entrusted its care to you.

An artisan got himself a bear cub and thought it would be hilarious to call it Black Beard, dressing it up as a romantic pirate. The shy bear has outgrown the artisan's little workshop, and since it wouldn't stand a chance if you were to release it into the wild, Aarhant has suggested you build a comfortable enclosure for it in a zoo.
Aarhant asks you to build a zoo for the animal.
Hannah is excited to welcome your first visitors.

Your flourishing city is starting to attract the attention of tourists! Build a public mooring to welcome them to your island. Invest into creating a beautiful and peaceful cultural landmark, and visitors will come pouring into your harbour, along with their money!
Build a [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]

An artisan is proudly regaling you with stories about his renowned ancestor — a wholesome-looking monk who in time became a famous comedian. He wants to give you one of his old works, handed down generation after generation, so you and the people of your city can learn more about the remarkable man.

According to Aarhant, the manuscript is of immense historical value. He has suggested you build a museum so you can put it on display, allowing your people to learn more about that hilarious old monk.
Aarhant suggests the artisan's gift belongs in a museum.
Hannah points out you'll need hops for beer, and suggests you settle a new island to procure them.
Hannah points out you'll need red peppers for canned food, and suggests you settle a new island to procure them.
Hannah is happy you now own an island with hops fertility.
Hannah is happy you now own an island with red pepper fertility.
Hannah is pleased you can now provide beer to your people.
Hannah is pleased you can now provide red pepper to your people.

Build a Trading Post on an island with hops fertility
(Deliver 10t timber and 8t steel beams to the island's coast to build the Trading Post)

Build a Trading Post on island with red pepper fertility
(Deliver 10t timber and 8t steel beams to the island's coast to build the Trading Post)
Having noticed that your island lacks the fertility to produce hops - a key ingredient in the brewing of beer - Hannah suggests you settle a new island to procure the missing resource.
Having noticed that your island lacks the fertility to produce red pepper - a key ingredient in the making of canned food - Hannah suggests you settle a new island to procure the missing resource.
Load a ship with at least 10t of timber and 8t of steel beams to build a Trading Post.
Sail around with your ship to seek out an island that has Hops Fertility.
Sail around with your ship to seek out an island that has Red Pepper Fertility.
Once you've spotted a likely island, sail close to any beach and select the transparent Trading Post silhouette to build it there. Confirm to complete the building.
Once you've harvested some hops, load it onto a ship and take it back to your main island to start producing Beer.
Once you've harvested some red pepper, load it onto a ship and take it back to your main island to start producing Canned Food.

Dearest sibling, you'll find your current island's fertilities and lodes displayed here.
As you can see, we cannot grow hops here, and therefore cannot produce beer. We must seek out another island where we can produce hops.

Dearest sibling, you'll find your current island's fertilities and lodes displayed here.
As you can see, we cannot grow red pepper here, and therefore cannot produce canned food. We must seek out another island where we can produce red pepper.
Dearest sibling, look here to find the fertilities and lodes of your current island.
As you can see, we cannot grow hops here, and therefore cannot produce beer. We must find an island where we can produce hops.
As you can see, we cannot grow red pepper here, and therefore cannot produce canned food. We must find an island where we can produce red peppers.
Trading posts can only be built on an island's beach. Click on this transparent silhouette of a Trading Post.

Here you can see the construction costs of a new Trading Post.
Confirm the order to build it here.
Aarhant fears you might lose control of your island.

One of your rivals is taking over your island's shares! Once they buy the last one, they'll gain total control over your island, and you'll lose it! Buy your shares back from your trading post before that happens!
Recover your island's shares.
Aarhant urges you to prepare for upcoming conflicts.
This is war! You must prepare to protect your coast from the enemy's attacks.

Aarhant suggests you increase your influence.

Influence is a powerful resource to invest in the areas that interest you the most, but you only have a finite supply. Expanding your city will increase your company level, which in turn will increase your influence.

Here you'll be able to see all of your tasks, along with any useful advice for completing them. Make sure you check it every once in a while!
Open the [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]
Aarhant worries about your people's happiness.
Happy people tend to prefer to go out on beautiful parades rather than destructive riots, and they may trust you with their problems and reward you for your troubles too. Lighten up their days!
Raise [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]' Happiness [Conditions QuestCondition CurrentAmount]/[Conditions QuestCondition Amount]

Unhappy people will rise against you, causing terrible damage to your city's economy which will only snowball over time. Once it's begun, only the police can restore order, but it would be wiser to prevent the situation from becoming so tense in the first place by looking after your people's happiness.
End the [AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Context]) Text]

Heavy industries and cramped building complexes increase the risk of a fire breaking out. Prevent a tragedy by making sure a fire patrol can reach any emergency quickly!

Hannah can't wait to see your first ships!

Isabel would like to offer you a ship.
Isabel Sarmento hands over the ship to you and wishes you well.

Receive:
[AssetData([Conditions QuestCondition Object]) Text]

Isabel Sarmento knows how hard it can be to begin anew far from home. She would like you to accept her help in the form of a well-provided ship, so maybe you too will consider helping her and her people in return.
The day and night cycle is set to off by default. You can activate it in Day and Night settings, or jump directly to a preset time in this menu.
Bente loves her pets, and her pets love potatoes! She needs as many potatoes as she can get to keep them happy!
Bente loves all kinds of animals. She doesn't understand why people think pigs are disgusting. She'd like to spread her love for them with a grand parade.
Bente needs more beams, but she'd prefer not to build another steelworks, as the pollution may damage the wildlife on her island.
Bente's planning a chocolatey surprise for the orphans, and she hopes you can oblige.
Bente gave all her bread away to people in need, but she forgot her people get hungry too! She needs your help to stock back up on it.
Bente needs new sails. Why? Because she gave hers away to those who are less privileged, of course.
Bente has no choice but to set her love of animals aside if she wants her crew to survive an expedition to the poles. Canned food would make for the perfect rations.
Bente has discovered that caoutchouc is the perfect cruelty-free replacement for leather, and would like you to deliver some to her.
Whalers have docked at Bente's harbour - a grave mistake, for she will protect cetacean life at any cost. She would never think of harming the crew, of course... But when they're all ashore...
One of Bente's expeditions didn't make it back to port safely. The crew are OK, but the precious hummingbirds they were carrying are still lost amongst the wreckage.
A visitor's ship has been in a terrible accident, and the passengers need to be saved! Bente has asked for your help.

Bente was awaiting the arrival of some precious relics from one of her expeditions, but it seems the sailors believed they were cursed, so they've thrown them overboard. She's asked you to recover the artefacts for her.
Bente wants to increase environmental awareness. She's positive that seeing you both cleaning the oceans together will, one day, make people understand.

Bente is confident that nothing bad will happen to her on her expeditions, but her advisors still worry it might be dangerous to go alone. She'd like you to escort her until her advisors start to relax.
Bente's cousin Alva paid her a visit, but decided to leave earlier than planned after meeting the household pets. Bente has asked if you would escort her cousin home.
Bente would like you to take pictures of her artefacts, which she can then frame and hang from the walls.
Bente would like you to build a zoo, to help the people of your city reconnect with nature.
Bente has so many artefacts, she can't have them all on display. She hopes you'll open a museum soon, so she can donate them to your collection.
Bente wants your help in bringing some wild animals on her island into the safety of her zoo for the winter.
Bente would like you to collect some exotic animals she has first dibs on from Madame Kahina.
Bente would like to gift you an extremely beautiful and loyal animal as a pet.
Bente has just returned from an eventful expedition - and since you're a close friend, she brought back a souvenir for you.
Bente would like to help you stave off any potential money problems with a small charitable donation.
Somewhat surprisingly, Bente wants you to smuggle some eastern treasures out of High Clarence Hall and return them to their rightful dynastic owners via Princess Qing.
George sent Bente some animals that were mistreated, but it seems like something has happened to them en route.

Bente's advisors think it's time for her to marry. They have a Mr. Bingle lined up, whom she's at least willing to meet. Sir Archibald would be the obvious person to bring them together at a garden party.
Bente needs a dress to wear to attend a garden party and meet her potential husband, Mr Bingle. Apparently, Madame Kahina has a nice selection for formal occasions.

It is with regret that Bente agrees, at the request of Sir Archibald and Mr. Bingle, to sever ties with Alonso Graves, with whom she is good friends. She asks if you could deliver him a letter and a parting gift.
Having received Bente's letter severing ties with him, Alonso would like to have a little tête-à-tête with Mr. Bingle. He asks you to arrange for them to meet.

In one final twist, Alonso would like you to photograph Mr. Bingle with the pigs in his pigsty. The image may encourage Bente to rethink any potential engagement, or indeed, any further association of any sort.
Bente thinks the young children the noble Beryl O'Mara rescued from the street deserve a little bit of pampering at the palace, and wants you to ask Sir Archibald if that would be OK.
Bente's proposal that Beryl's street children stay at High Clarence Hall for a short time has met with the royal seal of approval. It's up to you to ferry them there safely.
Bente is rather embarrassed to have to write a letter to Sir Archibald apologising for the behaviour of Beryl's street children at the palace. She wants you to deliver it.
Bente is worried she hasn't heard from her New World expedition in weeks. She wants you to find them, and revive the expedition with vital supplies. Perhaps you can also figure out what happened...

Having been found, Bente's expedition captain reaches out to you. Everyone aboard seems to be too stunned to remember what happened to them, and how they ended up being wrecked. Perhaps there are clues nearby...
Finally realising the sequence of events, the captain reluctantly agrees to lead you to the flotsam, so you can recover what he believes to be a cursed artefact.
Recovering the artefact does indeed seem to have cursed your ship, and you never found those missing crewmen... But Bente won't believe any of that, so you'd better bring her the mummy.

The mummy you gave Bente to put in her museum is seemingly responsible for an epidemic of disease in her city. Bente is understandably keen to obtain the emergency medical supplies Isabel Sarmento has on offer.
My assorted pets have such a healthy appetite, they go berserk for boiled potatoes! I really can't keep up with them! Please, bring me as many as you can!

Pigs are one of my favourite animals - so intelligent and cuddlesome! I fear most people just don't understand them. Oh, yes! How about we organise a parade to spread some goodwill for the little piggies!
I cannot risk building a steelworks when this island is home to the Ebony Jewelwing - the soot would smudge their delicate little wings! Perhaps I could buy my beams from you instead?
I love visiting the orphans, but it always breaks my heart... They're only children, they should be playing and scoffing sweets! I'd like to give them a treat - could I sneak some from your pantry?
You should have seen their innocent, hungry eyes... I just had to give them all the bread we had! It didn't even occur to me that my people need it too...
I need some new sails before I can set out! What happened to the old ones? Well... all those poor people were out in the cold, so I had to think quickly!

I normally prefer to live on nuts and fruits, but the captain is right - we can't venture out on a polar expedition without plenty of fatty food. Would you happen to have any canned food we could use?
I cannot believe I've been wearing leather boots when they could have been made of caoutchouc all along! If you were able to bring me some, you might help prevent the needless loss of animal lives...
I cannot simply look away from the red trail whalers leave in their wake. Quickly! Sink their ship while I entertain the crew at my harbour!
My expedition crashed during a storm! The crew saved their own lives, but they couldn't take the hyacinth macaws with them! Please, please - save them before it's too late!
What a terrible tragedy! A visitor's ship has capsized! We cannot stand idle - we must help the passengers!
Poor sailors' superstitions drove them to throw my precious relics overboard. Please retrieve the lost cargo before it's lost forever! I can take any silly curse they bear.
Our oceans are becoming more and more cluttered by the day! I fear for the marine life... Clean up with me, and people will surely start to follow our example!

I know my advisors only want the best for me, but sometimes they can be so... bothersome. They insist I shouldn't go alone on my expeditions. Please, would you sail with me a little bit, just to set their minds at ease?

Cousin Alva had to cut her visit short - apparently the poor thing is allergic to my pets! You should have seen her face when she opened the door to their welcome chorus! Could you see her home for me, perhaps?

My museum is coming along rather nicely, but as with everything, it can always be improved! If you could spare the time, I'd like to hang some pictures of my artefacts around the gallery - but I'll need a photographer first...

I know why you haven't built a zoo; you're worried it would be cruel. I felt the same, until I realised my zoo could protect endangered species from extinction! Not to mention educating people of all walks of life about the joy of the wilderness!

Why don't you build a museum? I have so many fascinating artefacts I could give you if you did! It's terrible, really - the display cabinets are so stuffed, I'm forced to keep most of my collection in a dusty undercroft...

I will not make a habit of interfering with nature, but I have heard the winter is likely to be particularly hard this year. As such, I'd prefer if the animals on my island were kept safe in the comfort of my zoo until the weather improves. Please say you're able to help?

Madame Kahina has recently imported some exotic animals, and I've decided I shall be the one to take care of them. They'll need a great deal of love, since they're all so far from home. Sadly, my ships are all on expeditions at the moment, so I wondered if you might collect them for me?
Here to collect Bente's animals? But you're three days early! They're still in their crates! If you want them now, you'll have to find them yourself.

Everyone needs love in their lives, and animals give it freely! Please, take care of this dear little cat. Since he's grown, I find I don't have quite so much time for him anymore. He is rather big these days, but I'm sure he'll make you very happy!

I'm back! I think that might just have been my best expedition yet. We would have been completely lost without the local guide, but instead we saw emerald forest weighed down with serpents; a funny sandy thingy where I sadly lost a few men; and in the end we found an enormous treasure! Here you go, you can have it.

A lack of material wealth should never hold us back from doing great deeds! I want to donate a small amount to help keep you on your feet. Sometimes when we run a little short on funds, we worry about relying too much on others. All I intend with this gift is to negate that sort of awkwardness in the future.

Princess Qing tells me that some heirlooms belonging to her forefathers remain locked away at High Clarence Hall, and the Emperor has written to the Queen several times to ask for them back. I know it's naughty, but if you could somehow get them to the Princess, the world would be a better place for it.

Dear Mr. Smith always keeps an eye out for mistreated animals, and sends them to me by sea. Unfortunately, this time, they seem unusually late. Something must have happened... Do you also have George's compassion? Could you rescue them for me?

My advisors always remind me how indecent it is for a young, wealthy lady like me to remain single. They've found a perfect suitor in Mr Bingle, apparently - a man I know nothing about. I suppose I should at least meet him. Perhaps Sir Archibald might introduce us?

"Mr . Bingle is a correct man who enjoys the hunt, and owns a textile business". Is it awful to say he doesn't sound too much fun? Well, perhaps I shouldn't judge just yet. If I'm to meet him at Sir Archibald's garden party, I'll need some dresses from the Emporium Exotique.

I'm afraid you arrived just as Mr. Bingle left. He said nice things about my dresses, but not the company I keep. I am not to meet with Alonso any more, he says. *sobs*. But as Sir Archibald says, it's probably for my own good. Anyway, I must go, or I shall be late for the garden party...

I keep hearing about Mr. Bingle. It makes me excited to finally meet him! BRING HIM TO ME! Hehe. Ahh, poor Bente - all these people around her, telling her what to do. She's just like a bird in one of those cages, eh?
It's funny. Mr. Bingle confessed to me that he has no interest in Bente - only her pigs. See for yourself, he's rolling out there in the mud right now. I'm sure she'd love to see a photograph?
Our dear child is ready for marriage? And to Mr. Bingle of all people? Well, please do give her this letter: an invitation to our little garden party, at which said Mr. Bingle will also be present.
Meet Graves? Fine! If he wants to meet, w-w-why not? If he thinks this will scare me away from Miss Jorgensen, he's very much mistaken.

Oh, this photograph is horrid! Did you take it? I mean, I adore animals, but not like this! How can I forgive myself for almost breaking ties with Alonso? He's proven once again to be the only *very* close friend I have.

Beryl seems to have done a wonderful job of teaching these street children good manners. I'm sure the Queen would be delighted to have them stay at the palace for a short time — it could help fulfil some of the promises to help the poor she's made as of late.

Sir Archibald didn't grimace too heavily as he announced the Queen had agreed to let the street children stay over at High Clarence Hall. Can you make sure they have a lovely, safe trip? I promised Beryl I'd take good care of them, you see.

I have written to Sir Archibald to apologise for the behaviour of the street children at the palace. Please, could you deliver my message? If Archie asks, tell him Beryl's agreed to pay any damages she can, though she did say that she isn't a woman of great family wealth. If the repairs are very expensive, it may be beyond her.
Oh Bente, you poor dear soul! Those children weren't merely a menace, they were a highly-organised gang of thieves! There's not a bit of silver cutlery left in all of High Clarence Hall!
The expedition to the ruins of the sun worshippers should have been back weeks ago! I do remember they were worried about a mysterious curse... I wonder if you might find them and help them?

Ahoy! Our heartiest thanks for your help. The last we remember, we were aboard our ship, carrying the sarcophagus we found in the cave of the sun worshippers. Then everything went black... I wonder if there are any clues nearby? I'll bet it was the curse...

Ah, I remember it all now! As we left the sunlit reef, the whale seemed angry and lashed out with its tail. Our helmsman must have panicked, as that's when we were wrecked! But that doesn't explain what happened to the artefact - or where the missing crew of the little boat went...

I warned you about the curse! The artefact, it must be destroyed! Bente won't listen to an old sea dog like me - she'll put it on display, God forbid! For all our sakes, destroy it and end this blight!

Oh, dear me! No sooner was the mummy exhibit opened to the public than a wave of disease seemed to wash over my lovely, happy city! Miss Sarmento has promised to find me some emergency supplies - please, you must help!
Now I remember! It was our helmsman! He seemed on edge from the moment we departed the caves. No sooner had we left port than he steered us into a reef!
Some of the crew went out on a dive to recover our navigation equipment... But when we winched them back up, all we found were severed cables! It's the curse, I tells yer!
This monster! That explains the dreadful eerie noise we heard in the darkness, but it doesn't explain how we came to be wrecked here...

A curse? Oh, how silly! Well, I'm glad neither of us believe in all that nonsense. Really, it isn't very fair on all those ancient civilisations that we always assume their legacies are nothing more than traps and curses. I shall immediately place this wonderful artefact on display for all to see!

Thank you for saving my people! I don't know how I shall ever thank you. Curse or coincidence, I promise to be a little more careful in the future. The lives of the living are worth more than anything else. Please, take this vile mummy with you - I don't want to see it ever again!
Look for the wild animals in the mountains on Bente's main island.

I was elated with your western method of preserving edibles in metal boxes, but I cannot help but taste the tang of brass in the ones we produce... Is there a secret to it that is lost on me? I desire to savour the difference in your canned food.
I am in awe of this horseless carriage. I understand it uses steam to move but... I do not comprehend how exactly it is done! I need to look at it more closely. Will you quench my curiosity?

Where I come from, lacquerware is an exquisite art passed on for generation. I am utterly unfamiliar to this wood veneer of the other New World, but I would love to experiment with this foreign material. Would you be able to provide it?
Oh, sweet explosions of golden orbs in my mouth! And I learned you have alchemists that extract the nectar and turn it into an enchanting beverage! May I be granted a taste?
The brutes I sent to retrieve my last shipment from Madame Kahina's harbour brought nothing but shattered porcelain... Will you be the steady hand to bring me a memento of my childhood...?
Friend, did you notice the terrible storm? My father sent precious presents to ease my homesickness, but I'm afraid they might have been torn from their course in the raging winds...
Dare I dream my words will ever reach the Queen's honourable ears...? You are in good terms with her Sir Archibald, are you not? Could you bring my poems to him and maybe spare a kind word...?

One of the things I miss the most is taking those long walks through the imperial gardens. I've been looking for curious and beautiful flora to garnish the grounds of my residence, and I hear Kahina has the seeds to grow pristine, cloud-like flowers.

Oh, no... My mother sends ships carrying "visitors"... But I am sure their true purpose is much darker than that. Please, just... Bring them here discreetly, so I can send them back before they embarrass me.

Sir Archibald sent me a note to thank me for the cookies, but I didn't send any! It must have been my mother... I know her - there is no way this gift had good intentions. Go there, and make the cookies vanish before someone cracks them open.

Oh, the delicate perfume of brewing tea. I miss it so much it hurts to remember... There isn't a day I don't regret leaving my favourite kettle back home. I know Beryl, too, is an avid tea-drinker. Maybe she has a fine kettle she could spare me?

I just received a report containing details of your trade history... But I didn't order it, I swear! It must have been one of my mother's uncalled-for 'favours'. The spies must be roaming your city. In the name of my family, I deeply apologise!
A beautiful flower that grows in the mountains has been haunting my dreams lately. I know I will not stop thinking about it until I can have some for my flower arrangements...
Wind-swollen sails are such an inspiring image, are they not? I would like to capture the words of homecoming they whisper in the wind, but I cannot see the docks from my study...
I remember the dolphins passing by our vessel when I first sailed to these lands, lifting every shadow of fear from my heart. Had I but an image of them to help me capture these emotions in a poem...
I envy the wisdom of elephants in these troubled times. Could I capture their mighty essence in ink and paper...? I wonder maybe if a had a picture...

My father has asked me to write a report about the wonders of the western railway system and its use in transporting oil, but I am at a loss for words at its technology. Could you take a picture of your oil harbour to illustrate my report?
I do not recognise my father's kindness in these words, but this request for images of Sir Archibald's headquarters does bear his seal... Do you keep your camera still?
Yesterday night I realised I never properly expressed my gratitude for your friendship. This token brought me many visions of home, I hope it now serves to remind you of me.
My sister is coming to visit! She wanted to contemplate all the marvels I wrote about with her own eyes. I need to prepare for her arrival, will you escort her safely into my longing arms?

I can never repay you for delivering my sister unscathed back to me. She is determined to experience every wonder hidden in this region. I told her many perils lurk beneath the surface, but she feels safe with you...

No... My sister has been taken! I... never should have entrusted you with her precious life... I beseech you, help me mend my reckless actions. This is all the gold I own, exchange it for my sister's freedom and bring her back to me.
Oh, is that all you have...? In that case, terribly sorry, but we do have a much higher bidder on this little princess' life.
My family is forever in your debt, dear friend. My sister will remember the beauty of your home with a sweet smile thanks to your kindness. She gave me this token for you, please accept it.
No, mei-mei! It... it cannot be... She only wanted to see her big sister's world... I will never be able to look at my father's face again... Our family is forever broken, thanks to you.

I... I am at a loss of words. You do not understand how much you have done for us, for my family. I owe my sister's life to your selfless actions. The Emperor is forever in your debt, dear friend. I am.

Father wrote. A close friend of the family set sail to deliver an important present to me... I am afraid this matter requires maximum discretion. Your ships will raise no suspicion, were you so kind as to retrieve it for me...

Oh no... How could this happen!? The gift, it was stolen from your Queen! My mother's counselor has prepared a gift to appease her, in the hope we can send it through Sir Archibald, but I dare not venture there myself...

Friend! I swear I know not what my mother had me send the Queen, but she stormed in here demanding I pledge allegiance to her! I will forever be despised in my country, but I have no other option... I must do this for my father...
Father comforted my doubtful heart, but mother... She has sent imperial warships to clean the stain I put on our family's name! Her shadow already looms on the horizon... Aid me, friend!
Is this what the Princess Qing would like me to hand the Queen on her behalf? Oh dear... Very well - I will make sure she receives it. Let us all brace ourselves...

It is over... It was no doubt the Empress' hand that steered this unfortunate chain of events in an attempt to tarnish father's reputation. I still cannot believe I stood up against her... You truly inspire endless courage, friend.

Father's always wanted to visit the Old World, but his obligations never allow him to leave his distinguished seat for long enough. I want to send him a piece of this land. The vessel that carries it, too, must represent the best of your culture. Do you have any suggestions?

The way it sways in the waves so majestically... Father deserves nothing less! I will command my shipyard to start its construction at once. I know you want to help - could you bring us the materials?
Nothing more beautiful ever sailed away from my shipyard. It's the perfect wrapping, but we still lack the gift... I've already had some ideas, but what would you suggest?

Friend! What a magnificent treasure we've put together. Only one more thing remains. A masterpiece from the past - something that truly represents the history of the West. Madame Kahina has a good eye for such treasures.
Oh, a present as grand as the land that inspired it, and as pre-eminent as the man that shall receive it. It is ready. Shall we gently guide this treasure home?

Normally, I don't participate in the excitement of expeditions, but this time, they've returned with a treasure that intrigues me: a tablet written in a forgotten language. I presume Madame Kahina must speak every language, whether new or ancient...

Oh! According to Madame Kahina's translation, the writing on the map points to a place in the middle of the sea. I need to know what lies beneath the surface! Maybe you have someone on your island who's studied the oceans, and might be able to help?
Oh! This person does seem most capable of finding out what it is the tablet speaks of. I will mark the place on your map - let's see what you discover.

I wouldn't believe it if I didn't hold them in my hands... Ancient scrolls, sealed under water for centuries! I will ask Madame Kahina to study them and produce their translations. I cannot wait to read these forgotten words! In the meantime, you can have the originals, as reward for all your efforts.
Indeed, I know this language: it is from the ancient Aegeans. I will write a translation for the Princess, free of charge. I do enjoy these tasks.

Our New Year is fast approaching! I would love to commemorate this passing of the year with something that represents both the fragility of time, and the technological advances of the era. Do you have anything in mind?

How could you!? Clocks are terrible luck, especially if given as a gift for the New Year! I guess as a foreigner, you cannot be blamed... I know what you can do, though. I need some fine cloth to decorate the streets. Think you can you provide that?
Oh, dear... How could you bring me white cloth!? This is a festival, not a funeral! Maybe just bring me some sweet refreshments, then. I don't see how you could go wrong with that...
Grapes! What a pleasant surprise! This time you hit the nail right on its head: they symbolise abundance and prosperity. Thank you for all your help and efforts - now the New Year festival may begin!

At first, I couldn't see past my heartbroken fog - but now that beauty has lifted the clouds from my eyes, I can recognise wonders I never could have dreamed of. If only more travellers from my homeland would feel welcome, and dare cast their anchor here...
The greatest gift I could grant you, friend, is the peace and tranquility of listening to the soft tinkling of water running from a nice pavilion. Please try it, and let me know what you think!

Princess Qing is doing her best to mimic the western way of preserving food in cans, but she believes she is not doing something right, for she perceives a metallic taste in the ones her company produces. She has asked you to bring her some of yours in an attempt to figure out what she is doing wrong.
The Princess is terribly curios about the steam carriage. She would like to know more about how it works and has asked you to deliver some to her.
The Princess would like to try using wood veneer to recreate the lacquered boxes from her home, she has asked you to provide it for her.
The Princess loves grapes; they're one of her most relished pleasures. She's heard of a special beverage crafted from their juice, and cannot wait to taste it.
Princess Qing's best tradeship has already ruined a perfect shipment of porcelain from Madame Kahina's harbour. This time, she has asked you to retrieve it for her.
Qing's father sent her a ship with presents from home, but they never arrived. She has asked you to keep an eye out for them and retrieve whatever you find.
Princess Qing has been working on her poems and wishes to have them read at the Queen's court. She has asked you to bring her manuscript to Sir Archibald and endorse her a little.

The Princess longs to have a beautiful garden like the ones she had back home. She's heard of a beautiful flower that will fill her grounds with fluffy clouds, and would love it if you could get the seeds for her from Madame Kahina.
The Empress has sent her daughter a visiting party from home, but Qing is certain they don't mean well. She'd like you to accompany them to her harbour with the utmost discretion.
The Princess is worried that the cookies Sir Archibald received might be a less than kind present from the Empress. She's asked you to smuggle them out of High Clarence Hall, before tragedy strikes.
The Princess misses her tea dearly, but she left her kettle back home. Luckily, Beryl too loves tea, so she figured she might have a spare kettle to lend her.
The Princess has alerted you that her mother has been sending spies to gather information about your trade partners. They lurk in the streets of your city, wearing black hooded robes.
The Princess' dreams have been haunted by a beautiful flower that only grows in the mountains. She wants to have some for her flower arrangements, but they're somewhat out of her reach.

The Princess is trying to write a poem about sails in the wind, but she is finding it hard to capture the image without looking at them. She needs you to take a picture she can keep by her desk to find inspiration.

Princess Qing remembers the hope and joy dolphins brought to her heart when she sailed for the Old World. She would like to write a poem about it, but she needs to remember the sight of them with a picture.
The Princess needs help with her next poem. Her source of inspiration, elephants, lay far away from her reach, but you can help her if you take a picture of one.

It seems like Emperor Qing is very interested in the railway system. The Princess has been tasked with writing a report about it, but she's asked if you could help her illustrate it by providing a picture of your oil harbour.
Qing has been tasked with delivering a picture of Sir Archibald's island. She asked you to take it for her.
The Princess deeply relishes your friendship. She would like to give you a little memento from the East so that you can remember her.
The Princess Qing's sister is paying her a visit and needs to be safely escorted to Qing's island while she's busy preparing everything for her arrival.
Qing's little sister has reached her destination safely thanks to you, and now she feels it is safe for her to visit every corner of the region as long as your warships come along.
Qing's sister is held prisoner by the mysterious attackers. She has asked you to deliver the ransom in gold and get her sister safe back to her.
Qing's sister's kidnappers have refused to release her. There is only one way left to break her free...

The Princess has received a letter from the Emperor telling her that a friend of the family was going to bring her a precious item. She has reasons to believe the situation demands discretion, and has asked you to retrieve it for her instead.

The gift Qing asked you to bring her was a treasured belonging of the Queen! The Princess has asked you to deliver it back to Sir Archibald along with a present, as she doesn't dare to go there herself.

Qing was set up and now the Queen demands that she pledges allegiance to her. She has no choice, even if bending the knee is against the Empress wishes, it is what she must do for her father, the Emperor.
The Empress was not happy to hear her daughter bent the knee before a western ruler and has sent a fleet to attack her! Qing has asked you to back her up in battle.

Princess Qing knows her father would love to leave his duties behind and travel the world. Unfortunately, the Emperor cannot afford to do so, and so she wants to send him a piece of the Old World, starting with a classical ship. Take a picture of a suitable one.
The Princess loves your suggestion of building a ship of the line, and has already begun her preparations. However, she needs your help in gathering the materials.
The ship is ready to set sail for the East, but first it needs to be filled with presents that represent the Old World. Qing looks to you for suggestions.

The Princess is elated at the gift you're helping her put together for her father, but it still requires one more thing: a treasure from the past. She'd like you to go to Madame Kahina, and look for something that fits the bill.
Qing's present for her father is finally ready to leave port. The Princess has asked that you escort it safely on its way.
Princess Qing's expedition has brought back an enigmatic tablet written in an old language. She'd like to know more about it, and thinks Madame Kahina may be able to tell you more.
The tablet found by Princess Qing's expedition seems to mark a place in the middle of the ocean. She'd like you to ask around your harbour, and see if you can find someone who can help you.
You found a diver that will be able to search the ocean for whatever lies beneath the waves. The Princess has marked the spot on your map - go forth, and bring her what you find.
